18-19. \\Lord Viṣṇu laughed loudly and spoke these words then: “Formerly you were oppressed by Daityas and protected by me. But today a great danger of everlasting nature has arisen from this Liṅga. It is not possible for me to protect you, O Suras, from the danger from this Liṅga.”

## \|\| 1.7.20 \|\|

*acyutenaivamuktāste devā ściṃtānvitābhavan \|*  
*tadā nabhogatā vāṇī uvācāśvāsya vai surān \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On being told thus by Viṣṇu, Devas became worried. Thereupon an ethereal voice spoke thus, consoling all the Suras:

## \|\| 1.7.21 \|\|

*etalliṃgaṃ saṃvṛṇuṣva pūjanāya janārdana \|*  
*piṃḍibhūtvā mahābāho rakṣasva sacarācaram \|*  
*tatheti matvā bagavānvīrabhadro'bhyapūjayat \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “O Janārdana, choose this Liṅga for worship. Becoming a mass of refulgence, O mighty one, protect the mobile and immobile beings.”

Saying “so be it” and honouring itjñord Vīrabhadra worshipped it.

## \|\| 1.7.22 \|\|

*brahmādibhaḥ suragaṇaiḥ sahitaistadānīṃ saṃpūjitaḥ śivavidhānarato mahātmā \|*  
*sravīrabhadraḥ śaśiśekharo'sau śivapriyo rudrasamastrilokyām \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. At that time, the noble-souled Vīrabhadra, having the moon for his crest and engaged in carrying out the orders of Śiva, was worshipped by the groups of Suras beginning with Brahmā, collectively. Vīrabhadra was a favourite of Śiva and was on a par with Rudra in the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.7.23-24 \|\|

*liṃgasyārcanayukto'sau vīrabhadro'bhavattadā \|*  
*tadrūpasyaiva liṃgasya yena sarvamidaṃ jagat \|\| 23 \|\|*

*udbhāti sthitimāpnoti tathā vilayameti ca \|*  
*talliṃgaṃ liṃgamityāhurlayanāttattvavittamāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Then Vīrabhadra was absorbed in worshipping the Liṅga. It (the Liṅga) had the same form wherefrom the entire universe takes it origin, derives sustenance and gets merged with it. The excellent ones among those who are the knowers of the

Reality call it Liṅga, because of its being a place of rest (to the absorbed).

## \|\| 1.7.25 \|\|

*brahmāṇḍāgolakairvyāptaṃ tathā rudrākṣabhūṣitam \|*  
*tathā liṃgaṃ mahajjātaṃ sarveṣāṃ duratikramam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Liṅga became pervaded by the spheres of the Cosmic Eggs. It was embellished with Rudrākṣas. It grew so large that it could not be surpassed by anyone.

## \|\| 1.7.26-27 \|\|

*tadā sarve'tha vibudhā ṛṣo vai mahāprabhāḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuśca mahāliṃgaṃ vedāvādaiḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 26 \|\|*

*aṇoraṇīyāṃstvaṃ deva tathā tvaṃ mahato mahān \|*  
*tasmāttvayā vidhātavyaṃ sarvaiṣāṃ liṃgapūjanam \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Then all Devas and sages of great lustre eulogized the great Liṅga by means of the Vedic words (Mantras) separately:

“O lord, you are minuter than the atom. So also you are greater than the greatest. Hence, O lord Śiva, you must make such arrangements as to make the worship of the Liṅga easy for everyone.”

## \|\| 1.7.28-35 \|\|

*tadānīmeva sarveṇa liṃgaṃ ca bahuśaḥ kṛtam \|*  
*satye brahmeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ vaikuṇṭhe ca sadāśivaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*amarāvatyāṃ supratiṣṭhamamareśvarasaṃjñakam \|*  
*varuṇeśvaraṃ ca vāruṇyāṃ yāmyāṃ kāleśvaraṃ prabhum \|\| 29 \|\|*

*nairṛteśvaraṃ ca nairṛtyāṃ vāyavyāṃ pāvaneśvaram \|*  
*kedāraṃ mṛtyuloke ca tathaiva amaresvaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

*oṃkāraṃ narmadāyāṃ ca mahākālaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*kāśyāṃ viśveśvaraṃ devaṃ prayāge laliteśvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

*triyambakaṃ brahmagirau kalau bhadreśvaraṃ tathā \|*  
*drākṣārāmeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ gaṃgāsāgarasaṃgame \|\| 32 \|\|*

*saurāṣṭre ca tathā liṃgaṃ someśvaramiti smṛtam \|*  
*tathā sarveśvaraṃ vindhye śrīśaile śikhareśvaram \|*  
*kāntyāmallālanāthaṃ ca siṃhanāthaṃ ca siṃgale \|\| 33 \|\|*

*virūpākṣaṃ tathā liṃgaṃ koṭiśaṅkarameva ca \|*  
*tripurāntakaṃ bhīmeśamamareśvarameva ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*bhogeśvaraṃ ca pātāle hāṭakeśvarameva ca \|*  
*evamādīnyanekāni liṃgāni bhuvanatraye \|*  
*sthāpitāni tadā devairviśvopakṛtihetave \|\| 35 \|\|*

28-35. At that time itself, many types of Liṅgas were evolved by Sarva (Śiva)\[3\], viz. the Brahmeśvara Liṅga in the world called Satya (god Brahmā’s region), Sadāśiva Liṅga in Vaikuṇṭha, a well-established Liṅga named Amareśvara in Amarāvatī (Indra’s capital), Varuṇeśvara Liṅga in the city of Varuṇa, Lord Kāleśvara in the city of Yama, Nairṛteśvara Liṅga in the city of Nirṛti, Pavaneśvara Liṅga in the city of Vāyu, in the Mṛtyuloka\[4\] Kedāra Liṅga as well as Amareśvara, Oṃkāra Liṅga as well as Mahākāla in the Narmadā (region), Lord Viśveśvara in Kāśī, Laliteśvara in Prayāga, Triyaṃbaka in Brahmagiri (Nasik District) as well as Bhadreśvara in Kali, Drākṣārāmeśvara Liṅga in the place of the Union of Gaṅgā with ocean, the Liṅga remembered as Someśvara in Saurāṣṭra, Sarveśvara Liṅga on the Vindhya, Śikhareśvara Liṅga on Śrīśaila, Mallālanātha (?) in Kānti, Siṃhanātha in Siṅgala (Sīṃhala), so also many Liṅgas such as Virūpākṣa Liṅga, Koṭiśaṅkara, Tripurāntaka, Bhīmeśa, Amareśvara, Bhogeśvara and Hāṭakeśvara in Pātāla. These and many other Liṅgas of this sort were installed in all the three worlds by Devas for helping the entire universe.

## \|\| 1.7.36 \|\|

*liṃgeśaiśca tathā sarvaiḥ pūrṇamāsījjagattrayam \|*  
*tathā ca vīrabhadrāṃśāḥ pūjārthamamaraiḥ kṛtāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. And thus all the three worlds became full of great Liṅgas. Similarly, gods created Vīrabhadrāṃśas (portions of Vīrabhadra) for worship.

## \|\| 1.7.37 \|\|

*tatra viṃśatisaṃskārāsteṣāmaṣṭādhikābhavan \|*  
*kathitāḥ śaṃkareṇaiva liṃgasyācanasūcakāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. There were twenty-eight Saṃskāras (consecratory rites) there in the process of worship of Liṅga. They were mentioned by Śaṅkara himself.

## \|\| 1.7.38-41 \|\|

*saṃti rudreṇa kathitāḥ śivadharmā sanātanāḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadro yathā rudrastathānye guravaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*gurorjātāśca guravo vikhyātā bhuvanatraye \|*  
*liṃgasya mahimāna tu nandī jānāti tattvataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tathā skando hi bhagavānnye te nāmadhārakāḥ \|*  
*yathoktāḥ śivadharamā hi nandinā parikīrttitāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*śailādena mahābhāgā vicitrā liṃgadhārakāḥ \|*  
*śavasyopari liṃgaṃ ca dhriyate ca purātanaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

38-41. There are eternal Śivadharmas mentioned by Rudra where Vīrabhadra, Rudra and other Gurus (preceptors) are remembered. The sons of Gurus also have become famous in the three worlds as Gurus. Only Nandī knows factually the greatness of Liṅga. So also lord Skanda and those others who bear his names.

All the Śivadharmas have been glorified as mentioned by Nandī, the son of Śilāda. Many wonderful persons of exalted nature have been glorified as bearers of Liṅgas.

Liṅga is held above a dead body by the ancient people.

## \|\| 1.7.42 \|\|

*liṃgena saha pañcatvaṃ liṃgena saha jīvitam \|*  
*ete dharmāḥ supratiṣṭhāḥ śailādena pratiṣṭhitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Living with Liṅga and dying with Liṅga—these virtuous rites have been established by Śailāda (Nandin).

## \|\| 1.7.43-45 \|\|

*dharmaḥ pāśupataḥ śreṣṭhaḥ skandena pratipālitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*śuddhā pañcākṣarī vidyā prāsādī tadanantaram \|*  
*ṣaḍakṣarī tathā vidyā prāsādasya ca dīpikā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*skandāttatsamanuprāptamagastyena mahātmanā \|*  
*paścādācāryabhedena hyāgamā bahavo'bhavan \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. The religion of the Pāśupata established by Skanda is the most excellent one. The five-syllabled Mantra (Na-maḥ-Śi-vā-ya) is the purest. Then comes the Prāsādī (Oṃkāra) Mantra. The six-syllabled Mantra (Oṃ, na-maḥ-Śi-vā-ya) is the illuminator of the Praṇava.

From Skanda it was acquired by the noble-souled Agastya. Afterwards due to the difference in the preceptors, many Āgamas were composed.

## \|\| 1.7.46 \|\|

*kiṃ tu vai bahunoktena śvi ityakṣaradvayam \|*  
*uccārayaṃti sa nityaṃ te rudrā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Of what avail is much talk? Those who utter the two syllables Śi-va everyday are Rudras themselves. There is no doubt in this matter.

## \|\| 1.7.47 \|\|

*satāṃ mārgaṃ puraskṛtya ye sarve te purāṃtakāḥ \|*  
*vīrā māheśvarājñeyāḥ pāpakṣayakarā nṛṇām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Those who follow the path of good people are all Purāntakas (Śiva). They should be known as heroes of Maheśvara. They destroy the sins of men.

## \|\| 1.7.48 \|\|

*prasaṃgenānupaṃkṣeṇa śradvayā ca yadṛcchayā \|*  
*śivabhaktiṃ prakurvanti ye vai te yāṃti sadgatim \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Those who perform rites of devotion incidentally, as a consequence of something else, by chance or as an act of faith, attain the goal of the good.

## \|\| 1.7.49 \|\|

*śrṛṇudhvaṃ kathayāmīha itihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*kṛtaṃ śivālayaṃ yacca pataṃgyā mārjanaṃ purā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Listen. I shall narrate an old legend in this connection. Sweeping was performed formerly by a female bird in a temple of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.7.50 \|\|

*āgatā bhakṣaṇārthaṃ hi naivedyaṃ kena cārpitam \|*  
*mārjanaṃ rajastasyāḥ pakṣābhyāmabhavatpurā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. It had come (into the temple) for the sake of food. The Naivedya was offered by someone. When it fluttered its wings, the dust particles happened to be swept away.

## \|\| 1.7.51 \|\|

*tena karmavipākena uttamaṃ svargamāgatā \|*  
*bhuktvā svargasukhaṃ cograṃ punaḥ saṃsāramāgatā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. As a result of that meritorious deed, she went to the excellent heaven. After enjoying the heavenly pleasures, she came back to the fierce world once again.

## \|\| 1.7.52 \|\|

*kāśirājasutā jātā sundarīnāma viśrutā \|*  
*pūrvābhyāsācca kalyāṇī babhūva paramā satī \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. She was born as the daughter of the king of Kāśī. She became famous by the name Sundarī. Thanks to the previous experience, that girl of auspicious features became a great chaste lady.

## \|\| 1.7.53 \|\|

*uṣasyuṣasi tanvaṃgī śivadvāraratā sadā \|*  
*saṃmārjanaṃ ca kurute bhaktyā paramayā yutā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Early in the morning, the lady of slender limbs was always present at the doorway of the temple of Śiva. With great devotion she used to sweep the premises.

## \|\| 1.7.54 \|\|

*svayameva tadā devī sundarī rājakanyakā \|*  
*tathābhūtāṃ ca tāṃ dṛṣṭvā ṛṣiruddālako'bravīt \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The gentle princess, Sundarī, did everything herself. On seeing her in that activity, Uddālaka, the sage, enquired:

## \|\| 1.7.55-56 \|\|

*sukumārī satī bāle svayameva kathaṃ śubhe \|*  
*saṃmārjanaṃ ca kuruṣe kanyake tvaṃ śucismite \|\| 55 \|\|*

*dāsī dāsyaśca bahavaḥ saṃti devi tavāgrataḥ \|*  
*tavājñayā kariṣyaṃti sarvaṃ saṃmārjanādikam \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. “O girl of splendid features, you are delicate in body. Why do you sweep yourself, O girl of bright smiles? O gentle lady, you have in front of you many men and women servants. At your bidding they will do all the sweeping work etc.”

## \|\| 1.7.57 \|\|

*ṛṣestadvacanaṃ śrutvā prahasyedamuvāca ha \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On hearing those words of the sage, she laughingly said thus:

## \|\| 1.7.58-62 \|\|

*śivasevāṃ prakurvāṇāḥ śivabhaktipuraskṛtāḥ \|*  
*ye narāścaiva nāryyaśca śivalokaṃ vrajaṃti vai \|\| 58 \|\|*

*saṃmārjanaṃ ca pāṇibhyāṃ padbhyāṃ yānaṃ śivālaye \|*  
*tasmānmayā ca kriyate saṃmārjanamataṃdritam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*anyatkiñcinna jānāmi ekaṃ saṃmārjanaṃ vinā \|*  
*ṛṣistadvacanaṃ śrutvā manasā ca vimṛśya hi \|\| 60 \|\|*

*anayā kiṃ kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ keyaṃ kasya prasādataḥ \|*  
*tadā jñānaṃ ca ṛṣiṇā tatsarvaṃ jñānacakṣuṣā \|*  
*vismayena samāviṣṭastūṣṇīṃbhūto'bhavattadā \|\| 61 \|\|*

*savismayo'bhūdatha tadviditvā uddālako jñānavatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ \|*  
*śivaprabhāvaṃ manasā viciṃtya jñānātparaṃ bodhamavāpa śāṃtaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

58-60a. “The men and women who render service to Śiva, those who are prompted by devotion to Śiva, do go to the world of Śiva. The sweeping must be done by one’s own hands. One should go to the temple on one’s own foot. Hence, sweeping is done by me unweariedly. I do not know anything else, excepting the single act of sweeping.”

60b-62. On hearing her words, the sage pondered: ‘Who is she? What has been done by her previously? By whose favour (did she get all these)?’ Then everything was understood by the sage through the eye of (the power of his) spiritual knowledge.

## \|\| 1.7.63 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Struck with wonder, he became silent. After knowing it, he became surprised. Thinking about the power of Śiva, Uddālaka, the most excellent among the learned ones, attained the greatest enlightenment. He became calm and quiescent.

## Chapter 8 - The Story of a Thief: Incarnation of Rāma

## \|\| 1.8.1-3 \|\|

*\| lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*taskaro'pi purā brahmansarvadharmabāhiṣkṛtaḥ \|*  
*brahmaghno'sau surāpaśca suvarṇasya ca taskaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*laṃpaṭohi mahāpāpa uttamastrīṣu sarvadā \|*  
*dyūtakārī sadā maṃdaḥ kitavaiḥ saha saṃgataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ekadā krīḍatā tena hāritaṃ dyūtamadbhutam \|*  
*kitavairmardyamāno hi tadā novāca kiñcana \|\| 3 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

1-3. O Brāhmaṇas, once there was a great sinner He was a thief. He was excommunicated from all religious rites. He was a Brāhmaṇa-slayer, a drink-addict and a thief of gold. He sought the company of excellent women in an illicit way. He was stupid and slow and always engaged in gambling along with gamblers and cunning fellows. Once while playing, he lost wonderfully (large amount). Smashed and hit by rogues and gamblers, he did not speak anything.

## \|\| 1.8.4-5 \|\|

*pīḍito'pyabhavattūṣṇīṃ tairuktaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ \|*  
*dyūte tvayā ca taddravyaṃ hāritaṃ kiṃ prayacchasi \|\| 4 \|\|*

*no vā tatkathyatāṃ śīghraṃ yāthātathyena durmate \|*  
*yaddhāritaṃ prayacchāmi rātrāvityabravīcca saḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Though he was harassed and tormented, he kept quiet. Then that great sinner was asked thus by them: “You have lost this much wealth in the game of dice. Are you going to give it or not? O wicked fellow, let this be told immediately and precisely.” Then he said: “What has been lost by me, I shall give at night.”

## \|\| 1.8.6 \|\|

*tairmuktastena vākyena gatāste kitavādayaḥ \|*  
*tadā niśīthasamaye gato'sau śivamaṃdiram \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thanks to that statement, he was released by them. Those gamblers and rogues then went away. Then at mid-night he went to the temple of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.8.7 \|\|

*śirodhiruhya śambhośca ghaṇṭāmādātumudyataḥ \|*  
*tāvatkailāsaśikhare śaṃbhuḥ provāca kiṃkarān \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Climbing on to the head of Śaṃbhu, he attempted to take the bell. At that time on the peak of Kailāsa, Śaṃbhu said to his servants:

## \|\| 1.8.8 \|\|

*anena yatkṛtaṃ cādya sarveṣāmadhikaṃ bhuvi \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva bhaktānāṃ variṣṭho'yaṃ ca matpriyaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “What has been done by this fellow today is far superior to anything done by anyone on the earth. He is the most excellent one among all my devotees, hence he is my great favourite.”

## \|\| 1.8.9 \|\|

*iti proktvāna yāmāsa vīrabhadrādibhirgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*te sarve tvaritā jagmuḥ kailāsācchivavallabhāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After saying this, he commanded the Gaṇas beginning with Vīrabhadra to bring him (the thief-gambler). They hurriedly started from Kailāsa, the favourite (resort) of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.8.10 \|\|

*sarvairḍamarunādena nāditaṃ bhuvanatrayam \|*  
*tāndṛṣṭvā sahasottīrya taskarosau durātmavān \|*  
*liṃgasya mastakātsadyaḥ palāyanaparo'bhavat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The three worlds were filled with the sound of Ḍamarus by all of them. On seeing them, the evil-minded thief got down suddenly from the top of the Liṅga and took to his heels immediately.

## \|\| 1.8.11-14 \|\|

*palāyamānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā vīrabhadraḥ samāhvayat \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kasmādvibhepi re manda devadevo mahesvaraḥ \|*  
*prasannastava jātodya udāracarito hyasau \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ityuktvā taṃ vimāne ca kṛtvā kailāsamāyayau \|*  
*pārṣado hi kṛtastena taskaro hi mahātmanā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tasmādbhāvyā śive bhaktiḥ sarveṣāmapi dehinām \|*  
*paśavo'pi hi pūjyāḥ syuḥ kiṃ punarmānavābhuvi \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. On seeing him fleeing, Vīrabhadra called him: “Whom do you fear, O stupid fellow? Maheśvara, the lord of Devas, has been pleased with you, as he is very liberal-minded.”

After saying thus and placing him in the aerial chariot, he came to Kailāsa. The thief was made an attendant by that noble-souled (lord).

Hence, devotion to Śiva must be preserved and cultivated by all embodied beings. Even animals will be worthy of being worshipped thereby. What to say of men on the earth?

## \|\| 1.8.15-16 \|\|

*ye tārkikāstarkaparāstatha mīmāṃsakāśca ye \|*  
*anyonyavādinaścānye cānye vātmavitarkakāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ekavākyaṃ na kurvaṃti śivārcanabahiṣkṛtāḥ \|*  
*tarko hi kriyate yaiśca tesarve kiṃ śivaṃ vinā \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. The followers of Tarka-śāstra are engaged in abstract reasoning and arguments. So are the followers of the Mīmāṃsā School. They go on arguing and disputing among themselves. And there are others who deliberate on and discuss about the existence, nature etc. of the Soul, but never reach any unanimity, or reconciliation of (their) differences. They are excluded from the worship of Śiva. Without Śiva, of what significance are they, by whom only arguments are forwarded?

## \|\| 1.8.17 \|\|

*tathā kiṃ bahunoktena sarve'pi sthirajaṃgamāḥ \|*  
*prāṇino'pi hi jāyaṃte kevalaṃ liṃgadhāriṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Of what avail is much talk? All mobile and immobile beings, all animals too, are born bearing the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.8.18 \|\|

*piṇḍīyuktaṃ yatā liṃgaṃ sthāpitaṃ ca yathā'bhavat \|*  
*tathā narā liṃgayuktāḥ piṇḍībhūtāstatā striyaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Just as the Liṅga is placed (and consecrated) in conjunction with the Piṇḍī (globular solid pedestal), so also men are endowed with Liṅgas and women afe Piṇḍīs.

## \|\| 1.8.19 \|\|

*śivaśaktiyutaṃ sarvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram \|*  
*taṃ śivaṃ mauḍhyatastyaktvā mūḍhāścānyaṃ bhajaṃti ye \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The entire universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings is endowed with (the union of) Śiva and Śakti. Those are foolish fellows who, out of delusion, eschew devotion to such Śiva and worship others.

## \|\| 1.8.20 \|\|

*dharmamātyaṃtikaṃ tucchaṃ naśvaraṃ kṣaṇabhaṃguram \|*  
*yo viṣṇuḥ sa śivo jñeyo yaḥ śivo viṣṇureva saḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Their Dharma is extremely insignificant, perishable and momentary. He who is Viṣṇu should be known as Śiva. He who is Śiva is Viṣṇu alone.

## \|\| 1.8.21 \|\|

*pīṭhikā viṣṇurūpaṃ syālliṃgarūpī maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tasmālliṃgārcanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sarveṣāmapi vai dvijāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The pedestal is the form of Viṣṇu and Maheśvara is in the form of Liṅga. Hence the worship of Liṅga, O Brāhmaṇas, is excellent for everyone.

## \|\| 1.8.22 \|\|

*brahmā maṇimayaṃ liṃgaṃ pūjayatyaniśaṃ śubham \|*  
*indro ratnamayaṃ liṃgaṃ candro muktāmayaṃ tathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Brahmā worships a Ruby-Liṅga always, Indra worships a Liṅga made of gems and Candra (the Moon-god) one of pearls.

## \|\| 1.8.23 \|\|

*bhānustāmramayaṃ liṃgaṃ pūjayatyaniśaṃ śubham \|*  
*raukmaṃ liṃgaṃ kuberaśca pāśī cāraktameva ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Bhānu (the Sun-god) always worships a splendid copper (-coloured) Liṅga. Kubera worships a golden Liṅga and Varuṇa a Liṅga red in colour.

## \|\| 1.8.24 \|\|

*yamo nīlamayaṃ liṃgaṃ rājataṃ nairṛtastathā \|*  
*kāśmīraṃ pavano liṃgamarcayatyaniśaṃ vibhoḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Yama worships a sapphire Liṅga, Nairṛta worships a silver Liṅga, Pavana (Wind-god) always worships a saffron Liṅga of the lord.

## \|\| 1.8.25 \|\|

*evaṃ te liṃgitāḥ sarve lokapālāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*tathā sarve'pi pātāle gaṃdharvāḥ kiṃnaraiḥ saha \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thus, all Guardians of the Quarters including Indra have been characterised as worshippers of Liṅga. So are all (persons) in the nether world and also Gandharvas and Kinnaras.

## \|\| 1.8.26-27 \|\|

*daityānāṃ vaiṣṇavāḥ kecitprahlādapramukhā dvijāḥ \|*  
*tathāhi rākṣasānāṃ ca vibhīṣaṇapurogamāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*baliśca namuciścaiva hiraṇyakaśipustathā \|*  
*vṛṣaparvā vṛṣaścaiva saṃhrādo bāṇa eva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Among Daityas, O Brāhmaṇas, there are certain devotees of Viṣṇu, the chief of whom was Prahlāda. So also among Rākṣasas, those having Vibhīṣaṇa as their leader. So also (were) Bali, Namuci, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Vṛṣaparvan, Vṛṣa, Saṃhrāda and Bāṇa.

## \|\| 1.8.28 \|\|

*ete cānye ca bahavaḥ śiṣyāḥ śukrasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*evaṃ śivārcanaratāḥ sarve te daityadānavāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. These and many others who were the disciples of the intelligent Śukra were engaged in worshipping Śiva. All these Daityas and Dānavas (were devotees of Śiva).

## \|\| 1.8.29-32 \|\|

*rākṣasā eva te sarve śivapūjānvitāḥ sadā \|*  
*hetiḥ prahetiḥ saṃyātirvighasaḥ praghasastathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vidyujjihvastīkṣṇadaṃṣṭro dhūmrākṣo bhīmavikramaḥ \|*  
*mālī caiva sumālī ca mālyavānatibhīṣamaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*vidyutkaiśastaḍijjihvo rāvaṇaśca mahābalaḥ \|*  
*kuṃbhakarṇo durādharṣo vegadarśī pratāpavān \|\| 31 \|\|*

*ete hi rākṣasāḥ śreṣṭhā śivārcanaratāḥ sadā \|*  
*liṃgamabhyarcya ca sadā siddhiṃ prāptāḥ purā tu te \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32. All the following were Rākṣasas and they were always engaged in the worship of Śiva. They were: Heti, Praheti, Saṃyāti, Vighasa, Praghasa, Vidyujjihva, Tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭra, Dhūmrākṣa of terrible valour, Mālī, Sumālī and the extremely terrible Mālyavān, Vidyutkeśa, Tadijjihva, Rāvaṇa of great strength, the invincible Kuṃbhakarṇa and Vegadarśī of great valour. These were great Rākṣasas, who were always engaged in worshipping Śiva. After worshipping the Liṅga formerly, they had always attained Siddhi.

## \|\| 1.8.33 \|\|

*rāvaṇena tapastaptaṃ sarveṣāmapi duḥkhaham \|*  
*tapodhipo mahādevastutoṣa ca tadā bhṛśam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. A severe penance unbearable to all was performed by Ṛāvaṇa. Then Mahādeva, the lord of penance, became much pleased.

## \|\| 1.8.34-35 \|\|

*varānprāyacchata tadā sarveṣāmapi durlabhān \|*  
*jñānaṃ vijñānasahitaṃ labdhaṃ tena sadāśivāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ajeyatvaṃ ca saṃgrāme dvaiguṇyaṃ śirasāmapi \|*  
*paṃcavaktro mahā devo daśavaktro'tha rāvaṇaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. He granted him boons very difficult to be achieved by all others. Wisdom with perfect knowledge was obtained by him from Sadāśiva. He further obtained (invinicibility) in battle and twice the number of heads (as those of god Śiva), for Mahādeva had only five faces, whereas Rāvaṇa had ten faces.

## \|\| 1.8.36 \|\|

*devānṛṣīnpitṝṃścaiva nirjitya tapasā vibhuḥ \|*  
*maheśasya prasādācca sarveṣāmadhiko'bhavat \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Thanks to the grace of Maheśa, that powerful (Rākṣasa) defeated Devas, sages and manes by means of his penance and became superior to all.

## \|\| 1.8.37 \|\|

*rājā trikūṭādhipatirmaheśena kṛto mahān \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca paramāsanamāstitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He was made the great king and ruler of Trikūṭa by Maheśa. He occupied the greatest and most excellent position (seat) among Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.8.38 \|\|

*tapasvināṃ parīkṣāyai yadṛṣīṇāṃ vihiṃsanam \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tena tadā viprā rāvaṇena tapasvinā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. It was for testing (the enduring capacity of) the sages that he harassed them. Violence towards the sages was indulged in, O Brāhmaṇas, by Rāvaṇa who was himself an ascetic, only because he wanted to test them.

## \|\| 1.8.39 \|\|

*ajeyo hi mahāñjāto rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭyaṃtaraṃ kṛtaṃ yena prasādācchaṃkarasya ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Rāvaṇa who made the whole world cry and scream, became great and invincible. Thanks to the grace and favour of Śaṅkara, another creation was evolved by him.

## \|\| 1.8.40 \|\|

*lokapālā jitāstena pratāpena tapasvinā \|*  
*brahmāpi vijito yena tapasā parameṇa hi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The guardians of the worlds were conquered by that ascetic by means of his valour. Brahmā too was subdued by him only through great penance.

## \|\| 1.8.41 \|\|

*amṛtāṃśukaro bhūtvā jito yena śaśī dvijāḥ \|*  
*dāhakatvājjito vahnirīśaḥ kailāsatolanāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. By becoming the nectar-rayed one, he conquered the Moon, O Brāhmaṇas. Through the power of burning, the Fire-god was conquered and Īśa (himself) was conquered by lifting up Kailāsa (mountain).

## \|\| 1.8.42 \|\|

*aiśvaryeṇa jitaścendro viṣṇuḥ sarvagatastathā \|*  
*liṃgārcanaprasādena trailokyaṃ ca vaśīkṛtam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Indra was conquered by means of his Aiśvarya (power and prosperity). So also Viṣṇu, the omnipresent one. By worshipping and propitiating the Liṅga, all the three worlds were controlled by him.

## \|\| 1.8.43 \|\|

*tadā sarve suragaṇā brahmaviṣṇupurogamāḥ \|*  
*merupṛṣṭhaṃ samāsādya sumaṃtraṃ cakrire tadā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. At that time, all the groups of Suras, with Brahmā and Viṣṇu as their leaders, gathered together on the top of Mem and began their deliberation and discussion:

## \|\| 1.8.44-45 \|\|

*pīḍitāḥ smo rāvaṇena tapasā duṣkareṇa vai \|*  
*gokarṇākhye girau devāḥ śrūyatāṃ paramādbhutam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*sākṣālliṃgārcanaṃ yena kṛtamasti mahātmanā \|*  
*jñānajñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ yadyatparamamadbhutam \|*  
*tatkṛtaṃ rāvaṇenaiva sarveṣāṃ duratikramam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. “We have been tormented by Rāvaṇa through his penance, very difficult to be performed (by others). O Devas, let this wonderful story be listened to. On the mountain named Gokarṇa, worship of the Liṅga itself was performed by that noble-souled (hero). What could be known only through knowledge, what could be achieved only through knowledge, whatever.great miracle was there, that which is very difficult to be surpassed by everyone—all these were done by Rāvaṇa alone.

## \|\| 1.8.46 \|\|

*vairāgyaṃ paramāsthāya audāryaṃ ca tato'dhikam \|*  
*tenaiva mamatā tyaktā rāvaṇena mahātmanā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He had adopted the greatest vairāgya (detachment) as well as liberal-midedness \[mindedness/mindness?\] greater even than that (vairāgya). The feeling of mamatā (mineness \[mindness?\]) was eschewed by the noble-souled Rāvaṇa.

## \|\| 1.8.47 \|\|

*saṃvatsarasahasrācca svaśiro hi mahābhujaḥ \|*  
*kṛttvā kareṇa liṃgasya pūjanārthaṃ samarpayat \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After a period of a thousand years, that (hero) of great arms cut one of his own head and offered it with his own hand, for the sake of worshipping the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.8.48 \|\|

*rāvaṇasya kabaṃdhaṃ ca tadagre ca samīpataḥ \|*  
*yogadhāraṇayā yuktaṃ parameṇa samādhinā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Ṛāvaṇa’s body short of one head stood in front of it in the vicinity. īt was endowed with Yogic dhāraṇā (steady abstraction) and the greatest samādhi (concentration).

## \|\| 1.8.49 \|\|

*liṃge layaṃ samādhāya kayāpi kalayā sthitam \|*  
*anyacchirovivṛścyaivaṃ tenāpi śivapūjanam \|*  
*kṛtaṃ naivānyamuninā tathā caivāpareṇahi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Fixing his attention deeply on the Liṅga after about a kalā, he cut off another head and worshipped Śiva with it. Such (performance of) worship was never done by any sage nor by anyone else.

## \|\| 1.8.50 \|\|

*evaṃ śirāṃsyeva bahūni tena samarpitānyeva śivārcanārthe \|*  
*bhūtvā kabaṃdho hi punaḥ punaśca śivo'sau varado babhūva \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Thus many heads were chopped off and offered by him in worshipping Śiva. Again and again he became a headless body. Then Śiva became a bestower of boons.

## \|\| 1.8.51 \|\|

*mayā vināsurastatra piṃḍībhūtena vai purā \|*  
*varānvaraya paulastya yatheṣṭaṃ tāndadāmyaham \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. ‘Formerly without being myself transformed into a Piṇḍī... O descendant of Pulastya, choose boons as you please. I shall grant you the same.’

## \|\| 1.8.52-53 \|\|

*rāvaṇena tadā coktaḥ śivaḥ paramamaṃgalaḥ \|*  
*yadi prasanno bhagavandeyo me vara uttamaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*na kāmaye'nyaṃ ca varamāśraye tvatpadāṃbujam \|*  
*yathā tathā pradātavyaṃ yadyasti ca kṛpā mayi \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Then Śiva of greatest auṣpiciousness was requested by Rāvaṇa: ‘If Your Lordship are pleased, the excellent boon should be given to me. I do not wish to seek any other boon. If you have merciful favour towards me, you should give me such a boon whereby I (always) resort to your feet.’

## \|\| 1.8.54 \|\|

*tadā sadāśivenokto rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ \|*  
*matprasādācca sarvaṃ tvaṃ prāpsyase manasepsitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Then Rāvaṇa who made the world cry and scream was told by Sādāśiva: ‘By my favour, you will obtain everything mentally desired by you.’

## \|\| 1.8.55-59 \|\|

*evaṃ prāptaṃ śivātsarvaṃ rāvaṇena sureśvarāḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvairbhavadbhiśca tapasā parameṇa hi \|\| 55 \|\|*

*vijetavyo rāvaṇoyamiti me manasi sthitam \|*  
*्cyutasya vacaḥ śrutvā brahmādyā devatāgaṇāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*ciṃtāmāpedire sarve ciraṃ te viṣayānvitāḥ \|*  
*brahmāpi ceṃdriyagrastaḥ sutā ramitumudyataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*iṃdro hi jārabhāvācca caṃdro hi gurutalpagaḥ \|*  
*yamaḥ kadaryabhāvācca caṃcalatvātsadāgatiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*pāvakaḥ sarvabhakṣitvāttathānye devatāgaṇāḥ \|*  
*aśaktā rāvaṇaṃ jetuṃ tapasā ca vijṛṃbhitam \|\| 59 \|\|*

55-59. It was thus, O leading Suras, that everything was. obtained by Rāvaṇa from Śiva. Hence this Rāvaṇa should be subdued by you all only through great penance. This is what I think.”

On hearing the words of Acyuta, the groups of Devas beginning with Brahmā became anxious, because all of them had been addicted to sensual pleasures.

Brahmā was overpowered by sexual desire and he attempted sexual act with his own daughter. Indra was an adulterer. Candra (the Moon-god) defiled the bed of his Guru (preceptor Bṛhaspati). Yama has been avaricious and stingy. Sadāgati (the Wind-god) has been fickle. Pāvaka has been indiscriminate in eating anything and everything. The others among the groups of Devas (had similar defects). Hence, all these were incapable of conquering Rāvaṇa who had become very great by means of penance.

## \|\| 1.8.60 \|\|

*śailādo hi mahātejā gaṇaśreṣṭhaḥ purātanaḥ \|*  
*buddhi mānnītinipuṇo mahābalaparākramī \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Śailāda was an elderly excellent Gaṇa of great splendour. He was intelligent, an expert in adopting the right course of action, highly powerful and very valorous.

## \|\| 1.8.61-62 \|\|

*śivapriyo rudrarūpī mahātmā hyuvāca sarvānatha ceṃdramukhyān \|*  
*kasmādyūyaṃ saṃbhramādāgatāśca etatsarvaṃ kathyatāṃ vistareṇa \|\| 61 \|\|*

*naṃdinā ca tadā sarve pṛṣṭāḥ procustvarānvitāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. He was a favourite of Śiva and was identical with Rudra. The noble-souled one asked all of them led by Indra, “Why have you all come here in great excitement? Let the whole thing be reported in detail.”

## \|\| 1.8.63 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*rāvaṇena vayaṃ sarve nirjitā munibhiḥ saha \|*  
*prasādayitumāyātāḥ śivaṃ lokeśvareśvaram \|\| 63 \|\|*

On being asked by Nandi, all of them hurriedly said then: Devas said:

63\. All of us along with the sages have been conquered by Rāvaṇa. We have come to propitiate Śiva, the lord of the lords, of the worlds.

## \|\| 1.8.64 \|\|

*prahasya bhagavānnaṃdī brahmāṇaṃ vai hyuvāca ha \|*  
*kva yūyaṃ kva śivaḥ śaṃbhustapasā parameṇa hi \|*  
*draṣṭavyo hṛdi madhyasthaḥ so'dya draṣṭuṃ na pāryate \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Lord Nandī laughed and said to Brahmā: “Where are you? Where is auspicious Śaṃbhu? (There is a world of difference between you two.) By means of great penance, he should be seen seated in the middle of the heart. He cannot be seen today.

## \|\| 1.8.65 \|\|

*yāvadbhāvā hyanekāśca iṃdriyārthāstathaiva ca \|*  
*yāvacca mamatābhāvastāvadīśo hi durlabhaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. As long as the emotional attitudes are too many, the objects of senses are plentiful and there is the feeling of mineness, so long Īśa is very difficult to be attained.

## \|\| 1.8.66 \|\|

*jiteṃdriyāṇāṃ śāṃtānāṃ tanniṣṭhānāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*sulabho liṃgarūpī syādbhavatāṃ hi sudurlabhaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Śiva in the form of the Liṅga is easy of access to those noble-souled ones who have subdued the senses, are quiescent and have stabilized themselves in him. He is very difficult to be obtained by you all.”

## \|\| 1.8.67 \|\|

*tadā brahmādayo devā ṛṣayaśca vipaścitaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya naṃdinaṃ prāhuḥ kasmāttvaṃ vānarānanaḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ kathayānyaṃ ca rāvaṇasya tapobalam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Then Brahma and other Devas as well as the learned sages bowed down to Nandī and said:

“Why do you have the face of a monkey? Tell us everything about it. Tell us about the power of the penance of Rāvaṇa.”

## \|\| 1.8.68-72 \|\|

*naṃdīśvara uvāca \|*  
*kubero'dhikṛtastena śaṃkareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*dhanānāmādipatye ca taṃ draṣṭuṃ rāvaṇo'tra vai \|\| 68 \|\|*

*āgacchattvarayā yuktaḥ samāruhya svavāhanam \|*  
*māṃ dṛṣṭvā cābravītkruddhaḥ kubero hyatra āgataḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tvayā dṛṣṭo'tha vātrāsau kathyatāmavilaṃbitam \|*  
*kiṃ kāryaṃ dhanadenādya iti pṛṣṭo mayā hi saḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tadovāca mahātejā rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ \|*  
*mayyaśraddhānvito bhūtvā viṣayātmā sudurmadaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*śikṣāpayitumārabdho maivaṃ kāryamiti prabho \|*  
*yathāhaṃ ca śriyā yukta āḍhyo'haṃ balavānaham \|*  
*tathā tvaṃ bhava re mūḍha mā mūḍhatvamupārjaya \|\| 72 \|\|*

Nandīśvara said:

68-70a. Kubera had been made by the noble-souled Śaṅkara the over-lord of wealth and assets. Rāvaṇa came here to see him, riding in his own vehicle. He was in a hurry. On seeing me, he said furiously: “Did Kubera come here? Was he seen by you here? Let this be told immediately.”

70b-72. He was asked by me: “What have you to do with Dhanada (Kubera) today?”

## \|\| 1.8.73 \|\|

*ahaṃ mūḍhaḥ kṛtastena kubereṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*mayā nirākṛto roṣāttapastepe sa guhyakaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

Then Rāvaṇa of great splendour, who made the world scream, said: “At the outset he (Kubera) had been indifferent towards me. He did not care for me. Addicted to sensual pleasures, as he is, he has been highly arrogant. He began to teach me saying, ‘O lord, it should not be done like this. Just as I am endowed with glory and splendour, just as I am rich and strong, so also you do become, O fool. Do not get into delusion and stupidity.’

73\. I have been made a fool and a deluded person by the noble-souled Kubera. On being turned out by me angrily, that Guḥyaka (i.e. Kubera) performed penance.

## \|\| 1.8.74 \|\|

*kuberaḥ sa hi naṃdinkimāgatastava maṃdiram \|*  
*dīyatāṃ ca kuberodya nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Did that Kubera come, O Nandī, to your abode? Let that Kubera be handed over (to me). You need not hesitate in this matter.”

## \|\| 1.8.75-79 \|\|

*rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā hyavocaṃ tvarito'pyaham \|*  
*liṃgakosi mahābhāga tvamahaṃ ca tathāvidhaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*ubhayoḥ samanāṃ jñātvā vṛthā jalpasi durmate \|*  
*yathoktaḥ sa tvavādīnmāṃ vadanārthe baloddhataḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*yathā bhavadbhiḥ pṛṣṭo'haṃ vadanārthe mahātmabhiḥ \|*  
*purāvṛttaṃ mayā proktaṃ śivārcanavidheḥ phalam \|*  
*śivena dattaṃ sālūpyaṃ na gṛhītaṃ mayā tadā \|\| 77 \|\|*

*yācitaṃ ca mayā śaṃbhorvadanaṃ vānarasya ca \|*  
*śivena kṛpayā dattaṃ mama kāruṇyaśālinā \|\| 78 \|\|*

*nirābhimānino ye ca nirdabhā niṣparigrahāḥ \|*  
*śaṃbhoḥ priyāste vijñeyā hyanye śivavabahiṣkṛtāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

75-79. On hearing the words of Rāvaṇa, I hurriedly replied: “You are a Liṅgaka (worshipper of Liṅga), an exalted one. I too am one like that. Knowing the equality between us both you are prattling in vain, O vicious one.”

As he was told thus, he in his arrogance due to his might, asked me about my face in the same manner as I have been asked about my face by you noble-souled ones. The old story was recounted by me about the benefit of the holy rite of the worship of Śiva. “Sārūpya (having the same form as that of the lord) was granted by Śiva, but it was not accepted by me then. The face of a monkey was requested by me from Śaṃbhu. It was then granted to me kindly by Śiva who is by nature compassionate.

Those who are devoid of false prestige, those who are free from arrogance and those who have no property or possessions, should be known as favourites of Śaṃbhu. Others are excluded by Śiva.”

## \|\| 1.8.80-86 \|\|

*tathāvadanmayā sārddhaṃ rāvaṇastapaso balāt \|*  
*mayā ca yācitānyeva daśa vaktrāṇi dhīmatā \|\| 80 \|\|*

*upahāsakaraṃ vākyaṃ paulastyasya tadā surāḥ \|*  
*mayā tadā hi śapto'sau rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*īdṛśānyeva vaktrāṇi yeṣāṃ vai saṃbhavaṃti hi \|*  
*taiḥ sameto yadā ko'pi naravaryo mahātapāḥ \|*  
*māṃ puraskṛtya sahasā haniṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*evaṃ śapto mayā brahmanrāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ \|*  
*arcitaṃ kevalaṃ liṃgaṃ vinā tena mahātmanā \|\| 83 \|\|*

*pīṭhikārūpasaṃsthena vinā tena surottamāḥ \|*  
*viṣṇunā hi mahābhāgāstasmātsarvaṃ vidhāsyati \|\| 84 \|\|*

*devadevo mahādevo viṣṇurūpī maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*sarve yūyaṃ prārthayaṃtu viṣṇuṃ sarvaguhāśayam \|\| 85 \|\|*

*ahaṃ hi sarvadevānāṃ purovartī bhavāmyataḥ \|*  
*te sarve naṃdino vākyaṃ śrutvā muditamānasāḥ \|*  
*vaikuṃṭhamāgatā gīrbhirviṣṇuṃ stotuṃ pracakrire \|\| 86 \|\|*

80-86a. Then Rāvaṇa said to me: “On the strength of my penance, I had been sensible enough to request for ten heads.”

At his derisive statement, Rāvaṇa who made the world scream, was cursed by me then:

“When an excellent man of great penance accompanied by those who have faces like this (monkey faces like mine) (comes to your city) keeping me at the head, he will undoubtedly kill you.”

Thus, O Brahmā, Rāvaṇa who made the world scream, was cursed by me. Only the Liṅga was worshipped by Ṛāvaṇa without the noble-souled Viṣṇu stationed in the form of the pedestal, O excellent Suras. Hence, O excessively fortunate ones, Maheśvara, Mahādeva, the lord of Devas, in the form of Viṣṇu will carry out everything. May all of you pray to Viṣṇu lying within the cavity of the heart of everyone. Therefore, I shall be at the head of all Devas.

86b. On hearing the words of Nandī, all of them became joyous in their minds. They came to Vaikuṇṭha and began to eulogize Viṣṇu by means of (good) words.

## \|\| 1.8.87 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namo bhagavate tubhyaṃ devadeva jagatpate \|*  
*tvadādhāramidaṃ sarvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram \|\| 87 \|\|*

Devas said:

87\. Obeisance to you, the lord, O lord of Devas, O lord of the universe. This entire universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings has you for its basis and support.

## \|\| 1.8.88 \|\|

*etalliṃgaṃ tvayā viṣṇo dhṛtaṃ vai piṇḍirūpiṇā \|*  
*mahāviṣṇusvarūpeṇa ghātitau madhukaiṭabhau \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. This Liṅga has been held by you, O Viṣṇu, in the form of the Piṇḍī (globular pedestal). In the form of Mahāviṣṇu (the demons) Madhu and Kaiṭabha were killed by you.

## \|\| 1.8.89 \|\|

*tathā kamaṭharūpeṇa dhṛto vai maṃdarācalaḥ \|*  
*varāharūpamāsthāya hiraṇyākṣo hatastvayā \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Similarly, in the form of a tortoise, the Mandara mountain was held up and supported by you (at the time of churning of ocean for nectar). Assuming the form of a boar, Hiraṇyākṣa was killed by you.

## \|\| 1.8.90 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipurdaityo hato nṛharirūpiṇā \|*  
*tvayā caiva balirbaddho daityo vāmanarūpiṇā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Hiraṇyakaśipu, the Daitya, was killed by you by assuming the form of Nṛhari (Man-lion). Bali, the Daitya, was held and bound by you in the form of Vāmana (Dwarf).

## \|\| 1.8.91 \|\|

*bhṛgūṇāmanvaye bhūtvā kṛtavīryātmajo hataḥ \|*  
*itopyasmānmahāviṣṇo tathaiva paripālaya \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The son of Kṛtavīrya (Sahasrārjuna) was killed by you after taking birth in the family of Bhṛgus. Hereafter too, O great Viṣṇu, protect us in the same manner.

## \|\| 1.8.92 \|\|

*rāvamasya bhayādasmāttrātuṃ bhūyorhasi tvaram \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. It behoves you to protect us instantaneously from the fear of Rāvaṇa.

## \|\| 1.8.93 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃprārthito devairbhagavānbhūtabhāvanaḥ \|*  
*uvāca ca surānsarvānvāsudevo jaganmayaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. On being entreated thus by Devas, the lord Vāsudeva, the sanctifier (the creator) of all living beings, who is immanent in the universe, said to all those Suras:

## \|\| 1.8.94 \|\|

*he devāḥ śrūyatāṃ vākyaṃ prastāvasadṛśaṃ mahat \|*  
*śailādiṃ ca puraskṛtya sarve yūyaṃ tvarānvitāḥ \|*  
*avatārānprakurvantu vānarīṃ tanumāśritāḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. “O Devas, let this important statement he heard. It is relevant to this occasion. With Śailādi (Nandin) as your head (leader), all of you immediately take incarnations in the form (bodies) of monkeys.

## \|\| 1.8.95 \|\|

*ahaṃ hi mānuṣo bhūtvā hyajñānena samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*saṃbhaviṣyāmyayodhyāyaṃ gṛhe daśarathasya ca \|*  
*brahmavidyāsahāyosmi bhavatāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. I shall become a human being enveloped by Ajñāna (Ignorance). I shall be born in Ayodhyā in the abode of Daśaratha for the attainment of your objectives. I am having Brahmavidyā (the knowledge of Brahman) as my assistant.

## \|\| 1.8.96 \|\|

*janakasya gṛhe sākṣādbrahmavidyā janiṣyati \|*  
*bhakto hi rāvaṇaḥ sākṣācchivadhyānaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Brahmavidyā herself will be born in the abode of Janaka. In fact, Rāvaṇa is (my) devotee as he is directly engaged in the meditation on Śiva.

## \|\| 1.8.97 \|\|

*tapasā mahatā yukto brahmavidyāṃ yadecchati \|*  
*tadā susādhyo bhavati puruṣo dharmanirjitaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. When a man endowed with great penance desires for Brahmavidyā, he can be easily managed and won over by means of virtue.”

## \|\| 1.8.98-100 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃbhāṣya bhagavānviṣṇuḥ paramamaṅgalaḥ \|*  
*vālī cendrāṃśasaṃbhūtaḥ sugrīvoṃ śumataḥ sutaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*tathā brahmāṃśasaṃbhūto jāmbavānnṛkṣakuñjaraḥ \|*  
*śilādatanayo naṃdī śivasyānucaraḥ priyaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*yo vai caikādaśo rudro hanūmānsa mahākapiḥ \|*  
*avatīrṇaḥ sahāyārthaṃ viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

98-100. After saying this, lord Viṣṇu, the highly auspicious one (vanished).

Vālī was born of a part of Indra. Sugrīva was the son of the Sun. Jāmbavān, the leading Ṛkṣa (bear), was born of a part of Brahmā. Naṇḍī, the son of Śilāda, who was a favourite follower of Śiva, incarnated as the great monkey Hanūmān for rendering assistance to Viṣṇu of unmeasured splendour.

## \|\| 1.8.101 \|\|

*maiṃdādayo'tha kapayaste sarve surasattamāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ sarve suragaṇā avateruryathā tatham \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. The monkeys beginning with Mainda were all the excellent Suras. Thus, all Suras incarnated in a befitting manner.

## \|\| 1.8.102 \|\|

*tathaiva viṣṇurutpannaḥ kauśalyānaṃdavarddhanaḥ \|*  
*viśvasya ramaṇāccaiva rāma ityucyate budhaiḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Similarly, Viṣṇu was born as one who increased the delight of Kausalyā. He is called Rāma by learned men, because he pleased and gratified the entire universe.

## \|\| 1.8.103 \|\|

*śeṣopi bhaktyā viṣṇośca tapasā'vātaradbhuvi \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Due to his devotion to Viṣṇu, Śeṣa descended on the earth by means of the power of his penance.

## \|\| 1.8.104 \|\|

*dordaṇḍāvapi viṣṇośca avatīrṇau pratāpinau \|*  
*śatrughnabharatākhyau ca vikhyātau bhuvanatraye \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The mighty arms of Viṣṇu incarnated as the valorous (Princes) named Śatrughṇa and Bharata well-renowned in the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.8.105 \|\|

*mithilādhipateḥ kanyā yā uktā brahmavādibhiḥ \|*  
*sā brahmavidyāvataratsurāṇāṃ kāryyasiddhaye \|*  
*sītā jātā lāṃgalasya iyaṃ bhūmivikarṣaṇāt \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. She who was mentioned as Brahmavidyā by the expounders of the Vedas, incarnated as the daughter of the ruler of Mithilā for the fulfilment of the task of Suras. She was born from a furrow arising from the ploughing of the field with the ploughshare.

## \|\| 1.8.106 \|\|

*tasmātsīteti vikhyātā vidyā sānvīkṣikī tadā \|*  
*mithilāyāṃ samutpannā maithitītyabhidhīyate \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Hence, she became famous as Sītā. She was the Science of Metaphysics (personified). Since she was born in Mithilā, she is called Maithilī.

## \|\| 1.8.107 \|\|

*janakasya kule jātā viśrutā janakātmajā \|*  
*khyātā vedavatī pūrvaṃ brahmavidyāghanāśinī \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. She was born in the family of Janaka. Hence, she is well-known as Janakātmajā (Jānakī). This Brahmavidyā, the destroyer of sins, was formerly known as Vedavatī.

## \|\| 1.8.108-110 \|\|

*sā dattā janakenaiva viṣṇave paramātmane \|\| 108 \|\|*

*tayātha vidyayā sārddhaṃ devadevo jagatpatiḥ \|*  
*ugre tapasi līno'sau viṣṇuḥ paramaduṣkaram \|\| 109 \|\|*

*rāvaṇaṃ jetukāmo vai rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ \|*  
*araṇyavāsamakaroddevānāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|\| 110 \|\|*

108-110. She was given by Janaka himself to Viṣṇu, the Supreme Soul. Along with her, the Vidyā (incarnated), Viṣṇu the greatest among the auspicious ones, the lord of Devas, the lord protector of the universe, became engaged in a severe penance. As he was desirous of defeating Rāvaṇa for the sake of the fulfilment of the task of Devas, the lotus-eyed Rāma stayed in forest (for the same purpose).

## \|\| 1.8.111 \|\|

*śeṣāvatāro'pi mahāṃstapaḥ paramaduṣkaram \|*  
*tatāpa parayā śaktyā devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Though the great incarnation of Śeṣa, (Lakṣmaṇa) performed an exceedingly difficult penance by means of his great Śakti (power), for the sake of the fulfilment of the task of Devas.

## \|\| 1.8.112-115 \|\|

*śatrughno bharataścaiva tepatuḥ paramaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*tato'sau tapasā yuktaḥ sārddhaṃ tairdevatāgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*sagaṇaṃ rāvaṇaṃ rāmaḥ ṣaḍbhirmāsairajīhanat \|*  
*viṣṇunā ghātitaḥ śastraiḥ śivasārūpyamāptavān \|\| 113 \|\|*

*sagamaḥ sa punaḥ sadyo baṃdhubhiḥ saha suvratāḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

*śivaprasādātsakalaṃ dvaitādvaitamavāpa ha \|*  
*dvaitādvaitavivekārthamṛpayopyatra mohitāḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ prāpnuvaṃtīha śivārcanaratā narāḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

112-115. Śatrughna and Bharata too performed very great penance. Rāma who was thus endowed with the power of penance and was assisted and accompanied by those groups of Devas, killed Ṛāvaṇa along with his followers within six months. Killed by Viṣṇu by means of weapons, O sages of holy rites, he attained Sārūpya (having the same form as the god) of Śiva, along with his kinsmen and followers. By the grace of Śiva, he became (realized) the entire Dvaitādvaita (the essence of the philosophy of dualism and non-dualism). Even the sages are deluded in the matter of discrimination between dualism and non-dualism. Men who are engaged in worshipping Śiva derive all those things.

## \|\| 1.8.116 \|\|

*ye'rcayaṃti śivaṃ nityaṃ liṃgarūpiṇameva ca \|*  
*striyo vāpyatha vā śūdrāḥ śvapacā hyaṃtyavāsinaḥ \|*  
*taṃ śivaṃ prāpnuvaṃtyeva sarvaduḥkhopanāśanam \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Those who continuously worship Śiva in the form of Liṅga, whether they be women or śūdras or cāṇḍālas or other low-caste people, do attain Śiva, the destroyer of all miseries.

## \|\| 1.8.117-118 \|\|

*paśavo'pi paraṃ yātāḥ kiṃ punarmānuṣādayaḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

*ye dvijā brahmacaryeṇa tapaḥ paramamāsthitāḥ \|*  
*varṣairanekairyajñānāṃ te'pi svargaparā bhavan \|\| 118 \|\|*

117-118. Even animals have attained the supreme lord. What then to say about human beings? The twice-born castes who have practised great penance observing the vow of celibacy and who have performed Yajñas for many years have attained (merely) Svarga (Heaven).

## \|\| 1.8.119-123 \|\|

*jyotiṣṭomo vājapeyo hyatirātrādayo hyamī \|*  
*yajñāḥ svargaṃ prayacchaṃti sattrīṇāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

*tatra svargasukhaṃ bhuktvā puṇyakṣayakaraṃ mahat \|*  
*puṇyakṣaye'pi yajvāno martyalokaṃ pataṃti vai \|\| 120 \|\|*

*patitānāṃ ca saṃsāre daivādbuddhiḥ prajāyate \|*  
*guṇatrayamayī viprāstāsutāstviha yoniṣu \|\| 121 \|\|*

*yathā sattvaṃ saṃbhavati sattvayuktabhavaṃ narāḥ \|*  
*rājasāśca tathā jñeyāstā masāścaiva te dvijāḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

*evaṃ saṃsāracakre'sminbhramitā bahavo janāḥ \|*  
*yadṛcchayā daivagatyā śivaṃ saṃsevate naraḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

119-123. There are many Yajñas such as Jyotiṣṭoma, Vājapeya, Atirātra and so on. These Yajñas undoubtedly do bestow heavenly pleasures on those who perform them. After enjoying the heavenly pleasures, when their merits become exhausted, those sacrificers come back to the mortal world. Having descended to the world, they are born in the different species with their intellect of the nature of the three Guṇas of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas. Thus, many souls wander about in cycles of birth and death. By chance or as good luck would have it, some of them serve Śiva.

## \|\| 1.8.124 \|\|

*śivadhyānaparāṇāṃ ca narāṇāṃ yatacetasām \|*  
*māyānirasanaṃ sadyo bhaviṣyati na cānyathā \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Instantaneous removal of Māyā takes place in the case of men who are engaged in regular meditation on Śiva and who have restrained their minds and not otherwise.

## \|\| 1.8.125 \|\|

*māyānirasanātsadyo naśyatyeva guṇatrayam \|*  
*yadā guṇatrayātīto bhavatīti sa muktibhāk \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. When Māyā is dispelled, the three Guṇas perish. Then a person transcends the three Guṇas and becomes liberated thereby.

## \|\| 1.8.126-128 \|\|

*tasmālliṅgārcanaṃ bhāvyaṃ sarveṣāmapi dehinām \|*  
*liṅgarūpī śivo bhūtvā trāyate saṃcarācaram \|\| 126 \|\|*

*purā bhavadbhiḥ pṛṣṭo'haṃ liṅgarūpī kathaṃ śivaḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ kathitaṃ viprā yāthātathyena saṃprati \|\| 127 \|\|*

*kathaṃ garaṃ bhakṣitavāñchivo lokamaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ śrūyatāṃ viprā yatāvatkathayāmi vaḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

126-128. Hence, the worship of Liṅga should be thought of and pursued by all embodied beings. Śiva assumes the form of Liṅga and protects all mobile and immobile beings.

Formerly I have been asked by you about how Śiva assumed the form of Liṅga. Everything has now been truthfully spoken (by me), O Brāhmaṇas.

How Śiva, the great lord of the worlds, swallowed poison (Halāhala), may be listened to, O Brāhmaṇas, I shall recount it to you as it actually took place.

## Chapter 9 - The Churning of the Ocean

## \|\| 1.9.1-2 \|\|

*lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*ekadā tu sabhāmadhya āsthito devarāṭ svayam \|*  
*lokapālaiḥ parivṛto devaiśca ṛṣibhistathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*apsarogaṇasaṃvīto gaṃdharvaiśca puraskṛtaḥ \|*  
*upagīyamānavijayaḥ siddhavidyādharairapi \|\| 2 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

1-2. On one occasion Indra, the lord of Devas, was seated in the middle of the assembly surrounded by the guardians of the worlds, Devas and Sages. He was encircled by bevies of celestial damsels and was honoured by Gandharvas. Songs in praise of his conquest were being sung by Siddhas and Vidyādharas.

## \|\| 1.9.3 \|\|

*tadā śiṣyaiḥ parivṛto devarājaguruḥ sudhīḥ \|*  
*āgato'sau mahābhāgo bṛhaspati rudāradhīḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At that time Bṛhaspati who was the scholarly preceptor of the king of Devas and was of exalted fortune and liberal-minded, came there surrounded by his disciples.

## \|\| 1.9.4 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasā devāḥ praṇemuḥ samupasthitāḥ \|*  
*iṃdropi dadṛśe tatra prāptaṃ vācaspatiṃ tadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing him Devas who had been sitting there promptly bowed down to him. Indra too had seen Vācaspati’s (Bṛhaspati’s) arrival.

## \|\| 1.9.5 \|\|

*novāca kiṃciddurmedhāvaco mānupuraḥsaram \|*  
*nāhvānaṃ nāsanaṃ tasya na visarjanameva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. But the vicious-minded lord did not utter a single word in his honour. No word of welcome, no offer of seat, no formal permission to leave was accorded to him.

## \|\| 1.9.6 \|\|

*śakraṃ pramattaṃ jñātvātha madādrājyasya durmatim \|*  
*tirodhānamanuprāpto bṛhaspatī ruṣānvitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Knowing that Śakra had become arrogant and evil-minded due to royal authority, Bṛhaspati became angry and he vanished.

## \|\| 1.9.7 \|\|

*gate devagurau tasminvimanaskā'bhavansurāḥ \|*  
*yakṣā nāgāḥ sagaṃdharvā ṛṣayo'pi tathā dvijāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When the preceptor of Devas had departed, Suras became dejected. Yakṣas, Serpents, Gandharvas and sages also became depressed in mind, O Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.9.8 \|\|

*gāṃdharvasyā vasāne tu labdhasaṃjño hariḥ surān \|*  
*papraccha tvaritenavai kva gato hi mahātapāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. At the end of the music recital, Indra (as it were) regained consciousness. He asked Suras immediately, “Where has (the preceptor) of great penance gone?”

## \|\| 1.9.9-10 \|\|

*tadaiva nāradenoktaḥ śakro devādhipastathā \|*  
*tvayā kṛtā hyavajñā ca gurornastyatra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*guroravajñayā rājyaṃ gataṃ te balasūdana \|*  
*tasmātkṣamāpanīyo'sau sarvabhāvena hi tvayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. At the very same time, Śakra, the lord of Devas, was informed by Nārada: “The preceptor has been insulted by you. There is no doubt about it. O slayer of Bala, your kingdom has gone due to the disrespect (shown by you) to the preceptor. Hence, by all means, you have to plead to him for forgiveness.”

## \|\| 1.9.11 \|\|

*etacchrutvā vacastasya nāradasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*āsanātsahasotthāya taiḥ sarvaiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*āgacchattvarayā śakro gurorgehamataṃdritaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On hearing these words of the noble-souled Nārada, Śakra suddenly got up from his seat. Surrounded by all of them (Devas etc.), he hastened to the abode of his preceptor promptly (without any slackness).

## \|\| 1.9.12 \|\|

*pṛṣṭvā tārāṃ praṇamyādau kva gato hi mahātapāḥ \|*  
*na jānāmītyuvācedaṃ tārā śakraṃ nirīkṣatī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He bowed down to Tārā at the outset and asked her, “Where has (our preceptor) of great penance gone?” Tārā stared at Śakra and said, “I do not know.”

## \|\| 1.9.13-15 \|\|

*tadā ciṃtānvito bhūtvā śakraḥ svagṛhamāvrajat \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare svarge hyaniṣṭāndbhutāni ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*abhavansarvaduḥkhārthe śakrasya ca mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*pātālasthena balinā jñātaṃ śakrasya ceṣṭitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yayau daityaiḥ parivṛtaḥ pātālādamarāvatīm \|*  
*tadā yuddhamatīvāsīddevānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Thereupon, Śakra became worried and returned to his own house. In the meantime, there appeared mysterious ill-omens in heaven, causing misery to everyone including the noble-minded Śakra himself.

All the activities of Śakra were known to Bali who was stationed in the nether worlds. Surrounded by Daityas, he went from Pātāla to Amarāvatī. Thereupon a great fight ensued between Devas and Dānavas.

## \|\| 1.9.16-18 \|\|

*devāḥ parājitā daityai rājyaṃ śakrasya tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*saṃprāptaṃ sakalaṃ tasya mūḍhasya ca durātmanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*nītaṃ sarvaprayatnena pātālaṃ tvaritaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*śukraprasādātte sarve tathā vijayino'bhavan \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śakro'pi niḥśriko jāto devaistyaktastato bhṛśam \|*  
*devī tirodhānagatā babhūva kamalekṣaṇā \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. Devas were defeated by Daityas. Instantaneously the whole of the kingdom of Śakra, the deluded and evil-minded one, was conquered by them and everything (belonging to Śakra) was quickly carried to Pātāla. It was by the grace of Śukra that all of them became victorious. Śakra became bereft of glory and splendour. So he was utterly abandoned by Devas. The goddess (of fortune) with lotus-like eyes vanished.

## \|\| 1.9.19 \|\|

*airāvato mahānāgastathaivoccaiḥśravā hayaḥ \|*  
*evamādīni ratnāni anekāni bahūnyapi \|*  
*nītāni sahasā daityairlobhādasādhuvṛttibhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The great elephant Airāvata, the horse Uccaiḥśravas and many other precious things and jewels were taken away immediately by Daityas of evil behaviour due to greed.

## \|\| 1.9.20 \|\|

*puṇyabhāṃji ca tānyeva patitāni ca sāgare \|*  
*tadā sa vismayāviṣṭo balirāha guruṃ prati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The good ones among them fell into the ocean. Bali who was surprised at this, remarked to his preceptor:

## \|\| 1.9.21 \|\|

*devānnirjitya cāsmābhirānītāni bahūni ca \|*  
*ratnāni tu samudre'tha patitāni tadadbhutam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “It is mysterious that many jewels brought by us after defeating Devas have fallen into the ocean.”

## \|\| 1.9.22-23 \|\|

*balestadvacanaṃ śrutvā uśanā pratyuvāca tam \|*  
*aśvamedhaśatenaiva surarājyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*dīkṣitasya na saṃdehastasmādbhokta sa eva ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*aśvamedhaṃ vinā kiṃcitsvargaṃ bhoktaṃ na pāryate \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. On hearing the words of Bali, Uśanas (i.e. Śukra) replied to him: “One can attain the heavenly kingdom only through performance of a hundred horse-sacrifices. There is no doubt about it that it will be acquired by one who is initiated in it. Hence, the enjoyer is also he himself. Without performing a horse-sacrifice, heavenly pleasures cannot at all be enjoyed.”

## \|\| 1.9.24 \|\|

*gurorvacanamājñāya tūṣṇīṃbhūto balistataḥ \|*  
*babhūva devaiḥ sārddhaṃ ca yathocitamakārayat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Understanding the utterance of his preceptor, Bali became quite silent. What was proper and befitting was carried out through and along with Devas.

## \|\| 1.9.25 \|\|

*indropi śocyatāṃ prāpto jagāma parameṣṭhinam \|*  
*vijñāpayāmāsa tathā sarvaṃ rājyabhayādikam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Indra too, on attaining a miserable plight, went to Parameṣṭhin (Brahmā) and informed him of everything, such as the danger to his kingdom and other things.

## \|\| 1.9.26-28 \|\|

*śakrasya vacanaṃ śrutvā parameṣṭhī uvāca ha \|\| 26 \|\|*

*saṃmilitvā surānsarvāṃstvayā sākaṃ tvarānvitāḥ \|*  
*ārādhanārthaṃ gacchāmo viṣṇuṃ sarveśvareśvaram \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tatheti gatvā te sarve śakrādyā lokapālakāḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ ca puraskṛtya taṭaṃ kṣīrārṇavasya ca \|*  
*prāpyopaviśya te sarve hariṃ stotuṃ pracakramuḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. On hearing the words of Śakra, Parameṣṭhī said: “We shall gather together all the Suras and go immediately along with you to Viṣṇu, the lord of all lords, in order to propitiate him.”

Saying “So be it” all those guardians of the worlds beginning with Śakra went to the shore of the Milk Ocean with Brahmā at their head. After sitting there all of them began to eulogize Hari.

## \|\| 1.9.29-31 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*devadeva jagānnātha surāsuranamaskṛta \|*  
*puṇyaślokāvyayānaṃta paramātmannamo'stu te \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yajño'si yajñarūpo'si yajñāṃgo'si ramāpate \|*  
*tato'dya kṛpayā viṣṇo devānāṃ varado bhava \|\| 30 \|\|*

*guroravajñayā cādya bhraṣṭarājyaḥ śatakratuḥ \|*  
*jātaḥ surarṣibhiḥ sākaṃ tasmādenaṃ samuddhara \|\| 31 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

29-31. O lord of the universe, O lord of Devas bowed down to by Suras as well as Asuras, obeisance to you, O great Ātman, of auspicious reputation, O infinite one, O immutable one, free from decay.

You yourself are Yajña. You are of the form of Yajña, O consort of Lakṣmī. Hence, be the bestower of boons unto the Devas.

By insulting his preceptor, Indra has lost (everything) from his kingdom along with the celestial sages. Hence redeem him.

## \|\| 1.9.32 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*dukokalajñayā sarvaṃ nasyatīti kimadbhutam \|*  
*ye pāpino hyadharmiṣṭhāḥ kevalaṃ viṣayātmakāḥ \|*  
*pitarau niṃditau yaiśca nirdaivātvena saṃśayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

The Lord said:

32\. There is no wonder in the fact that everything perishes by insulting the preceptor. Those who are sinners, who are completely engaged in evil activities, who indulge only in sensual pleasures and by whom parents are censured, are undoubtedly godless ones.

## \|\| 1.9.33 \|\|

*anena yatkṛtaṃ brahmansadyastatphalamāgatam \|*  
*karmaṇā cāsya śakrasya sarveṣāṃ saṃkaṭāgamaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Immediately he has acquired the fruit, O Brahmā, of what he has committed. Difficulty and misfortune have befallen all due to the act of this Śakra.

## \|\| 1.9.34 \|\|

*viparīto yadā kālaḥ puruṣasya bhavettadā \|*  
*bhūtamaitrīṃ prakurvaṃti sarvakāryārthasiddhaye \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. When a person faces adverse circumstances, they say that, he must be friendly with all living beings in order to achieve all his purposes.

## \|\| 1.9.35 \|\|

*tena vai kāraṇeneṃdra madīyaṃ vacanaṃ kuru \|*  
*kāryahetostvayā kāryo daityaiḥ saha samāgamaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. For that reason, Indra, do as I suggest. For the realization of your purpose, alliance should be formed by you with Daityas.

## \|\| 1.9.36 \|\|

*evaṃ bhagavatādiṣṭaḥ śakraḥ paramabuddhimān \|*  
*amarāvatīṃ yayau hitvā sutalaṃ daivataiḥ saha \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On being commanded by the lord, the highly intelligent Śakra left Amarāvatī and went to Sutala along with Devas.

## \|\| 1.9.37 \|\|

*indraṃ samāgataṃ śrutvā iṃdraseno ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*babhūva saha sainyena haṃtukāmaḥ puraṃdaram \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On seeing that Indra had come, Indrasena became furious. Along with his army, he was desirous of killing Indra.

## \|\| 1.9.38 \|\|

*nāradena tadā daityā baliśca balināṃ varaḥ \|*  
*nivāritastadvadhācca vākyairuccāvacaistathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Then by means of different types of (consoling) words, Daityas and Bali, the most excellent one among strong persons, were prevented from killing him by Nārada.

## \|\| 1.9.39-40 \|\|

*ṛṣestasyaiva vacanāttyaktamanyurbalistadā \|*  
*babhūva saha sainyena āgato hi śatakratuḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*indrasenena dṛṣṭo'sau lokapālaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*uvāca tvarayā yuktaḥ prahasanniva daityarāṭ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. At the instance of that same sage, Bali controlled (abandoned) his anger. Indra then came in along with his array. He was seen by Indrasena surrounded by the guardians of the worlds. The king of Daityas hastened to tell him laughingly:

## \|\| 1.9.41 \|\|

*kasmādihāgataḥ śakra sutalaṃ prati kathyatām \|*  
*tasyaitadvacanaṃ śrutvā smayamāna uvācatam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “Wherefore have you come here to Sutala, O Śakra? Let it be mentioned.” On hearing these words, he said smilingly:

## \|\| 1.9.42 \|\|

*vayaṃ kaśyapadāyādā yūyaṃ sarve tathaiva ca \|*  
*yathā vayaṃ tathā yūyaṃ vigraho hi nirarthakaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. “We are the descendants of Kaśyapa. All of you are also so. Just as we are, so also you are. Clash and quarrel is meaningless.

## \|\| 1.9.43 \|\|

*mama rājyaṃ kṣaṇenaiva nītaṃ daivavaśāttavayā \|*  
*tathā hyetāni tānyena ratnāni subahūnyapi \|*  
*gatāni tatkṣaṇādeva yatnānītāni vai tvayā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. As fate would have it, my kingdom was seized by you instantaneously. So also many gems were taken away by you. Though brought with very great effort, they too have gone.

## \|\| 1.9.44 \|\|

*tasmādvimarśaḥ kartavyaḥ puruṣeṇa vipaścitā \|*  
*vimarśajjāyate jñānaṃ jñānānmokṣo bhaviṣyati \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Hence a learned person must deliberate and ponder. One gets knowledge by means of deliberation and liberation originates from knowledge.

## \|\| 1.9.45 \|\|

*kiṃ tu me bata uktena jāne na ca tavāgrataḥ \|*  
*śaraṇārthī hyahaṃ prāptaḥ suraiḥ saha tavāṃtikam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. But alas! of what avail is my utterance in front of you? I do not know. I have approached you along with Suras as a person seeking refuge.”

## \|\| 1.9.46 \|\|

*etacchrutvā tu śakrasya vākyaṃ vākyavidāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*prahasyovāca matimāñchakraṃ prati vidāṃ varaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On hearing these words of Śakra, the intelligent (Daitya), the most excellent one among knowers (learned), the most excellent one among those who know what to say, said laughingly to Śakra:

## \|\| 1.9.47 \|\|

*tvamāgatosi deveṃdra kimarthaṃ tanna vedmayaham \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “For what purpose, O Devendra, you have come, I do not know.”

## \|\| 1.9.48 \|\|

*śakrastadvacanaṃ śrutvā hyaśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*kiṃcinnovāca tatrainaṃ nārado vākyamabravīt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On hearing those words, Śakra’s eyes became filled with tears. He did not say anything. Nārada spoke to him the following words:

## \|\| 1.9.49 \|\|

*bale tvaṃ kiṃ na jānāsi kāryākāryavicāraṇām \|*  
*dharmo hi mahatāmeṣa śaraṇāgatapālanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. “O Bali, don’t you know the difference between right and wrong activities? This is the virtue of great men. They protect those who seek refuge in them.

## \|\| 1.9.50 \|\|

*śaraṇāgataṃ ca vipraṃ ca rogiṇaṃ vṛddhameva ca \|*  
*yaetānna ca rakṣaṃti te vai brahmahaṇo narāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Those who do not protect the one who seeks refuge, a Brāhmaṇa, a sick man and an old man, are (really) slaughterers of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.9.51-52 \|\|

*śaraṇāgataśabdena āgatastava sannidhau \|*  
*saṃrakṣaṇāya yogyaśca tvayā nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*evamukto nāradena tadā daityapatiḥ svayam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vimṛśya parayā buddhyā kāryākāryavicāraṇām \|*  
*śakraṃ prapūjayāmāsa bahumānapuraḥsaram \|*  
*lokapālaiḥ sametaṃ ca tathā suragaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. He has come to your presence with words asking for refuge. He is worthy of being protected by you. There is no doubt in this matter.” On being told thus by Nārada, the lord of Daityas himself pondered over everything with great understanding regarding what was right and what was wrong. With great respect, he honoured Śakra along with the guardians of the worlds as well as the groups of Devas.

## \|\| 1.9.53 \|\|

*pratyayārthaṃ ca sattvāni hyanekāni vratāni vai \|*  
*balipratyayabhūtāni sa cakāraḥ puraṃdaraḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. For the sake of credence, Puranadara performed many good holy observances of the Sāttvika quality which created confidence in Bali.

## \|\| 1.9.54 \|\|

*evaṃ sa samayaṃ kṛtvā śakraḥ svārthaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*balinā saha cāvāsīdarthaśāstraparo mahān \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thus Śakra entered into an agreement with Bali in order to further his selfish ends. That great lord stayed with Bali solely devoting himself to the (precepts in the) science of political economy.

## \|\| 1.9.55 \|\|

*evaṃ nivasatastasya sutale'pi śatakratoḥ \|*  
*vatsarā bahavo hyāsaṃstadā buddhimakalpayat \|*  
*saṃsmṛtya vacanaṃ viṣṇorvimṛśya ca punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thus Indra passed many years living in Sutala. Remembering the words of Viṣṇu and pondering over them again and again, he thought of a plan.

## \|\| 1.9.56 \|\|

*ekadā tu sabhāmadhya āsīno devarāṭsvayam \|*  
*uvāca prahasanvākyaṃ balimuddiśya nītimān \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Once the king of Devas himself was sitting in the middle of the assembly (of Bali). Conversant with the right policy, he spoke laughingly these words to Bali:

## \|\| 1.9.57-58 \|\|

*prāptavyāni tvayā vīra asmākaṃ ca tvayā bale \|*  
*gajādīni bahūnyeva ratnāni vividhāni ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

*gatāni tatkṣaṇādeva sāgare patitāni vai \|*  
*prayatno hi prakartavyo hyasmābhistvayānvitaiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. “Many gems and jewels, elephants etc. have dropped into the ocean, while you were bringing them here. They belonged to us then. They should be recovered from the ocean by you as well as by us, O heroic one.

## \|\| 1.9.59 \|\|

*teṣāṃ coddharaṇe daitya ratnānāmiha sāgarāt \|*  
*tarhi nirmathanaṃ kāryaṃ bhavatā kāryasiddhaye \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. We must hurry up in exerting ourselves to recover those jewels from the ocean. Hence, it must be churned by you for the purpose of achieving the desired result.”

## \|\| 1.9.60 \|\|

*baliḥ pravartitastena śakreṇa surasūdanaḥ \|*  
*uvāca śakraṃ tvaritaḥ kenedaṃ mathanaṃ bhavet \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Induced thus by Śakra, Bali, the slayer of Suras, spoke to Śakra immediately, “By whom and with what should the churning be done?”

## \|\| 1.9.61-63 \|\|

*tadā nabhogatā vāṇī meghagaṃbhīraniḥsvanā \|*  
*uvāca devā daityāśca maṃthadhvaṃ kṣīrasāgaram \|\| 61 \|\|*

*bhavatāṃ balavṛddhiśca bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*maṃdaraṃ caiva maṃthānaṃ rajjuṃ kuruta vāsukim \|*  
*paścāddevāśca daityāśca melayitvā vimathyatām \|\| 63 \|\|*

61-63. Then an ethereal voice with the majestic rumbling sound of cloud said: “O Devas, O Daityas, do churn the Ocean of Milk. There is no doubt about this that your strength will increase. Make the Mandara mountain the churning rod and Vāsuki the requisite rope. Afterwards, O Devas and Daityas, join together and let the ocean be churned.”

## \|\| 1.9.64 \|\|

*nabhogatāṃ ca tāṃ vāṇīṃ niśamyātha tadāḥsurāḥ \|*  
*daityaiḥ sārddhaṃ tataḥ sarva udyamaṃ cakrurudyatāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. On hearing the words of that ethereal voice, all Suras exerted themselves along with Daityas.

## \|\| 1.9.65 \|\|

*pātālānnirgatāḥ sarve tadā te'tha surāsurāḥ \|*  
*ājagmuratulaṃ sarve maṃdaraṃ parvatottamam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Those Suras and Asuras came out of Pātāla. They all came to the matchless, excellent mountain Mandara.

## \|\| 1.9.66 \|\|

*daityāśca koṭisaṃkhyākāstathā devā na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*udyuktāḥ sahasā prā'yurmaṃdaraṃ kanakaprabham \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Daityas were ten million in number. So also were Devas undoubtedly. Preparing themselves, they came to Mandara having golden lustre.

## \|\| 1.9.67-68 \|\|

*saratnaṃ vartulākāraṃ sthūlaṃ caiva mahāprabham \|*  
*anekaratnasaṃvītaṃ nānādrumaniṣevitam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*caṃdanaiḥ pārijātaiśca nāgapunnāgacaṃpakaiḥ \|*  
*nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇaṃ siṃhaśārdūlasevitam \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. It abounded in gems and precious stones. It was globular in shape. It was very big and exceedingly lustrous. Many gems were (lying scattered) all round. It had many trees such as sandal tree, Pārijāta, Nāga, Punnāga and Caṃpaka. It was full of various kinds of animals and deer, lions and tigers.

## \|\| 1.9.69 \|\|

*mahāśailaṃ dṛṣṭvā te surasattamāḥ \|*  
*ūcuḥ prāṃjalayaḥ sarve tadā te surasattamāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. On seeing such a great mountain, all the excellent Suras, joined their palms in reverence and said:

## \|\| 1.9.70 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*adre surā vayaṃ sarve vijñaptumiha cāgatāḥ \|*  
*tacchṛṇuṣva mahāśaila pareṣāmupakārakaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

Devas said:

70\. O mountain, all of us, the Suras have come here to submit to you. "Listen to it, O great mountain, the helper of others.

## \|\| 1.9.71-72 \|\|

*evamuktastadā śailo davairdaityaiḥ sa maṃdaraḥ \|*  
*uvāca niḥsṛto bhūtvā paraṃ vigrahavānvacaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tena rūpeṇa rūpī sa parvato maṃdarācalaḥ \|*  
*kimarthamāgatāḥ sarve matsamīpaṃ taducyatām \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. On being requested thus by Devas and Daityas then, the mountain Mandara came out in an embodied form and ia that form the mountain Mandara said: “What for have all of you come to me? Let that be mentioned.”

## \|\| 1.9.73 \|\|

*tadā baliruvācedaṃ prastāvasadṛśaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*iṃdropi tvarayā yukto babhāṣe sūnṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Then Bali said these words befitting the occasion. Indra too hurriedly spoke these courteous and sincere words:

## \|\| 1.9.74 \|\|

*asmābhiḥ saha kāryārthe bhava tvaṃ maṃdarācala \|*  
*amṛtotpādanārthe tvaṃ maṃthānaṃ bhava suvrata \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. “O mountain Mandara, you cooperate with us in a great undertaking. O observer of holy vows, you should be the churning rod for the production of nectar.”

## \|\| 1.9.75 \|\|

*tatheti matvā tadvākyaṃ devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|*  
*ūce devāsurāṃścedamindraṃ prati viśeṣataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Saying “So be it” and honouring their words, because it was for the accomplishment of the task of Devas, he spoke these words to Devas and Asuras and particularly to Indra:

## \|\| 1.9.76 \|\|

*cheditau ca tvayā pakṣau vajreṇa śataparvaṇā \|*  
*gaṃtuṃ kathaṃ samartho'haṃ bhavatāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. “My wings have been cut (by you) with the thunderbolt of hundred spikes. How is it possible for me to go for realizing your purpose?”

## \|\| 1.9.77 \|\|

*tadā devāsurāḥ sarve stūyamānā mahācalam \|*  
*utpāṭayeyuratulaṃ maṃdaraṃ ca tatodbhutam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Then all Devas and Asuras praised the mountain. They then uprooted that incomparable and wonderful Mandara mountain.

## \|\| 1.9.78 \|\|

*kṣīrārṇavaṃ netukāmā hyaśaktāste tato'bhavan \|*  
*parvataḥ patitaḥ sadyo devadaityopari dhruvam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. But, though they were desirous of taking it to the Milky Ocean, they proved incapable of doing it. The mountain fell on Devas and Daityas.

## \|\| 1.9.79 \|\|

*kecidbhagnā mṛtāḥ kecitkecinmūrchāparā bhavan \|*  
*parīvādaratāḥ kecitkecitkleśatvamāgatāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Some were crushed. Softie died. Some fell into a swoon. Some of them began to blame and censure and some suffered great pain.

## \|\| 1.9.80 \|\|

*ेvaṃ bhagnodyamā jātā asurāḥsuradānavāḥ \|*  
*cetanāṃ paramāṃ prāptāstuṣṭuvurjagadīśvaram \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Thus, Asuras, Suras and Dānavas failed in their attempt. When they regained consciousness, they eulogized the Lord of the universe:

## \|\| 1.9.81 \|\|

*rakṣarakṣa mahāviṣṇo śaraṇāgatavatsala \|*  
*tvayā tatamidaṃ sarvaṃ jaṃgamājaṃgamaṃ ca yat \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. “Save us, save us, O great Viṣṇu, O lord compassionate to those who seek refuge. The entire world, mobile as well as immobile, is pervaded by you.”

## \|\| 1.9.82-83 \|\|

*devānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthaṃ prādurbhūto haristadā \|*  
*tāndṛṣṭvā sahasā viṣṇurgaruḍopari saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*līlayā parvataśreṣṭhamuttabhyāropayatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*garutmati tadā devaḥ sarveṣāmabhayaṃ dadau \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. Then Hari appeared before them for the accomplishment of the purpose of Devas. Viṣṇu who was seated on Garuḍa, saw them and suddenly and sportingly lifted up the excellent mountain and placed it on Garuḍa. Then, the lord granted all of them protection from fear.

## \|\| 1.9.84 \|\|

*tata utthāya tāndevānkṣīrosyottaraṃ taṭam \|*  
*nītvā taṃ parvataṃ vṛddhaṃ nikṣipyāpsu tato yayau \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Rising from there (and taking leave of) those Devas, he took the old mountain to the northern shore of the Ocean of Milk. After placing it in the waters, he went away from that place.

## \|\| 1.9.85 \|\|

*tadā sarve suragaṇāḥ svāgatya asuraiḥ saha \|*  
*vāsukiṃ ca samādāya cakrire samayaṃca tam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Then all those groups of Suras arrived there along with Asuras, taking Vāsuki with them. Then they made the agreement.

## \|\| 1.9.86 \|\|

*maṃthānaṃ maṃdaraṃ caiva vāsukiṃ rajjumeva ca \|*  
*kṛtvā surā'surāḥ sarve mamaṃthuḥ śrīrasāgaram \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. After making Mandara the churning rod and Vāsuki the rope, all of them, Suras and Asuras, churned the Ocean of Milk.

## \|\| 1.9.87 \|\|

*kṣīrābdhermathyamānasya parvato hi rasātalam \|*  
*gataḥ sa tatkṣaṇādeva kūrmo bhūtvā ramāpatiḥ \|*  
*uddhṛtastatkṣaṇādeva tadadbhutamivābhavat \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. As the Ocean of Milk was being churned, the mountain sank deep into Rasātala. At that very instant, the Lord of Ramā, Viṣṇu, became a tortoise and lifted it up. That was something really marvellous.

## \|\| 1.9.88 \|\|

*bhrāmyamāṇastataḥ śailo noditaḥ suradānavaiḥ \|*  
*bhramamāṇo nirādhāro bodhaśceva guruṃ vinā \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. When the mountain rotated, it was further pulled and pushed by Suras and Dānavas. Now it rotated without any basis, like the understanding without a preceptor.

## \|\| 1.9.89 \|\|

*paramātmā tadā viṣṇurādhāro maṃdarasya ca \|*  
*dorbhiścaturbhiḥ saṃgṛhya mamaṃthābdhiṃ sukhāvaham \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Viṣṇu, the supreme soul, then became the basic support of the Mandara mountain. With his four hands he gathered it up and churned pleasantly.

## \|\| 1.9.90 \|\|

*tadā surāsurāḥ sarve mamaṃthuḥ kṣīrasāgaram \|*  
*ekībhūtvā balenaivamatimātraṃ balotkaṭāḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Then all Suras and Asuras churned the Ocean of Milk after uniting together. Very powerful themselves, by uniting together, they became all the more powerful.

## \|\| 1.9.91 \|\|

*pṛṣṭhakaṃṭhorujānvaṃtaḥ kamaṭhasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tathāsau parvataśreṣṭho vajrasāramayo dṛḍhaḥ \|*  
*ubhayorgharṣaṇādeva vaḍavāgniḥ samutthitaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The excellent mountain had adamantine strength. It rolled on the back, neck, thighs and the space between the knees of the noble-souled tortoise. Due to the friction of these two, submarine fire was generated.

## \|\| 1.9.92 \|\|

*halāhalaṃ ca saṃjātaṃ tadṝṣṭvā nāradena hi \|*  
*tato devānuvācedaṃ devarṣiramitadyutiḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. The Halāhala poison too emerged and it was seen by Nārada. Thereafter, the celestial sage of unmeasured splendour spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.9.93-94 \|\|

*na kāryaṃ mathanaṃ cābdherbhavadbhiradhunā'khilaiḥ \|*  
*prārthayadhvaṃ śivaṃ devāḥ sarve dakṣasya yājanam \|*  
*tadvismṛtiṃ ca voyātaṃ vīrabhadreṇa yatkṛtam \|\| 93 \|\|*

*tasmācchivaḥ smaryatāṃ cāśu devāḥ paraḥ parāṇāmapi vā paraśca \|*  
*parātparaḥ paramānaṃdarūpo yogidhyeyo niṣprapaṃco hyarūpaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

93-94, “The churning of the ocean should not be carried on by you all now. O Devas, all of you pray to Śiva. Have you forgotten the sacrifice of Dakṣa and what Vīrabhadra did there?

Hence, let Śiva be immediately remembered, O Devas. He is greater than the greatest; he is beyond the greatest. He is the embodiment of supreme bliss. He is worthy of being meditated upon by Yogins; he has no form. (As a matter of fact) however, he is formless and unmanifest (or without diversity).”

## \|\| 1.9.95 \|\|

*te mathyamānāstvaritā devāḥ svātmārthasādhakāḥ \|*  
*abhilāṣaparāḥ sarve na śrṛṇvaṃti yato jaḍāḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Devas were eager to achieve their purpose. Therefore, they hurriedly went on churning the ocean. All those who are overwhelmed by desires do not listen (to the advice of others), because they become irrational and stupid.

## \|\| 1.9.96 \|\|

*upadeśaiśca bahubhirnopadeśyāḥ kadācana \|*  
*te rāgadveṣasaṃghātāḥ sarve śivaparāṅmukhāḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. They should not be given many pieces of advice and instructions. They are subject to Rāga (desire) and Dveṣa (hatred). All of them are averse to Śiva.

## \|\| 1.9.97 \|\|

*kevalodyamasaṃvītā mamaṃthuḥ kṣīrasāgaram \|*  
*atinirmathanājjātaṃ kṣīrābdheścahalāhalam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. With their sheer continuous exertion, they churned the Ocean of Milk. Due to excessive churning, the poison called Halāhala was generated from the Ocean of Milk.

## \|\| 1.9.98 \|\|

*trailokyadahane prauḍhaṃ prāptaṃ haṃtuṃ divaukasaḥ \|*  
*ata ūrdhvaṃ diśaḥ sarvā vyāptaṃ kṛtsnaṃ nabhastalam \|*  
*grasituṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ kālakūṭaṃ samabhyayāt \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. It was strong enough to burn down the three worlds. It came up to kill the heaven-dwellers. It went up still further and spread to all quarters. The entire sky was pervaded by it. The Kālakūṭa poison advanced to consume all the living beings.

## \|\| 1.9.99 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā bṛhaṃtaṃ svakarasthamojasā taṃ sarparājaṃ saha parvatena \|*  
*tatraiva hitvāpayayustadānīṃ palāyamānā hyasuraiḥ sametāḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. They observed the huge king of serpents grasped by their own hands. They left him there along with the mountain and then went (immediately) away. They fled along with Asuras.

## \|\| 1.9.100 \|\|

*tathaiva sarva ṛṣayo bhṛgvādyāḥ śataśāmyati \|*  
*dakṣasya yajanaṃ tena yathā jātaṃ tathābhavat \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. So also the sages beginning with Bhṛgu, sages in hundreds (fled in all directions). It was like what happened at the sacrifice of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 1.9.101 \|\|

*satyalokaṃ gatāḥ sarve bhuguṇā noditā bhṛśam \|*  
*vedavākyaiśca vividhaiḥ kālakūṭaṃ śataśastataḥ \|*  
*devā nāstyatra saṃdehaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmi vaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Earnestly urged by Bhṛgu, all of them went to Satyaloka: “This poison Kālakūṭa will be quelled by means of various Vedic Sentences. O Devas, there is no doubt in this matter. It is true; I am speaking the truth unto you.”

## \|\| 1.9.102 \|\|

*bhṛguṇoktaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā kālakūṭaviṣārdditāḥ \|*  
*satyalokaṃ samāsādya brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. On hearing these words uttered by Bhṛgu, all of them distressed by the poison Kālakūṭa went to Satyaloka and sought refuge in Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.9.103 \|\|

*tadā jājvalyamānaṃ vai kālakūṭaṃ prabhojjavalam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā brahmātha tāndṛṣṭvā hyakarmajñānasurāsurān \|*  
*teṣāṃ śapitumārebhe nāradena nivāritaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Brahmā saw the blazing Kālakūṭa with sparkling lustre. He found that Suras and Asuras were ignorant of their duties. He was about to curse them, but he was prevented by Nārada.

## \|\| 1.9.104 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*akāryaṃ kiṃ kṛtaṃ devāḥ kasmātkṣobhoyamudyataḥ \|*  
*īśvarasya ca jāto'dya nānyathā mama bhāṣitam \|\| 104 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

104\. O Devas, what a wrong thing has been committed by you? Why has this explosive thing cropped up? It is Īśvara’s anger. My speech cannot be otherwise.

## \|\| 1.9.105 \|\|

*tato devaiḥ parivṛto vedopaniṣadaistathā \|*  
*nānāgamaiḥ parivṛtaḥ kālakūṭabhayādyayau \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Thereupon, surrounded by Devas, the Vedas, the Upāniṣads and the different kinds of Āgamas, he proceeded ahead out of fear of the Kālakūṭa.

## \|\| 1.9.106 \|\|

*tataściṃtānvitā devā idamūcuḥ parasparam \|*  
*avidyākāmasaṃvītāḥ kuryāmaḥ śaṃkaraṃ ca kam \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Then, Devas who were worried said to to one another, “We are enveloped in Avidyā (nescience) and lust. How can we do anything to Śaṅkara?”

## \|\| 1.9.107 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ ca puraskṛtya tadā devāstvarānvitāḥ \|*  
*vaikuṇṭhamāvrajansarve kālakūṭa bhayārdditāḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Then Devas kept Brahmā at their head and hurriedly went to Vaikuṇṭha, because they were afraid of Kālakūṭa.
