31-32. “None of you need worry about this. If you are cut off into several parts, you will grow further with many branches by the grace of Indra. Then you will be permanently endowed with (possession of branches).” On being told thus, all of them partially accepted the (sin of) the slaughter.

## \|\| 1.16.33 \|\|

*tato hyapaḥ samāhūya ūcuḥ sarve divaukasaḥ \|*  
*adbhiśca gṛhyatāmadya hatyāṃśaḥ kāryasiddhaye \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then they called the Waters and all the heaven-dwellers spoke thus to the Waters: “Let a part of the (sin of) Brāhmaṇa’s slaughter be taken up by the Waters for the sake of realizing the objectives (of Devas).”

## \|\| 1.16.34-35 \|\|

*tadā hyāpo militvātha ūcuḥ sarvāḥ purodhasam \|*  
*yāni kāni ca pāpāni tathā duścaritāni ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*asmatsaṃparkasaṃbaṃdhātsnānaśaucāśanādibhiḥ \|*  
*punaṃti prāṇinaḥ sarve pāpena pariveṣṭitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Then all the Waters joined together and said to the priest (Bṛhaspati): “All the living beings enveloped by sins sanctify themselves by dispelling whatever sins and evils they are tainted with, by coming into contact with us, through ablutions, cleansing processes and drinking.”

## \|\| 1.16.36-38 \|\|

*tāsāṃ vacanamākarṇya bṛhaspatiruvāca ha \|*  
*mā bhayaṃ kriyatāmāpa enasā dustareṇa hi \|\| 36 \|\|*

*āpaḥ punaṃtu sarveṣāṃ carācaranivāsinām \|*  
*tadā striyaḥ samāhūya bṛhaspatiruvāca ha \|\| 37 \|\|*

*adyaiva grāhye hatyāṃśaḥ sarvakāryārthasiddhaye \|*  
*niśamya tadgurorvākyamūcuḥ sarvāścayopitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. On hearing their words, Bṛhaspati said: “O Waters, do not be afraid of the sin, though it is difficult to be crossed. Let the Waters sanctify all living beings, mobile and immobile.”

## \|\| 1.16.39-40 \|\|

*pāpamācarate yoṣā tena pāpena nānyathā \|*  
*lipyaṃte bahavaḥ pakṣā iti vedānuśāsanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*śrutamasti na te kiṃciddhepurodho vimṛśyatām \|*  
*yoṣidbhiḥ procyamāno'pi uvācātha bṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Then Bṛhaspati called women and said: “Now itself a part of the (sin of) Brāhmaṇa-slaughter should be taken up for the sake of realizing the objectives of all.”

On hearing the words of Guru (Bṛhaspati), all the women said:

39-40. “This is the injunction of the Vedas that if a woman commits a sin, other (many) members of her family become tainted with it and not otherwise. O priest, has this not been heard by you? Let it be pondered over.”

## \|\| 1.16.41-42 \|\|

*mā bhayaṃ kriyatāṃ sarvāḥ pāpādasmātsulocanāḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyāṇāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ bhaviṣyati phalapradaḥ \|*  
*hatyāṃśo yo hi sarvāsāṃ yathākāmitvameva ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

*evamaṃśāśca tyāyāścatvāraḥ kalpitāḥ suraiḥ \|*  
*nivāsamakarotsadyasteṣuteṣu dvijottamāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

On being told thus by the women, Bṛhaspati said:

41-42. “Do not be afraid of this sin, O ye ladies of beautiful eyes. This (act of yours) will bestow benefits on other ladies of the future. The part of the (sin of) slaughter will benefit everyone. (Further) you will have Yathākāmitva (‘ability to love to the heart’s content’).” Thus, four parts of the sin of slaughter were allotted by Suras. The sin of slaughter stayed in those beings, O excellent Brāhmaṇas,

## \|\| 1.16.43 \|\|

*niṣpāpo hi tadā jāto maheṃdro hyabhiṣecitaḥ \|*  
*devapuryāṃ suragaṇaistathaiva ṛṣabhiḥ saha \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Mahendra then became free from sins and he was crowned in the city of Devas by the groups of Devas along with the sages.

## \|\| 1.16.44 \|\|

*śacyā sameto hi tadā puraṃdaro babhūva viśvādhipatirmahātmā \|*  
*devaiḥ sameto hi mahānubhāvairmunīśvaraiḥ siddhagaṇaistadānīm \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Accompanied by Śacī, the noble-souled Purandara became the overlord of the universe. He was accompanied by Devas, the leading sages of great magnanimity and groups of Siddhas too.

## \|\| 1.16.45 \|\|

*tadāgnayaḥ śobhanā vāyavaśca sarve grahāḥ suprabhāḥ śāṃtiyuktāḥ \|*  
*jātāḥ sadyaḥ pṛthivī śobhamānā tathādrayo maṇiprabhavā babhūvuḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Then, fires and winds became splendid. All the planets were lustrous and quiescent. The earth shone with great splendour; so also the mountains yielded gems and jewels.

## \|\| 1.16.46-48 \|\|

*prasannāni tathā hyāsanmanāṃsi ca manasvinām \|\| 46 \|\|*

*nadyaścāmṛtavāhinyo vṛkṣā hyāsansadāphalāḥ \|*  
*akṛṣṭapacyauṣadhayo babhūvuścamṛtopamāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*aikapadyena sarveṣāmiṃdralokanivāsinām \|*  
*babhūva paramotsāho mahāmodakarastathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. The minds of learned men became delighted. Rivers flowed with nectarine waters. Trees yielded fruits perpetually. Planets and medicinal herbs grew and matured without being cultivated. They were comparable to nectar (in taste and effect). The inhabitants of Indra’s world were all enthusiastic and exceedingly joyous.

## \|\| 1.16.49 \|\|

*lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare tvaṣṭā dṛṣṭvā ceṃdramahotsavam \|*  
*babhūva ruṣi to'tīva putraśokaprapīḍitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

49\. In the meantime, Tvaṣṭṛ who witnessed the celebrations in honour of Indra became exceedingly infuriated and was afflictted with sorrow for his (dead) son.

## \|\| 1.16.50-51 \|\|

*jagāma nirvedaparastapastaptuṃ sudāruṇam \|*  
*tapasā tena saṃtuṣṭo brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tvaṣṭāramabravīttuṣṭo varaṃ varaya suvrata \|*  
*tadā vavre varaṃ tvaṣṭā sarvalokabhayāvaham \|*  
*varaṃ putro hi dātvoya devānāṃ hi bhayāvahaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. With great dejection, he went (to forest) for performing a severe penance. Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, became pleased with that penance. Being delighted he said to Tvaṣṭṛ, “O (Tvaṣṭṛ) of good holy rites, choose your boon.”

Thereupon, Tvaṣṭṛ chose a boon that caused fear to all the worlds:

“A son who will be terrifying Devas should be given as boon.”

## \|\| 1.16.52 \|\|

*tatheti ca varo datto brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*varadānātsadya eva babhūva puruṣastadā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Saying “So be it”, the boon was granted by Brahmā Parameṣṭḥīn. No sooner had the boon been granted than a person appeared there.

## \|\| 1.16.53 \|\|

*vṛtranāmāṃkitastatra daityo hi paramādbhutaḥ \|*  
*dhanuṣāṃ śatamātraṃ hi pratyahaṃ vavṛdhe'suraḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He was a wonderful Daitya named Vṛtra. Everyday, the Asura increased by a hundred Dhanus (1 Dhanus= about 2 metres) in stature and size.

## \|\| 1.16.54 \|\|

*pātālānnirgatā daityā ye purā'mṛtamaṃthane \|*  
*ghātitāḥ surasaṃghaiśca bhṛguṇā jīvitāstvarāt \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Those Daityas who had been killed by the groups of Suras at the time of the churning of the Milk Ocean and were resuscitated to life quickly by Bhṛgu, came out of Pātāla.

## \|\| 1.16.55 \|\|

*sarvaṃ mahītalaṃ vyāptaṃ tenaikena mahātmanā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The whole of the earth was pervaded by that Asura of great soul.

## \|\| 1.16.56 \|\|

*tadā sarve'pi ṛṣayo vadhyamānāstapasvinaḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ tvaritāḥ sarve ūcurvyasanamāgatam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Then, all the sages who had been hurt and injured and all the ascetics hurriedly reported to Brahmā about the calamity that had befallen them. So also did Indra and other Devas and Gandharvas along with the groups of Maruts.

## \|\| 1.16.57 \|\|

*tathā ceṃdrādayo devā gaṃdharvāḥ samarudgaṇāḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇā kathitaṃ sarvaṃ tvaṣṭuścaitaccikīrṣitam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Everything that Tvaṣṭṛ intended to do was told by Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.16.58-59 \|\|

*bhavadvadhārthaṃ janitastapasā parameṇa tu \|*  
*vṛttronāma mahātejāḥ sarvadaityāpidho mahān \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tathāpi yatnaḥ kriyatāṃ yathā vadhyo bhavedasau \|*  
*niśamya brahmaṇo vākyamūcurddevāḥ savāsavāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. “By performing very severe penance, a great overlord of all Daityas called Vṛtra, of great refulgence, has been created for killing you (all).

Still endeavour may be made to see that this Daitya is killed.”

On hearing the words of Brahmā, Devas including Vāsava spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.16.60 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadā iṃdro hi hatyāyā vimuktaḥ sthāpito divi \|*  
*tadāsmābhirakāryaṃ vai kṛtamasti durāsadam \|\| 60 \|\|*

Devas said:

60\. When Indra was absolved of the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaugh-ter and established (as a ruler) in the heaven, something which should not have been done and which is hard to be born, had been done by us.

## \|\| 1.16.61 \|\|

*śastrāṇyastrāṇyanekāni saṃkṣiptāni hyabuddhitaḥ \|*  
*dadhīca syāśrame brahmankiṃ kāryaṃ karavāmahe \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Many weapons and missiles had been foolishly thrown in the hermitage of Dadhīca. What shall we do now, O Brahmā?

## \|\| 1.16.62 \|\|

*tacchrutvā prahasanvākyaṃ devānbrahmā tadā'bravīt \|*  
*ciraṃ sthitāni vijñāyāgacchadhvaṃ tāni vai surāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On hearing those words, Brahmā laughingly said to Devas: “They have remained there for a long time. Enquire and return, O Suras.”

## \|\| 1.16.63 \|\|

*gatvā devāstadā sarve nāpaśyansvaṃ svamāyudham \|*  
*papracchuśca dadhīciṃ te so'vādīnnaiva vedbhayaham \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. All the Devas went there, but could not see their respective weapons. They asked Dadhīci and he replied: “I do not know.”

## \|\| 1.16.64-65 \|\|

*punarbrahmāṇamāgātya ūcuḥ sarve munervacaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*brahmovāca tadā devānsarveṣāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|*  
*tasyāsthīnyeva yācadhvaṃ pradāsyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. Again they came to Brahmā and all of them told him what the sage said.

Brahmā then said to Devas: “Request him for his bones for the sake of accomplishing the objectives of all (of you). He will undoubtedly give (them).”

## \|\| 1.16.66-67 \|\|

*tacchrutvā brāhmaṇo vākyaṃ śakro vacanamabravīt \|\| 66 \|\|*

*viśvarūpo hato deva devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|*  
*eka eva tadā brahmanpāpiṣṭho'haṃ kṛtaḥ suraiḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. On hearing the words of Brahmā, Śakra spoke: “O lord, for the sake of accomplishing the objectives of Devas, Viśvarūpa was killed. But I alone was made the most (condemned) sinner by Suras, O Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.16.68 \|\|

*tathā purodhasā caiva niḥśrīkastatkṣaṇātkṛtaḥ \|*  
*diṣṭyā paramayā cāhaṃ praviṣṭo nijamaṃdiram \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Further, at the very same instant, I was made niḥśrīka (‘devoid of glory and splendour’) by my preceptor. It was indeed a good luck that I have now entered my mansion.

## \|\| 1.16.69 \|\|

*dadhīcaṃ ghātayitvā vai tasyāsthīni bahūnyapi \|*  
*astrāṇi tāni bhagavankṛtāni hyaśubhāni vai \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Even if, after getting Dadhīci killed, many of his bones (are taken) and weapons are made from them, those (bone-made) weapons will be inauspicious, O Lord.

## \|\| 1.16.70 \|\|

*tvaṣṭrā hi janito yo vai vṛtro nāmaiṣa daityarāṭ \|*  
*kathaṃ taṃ ghātayāmyevaṃ satataṃ pāpabhīruṇā \|*  
*śakreṇoktaṃ niśamyātha brahmā vākyamuvāca ha \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Thus, I am perpetually in fear of sin. How can I kill this king of Daityas named Vṛtfa who has been begotten by Tvaṣṭṛ?”

Hearing the words of Śakra who was perpetually in fear of sins, god Brahmā spoke thus: He enlightened (Indra) through the instruction of Arthaśāstra.

## \|\| 1.16.71 \|\|

*arthaśāstrapareṇaiva vidhinā tamabodhayat \|*  
*ātatāyinamāyāṃtaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vā tapasvinam \|*  
*haṃtukāmaṃ jighāṃsīyānna tena brahmahā bhavet \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. “One can withstand and even kill a desperado whether he be a Brāhmaṇa or an ascetic in case he rushes at one and desires to kill one. One does not become a Brāhmaṇa-slayer thereby.”

## \|\| 1.16.72 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*dadhīcasya vadhādbrahmannahaṃ bhīto na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tasmādbrahmavadhātsatyaṃ mahadeno bhaviṣyati \|\| 72 \|\|*

Indra said:

72\. I am afraid of causing the death of Dadhīca, O Brahmā. There is no doubt about this that a great sin will result from that Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.

## \|\| 1.16.73 \|\|

*ato na kāryamasmābhirbrāhmaṇānāṃ tu helanam \|*  
*helanādbahavo doṣā bhaviṣyaṃti na cānyathā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Hence, Brāhmaṇas should not be slighted or insulted by us. Many defects result from insulting (them). It cannot be otherwise.

## \|\| 1.16.74 \|\|

*adṛṣṭaṃ paramaṃ dharmyaṃ vidhinā parameṇa hi \|*  
*kartavyaṃ manasā caivaṃ puruṣeṇa vijānatā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Only that which brings about great merits should be done by a wise man. Only such acts should a learned man think of doing (and plan).

## \|\| 1.16.75-77 \|\|

*niḥspṛhaṃ tasya tadvākyaṃ śrutvā brahmā hyuvāca tam \|*  
*śakrasvabuddhyāvartasva dadhīciṃ gaccha satvaram \|\| 75 \|\|*

*yācasva tasya cāsthīni dadhīceḥ kāryagauravāt \|*  
*guruṇā sahitaḥ śakro devaiḥ saha samanvitaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*tatheti gatvā te sarve dadhīcasyāśramaṃ śubham \|*  
*nānāsattvasamāyuktaṃ vairabāvavivarjitam \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. On hearing his disinterested words, Brahmā spoke to him:

“O Śakra, make use of your own intelligence. Go to Dadhīci quickly. Ṛequest for Dadhīci’s bones in view of the gravity of the matter.” Saying “So be it”, Śakra, accompanied by his preceptor and Devas, went to the auspicious hermitage of Dadhīca, which contained different kinds of animals devoid of their natural animosity.

## \|\| 1.16.78-80 \|\|

*mārjāramūṣakāścaiva parasparamudānvitāḥ \|*  
*aikapadyena siṃhāśca gajinyaḥ kalabhaiḥ saha \|\| 78 \|\|*

*tathā jātyaśca vividhāḥ krīḍāyuktāḥ parasparam \|*  
*nakulaiḥ saha sarpāśca krīḍāyuktāḥ parasparam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*evaṃvidhānyanekāni hyaścaryāṇi tadāśrame \|*  
*paśyaṃto vibudhāḥ sarve vismayaṃ paramaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

78-80. Cats and mice were joyous in each other’s company. Lions and she-elephants along with their young ones found joy in remaining in the same place. Different species of animals were engaged in sports in one another’s company. Serpents and mongooses were playing about in one another’s company. Devas-who saw these and many other miraculous things in that hermitage were surprised very much.

## \|\| 1.16.81-82 \|\|

*athāsane muniśreṣṭhaṃ dadṛśuḥ paramāsthitam \|*  
*tejasā parameṇaiva bhrājamānaṃ yathā ravim \|\| 81 \|\|*

*vibhāvasuṃ dvitīyaṃ vā suvarcasahitaṃ tadā \|*  
*yathā brahmā hi sāvitryā tathāsau munisattamaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. They saw the pre-eminent sage seated in his excellent seat. He was shining with great splendour like the sun or like a second fire. The excellent sage was accompanied by ṭhis wife) Suvarcā, just as Brahmā is accompanied by Sāvitrī.

## \|\| 1.16.83-85 \|\|

*taṃ praṇamya tato devā vacanaṃ cedamabruvan \|*  
*tvaṃ dātā triṣu lokeṣu tvatsakāśamihagatāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*niśamya vacanaṃ teṣāṃ devānāṃ bhunirabravīt \|*  
*kimartha māgatāḥ sarve vadadhvaṃ tatsurottamāḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*prayacchāmi na saṃdeho nānyathā mama bhāṣitam \|*  
*tadocuḥ sahitāḥ sarve dadhīciṃ svārthakāmukāḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

83-85. After bowing down to him Devas spoke these words:

“You are a donor (famous) in the three worlds. (Hence) we have come to you.”

On hearing the words of those Devas, the sage spoke: “O excellent Suras, tell me what for have all of you come. I shall give it. There is no doubt about it. My word cannot be otherwise.”

Then all those Suras in a body said to Dadhīci, as they were seekers of their own selfish interests:

## \|\| 1.16.86-88 \|\|

*bhayabhītā vayaṃ vipra bhavaddarśanakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*trātāraṃ tvāṃ samākarṇya brahmaṇā noditā vayam \|\| 86 \|\|*

*samprāptā viddhi tatsarvaṃ dātumarho'tha suvrata \|\| 87 \|\|*

*niśamya vacanaṃ teṣāṃ kiṃ dātavyaṃ taducyatām \|\| 88 \|\|*

86-88. “We have been desirous of seeing you as all of us are (mortally) afraid of dangers, O Brāhmaṇa. Hearing about you as a saviour, Brahmā has urged us. So we have come. Understand all these things. O sage of good holy rites, it behoves you to give us.”

On hearing their words (the sage said): “Let it be mentioned what should be given?”

## \|\| 1.16.89-90 \|\|

*tato devābruvanvipra daityānāṃ nidhanāyanaḥ \|*  
*śastranirmāṇakāryārthaṃ tavāsthīni prayaccha vai \|\| 89 \|\|*

*prahasyovāca viprarṣistiṣṭhadhvaṃ kṣaṇameva hi \|*  
*svayameva tvahaṃ devāstyakṣyāmyadya kalevaram \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. Then Devas said: “O Brāhmaṇa, give us your bones for the sake of making weapons in order to destroy Daityas.”

## \|\| 1.16.91-93 \|\|

*ityuktvā tānatho patnīṃ samāhūya suvarcasam \|*  
*provāca sa mahātejāḥ śrṛṇu devī śucismite \|\| 91 \|\|*

*asthyarthaṃ yācito devaistyajāmyetatkalevaram \|*  
*brahmalokaṃ vrajāmyadya parameṇa samādhinā \|\| 92 \|\|*

*mayi yāte brahmalokaṃ tvaṃ svadharmeṇa tatra mām \|*  
*prāpsyasyeva na saṃdeho vṛthā cintāṃ ca mā kṛthāḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

Then the Brāhmaṇical sage laughed and said: “Wait for a moment, O Devas. I shall myself give up my body today.”

91-93. After saying this to them, he called his wife Suvarcā. The sage of great splendour said: “Listen, O gentle lady of pure smiles. I have been requested by Devas for my bones. I am forsaking this body. I shall go to the world of Brahmā by means of profound meditation. There is no doubt about this that when I have gone to the world of Brahmā, you will also attain me there by means of your own virtue. Do not become worried over this unnecessarily.”

## \|\| 1.16.94 \|\|

*ityuktvā tāṃ svapatnīṃ sa preṣayāmāsa cāśramam \|*  
*tato devāgrato vipraḥ samādhimagamattadā \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. After saying this to his wife, he sent her to his own hermitage. Then, the Brāhmaṇa went into a state of concentration in the presence of the Devas,

## \|\| 1.16.95 \|\|

*samādhinā pareṇaiva visṛjya svaṃ kalevaram \|*  
*brahmalokaṃ gataḥ sadyaḥ punarnāvartate yataḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. By means of the greatest concentration of mind, he cast off his own body. Immediately he went to the world of Brahmā from where no one returns.

## \|\| 1.16.96 \|\|

*dadhīcināmā munivṛṃdavaryaḥ śivapriyaḥ śivadīkṣābhiyuktaḥ \|*  
*paropakārārthamidaṃ kalevaraṃ śīghraṃ sa vipro'tyajadātmanā tadā \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The most excellent one among the groups of sages, named Dadhīci was a favourite (devotee) of Śiva. He was initiated (in the cult) of Śiva. It is for the sake of helping others that the Brāhmaṇa quickly abandoned his body at that time.

## Chapter 17 - Vṛtra Killed: Bali Prepares for War

## \|\| 1.17.1-3 \|\|

*\| lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ sarve suragaṇā dṛṣṭvā taṃ vilayaṃ gatam \|*  
*ciṃtayaṃtaḥ suragaṇāḥ kathaṃ ca vidadhāmahe \|\| 1 \|\|*

*surabhiṃ cāhvayitvātha tadovāca śacīpatiḥ \|*  
*kalevaraṃ dadhīcasya lihyāstvaṃ vacanānmama \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tatheti ca vacomatvā tatkṣaṇādeva lihya tat \|*  
*nirmāṃsaṃ ca kṛtaṃ sadyastayā dhenvā kalevaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

1-3. Then on seeing him absorbed (in the Supreme Spirit), the groups of Suras began to think: ‘How do we make (the weapons out of this body)?’ Then the consort of Śacī called Surabhi (the divine cow) and said: “At my instance lick up the body of Dadhīca.” Saying “So be it” and honouring his words, Surabhi licked the body at the same instant. The body was immediately made rid of all flesh by that cow.

## \|\| 1.17.4-5 \|\|

*jagṛhustāni cāsthīni cakruḥ śastrāṇi vai surāḥ \|*  
*tasya vaṃśodbhavaṃ vajraṃ śiro brahmaśirastathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*anyāni cāsthīni bahūni tasya ṛṣestadānīṃ jagṛhuḥ surāśca \|*  
*tathā śirājālamayāṃśca pāśāṃścakruḥ surā vairayutāśca daityān \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Suras picked up those bones and made weapons out of them. The weapon Vajra (thunderbolt) was made out of his backbone and the weapon Brahmaśiras was made out of his skull. Suras picked up many other bones of that sage (and made weapons out of them). Similarly, Suras who were naturally inimical to Daityas, made nooses out of his clusters of nerves and veins.

## \|\| 1.17.6 \|\|

*śastrāṇi kṛtvā te sarve mahābalaparākramāḥ \|*  
*yayurdevātastvarāyuktā vṛtraghātanatatparāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After making the weapons, all Suras of great strength and exploit hurried back, eager to kill Vṛtra.

## \|\| 1.17.7 \|\|

*tataḥ suvarccāśca dadhīcipatnī yā preṣitā sā surakāryasiddhaye \|*  
*vyalokayattatra sametya sarvaṃ mṛtaṃ patiṃ dehamatho dadarśatam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then Suvarcā, the wife of Dadhīci, who had been sent away for the purpose of accomplishing the objectives of Suras, came back to that place and saw the dead body of her husband.

## \|\| 1.17.8 \|\|

*jñātvā ca tatsarvamidaṃ surāṇāṃ kṛtyaṃ tadānīṃ ca cukopa sādhvī \|*  
*dadau satī śāpamatīva ruṣṭā tadā suvarcā ṛṣivaryapatnī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On coming to know that everything had been the work of Suras, the chaste lady became immediately infuriated. The chaste lady Suvarcā, the wife of the excellent sage, became extremely enraged and pronounced a curse:

## \|\| 1.17.9 \|\|

*aho surā duṣṭatarāśca sarve sarve hyaśaktāśca tathaiva lubdhāḥ \|*  
*tasmācca sarve'prajaso bhavaṃtu divaukaso'dyaprabhṛtityuvāca sā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “O Suras, all of you are very wicked. All of you are weak and greedy. Hence, from today onwards all the heaven-dwellers shall be issueless.”

## \|\| 1.17.10 \|\|

*eva śāpaṃ dadau teṣāṃ surāṇāṃ sā tapasvinī \|*  
*pravīśyāśvatthamūle sā svodaraṃ dārayattadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thus, that ascetic lady cursed those Suras and then came to the root of an Aśvattha tree, (the Indian fig tree) There she tore up her belly.

## \|\| 1.17.11 \|\|

*nirgato jaṭharādgarbho dadhīcasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*sākṣādrudrāvatāro'sau piplādo mahāprabhaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. From the belly, the foetus of the noble-souled Dadhīca came out. It was Pippalāda of great lustre. He was a direct incarnation of Rudra.

## \|\| 1.17.12-13 \|\|

*prahasya jananī garbhamuvāca ruṣitekṣaṇā \|*  
*suvarcā taṃ pippalādaṃ ciraṃ tiṣṭhāsya sannidhau \|\| 12 \|\|*

*aśvatthasya mahābhāga sarveṣāṃ saphalo bhaveḥ \|*  
*tathaiva bhāṣamāṇā sā suvarcā tanayaṃ prati \|*  
*patimanvagamatsādhvī parameṇa samādhinā \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. With eyes (flared up) with wrath, the mother Suvarcā laughed (in derision) and spoke to Pippalāda, the foetus: “Stay here for a long time near this Aśvattha, O highly magnificent son. Be fruitful unto all.” Speaking thus to her son, that chaste lady Suvarcā followed her husband by means of the greatest Samādhi (concentration).

## \|\| 1.17.14 \|\|

*evaṃ dadhīcapatnī sā patinā svargamāvrajat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thus, that wife of Dadhīca went to Heaven along with her husband.

## \|\| 1.17.15 \|\|

*te devāḥ kṛtaśastrāstrā daityānprati samutsukāḥ \|*  
*ājagmuśceṃdramukhyāste mahābalaparākramāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After making the missiles and the weapons, Devas of great might and exploits, who were eager to (fight) with Daityas, returned with Indra at their head.

## \|\| 1.17.16 \|\|

*guruṃ puraskṛtya tadājñayā te gaṇāḥ surāṇāṃ bahavastadānīm \|*  
*bhuvaṃ samāgatya ca madhyadeśamūcuśca sarve paramāstrayuktāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Honouring Guru and abiding by his bidding, the many groups of Suras, of great strength and exploit—all of them equipped with great weapons and missiles, came to the earth, the Middle Land (world), and spoke (among themselves).

## \|\| 1.17.17 \|\|

*samāgatānupasṛtya devāṃśceṃdrapurogamān \|*  
*yayau vṛtro mahādaityo daityavṛndasamāvṛtaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On hearing that Devas with Indra as their leader had come, Vṛtra, the great Daitya, went (there) accompanied by the groups of Daityas.

## \|\| 1.17.18 \|\|

*yathā merośca śikharaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pradṛśyate \|*  
*tathā so'pi mahātejā viśvakarmmasuto mahān \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Just as the peak of Meru is completely visible, so appeared that great son of Viśvakarman, with great refulgence.

## \|\| 1.17.19 \|\|

*tena dṛṣṭo mahendraśca maheṃdreṇa mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca darśanaṃ ca mahādbhutam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Mahendra was seen by him. The great Asura was seen by Mahendra. The meeting of Devas and Dānavas was exceedingly wonderful.

## \|\| 1.17.20 \|\|

*tadā te baddhavairāśca devadaityāḥ parasparam \|*  
*anyonyamabhisaṃrabdhā jagarjuḥ paramādbhutam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Devas and Daityas who had harbored bitter hatred for one another became furious with one another.

## \|\| 1.17.21 \|\|

*vāditrāṇi ca bhīmāni vādyamānāni sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*śrūyaṃte'tra gabhīrāṇi surā surasamāgame \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. During that encounter between Suras and Asuras, terrible, high-sounding instruments of martial music were played everywhere and their majestic loud report was heard everywhere.

## \|\| 1.17.22 \|\|

*vādyamāneṣu tūryeṣu te sarve tvarayānvitāḥ \|*  
*anekaiḥ śastrasaṃghātairjaghnuranyonyamojasā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. As the instruments were being played, all of them hurriedly and powerfully struck one another with many groups of weapons.

## \|\| 1.17.23 \|\|

*tadā devāsure yuddhe trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*bhayena mahatā yuktaṃ babhūva gatacetanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In that war between Devas and Asuras, all the three worlds including mobile and immobile beings, were overwhelmed by great fear and became unconscious.

## \|\| 1.17.24 \|\|

*cheditāḥ sphoṭitāścaiva kecicchastrairdvidhā kṛtāḥ \|*  
*nārācaiśca tathā kecicchastrāstraiḥ śakalīkṛtāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Some were cut and broken into two with the weapons. Some were injured by means of arrows and some cut into pieces with Nārāca arrows, weapons and missiles.

## \|\| 1.17.25 \|\|

*bhallaiścerurhatāḥ kecidvyaṃgabhūtā divaukasaḥ \|*  
*raśmayo meghasaṃbhūtāḥ prakāśaṃte nabhassviva \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Some of the heaven-dwellers were maimed and crippled with Bhallas (arrows with crescent-shaped heads). They moved about like the streaks of lightning from clouds that shine in the sky.

## \|\| 1.17.26-27 \|\|

*śirāṃsi patitānyeva bahūnica nabhastalāt \|*  
*nakṣatrāṇīva ca yathā mahāpralayasaṃkulam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pravartitaṃ madhyadeśe sarvabūtakṣayāvaham \|*  
*śakreṇa saha saṃgrāmaṃ cakāra namucistadā \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Many heads fell from the sky like stars as though the great confusion and consternation of Mahāpralaya (the great annihilation) had overrun the Middle World, causing the destruction of all living beings. Then Namuci fought with Śakra.

## \|\| 1.17.28-29 \|\|

*vajreṇa jaghne tarasā namuciṃ devarāṭ svayam \|*  
*na romaikaṃ ca trucitaṃ tamucerasurasya ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vajreṇāpi tadā sarve vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*asurāśca surāścaiva maheṃdro vrīḍitastadā \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The king of Devas himself hit Namuci with great force by means of his Vajra. But not even a single hair of the Asura Namuci was cut by that Vajra. All the Asuras and Suras were much surprised at this. Mahendra became ashamed.

## \|\| 1.17.30 \|\|

*gadayā namuciṃ jaghne gadā sāpi vicūrṇitā \|*  
*namuceraṃgalagnāpi papāta vasudhātale \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He struck Namuci with his club, but as soon as that club came into contact with Ṇamuci’s body, it was smashed into pieces and fell down on the earth.

## \|\| 1.17.31 \|\|

*tathā śūlena mahatā taṃ jaghāna puraṃdaraḥ \|*  
*tacchūlaṃ śatadhā cūrṇaṃ namuceraṃgamāśritam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Similarly, Purandara struck him with a great spear. That spear colliding with Namuci’s limbs split into a hundred pieces,

## \|\| 1.17.32-33 \|\|

*evaṃ taṃ vavidhaiḥ śastrairājaghāna surārihā \|*  
*prahasya māno namucirna jaghāna puraṃdaram \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tūṣṇīṃbhūtastadā ceṃdraściṃtayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ kāryaṃ kimakāryaṃ vā itīṃdro nāvidattadā \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Thus, the slayer of the enemies of Suras struck him with various kinds of weapons. But, Namuci went on smiling and laughing. He did not strike Purandara.

Beset with great worry and thought, Indra kept quiet. He did not know what should be done or what should not be done.

## \|\| 1.17.34 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra mahāyuddhe mahābhaye \|*  
*jātā nabhogatā vāṇī iṃdrasuddiśya satvaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. In the meantime, during that terrific great battle, an ethereal voice was heard immediately, addressing Indra:

## \|\| 1.17.35-36 \|\|

*jahyenamadyāśu maheṃdra daityaṃ divaukasāṃ ghorataraṃ bhayāvaham \|*  
*phenena caivāśu mahāsurendramapāṃ samīpena durāsadena \|\| 35 \|\|*

*anyena śastreṇa ca āhato'sau vadhyaḥ kadācinna bhavatyayaṃ tu \|*  
*tasmācca deveśa vadhārthamasya kuru prayatnaṃ namucerdurātmanaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. “Kill this Daitya today immediately, O Mahendra. He is getting terrible and striking terror into the heaven-dwellers. Kill this great leader of Asuras quickly by means of the foam which is near the waters and which is hard to be borne. If struck with any other weapon, he can never be killed. Hence, O lord of Devas, make all possible endeavour to kill this evil-minded Namuci.”

## \|\| 1.17.37 \|\|

*niśamya vācaṃ paramārthayuktāṃ daivīṃ sadānaṃdakarīṃ śubhāvahām \|*  
*cakre paraṃ yatnavatāṃ variṣṭho gatvodadheḥ pāramanaṃtavīryaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On hearing the divine speech that was characterized by truth, that caused perpetual delight and was conducive to auspiciousness, (Indra) who was the most excellent one among those who endeavour, went to the other shore of the ocean and attempted (to kill Namuci) as he had infinite fund of vigour.

## \|\| 1.17.38 \|\|

*tatrāgataṃ samīkṣyātha namuciḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ \|*  
*hatvā śūlena deveṃdraṃ prahasannidamabravīt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On seeing him to have come there, Namuci became exceedingly angry. He struck Devendra with his spear and laughingly asked:

## \|\| 1.17.39 \|\|

*samudrasya taṭaḥ kasmātsevitaḥ surasattama \|*  
*vihāya raṇabhūmiṃ ca tyaktaśastro'bhavadbhavān \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. “Why have you resorted to the shore of the ocean? You have left the battlefield. You have even abandoned your weapon.

## \|\| 1.17.40 \|\|

*tvadīyenaiva vajreṇa kiṃ kṛtaṃ mama durmate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O evil-minded one, what (harm) has been done to me even by your own Vajra?

## \|\| 1.17.41-42 \|\|

*tathānyāni ca śastrāṇi astrāṇi subahūni ca \|*  
*gṛhītāni purā maṃda haṃtuṃ māmeva cādhunā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kiṃ kariṣyasi māṃ haṃtuṃ yuddhāya samupasthitaḥ \|*  
*kena śastreṇa re maṃda yoddhumicchasi saṃyuge \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Similarly many other missiles and weapons had been taken up by you previously to kill me, O dull-witted one. Now what will you do to kill me? You have come here to fight, but, O fool, with what weapon do you wish to fight in this battle?

## \|\| 1.17.43 \|\|

*tvāṃ gātayāmi cādyaiva yadi tiṣṭhasi saṃyuge \|*  
*no cedgaccha mayā muktaściraṃ jīva sukhī bhava \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. I will kill you today itself, if you stand here in the battle. If not, go, being set free by me. “Live long and be happy.”

## \|\| 1.17.44 \|\|

*evaṃ sa garvitaṃ tasya vākyamāhavaśobhinaḥ \|*  
*śrutvā maheṃdro'pi ruṣā jagṛhe phenamadbhutam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On hearing these arrogant words of that (Daitya) who shone in the battle, Mahendra too became furious. He took up the mysteriously wonderful foam.

## \|\| 1.17.45 \|\|

*phenaṃ karasthaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu asurā jahasustadā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On seeing the foam in his hand, Asuras laughed.

## \|\| 1.17.46 \|\|

*kṣayaṃ gatāni cāstrāṇi penenaiva puraṃdaraḥ \|*  
*haṃtumicchati māmadya śatakraturudāradhīḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Namuci said (to himself), ‘He has exhausted his weapons. Therefore, Purandara wishes to kill me today by means of this foam alone. Indeed Śatakratu (Indra) is liberal-minded.’

## \|\| 1.17.47-48 \|\|

*evaṃ prahasya namucirajñāya puraṃdaram \|*  
*sāvajñaṃ puratastasthau namucirdaityapuṃgavaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tadaiva taṃ sa phenena śīghramiṃdro jaghāna ha \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. He thus slighted Purandara laughingly. Namuci, the great Daitya, stood in front of him displaying his contemptuous disregard. At that very moment Indra killed him quickly with the foam.

## \|\| 1.17.49 \|\|

*hate tu namucau devāḥ sarve caiva mudānvitāḥ \|*  
*sādhusādhviti śabdena ṛṣayaścābhyapūjayan \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. When Namuci was killed, all the Devas became delighted. The sages honoured (Indra) with the words “Well done, well done.”

## \|\| 1.17.50 \|\|

*tadā sarve jayaṃ prāptā hatvā namucimāhave \|*  
*daityāste kopasaṃrabdhā yoddhukāmā mudānvitāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. After the killing of Namuci in the battle, all Devas became victorious. Daityas were excited with anger. They were furiously desirous of fighting (with Devas).

## \|\| 1.17.51 \|\|

*punaḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha \|*  
*śastrāstrairbahudhā muktaiḥ parasparavadhaiṣibiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The battle was resumed. Devas fought with Dānavas equipped with many kinds of weapons and missiles. Both were desirous of killing one another.

## \|\| 1.17.52 \|\|

*yadā te hyasurā devaiḥ pātitāśca punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*tadā vṛtro mahātejāḥ śatakratumupāvrajat \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. When those Asuras were being struck down again and again, Vṛtra, of great refulgence, approached Śatakratu (Indra).

## \|\| 1.17.53 \|\|

*vṛtraṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā sarve sasurāsuramānavāḥ \|*  
*bhayena mahatāviṣṭāḥ patitā bhuvi śerate \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. On seeing Vṛtra, all of them including Suras, Asuras and human beings were overcome by great fear. They fell on the ground and lay there.

## \|\| 1.17.54 \|\|

*evaṃ bhīteṣu sarveṣu surasiddheṣu vai tadā \|*  
*iṃdraścairāvaṇārūḍho vajrapāṇiḥ pratāpavān \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. When all the Suras and Siddhas became frightened, the valorous Indra (came there) riding on Airāvaṇa (i.e. Airāvata) (armed) with the thunderbolt in his hand.

## \|\| 1.17.55 \|\|

*chatreṇa dhriyamāṇena cāmareṇa virājitaḥ \|*  
*tadā sarvaiḥ sameto hi lokapālaiḥ pratāpitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He shone by an umbrella that was held (over him) and the chowries (by his side) too. He was accompanied by all the Guardians of the Quarters. He was endowed with great power of exploit.

## \|\| 1.17.56 \|\|

*vṛtraṃ vilokya te sarve lokapālā maheśvarāḥ \|*  
*bhayabhītāśca te sarve śivaṃ śaraṇamanvayuḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. On seeing Vṛtra, all the great Devas and the Guardians of the Quarters became terrified. All of them sought refuge in Śiva.

## \|\| 1.17.57 \|\|

*manasāciṃtayansarve śaṃkaraṃ lokaśaṃkaram \|*  
*liṃgaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivanmaheṃdro jayakāmukaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. All of them mentally contemplated Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds. Mahendra who was desirous of victory, duly worshipped the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.17.58 \|\|

*guruṇā viditaḥ sadyo viśvāsena pareṇa hi \|*  
*uvāca ca tadā śakraṃ bṛhaspatirudāradhīḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. This was understood immediately by Guru (Bṛhaspati). With great confidence, the highly intelligent Bṛhaspati said to Śakra:

## \|\| 1.17.59-60 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*kārtike śuklapakṣe tu maṃdavāre trayodaśī \|*  
*samagrā yadi labhyeta sarvaprāptayai na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ pradoṣasamaye liṃgarūpī sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*pūjanīyo hi deveṃdra sarvakāmārthasiddhaye \|\| 60 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:

59-60. The bright half of the lunar month of Kārttika (October-November), Saturday and Trayodaśī (thirteenth day)—when all these are concurrent, it is undoubtedly conducive to the accomplishment of everything. On that day, at the time of dusk, Sadāśiva should be worshipped in the form of Liṅga, O Devendra, for the accomplishment of all desired objectives.

## \|\| 1.17.61 \|\|

*snātvā madhyāhnasamaye tilāmalakasaṃyutam \|*  
*śivasya kuryādgaṃdhapuṣpaphalādibhiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The devotee should take his bath at midday and worship Śiva with sweet scents, fragrant flowers, fruits etc. together with gingelly seeds and emblic myrobalan.

## \|\| 1.17.62 \|\|

*paścātpradoṣavelāyāṃ sthāvaraṃ liṃgamarccayet \|*  
*svayaṃbhu sthāpitaṃ cāpi pauruṣeyamapauruṣam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Afterwards, at the time of dusk, he should worship an immobile Liṅga, whether it is self-existent or an installed one, whether it is man-made or of divine origin.

## \|\| 1.17.63 \|\|

*jane vā vijane vāpi araṇye vā tapovane \|*  
*talliṃgamarccayedbhaktyā pradoṣe tu viśeṣataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The devotee should worship that Liṅga with great devotion, whether in the midst of people or in a lonely place, in a forest or in a penance-grove. He should particularly worship at the time of dusk.

## \|\| 1.17.64 \|\|

*grāmadbahiḥ sthitaṃ liṃgaṃ grāmācchataguṇaṃ phalam \|*  
*brāhmacchataguṇaṃ puṇyamaraṇye liṃgamadbhutam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. If the Liṅga is stationed outside a village, it is a hundred times more efficacious than when it is in the village. The merit of the worship of the wonderful Liṅga in a forest is one hundred times more than when it is outside the village.

## \|\| 1.17.65 \|\|

*āraṇyācchataguṇaṃ puṇyamarcitaṃ pārvataṃ yathā \|*  
*pārvatāccaiva liṃgācca phalaṃ cāyutasaṃjñitam \|*  
*tapovanāśritaṃ liṃgaṃ pūjitaṃ vā mahāphalam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. If the Liṅga is worshipped on a mountain, it is a hundred times more efficacious than when it is worshipped in a forest. If the Liṅga installed in a penance-grove is worshipped, it yields a great benefit. It is ten thousand times more efficacious than the Liṅga stationed on a mountain.

## \|\| 1.17.66 \|\|

*tasmādetadvibhāgena śivapūjanārcanaṃ budhaiḥ \|*  
*kartvayaṃ nipuṇatvena tīrthasnānādikaṃ tathā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Hence the worship of Śivaliṅga should be performed efficiently by wise men on the basis of this difference. A holy dip in the sacred spot and other similar rites should also be diligently performed.

## \|\| 1.17.67 \|\|

*paṃcapiṃḍānsamuddhṛtya snānamātreṇa śobhanam \|*  
*kūpe snānaṃ prakurvīta uddhṛtena viseṣataḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. If the devotee offers five piṇḍas (rice balls) accompanied by holy dip alone, it is splendid. One should perform the holy ablution in a well especially with the water drawn.

## \|\| 1.17.68 \|\|

*taḍāge daśa piṃḍāṃśca uddhṛtya snānamācaret \|*  
*nadīsnānaṃ viśṣṭaṃ ca mahānadyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. One should perform the holy dip in a lake after offering ten piṇḍas. The holy dip in a river is especially superior and particularly so in a great river.

## \|\| 1.17.69 \|\|

*sarveṣāmapi tīrthānāṃ gaṃgāsnānaṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*devakhāte ca tattulyaṃ praśastaṃ snānamācaret \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The holy dip in Gaṅgā is superior to that in all the other holy spots and waters. If the holy dip is performed in a Devakhāta (natural pond or reservoir) it is equal in efficacy to a dip in Gaṅgā. The devotee should perform the rite of holy ablution in a praiseworthy manner.

## \|\| 1.17.70 \|\|

*pradīpānāṃ sahasreṇa dīpanīyaḥ sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*tathā dīpaśatenāpi dvātriṃśaddīpamālayā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Illumination should be offered to god Sadāśiva with a thousand lamps or a hundred lamps or a series of thirty-two lamps.

## \|\| 1.17.71-72 \|\|

*ghṛtena dīpayeddīpāñchivasya parituṣṭaye \|*  
*tathā phalaiśca dīpaiśca naivedyairgaṃdhadhūpakaiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirliṃgarūpī sadā śivaḥ \|*  
*pūjyaḥ pradoṣavelāyāṃ nṛbhiḥ sarvārthasiddhaye \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72- For the sake of Śiva’s gratification, the devotee should illuminate the lamps with ghee. For the attainment of all desired objects Sadāśiva should be worshipped at the time of dusk, in the form of a Liṅga, by men with fruits, lamps, food-offerings, sweet scents, incense and all the sixteen Upacāras (i.e. modes of rendering service during worship) for the fulfilment of all objects.

## \|\| 1.17.73 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇaṃ prakurvīta śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tathā \|*  
*namaskārānprakurvīta tāvatsaṃkhyānprayatnataḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The devotee should circumambulate (Śiva) one hundred and eight times. He should as well exert himself to perform as many prostrations (before Śiva).

## \|\| 1.17.74 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇanamaskāraiḥ pūjanīyaḥ sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*nāmnāṃ śatena rudro'sau stavanīyo yatāvidhi \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Sadāśiva should be honoured and worshipped by means of circumambulations and prostrations. Rudra should be eulogized by reciting his hundred names.

## \|\| 1.17.75 \|\|

*namo rudrāya bhīmāya nīlakaṇṭhāya vedhase \|*  
*kaparddhine sureśāya vyomakeśāya vai namaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. “Obeisance to Rudra, to Bhīma (the terrible one), to Nīlakaṇṭha (blue-throated god), to Vedhas (the creator), to Kapardin (one having matted hair), to Sureśa (the lord of Devas); obeisance indeed to Vyomakeśa (sky-haired);

## \|\| 1.17.76 \|\|

*vṛṣadhvajāya somāya nīlakaṇṭhāya vai namaḥ \|*  
*digaṃbarāya bhargāya umākāṃtakaparddine \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. to Vṛṣadhvaja (bull-bannered god), to Soma (one accompanied by Umā), to Nīlakaṇṭha, to Digaṃbara (one with the quarters for garments), to Bharga (refulgent one), to Umākānta (the husband of Umā), to Kapardīn;

## \|\| 1.17.77 \|\|

*tapomayāya vyāptāya śipiviṣṭāya vai namaḥ \|*  
*vyālapriyāya vyālāya vyālānāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. to Tapomaya (one who is of the nature of penance), to Vyāpta (one who is pervaded). Obeisance indeed to Śipiviṣṭa (one who is pervaded by rays), to Vyālapriya (one who is fond of serpents), to Vyāla (one who is identical with serpents); obeisance to the lord of serpents,

## \|\| 1.17.78 \|\|

*mahīdharāya vyāghrāya paśūnāṃ pataye namaḥ \|*  
*tripurāṃtakasiṃhāya śārdūlograravāya ca \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. to Mahīdhara (one who supports the earth), to Vyāghra (the tiger); obeisance to the lord of Paśus (individual souls), to Trīpurāntakasiṃha (leonine destroyer of Tripura), to Śārdūlograrava (one whose roaring sound is as dreadful as that of a tiger);

## \|\| 1.17.79 \|\|

*mīnāya mīnanāthāya siddhāya parameṣṭhine \|*  
*kāmāṃtakāya buddhāya buddhīnāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. to Mīna (fish), to Mīnanātha (to the lord of fishes), to Siddha, to Parameṣṭhin, to Kāmāntaka (the destroyer of Kāma), to Buddha (the enlightened one); obeisance to the lord of the intellect,

## \|\| 1.17.80 \|\|

*kapotāya viśiṣṭāya śiṣṭāya paramātmane \|*  
*vedāya vedabījāya devaguhyāya vai namaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. to Kapota (pigeon), to Viśīṣṭa (superior one), to Śiṣṭa (of good discipline), to Paramātman (the Supreme Soul),to Veda, to Vedābīja (seed of the Vedas); obeisance indeed to Devaguhya (secret known only to gods);

## \|\| 1.17.81 \|\|

*dīrghāya dīrghadīrghāya dīrghārghāya mahāya ca \|*  
*namo jagatpratiṣṭhāya vyomarūpāya vai namaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. to Dīrgha (long one), to Dīrghadīrgha (longer than the long one), to Dīrghārgha (one of long respectable offering), to Maha (festival); obeisance to Jagatpratiṣṭha (one who is established in the universe); obeisance indeed to Vyomarūpa (one in the form of the firmament);

## \|\| 1.17.82 \|\|

*gajāsuravināśāya hyaṃdhakāsurabhedine \|*  
*nīlalohitaśuklāya caṇḍamuṇḍapriyāya ca \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. to Gajāsuravināśa (one who has destroyed the demon in the form of an elephant), to Andhakāsurabhedin (one who has split the demon Andhaka), to Nīlalohitaśukla (one of blue, red and white colours), to Caṇḍa-Muṇḍapriya \[Caṇḍamuṇḍapriya\] (one who is fond of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa);

## \|\| 1.17.83 \|\|

*bhaktipriyāya devāya jñānajñānāvyayāya ca \|*  
*maheśāya namastubhyaṃ mahādevaharāya ca \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. to Bhaktipriya (one who is fond of devotion), to Deva (resplendent lord), to Jñānajñāna (knowledge of knowledges) to Avyaya (the immutable), to Maheśa (the great lord), O Mahādeva. Obeisance to you, to Hara (the destroyer);

## \|\| 1.17.84 \|\|

*trinetrāya trivedāya vedāṃgāya namonamaḥ \|*  
*arthāya artharūpāya paramārthāya vai namaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. to Trinetra (the three-eyed god), Triveda (one who is eulogized in the three Vedas); obeisance, obeisance to Vedāṅga (the embodiment of Vedas), to Artha (wealth), to Artharūpa (one who has the form of wealth); obeisance indeed to Paramārtha (the Ultimate Reality),

## \|\| 1.17.85 \|\|

*viśvarūpāya viśvāya viśvanātāya vai namaḥ \|*  
*śaṃkarāya ca kālāya kālāvayavarūpiṇe \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. to Viśvarūpa (one who has the cosmic form), to Viśva (the universe). Obeisance indeed to Viśvanātha (lord of the universe), to Śaṅkara (the benefactor), to Kāla (god of Death), to Kālāvayavarūpin (one who is in the form of the units of time);

## \|\| 1.17.86 \|\|

*arūpāya ca sūkṣmāya sūkṣmasūkṣmāya vai namaḥ \|*  
*śmaśānavāsine tubhyaṃ namaste kṛttivāsase \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. to Arūpa (formless), to Sūkṣma (the subtle one). Obeisance indeed to the subtler than the subtlest. Obeisance to you who reside in the cremation ground; obeisance to you, wearer of the elephant hide,

## \|\| 1.17.87 \|\|

*śaśāṃkaśekharāyaiva rudraviśvāśrayāya ca \|*  
*durgāya durgasārāya durgāvayavasākṣiṇe \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. to Śaśāṅka-śekhara \[Śaśāṅkaśekhara\] (one who has the moon as the crest-jewel), to Rudra, to Viśvāśraya (the support of the universe), to Durga (unattainable), to Durgasāra (the essence of the unattainables), to Durgāvayavasākṣin (one who is witness unto the limbs of Durgā);

## \|\| 1.17.88 \|\|

*liṃgarūpāya liṃgāya liṃgānāṃ pataye namaḥ \|*  
*praṇavarūpāya praṇavārthāya vai namaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. to Liṅgarūpa (one who is in the form of the Liṅga), to Liṅga; obeisance to the lord of Liṅgas; obeisance to Oṃkāra; obeisance indeed to Praṇavārtha (the meaning of Praṇava).

## \|\| 1.17.89 \|\|

*namonamaḥ kāraṇakāraṇāya te mṛtyuṃjayāyātmabhavasvarūpiṇe \|*  
*triyaṃbakāyāsitakaṃṭha bharga gauripate sakalamaṃgalahetave namaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Obeisance, obeisance to you, the cause of the causes, to Mṛtyuñjaya (the conqueror of Death), to Ātmasvarūpin (one who is in the form of the Soul), to Bhavasvarūpīn \[Bhavasvarūpin?\] (one who is of the form of the world), to Triyaṃba (one who has three eyes), O Asitakaṇṭha (dark-throated), O Bharga (refulgent one).

O Gaurīpati (Consort of Gaurī), obeisance to Sakalamaṅgalahetu (the cause of all auspiciousness).”

## \|\| 1.17.90 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*nāmnāṃ śataṃ maheśasya uccāryaṃ vratinā tadā \|*  
*pradakṣiṇanamaskārairetatsaṃkhyaiḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*kāryaṃ pradoṣasamaye tuṣṭyarthaṃ saṃkarasya ca \|\| 90 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:

90\. The hundred names of Maheśa should be repeated always by a Vratin (‘observer of holy vows’) along with circumambulations and prostrations of that number with great effort. This should be done at the time of dusk for the sake of gratifying Śaṅkara,

## \|\| 1.17.91 \|\|

*evaṃ vrataṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ tava śakra mahāmate \|*  
*śīghraṃ kuru mahābhāga paścādyuddhaṃ kuru prabho \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Such is the holy observance fully explained to you, O Śakra, of great intellect. Perform this quickly. O lord of exalted fortune, fight only afterwards, O Lord.

## \|\| 1.17.92 \|\|

*śaṃbhoḥ prasādātsarvaṃ te bhaviṣyati jayādikam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. By the grace of Śaṃbhu, victory etc. will come to you.

## \|\| 1.17.93 \|\|

*vṛtro hyayaṃ mahātejā daiteyastapasā purā \|*  
*śivaṃ prasādayāmāsa parvate gaṃdhamādane \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. This highly refulgent Daitya has formerly propitiated god Śiva by (performing) penance on mountain Gandhamādana.

## \|\| 1.17.94 \|\|

*nāmnā citraratho rājā vanaṃ citrarathasya tat \|*  
*etajjānīhi bho indra śivapuryāḥ samīpataḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. There was a king named Citraratha. Know, O Indra, that his park was near the city of Śiva. His park was named Caitraratha.

## \|\| 1.17.95 \|\|

*yasminvane mahābhāga na saṃti ca ṣaḍūrmayaḥ \|*  
*tasmāccaitrarathaṃ nāma vanaṃ paramamaṃgalam \|*  
*tasya rājñaḥ śivenaiva dattaṃ yānaṃ mahādbhutam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. O Indra of exalted fortune, the six infirmities of human beings (viz. grief, delusion, old age, death, hunger and thirst) do not find a place in that park. Hence that park named Caitraratha was exceedingly auspicious.

## \|\| 1.17.96 \|\|

*kāmagaṃ kiṃkiṇīyuktaṃ siddhacāraṇasevitam \|*  
*gaṃdharvairapsaroyakṣaiḥ kiṃnarairupaśobhitam \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. A wonderful vehicle had been given to that king by Śiva himself. The vehicle could go wherever one desired to go. It was fitted with small ornamental tinkling bells and was attended upon by Siddhas and Cāraṇas. It was rendered resplendent by Gandharvas, Apsarās, Yakṣas and Kinnaras.

## \|\| 1.17.97 \|\|

*tatastenaiva yānena pṛthivīṃ paryaṭanpurā \|*  
*tathā girīśamukhyāṃśca dvīpāṃśca vividhāṃstathā \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Once he was wandering round the earth, big mountains, different kinds of islands etc.

## \|\| 1.17.98-99 \|\|

*ekadā paryaṭanrājā nāmnā citraratho mahān \|*  
*kailāsamāgatastatra sa dadarśa parādbhutam \|\| 98 \|\|*

*sabhātalaṃ maheśasya gaṇaiścaiva virājitam \|*  
*arddhāgalagnayā devyā śobhitaṃ ca maheśvaram \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. Once in the course of his wanderings, the great king named Citraratha came to Kailāsa. There he saw an exceedingly wonderful assembly hall of Maheśa, that shone on account of the Gaṇas. He saw Maheśvara also who looked splendid with the goddess adhering to half of his body.

## \|\| 1.17.100-101 \|\|

*nirīkṣya devyā sahitaṃ sadāśivaṃ devyānvitaṃ vākyamidaṃ babhāṣe \|\| 100 \|\|*

*vayaṃ ca śaṃbho viṣayānvitāśca maṃtryādayaḥ strījitāścāpi cānye \|*  
*na lokamadhye vayameva cājñāḥ strīsevanaṃ lajjayā naiva kurmaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

100-101. When he saw Sadāśiva accompanied by the goddess (as well as closely joined to the goddess), he spoke these words: “We, the ministers etc. and others, O Śaṃbhu, cling to worldly pleasures. Others there are who are enslaved by (and enamoured of) women. We are indeed ignorant too, but out of shyness we do not enjoy the company of women in the midst of people.”

## \|\| 1.17.102-104 \|\|

*etadvākyaṃ niśamyātha maheśaḥ prahasanniva \|*  
*uvāca nyāyasaṃyuktaṃ sarveṣāmapi śrṛṇvatām \|\| 102 \|\|*

*bhayaṃ lokāpavādācca sarveṣāmapi nānyathā \|*  
*grāsitaṃ kālakūṭaṃ ca sarveṣāmapi durjaram \|\| 103 \|\|*

*tathāpi upahāso me kṛto rājñā hi durjaraḥ \|*  
*taṃ citrarathamāhūya girijā vākyamabravīt \|\| 104 \|\|*

102-104. On hearing these words, Maheśa laughingly said in a just and proper manner, even as all were listening: “All are afraid of popular censure and not otherwise. The poison Kālakūṭa which could not be digested by anyone was swallowed (by me). Still a mocking criticism about me was made by this king. This is difficult to be digested by me.”

Girijā called Citraratha and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.17.105 \|\|

*gīrijovāca \|*  
*re durātmankathaṃ tvajña śaṃkaraścopahāsitaḥ \|*  
*mayā sahaiva maṃdātmandrakṣyase karmaṇaḥ phalam \|\| 105 \|\|*

Girijā said:

105\. O evil-minded one, O ignorant fellow, why was Śaṅkara mocked at and ridiculed along with me? O dull-witted one, you will see the consequences of your action.

## \|\| 1.17.106 \|\|

*sādhūnāṃ samacittānāmupahāsaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*devo vāpyatha vā martyaḥ sa vijñeyo'dhamādhamaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. He who mocks and ridicules equanimous and even-minded good people, whether he is a Deva or a human being, should be known as the meanest of all mean people.

## \|\| 1.17.107 \|\|

*ete munīṃdrāśca mahānubhāvāstathā hyamī ṛṣayo vedagarbhāḥ \|*  
*tathaiva sarve sanakādayo hyamī ajñāśca sarve śivamarcayaṃte \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. These leading sages of great magnanimity, those anchorites steeped in the Vedas and these (philosophers) Sanaka and others, worship Śiva. Are they ignorant ones?

## \|\| 1.17.108 \|\|

*re mūḍha sarveṣu janeṣvabhijñastvameva evādya na cāpare janāḥ \|*  
*tasmādabhijñaṃ hi karomi daityaṃ devairdvijaiścāpi bahiṣkṛtaṃ tvām \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. O confounded one, among all the people (you suppose that) you alone are Abhijña (one with rich experience and profound knowledge) and not other people. Therefore, I shall make you a wiseacre Daitya excluded (excommunicated) by Devas and Brāhmaṇas.

Bṛhaspati continued:

## \|\| 1.17.109 \|\|

*evaṃ śaptastayā devyā bhavānyā rājasattamaḥ \|*  
*rājā citrarathaḥ sadyaḥ papāta sahasā divaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. On being cursed thus by goddess Bhavānī, the excellent king Citraratha, immediately fell from heaven.

## \|\| 1.17.110 \|\|

*āsurīṃ yonimāsādya vṛtronāmnā'bhavattadā \|*  
*tapasā parameṇaiva tvaṣṭrā saṃyojitaḥ kramāt \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. He took birth in the race of Asuras and came to be known by the name Vṛtra. He was gradually made to perform penance by Tvaṣṭṛ.

## \|\| 1.17.111-112 \|\|

*tapasā tena mahatā ajeyo vṛtra ucyata \|*  
*tasmācchaṃbhuṃ samabhyarcya pradoṣe vidhinā'dhunā \|\| 111 \|\|*

*jahi vṛtraṃ mahādaityaṃ devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|*  
*gurostadvacanaṃ śrutvā uvācātha śatakratuḥ \|*  
*sodyāpanavidhiṃ brūhi pradoṣasya ca me'dhunā \|\| 112 \|\|*

111-112. It is said that Vṛtra became invincible on account of that great penance. Hence worship god Śaṃbhu now during the time of dusk in accordance with the prescribed method. Then kill Vṛtra, the great Daitya, for accomplishing the cause of Devas.

## \|\| 1.17.113 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*kārtike māsi saṃprāpte maṃdavāre trayodaśī \|*  
*saṃpūrtistu bhavettatra saṃpūrṇavratasiddhaye \|\| 113 \|\|*

On hearing these words of his preceptor, Indra said: “Tell me the mode of the performance of the worship of (Śiva) during Pradoṣa (dusk time) along with its Udyāpanavidhi (the concluding rites).”

Bṛhaspati said:

113\. In the month of Kārttika when Saturday and Trayodaśī (13th day) coincide, all the requirements are complete for the sake of getting the benefit of the entire holy rite.

(Procedure of worshipping god Śiva)

## \|\| 1.17.114-115 \|\|

*vṛṣabho rājataḥ kāryaḥ pṛṣṭhe tasya supīṭhakam \|*  
*tasyoparinyaseddevamumākāṃtaṃ trilocanam \|\| 114 \|\|*

*paṃcavaktraṃ daśabhujamarddhāṃge girijāṃ satīm \|*  
*evaṃ comāmaheśaṃ ca sauvarṇaṃ kārayedbudhaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

114-115. A silver bull should be made. There must be a good Pīṭha (seat) upon its back. The devotee must keep the Three-eyed Lord, the consort of Umā, upon it. The lord must have five faces and ten hands. Half of Ms body must be the chaste daughter of the Mountain. Thus both Umā and Maheśa should be made of gold by the learned devotee.

## \|\| 1.17.116 \|\|

*savṛṣaṃ tāmrapatre ca vastreṇa pariguṃṭhite \|*  
*sthāpayitvomayā sārddhaṃ nānābogasamanvitam \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. All these (the bull etc.) must be placed in a copper plate and covered with a cloth. The Liṅga must be placed along with Umā with all the necessary offerings of enjoyment (food offerings, scents, incense etc.).

## \|\| 1.17.117 \|\|

*vidhinā jāgaraṃ kuryādrātrau śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*paṃcāmṛtena snapanaṃ kāryamādau prayatnataḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. During the night the devotee should keep a vigil in accordance with the injunctions and with great faith.

At the outset the bathing rite should be performed with Pañcāmṛta (five sweet ingredients in fluid form). (Then the following Mantras should be recited in offering each.)

(The Mantra at the time of bathing the god with cow’s milk:)

## \|\| 1.17.118 \|\|

*gokṣīrasnānaṃ deveśa gokṣīreṇa mayā kṛtam \|*  
*snapanaṃ devadeveśa gṛhāṇa parameśvara \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. “O lord of Devas, O lord of the chiefs of Devas, bathing is offered by me with cow’s milk. Accept it, O Parameśvara (great Lord).”

(The Mantra while bathing the god with curds:)

## \|\| 1.17.119 \|\|

*dadhnā caiva mayā deva snapanaṃ kriyate'dhunā \|*  
*gṛhāma ca mayā dattaṃ suprasanno bhavādya vai \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. “O Lord, bathing is performed by me now with curds. Accept what has been offered by me. Be highly delighted now.”

(The Mantra at the time of bathing with ghee:)

## \|\| 1.17.120 \|\|

*sarpiṣā ca mayā deva snapanaṃ kriyate'dhunā \|*  
*gṛhāṇa śraddhayā dattaṃ tava prītyarthameva ca \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. “O Lord, bathing is performed by me now with ghee. Accept what has been offered with faith for the sake of gratifying you.”

(The Mantra for bath with honey:)

## \|\| 1.17.121 \|\|

*idaṃ madhu mayā dattaṃ tava prītyarthameva ca \|*  
*gṛhāma tvaṃ hi deveśa mama śāṃtiprado bhava \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. “This honey is given by me for the sake of your pleasure. Accept it, O Lord of Devas. Be the bestower of tranquillity on me.”

(The Mantra while offering bath with sugar:)

## \|\| 1.17.122 \|\|

*sitayā devadeveśa snapanaṃ kriyate'dhunā \|*  
*gṛhāṇa śraddhayā dattāṃ suprasanno bhava prabho \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. “O lord, bathing is performed by me now, O lord of the chiefs of Devas, with sugar. Accept this which has been offered with faith. O Lord, be delighted.”

## \|\| 1.17.123 \|\|

*evaṃ paṃcāmṛtenaiva snapanīyo vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|*  
*paścādarghyaṃ pradātavyaṃ tāmrapātreṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*anenaiva ca maṃtreṇa umākāṃtasya tṛṣṭaye \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Thus the Bull-bannered Lord must be bathed in Pañcāmṛta. Afterwards Arghya (materials of worship) must be offered by the intelligent devotee in a copper vessel with this following Mantra for the gratification of the consort of Umā:

(Mantra for offering of Arghya:)

## \|\| 1.17.124 \|\|

*arghyo'si tvamumākāṃta argheṇānena vai prabho \|*  
*gṛhāṇa tvaṃ mayā dattaṃ prasanno bhava śaṃkara \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. “You are the most befitting person for being worshipped by this Arghya, O consort of Umā. Accept this, O Lord, offered by me. Be pleased, O Śaṅkara.”

(Mantra for offering Pādya:)

## \|\| 1.17.125 \|\|

*mayā dattaṃ ca te pādyaṃ puṣpagaṃdhasamanvitam \|*  
*gṛhāṇa devadeveśa prasanno varado bhava \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. “Accept, O Lord of the chiefs of Devas, the Pādya (water for washing the feet) offered by me to you along with fragrant flowers and sweet scents. Be pleased. Be the bestower of boons.”

(Mantra for offering a seat:)

## \|\| 1.17.126 \|\|

*viṣṭaraṃ viṣṭareṇaiva mayā dattaṃ ca vai prabho \|*  
*śāṃtyarathaṃ tava deveśa varado bhava me sadā \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. “A seat along with another seat has been offered by me, O Lord, for the sake of your peace and calmness. O Lord of Devas, always be the bestower of boons on me.”

(Mantra at the time of offering Ācamanīya:)

## \|\| 1.17.127 \|\|

*ācamanīyaṃ mayā dattaṃ tava viśveśvara prabho \|*  
*gṛhāṇa parameśāna tuṣṭo bhava mamādya vai \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. “Ācamanīya (i.e. water for the ceremonial sipping) has been given to you. O Lord Viśveśvara, accept; O great Īśāna, be delighted with me today, O Lord.”

(Mantra while offering the sacred thread:)

## \|\| 1.17.128 \|\|

*brahmagranthisamāyuktaṃ brahmakarmapravartakam \|*  
*yajñopavītaṃ sauvarṇaṃ mayā dattaṃ tava prabho \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. “A golden sacred thread which consists of Brahmagranthi (knot) and which causes all holy rites to function is offered by me to you, O Lord.”

(Mantra while offering sandal paste:)

## \|\| 1.17.129 \|\|

*sugaṃdhaṃ caṃdanaṃ deva mayā dattaṃ ca vai prabho \|*  
*bhaktyā para mayā śaṃbho sugaṃdhaṃ kuru māṃ bhava \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. “Sweet scents and sandal paste have been offered by me, O Lord, with great devotion. O Śaṃbhu, Bhava, make me fragrant.”

(Mantra while offering a lamp:)

## \|\| 1.17.130 \|\|

*dīpaṃ hi paramaṃ śaṃbho ghṛtaprajvalitaṃ mayā \|*  
*dattaṃ gṛhāṇa deveśa mama jñānaprado bhava \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. “O Śaṃbhu, an excellent lamp kindled with ghee has. been offered by me. Accept it, O Lord of Devas. Be the bestower of knowledge on me.”

(Mantra while offering incense:)

## \|\| 1.17.131 \|\|

*dīpaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ paramaṃ sarvauṣadhivijṛṃbhitam \|*  
*gṛhāṇa parameśāna mama śāṃtyarthameva ca \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. “Excellently superior lamp invigorated with all medicinal herbs (has been offered by me). Accept it, O great Īśāna, for the sake of my peace and calmness.”

(Mantra before Āratī—Waving of lamps:)

## \|\| 1.17.132 \|\|

*dīpāvaliṃ mayā dattāṃ kṛhāṇa parameśvara \|*  
*ārārtikapradānena mama tejaḥ prado bhava \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. “O Parameśvara, accept the row of lamps offered by me. By virtue of my offering of waving of lights, be the bestower of splendour on me.”

## \|\| 1.17.133 \|\|

*phaladīpādinaivedyatāṃbūlādikrameṇa ca \|*  
*pūjanīyo vidhānajñaistasyāṃ rātrau prayatnataḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. By persons who are conversant with injunctions (regarding worship) the Lord should be (carefully and) deligently worshipped on that night (by offerings) in the following order: fruits, lights etc. food-offering, betel-leaf etc.

## \|\| 1.17.134 \|\|

*paścājjāgaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ gṛhe vā devatālaye \|*  
*vitānamaṃḍapaṃ kṛtvā nānāścaryasamanvitam \|*  
*gītavāditranṛtyena arcanīyaḥ sadāśivaḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. The devotee must keep awake thereafter whether in a house or in a temple. The canopy over the dais must be put up with various, wonderful decorations. God Sadāśiva should be worshipped by means of songs, musical instruments and dance.

## \|\| 1.17.135 \|\|

*anenaiva vidhānena pradoṣodyāpane vidhiḥ \|*  
*kārye vidhimatā śakra sarvakāryārthasiddhaye \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. It is in accordance with these injunctions that the concluding rites in the worship at Pradoṣa should be performed duly for the sake of the fulfilment of all objects.

## \|\| 1.17.136 \|\|

*guruṇā kathitaṃ sarvaṃ taccakāra śatakratuḥ \|*  
*tenaiva ca sahāyena iṃdro yuddhaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. Śatakratu (Indra) performed everything mentioned by Guru (Bṛhaspati). With him as his main help, Indra engaged himself in the battle.

## \|\| 1.17.137 \|\|

*vṛtraṃ prati suraiḥ sārddhaṃ yuyudhe ca śatakratuḥ \|*  
*tumulaṃ yuddhamabhavaddevānāṃ dānāvaiḥ saha \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. Śatakratu fought against Vṛtra along with Suras. The fight between Devas and Dānavas was fierce.

## \|\| 1.17.138 \|\|

*tasminsutumule gāḍhe devadaityakṣayāvahe \|*  
*dvaṃdvayuddhaṃ sutumulamativelaṃ bhayāvaham \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. In that exceedingly fierce battle that caused destruction among Devas and Daityas, the duels were extremely terrifying and tumultuous:

## \|\| 1.17.139-142 \|\|

*vyomo yamena yuyudhe hyagninā tīkṣṇakopanaḥ \|*  
*varuṇena mahādaṃṣṭro vāyunā ca mahābalaḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

*dvandvayuddha ratāḥ sarve anyonyabalakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

*tathaiva te devavarā mahābhujāḥ saṃgrāmaśūrā jayinastadā'bhavan \|*  
*parājayaṃ daityavārāśca sarve prāptāstadānīṃ paramaṃ samaṃtāt \|\| 141 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā surairdaityavarānparājitānpalāyamānānatha kāndiśīkān \|*  
*tadaiva vṛtraḥ parameṇa manyunā mahābalo vākya midaṃ babhāṣe \|\| 142 \|\|*

139-142. Vyoma fought with Yama. Tīkṣṇakopana fought with Agni, Mahādaṃṣṭra fought with Varuṇa and Mahābala fougḥt with Vāyu. All those engaged in duels were desirous of (suppressing) the strength of one another. The excellent Devas of powerful arms were heroic in battle. They became victorious then. All the leading Daityas met with very great defeat on all fronts. On seeing the leading Daityas defeated by Suras, running away as fugitives, Vṛtra of great strength spoke these words with extreme wrathfulness:

## \|\| 1.17.143 \|\|

*vṛtra uvāca \|*  
*he daityāḥ paramārtāśca kasmādyūyaṃ bhayāturāḥ \|*  
*palāyanaparāḥ sarve visṛjya raṇamadbhutam \|\| 143 \|\|*

Vṛtra said:

143\. O Daityas, why are you greatly distressed? Why are you so frightened? All of you are running away abandoning the war of wonderful (events).

## \|\| 1.17.144-145 \|\|

*svaṃsvaṃ parākramaṃ vīrā yuddhāya kṛtaniścayāḥ \|*  
*darśayadhvaṃ suragaṇāssūdayadhvaṃ mahābalāḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

*gadābhiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ śaktitomaramudgaraiḥ \|*  
*asibhirbhi dipālaiśca pāśatomaramuṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 145 \|\|*

144-145. O heroes, resolve to fight. Display your respective valour. O mighty ones, kill the groups of Suras with maces, spears with sharp edges, swords, javelins, iron clubs, mallets, swords with thin edges, small javelins hurled at the enemies, nooses, maces and even your fists.

## \|\| 1.17.146 \|\|

*tadā devāśca yuyudhurdadhīcāsthisamudbhavaiḥ \|*  
*śastrairastraiśca paramairasurānsamadārayan \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. Then Devas fought Asuras with great weapons and missiles made out of Dadhīci’s bones. They tore up Asuras.

## \|\| 1.17.147 \|\|

*punardaityā hatā devaiḥ prāptāstepi parājayam \|*  
*punaśca tena vṛtreṇa nodyamānāḥ surānprati \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. This was repeated often. Again and again Daityas were killed by Devas. They met with defeat. Again and again, they were urged by Vṛtra to fight Suras.

## \|\| 1.17.148 \|\|

*yadā hi te daityavarāḥ sureśairnihanyamānāśca vidudruvurdiśaḥ \|*  
*keciddṛṣṭvā dānavāste tadānīṃ bhītitrastāḥ klībarūpāḥ krameṇā \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. The excellent Daityas were being killed by the leading Suras. They fled in all directions. Some of the Dānavas were frightened so much that they appeared to be eunuchs.

## \|\| 1.17.149-153 \|\|

*vṛtreṇa kopinā caivaṃ dhikkṛtā daityapuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*he pulomanmahābhāga vṛṣaparvannamostu te \|\| 149 \|\|*

*he dhūmrākṣa mahākāla mahādaitya vṛkāsura \|*  
*sthūlākṣa he mahādaitya sthūladaṃṣṭra namostu te \|\| 150 \|\|*

*svargadvāraṃ vihāyaiva kṣatriyāṇāṃ manasvinām \|*  
*palāyadhve kimarthaṃ vā saṃgrāmāṅgaṇamuttamam \|\| 151 \|\|*

*saṃgare maraṇaṃ yeṣāṃ te yāṃti paramaṃ padam \|*  
*yatra tatra ca lipseta saṃgrāme maraṇaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

*tyajanti saṃgaraṃ ye vai te yāṃti nirayaṃ dhruvam \|\| 153 \|\|*

149-153. The leading Daityas were rebuked and censured by furious Vṛtra: “O Puloman of great fortune; O Vṛṣaparvan, obeisance to you. O Dhūmrākṣa, O Mahākāla, O Vṛkāsura, the great Daitya, O Sthūlākṣa, the eminent Daitya, O Sthūladaṃṣṭra, obeisance to you. The excellent battlefield is the gateway to heaven for Kṣatriyas of great magnanimity. Why do you abandon it and run away? Those who meet death in the battlefield attain the greatest position. A learned man must desire to die in battle. Those who forsake the battle(field) certainly go to hell.

## \|\| 1.17.154-155 \|\|

*ye brāhmaṇārthe bhṛtyārthe svārthe vai śastrapāṇayaḥ \|*  
*saṃgrāmaṃ ye prakurvaṃti mahāpātakino narāḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

*śastraghātahatā ye vai mṛtā vā saṃgare tathā \|*  
*te yāṃti paramaṃ sthānaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 155 \|\|*

154-155. If men who have committed great sins fight in a battlefield with weapons in their hands for the sake of Brāhmaṇas, their servants or for their own sake and get killed being hit with weapons in the battle, they go to the highest region. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.17.156 \|\|

*śastrairvicchinnadehā ye gavārthe svāmikāraṇāt \|*  
*raṇe mṛtāḥ kṣatā ye vai te yāṃti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. Those whose bodies are cut off by means of weapons for taking up the cause of cows or their own masters, those who die or those who are wounded in war do attain the greatest goal (heaven).

## \|\| 1.17.157 \|\|

*tasmādraṇe'pi ye śūrāḥ pāpino nihatāḥ puraḥ \|*  
*prāpnuvaṃti paraṃ sthānaṃ durlabhaṃ jñānināmapi \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. If persons of great heroism are killed in battle, they attain the greatest region even if they be sinners. They attain the region not easy of access even to the learned men.

## \|\| 1.17.158-159 \|\|

*athavā tīrthagamanaṃ vedādhyayanameva ca \|*  
*devatārcanayajñādiśreyāṃsi vividhāni ca \|\| 158 \|\|*

*aikapadyena tānyeva kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|*  
*saṃgrāme patitānāṃ ca sarvaśāstreṣvayaṃ vidhiḥ \|\| 159 \|\|*

158-159. Pilgrimage to holy places, study of the Vedas, worshipping of the deities, performances of Yajñas and other different kinds of holy rites conducive to welfare—all put together do not deserve even a sixteenth part of the holy action of those who fall in battle. This has been laid down in all the saered treatises.

## \|\| 1.17.160 \|\|

*tasmādyuddhāvadānaṃ ca kartavyamaviśaṃkitaiḥ \|*  
*bhavadbhirnānyathā kāryaṃ devavākyapramāṇataḥ \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. Hence the valorous and glorious act of fighting should be carried out by you without suspicion or fear. It should not be otherwise, because the Vedic statements are authoritative.

## \|\| 1.17.161 \|\|

*yūyaṃ sarve śauravṛttyā sametāḥ kulena śīlena mahānubhāvāḥ \|*  
*padāni tānyeva palāyamānā gacchaṃtyaśūrā raṇamaṃḍalācca \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. All of you belong to the profession of heroes. You are magnanimous and dignified due to nobility of birth and course of conduct, but if you run away from the war-zone like cowards, you are sure to go to those worlds of cowards like them.

## \|\| 1.17.162 \|\|

*ta eva sarve khalu pāpalokāngacchaṃti nūnaṃ vacanātsmṛteśca \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. According to Smṛtis, all of them (cowards) certainly go to the world of sinners (i.e. hell).

## \|\| 1.17.163 \|\|

*ye pāpiṣṭhāstvadharmmasthā brahmaghnā gurutalpagāḥ \|*  
*narakaṃ yāṃti te pāpaṃ tathaiva raṇavicyutāḥ \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. Those worst sinners who adhere to unrighteous things, the slayers of Brāhmaṇas and the defilers of the preceptors’ bed go to hell. In the same manner those who stray away (desert) from war, incur the same sin and go to hell.

## \|\| 1.17.164-165 \|\|

*tasmādbhavadbhiryoddhavyaṃ svāmikāryabharakṣamaiḥ \|*  
*evamuktāstadā tena vṛtreṇāpi mahātmanā \|\| 164 \|\|*

*cakruste vacaṃnaṃ tasya asurāśca surānprati \|*  
*cakruḥ sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ sarvalokabhayaṃkaram \|\| 165 \|\|*

164-165. Hence you people who are capable of bearing the burden of the work of your master must fight.”

On being told thus by the noble-souled Vṛtra, the Asuras carried out his words. They fought a furious battle with Suras terrifying all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.17.166 \|\|

*tasminpravṛtte tumule vigāḍhe vṛtro mahādaityapatiḥ sa ekaḥ \|*  
*uvāca roṣeṇa mahādbhutena śatakratuṃ devavaraiḥ sametam \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. When that tremendous and tumultuous battle ensued, Vṛtra, the sole lord of the great Daityas, who was overwhelmed by extraordinary wrath, said to Indra accompanied by the excellent Devas:

## \|\| 1.17.167 \|\|

*vṛtra uvāca \|*  
*śrṛṇu vākyaṃ mayā coktaṃ dharmmārthasahitaṃ hitam \|*  
*tvaṃ devānāṃ patirbhūtvā na jānāsi hitāhitam \|\| 167 \|\|*

Vṛtra said:

167\. Listen to the words uttered by me. It is conducive to your welfare. It is connected with virtuous objects. Although you are the lord of Devas, you do not know what is good and what is not.

## \|\| 1.17.168 \|\|

*kiṃbalārthaparo bhūtvā viśvarūpo hatastvayā \|*  
*prāptamadyaiva bho iṃdra tasyedaṃ karmmaṇaḥ phalam \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. What were your objectives for which Viśvarūpa was killed by you?

## \|\| 1.17.169 \|\|

*ye dīrghadarśino maṃdā mūḍhā dharmabahiṣkṛtāḥ \|*  
*akalpāḥ kāryasiddhyarthaṃ yatkurvaṃti ca niṣphalam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ viddhi deveṃdra manasā saṃpradhāryatām \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. Whatever these persons do for the accomplishment of their tasks is futile: Those who do not see far into the future, those who are foolish and confounded, those who are excluded from piety and virtue and those who are incompetent. Know all these, O Devendra. Let it be pondered over mentally.

## \|\| 1.17.170 \|\|

*tasmāddharmmaparo bhūtvā yudhyasva gatakalmaṣaḥ \|*  
*bhrātṛhā tvaṃ mamaiveṃdra tasmāttvā ghātayāmyaham \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. Hence be virtuous and free from the taint of sin. Then fight with me. You are the slayer of my brother, O Indra. Hence I will kill you.

## \|\| 1.17.171 \|\|

*mā prayāhi sthiro bhūtvā devaiśca parivāritaḥ \|*  
*eva muktastu vṛtreṇa śakro'tīva ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*airāvataṃ samāruhya yayau vṛtrajighāṃsayā \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. Be steady. Do not run away surrounded by Devas.

On being told thus by Vṛtra, Śakra became exceedingly furious. He mounted on the elephant Airāvata and went ahead with a desire to kill Vṛtra.

## \|\| 1.17.172 \|\|

*iṃdramāyāṃtamālokya vṛtro balavatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*uvāca prahasanvākyaṃ sarveṣāṃ śrṛṇvatāmapi \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. On seeing Indra coming, Vṛtra, the most excellent one among the powerful persons, said laughingly even as all the others were listening (to it):

## \|\| 1.17.173 \|\|

*ādau māṃ praharasveti tasmāttvāṃ ghātayāmyaham \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. “Strike me at the outset. Then I shall kill you.”

## \|\| 1.17.174 \|\|

*ityevamukto deveṃdro jaghāna gadayā bhṛśam \|*  
*vṛtraṃ balavatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jānudeśe mahābalam \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. On being told thus, Devendra hit hard with his mace Vṛtra of great strength and the most excellent one among those who possess power at the knee.

## \|\| 1.17.175 \|\|

*tāmāpataṃtiṃ jagrāha kareṇaikena līlayā \|*  
*tayaivainaṃ jaghānāśu gadayā tridiveśvaram \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. Seeing that mace coming, Vṛtra caught hold of it sportively. With that very same mace, he struck back immediately Indra, the king of heaven.

## \|\| 1.17.176 \|\|

*sā gadā pātayāmāsa savajraṃ ca puraṃdaram \|*  
*patitaṃ śakramālokya vṛtra ūce surānprati \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. That Gadā (mace, iron club) knocked down Purandara, along with his Vajra. On seeing Śakra fallen, Vṛtra spoke to Suras:

## \|\| 1.17.177 \|\|

*nayadhvaṃ svāminaṃ devāḥ svapurīmamarāvatīm \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. “O Devas, take your lord to your own city Amarāvatī.”

## \|\| 1.17.178-179 \|\|

*etacchrutvā vacaḥ satyaṃ vṛtrasya ca mahātnaḥ \|*  
*tathā cakruḥ surāḥ sarve raṇācceṃdraṃ samutsukāḥ \|\| 178 \|\|*

*apovāhya gajasthaṃ hi parivārya bhayāturāḥ \|*  
*surāḥ sarve raṇaṃ hitvā jagmuste tridivaṃ prati \|\| 179 \|\|*

178-179. On hearing these truthful words of the noble-souled Vṛtra, all the Suras did so. Eagerly they removed him even while he was seated on the elephant, from the battlefield and surrounded him with fear. All those Suras left the battlefield and went to heaven.

## \|\| 1.17.180 \|\|

*tato gateṣu deveṣu nanarta ca mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*vṛtro jahāsa ca paraṃ tenā pūryata diktaṭam \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. When Devas had departed, the great Asura Vṛtra danced and laughed loudly and thereby the quarters were filled with that (sound).

## \|\| 1.17.181 \|\|

*cacāla ca mahī sarvā saśailavanakānanā \|*  
*cukṣubhe ca tadā sarvaṃ jaṃgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ tathā \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. The entire earth including the mountains, parks and forests shook and trembled. All mobile and immobile things became agitated.

## \|\| 1.17.182 \|\|

*śrutvā prayātaṃ deveṃdraṃ brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*upayāto'tha deveṃdra svakamaṇḍaluvāriṇā \|*  
*aspṛśallabdhasaṃjño'bhūttatkṣaṇācca puraṃdaraḥ \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. On hearing that Devendra had gone (from the battlefield), Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, came near him. With the water from his Kamaṇḍalu, he touched (sprinkled) Devendra. At that very same instant, Purandara regained consciousness.

## \|\| 1.17.183 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā pitāmahaṃ cāgre vrīḍāyukto'bhavattadā \|*  
*maheṃdraṃ trapayā yuktaṃ brahmovāca pitāmahaḥ \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. Seeing Brahmā in front of him, Indra became ashamed. Brahmā, the grandfather, said to Mahendra who felt ashamed:

## \|\| 1.17.184 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*vṛtro hi tapasā yukto brahmacaryavrate sthitaḥ \|*  
*tvaṣṭuśca tapasā yukto vṛtraścāyaṃ mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*ajeyastapasogreṇa tasmāttvaṃ tapasā jaya \|\| 184 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

184\. Vṛtra is endowed with the power of penance (done by himself). He is endowed with the power of penance of Tvaṣṭṛ also. He abides by the holy rite and vow of celibacy. This Vṛtra of great fame has become invincible due to his severe penance. Hence conquer him by means of penance.

## \|\| 1.17.185 \|\|

*vṛtrāsuro daityapatiśca śakra te samādhinā parameṇaiva jayyaḥ \|*  
*niśamya vākyaṃ parameṣṭhino hariḥ sasmāra devaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajaṃ tadā \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. Vṛtrāsura, the lord of Daityas, can be conquered only through great penance, O Śakra.

On hearing the words of Brahmā, Hari (i.e. Indra) remembered the Bull-bannered Lord.

## \|\| 1.17.186 \|\|

*stutyā tadātaṃ stavamāno mahātmā puraṃdaro guruṇā nodito hi \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. The noble-souled Purandara urged by his (preceptor) Bṛhaspati began to eulogize (Lord Śiva) with a prayer.

Indra prayed:

## \|\| 1.17.187 \|\|

*iṃdra uvāca \|*  
*namo bhargāya devāya devānāmatidurgama \|*  
*varado bhava deveśa devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|\| 187 \|\|*

187\. Obeisance to lord Bharga, who is very difficult to be approached by Devas. O lord of Devas, be the bestower of boons for the sake of the accomplishment of the tasks of Devas.

## \|\| 1.17.188 \|\|

*evaṃ stitiparo bhūtvā śacīpatirudāradhīḥ \|*  
*svakāryadakṣo maṃdātmā prapaṃcābhirataḥ khalu \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. The liberal-minded consort of Śacī was thus engaged in eulogy. Indeed he was very prompt and skilful in matters concerning himself. He was slow-witted but was certainly devoted to worldly (pleasures).

## \|\| 1.17.189 \|\|

*prapaṃcābhiratā mūḍhāḥ śivabhaktiparā hyapi \|*  
*na prāpnuvaṃti te sthānaṃ paramīśasyarāgiṇaḥ \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. Deluded persons devoted to worldly pleasures do not attain the highest region of Īśa, even if they are engaged in devotion to Śiva (as) they are passionate and sensualist.

## \|\| 1.17.190-192 \|\|

*nirmalā nirahaṃkārā ye janāḥ paryupāsate \|*  
*mṛḍaṃ jñānapradaṃ ceśaṃ pareśaṃ śaṃbhumeva ca \|\| 190 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ pareṣāṃ varada ihāmutra ca śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*maheṃdreṇa stutaḥ śarvo rāgiṇā parameṇa hi \|\| 191 \|\|*

*rāgiṇāṃ hi sadā śaṃbhurdurlabho nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tasmādvirāgiṇāṃ nityaṃ sanmukho hi sadāśivaḥ \|\| 192 \|\|*

190-192. Those people who are free from impurities, egotism and arrogance and who worship Mṛḍa (the Gracious), īśa (the Supreme Lord), Śaṃbhu, the greatest lord, who bestows perfect knowledge are really great people. Śaṅkara is the bestower of boons on them both here and hereafter.

Mahendra was a great sensualist. Śarva had been eulogized by Mahendra who was passionate.

There is no doubt that Śaṃbhu can rarely be approached by sensualists. Hence Sadāśiva can always be visualized directly by non-sensualists.

## \|\| 1.17.193 \|\|

*rājā surāṇāṃ hi mahānurāgī svakarmasaṃsiddhimahāpravīṇaḥ \|*  
*tasmātsadā kleśaparaḥ śacīpatiḥ svakāmabhāvātmaparo hi nityam \|\| 193 \|\|*

193\. Indeed the king of Suras was exceedingly passionate. He (professed to be) very efficient in accomplishing his own tasks. Hence Śacīpati (Indra) (had) always to strain and exert himself. He was perpetually indulgent in his own lust and similar emotions of the heart.

## \|\| 1.17.194-195 \|\|

*stavamānaṃ tadā ceṃdramabravītkāryagauravāt \|*  
*vijñāyākhiladṛgdraṣṭā maheśo liṃgarūpavān \|\| 194 \|\|*

*iṃdra gaccha suraiḥ sārddhaṃ vṛtraṃ vai dānavaṃ prati \|*  
*tapasaiva ca sādhyo'yaṃ raṇe jetuṃ śatakrato \|\| 195 \|\|*

194-195. On account of the seriousness of the matter, Maheśa, of the form of the Liṅga, who was the seer and vision of all, understood (everything) and spoke to Indra who was eulogizing: “O Indra, go to Vṛtra, the Dānava, along with Suras. O Śatakratu (Indra), he can be conquered in the battle only through the power of penance.”

## \|\| 1.17.196 \|\|

*iṃdra uvāca \|*  
*kenopāyena sādhyo'yaṃ vṛtro daityavaro mahān \|*  
*tcachīghraṃ kathyatāṃ śaṃbho yena me vijayo bhavet \|\| 196 \|\|*

Indra said:

196\. By what means can this great and excellent Daitya be conquered? O Śaṃbhu, let that be mentioned immediately whereby my success can be (achieved).

## \|\| 1.17.197 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*raṇe na śakyate haṃtumapi devavarairapi \|*  
*tasmāttvayā hi kartavyaṃ kutsitaṃ karma cādya vai \|\| 197 \|\|*

Rudra said:

197\. He cannot be killed in battle even by the excellent Devas. Hence a mean act (of trickery) must be performed by you today.

## \|\| 1.17.198 \|\|

*asya śāpaḥ purā dattaḥ pārvatyā mama sannidhau \|*  
*asau citraratho nāmnā vikhyāto bhuvanatraye \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. Formerly this (demon) had been cursed by Pārvatī in ray presence. (At that time) he had been a king named Citraratha, well reputed in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.17.199 \|\|

*paryaṭansu vimānena mayā dattena bhāsvatā \|*  
*upahāsādimāṃ yoniṃ saṃprāpto datyapuṃgavaḥ \|\| 199 \|\|*

199\. He was wandering (here and there) in an excellent refulgent aerial chariot given by me. The leading Daitya had to be born of this womb (of a Daitya) because of His satirical ridicule.

## \|\| 1.17.200-201 \|\|

*tasmādajeyaṃ jānīhi raṇe raṇavidāṃ vara \|*  
*evamukto maheṃdro'yaṃ śaṃbhunā yoginā bhṛśam \|\| 200 \|\|*

*tatheti matvā śakro'sau niyamaṃ tamupādade \|\| 201 \|\|*

200-201. Hence, O excellent one among those who are expert in wars, know him to be invincible in war.

Thus Mahendra was told by Śaṃbhu, the greatest Yogin. Saying “So be it” and honouring it, Śakra took up devout observances and restraints.

## \|\| 1.17.202 \|\|

*raṃdhraṃ pratīkṣya vṛtrasya tatsamīpe sahasrakam \|*  
*vatsarāṇāṃ mahābhāgā vasanhaṃtuṃ mano dadhe \|\| 202 \|\|*

202\. O highly fortunate sages, he made up his mind to stay near Vṛtra for a thousand years waiting for a weak and vulnerable point in order to kill Vṛtra.

## \|\| 1.17.203 \|\|

*aṃtarvedyāṃ bahiḥ sthitvā vajrapāṇiranujñayā \|*  
*guroḥ purodhasaścaiva svakāryamakarodbhṛśam \|\| 203 \|\|*

203\. With the permission of Guru (Bṛhaspati), his priest, the thunderbolt-armed Indra stood out of Antaredī and carried on his activities vigorously.

## \|\| 1.17.204 \|\|

*ekadā narmmadāyāṃ vai vṛtro dānavapuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*daityaiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvaiḥ samāyāto yadṛcchayā \|\| 204 \|\|*
