*pipīlikābhirbahubhirdaṃśaiścaiva samāvṛtam \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. As he was engaged in the great penance his body was eaten by many ants and covered with biting gad-flies.

## \|\| 1.18.182 \|\|

*abhavattasya tajjñātvā sureṃdro hyagamatpurā \|*  
*nagaraṃ tasya ca tadā sainyena mahatā vṛtaḥ \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. On coining to know of it, Surendra formerly went to his city and besieged it with a great army.

## \|\| 1.18.183-184 \|\|

*tatsannidhau hatāḥ sarve asurā daityaśatruṇā \|*  
*viṃdhyā tu mahiṣī tasya nīyamānā nivāritā \|\| 183 \|\|*

*nāradena purā rājankiṃcitkāryaṃ cikīrṣuṇā \|*  
*śaṃbhoḥ prasādādakhilaṃ manasā yatsamīkṣitam \|*  
*daityeṃdreṇa ca tatsarvaṃ tapasaiva vaśīkṛtam \|\| 184 \|\|*

183-184. In his presence all the Asuras were killed by the enemy of Daityas. His queen Vindhyā was being taken away,

but, O King, was prevented by Nārada who was desirous of doing something. By the grace of Śaṃbhu, all those things which had been desired mentally by the lord of Daityas were won over by means of penance alone.

## \|\| 1.18.185-186 \|\|

*tasyāḥ putro mahātejā yena nīto'bhavatsabhām \|*  
*tasya putro mahābhāga pitā te pitṛvatsalaḥ \|*  
*nāmnā virocano vidvāniṃdro yena mahātmanā \|\| 185 \|\|*

*dānena toṣito rājansvenaiva śirasā tadā \|*  
*tasyātmajosi bho rājankṛtaṃ te paramaṃ yaśaḥ \|\| 186 \|\|*

185-186, Her son was that person of great splendour (i.e. Prahlāda) by whom his own son, i.e. your father who was a favourite of his father, was led to the Assembly, O King of great fortune. Your father was known by the name Virocana. It was by that noble-souled (Daitya) that the learned Indra was propitiated by the offer of his own head. O King, you are his son. Great fame has been earned by you.

## \|\| 1.18.187 \|\|

*yaśodīpena mahatā dagdhāḥ śalabhavatsurāḥ \|*  
*iṃdropi nirjito yena tvayā nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 187 \|\|*

187\. By the great lamp of your fame, Suras have been burnt like locusts and fireflies. There is no doubt about this that even Indra has been conquered by you.

## \|\| 1.18.188 \|\|

*śrutamasti mayā sarvaṃ caritaṃ tava suvrata \|*  
*alpako'hamihāyāto brahmacaryavrate sthitaḥ \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. All your activities have been heard by me, O Daitya of good holy rites. I am a small insignificant person clinging to my vow of celibacy.

## \|\| 1.18.189 \|\|

*uṭajārthe ca me dehi bhūmīṃ bhūmibhṛtāṃvara \|*  
*baṭostasyaiva tadvākyaṃ śrutvā balirabhāṣata \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. For the sake of a hut give me some ground, O most excellent one among the kings of earth.

On hearing the words of that Baṭu, Bali spoke:

## \|\| 1.18.190-191 \|\|

*he baṭo paṃḍito bhūtvā yaduktaṃ vacanaṃ purā \|*  
*śiśutvāttanna jānāsi śrutvā manye yathārthataḥ \|\| 190 \|\|*

*vada śīghraṃ mahābhāga kiyanmātrāṃ mahīṃ tava \|*  
*dāsyāmi tvaritenaiva manasā tadvimṛśyatām \|\| 191 \|\|*

190-191. “O Baṭu, you are a scholar. What you have spoken before, you yourself do not know, because you are only a child. On hearing it, I think that it is truthful.

Speak quickly, O highly fortunate one, how much ground shall I give you? Ponder over it quickly in your mind.”

## \|\| 1.18.192 \|\|

*tadāha vāmano vākyaṃ smayanmadhurayā girā \|*  
*asaṃtoṣaparā ye ca viprā naṣṭā na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 192 \|\|*

192\. Then Yāmana spoke these sweet words smilingly:

“Those Brāhmaṇas who are not contented are undoubtedly doomed.

## \|\| 1.18.193-194 \|\|

*saṃtuṣṭā ye hi viprāste nānye veṣadharā hyamī \|*  
*svadharmaniratā rājannirdaṃbhā niravagrahāḥ \|\| 193 \|\|*

*nirmatsarā jitakodhāvadānyā hi mahāmate \|*  
*viprāste hi mahābhāga tairiyaṃ dhāryate mahī \|\| 194 \|\|*

193-194. Those are Brāhmaṇas who are contented, not others. They are Brāhmāṇas in disguise. They (i.e. real Brāhmaṇas) are engaged in their own duty, O King. They are devoid of arrogance. They have no hindrance (of any kind). They are free from jealousy. They have conquered anger and are liberal-minded, O highly intelligent one. They are real Brāhmaṇas, O highly fortunate one. This earth is sustained by them.

## \|\| 1.18.195 \|\|

*manasvī tvaṃ bahutvācca dātāsi bhuvanatraye \|*  
*tathāpi me pradātavyā mahī tripadasaṃmitā \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. You are lofty-minded. You have plenty. You are the sole donor in the three worlds. Still the ground measured up to three paces should be given to me.

## \|\| 1.18.196 \|\|

*bahutve nāsti me kāryaṃ mahyā vai surasūdana \|*  
*praveśamātramuṭajaṃ tathā mama bhaviṣyati \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. I have nothing to do with plenty of earth, O slayer of Suras. It will serve as a hut with a mere entrance.

## \|\| 1.18.197 \|\|

*tripadaṃ pūryate'smākaṃ vastuṃ nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*dehi me kramato rājanyāvadbhūmibhaviṣyati \|*  
*tāvatsaṃkhyā pradātavyā yadi dātāsi bho bale \|\| 197 \|\|*

197\. Three paces of ground are enough for our purpose. There is no doubt about it. I shall take the steps and give me the ground as much as I cover. Only that number (of steps) need be given to me if you are a real donor.”

## \|\| 1.18.198 \|\|

*prahasya tamuvācedaṃ balirvairocanātmajaḥ \|*  
*dāsyāmi te mahīṃ kṛtsāṃ saśailavanakānanām \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. Bali, the son of Virocana, laughed and said this:

“I shall give you the entire earth including mountains, parks and forests.

## \|\| 1.18.199-202 \|\|

*madīyāṃ vai mahābhāga mayā dattāṃ gṛhāma vai \|*  
*yācako'si baṭo paśya dānaṃ daityāprayācase \|\| 199 \|\|*

*yācako hyalpako vāstu dātā sarvaṃ vimṛśya vai \|*  
*tathā vilokya cātmānaṃ hyarthibhyaśca dadāti vai \|\| 200 \|\|*

*ātmaupamyena sarvatra yo dadāti hyudāradhīḥ \|*  
*tasmānna yācitavyaṃ hi arthinā maṃdabhāginā \|\| 201 \|\|*

*baṭo dadāmyahaṃ te'dya sasailavanakānanām \|*  
*pṛthvīṃ saparvatāṃ sābdhiṃ nānyathā mama bhāṣitam \|\| 202 \|\|*

199-202. O highly fortunate one, take this which belongs to me and given to you by me. See, O Baṭu, you are the person who is an entreater and that you are begging of a Daitya. Whether the beggar is insignificant or not, the donor sees himself (i.e. considers his capacity) and gives away things to those who seek them. He is the real liberal-minded person who gives away commensurately with his own status. Hence a suppliant who is unfortunate should not go abegging. O Baṭu, I shall give you the entire earth today, including the mountains, parks and forests and oceans. My statement cannot be otherwise.”

## \|\| 1.18.203 \|\|

*punaḥ provāca sa baṭurvirocanasutaṃ prati \|*  
*pūryate mama daityeṃdra kramato hi padaistribhiḥ \|\| 203 \|\|*

203\. The Baṭu said once again to the son of Virocana: “My (need) is fulfilled, O great Daitya, by taking land covered in three steps.”

## \|\| 1.18.204 \|\|

*baṭostadvacanaṃ śrutvā asurendro balistadā \|*  
*uvāca prahasanvākyaṃ manyamāno balirbhṛśam \|*  
*gṛhyatāṃ ca mayā dattāṃ padaistribhiralaṃkṛtām \|\| 204 \|\|*

204\. On hearing those words, Bali, the lord of Asuras, spoke these words laughingly: “Let the space adorned by three steps and given by me, be accepted.”

## \|\| 1.18.205 \|\|

*ityukto vāmanaḥ prāha prahasannasuraṃ prati \|*  
*saṃkalpya sakalāṃ pṛthvīṃ dātumarhasi suvrata \|\| 205 \|\|*

205\. On being told thus, Vāmana laughingly said to the Asura: “Intending the whole of the earth (for dāna), it behoves you to give it, O Daitya of good holy rites.”

## \|\| 1.18.206 \|\|

*tatheti matvā balinā supūjitaḥ sa vāmanaḥ kaśyapanaṃdano mahān \|*  
*balistadānīṃ sahasā nitāṃtaṃ saṃstūyamānastvṛṣibhirmunīṃdraiḥ \|\| 206 \|\|*

206\. Thinking that it should be so, Vāmana, the great son of Kaśyapa, was adored well by Bali. Bali was then eulogized well by the sages and leading ascetics.

## \|\| 1.18.207 \|\|

*taṃ pūjayitvā sa baliryāvaddātuṃ samudyataḥ \|*  
*guruṇā vārita stāvadvirocanasuto mahān \|\| 207 \|\|*

207\. While after worshipping Vāmana, Bali was about to give (the gift), that great son of Virocana was prevented by his preceptor.

## \|\| 1.18.208 \|\|

*na dātavyaṃ tvayā dānaṃ viṣṇave baṭurūpiṇe \|*  
*iṃdrārthamāgataḥ sadyo yajñavighnaṃ karoti te \|*  
*tasmāttvayā na pūjyo hi viṣṇuradhyātmadīpakaḥ \|\| 208 \|\|*

208\. “This gift should not be offered by you to Viṣṇu in the form of a Baṭu. He has come here for the sake of Indra. He will create obstacles in your Yajña. Hence Viṣṇu, the illuminator of spiritual life, should not be worshipped by you.

## \|\| 1.18.209-211 \|\|

*purā kṛtamanenaiva mohinīrūpadhāriṇā \|*  
*devebhyaścāmṛtaṃ dattaṃ rāhuryena hato mahān \|\| 209 \|\|*

*yena vidrāvitā daityāḥ kālanemirhato balī \|\| 210 \|\|*

*evaṃvidho'yaṃ puruṣo mahātmā sa īśvaro viśvapatiḥ sa eva \|*  
*vimṛśya sarvaṃ manasā mahāmate hitāhitaṃ kartumi hārhasi tvam \|\| 211 \|\|*

209-211. Formerly much has been done by this one assuming the form of Mohinī, the enchantress. Nectar was given to Devas and the great Rāhu was killed. Daityas were routed. The powerful Kālanemi was killed. Such is he. He is the noble-souled Puruṣa. He is Īśvara. He alone is the lord of the universe. Ponder over everything, O highly intelligent one, mentally. It behoves you to do what is conducive to your welfare or otherwise.”

## Chapter 19 - Śukra Curses Bali: Vāmana Grants Boon to Bali

## \|\| 1.19.1 \|\|

*lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ saṃbodhito daityo guruṇā bhārgaveṇa hi \|*  
*uvāca prahasanvākyaṃ meghagaṃbhīrayā girā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

1\. On being addressed thus by his preceptor Bhārgava, the Daitya laughed and spoke these words in a voice as majestic as the (thundering) sound of the cloud:

## \|\| 1.19.2 \|\|

*tvayoktohaṃ hitārthāya yairvākyaiścālito'smyaham \|*  
*tava vākyaṃ mama prītyai hitamapyahitaṃ bhavet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. “I have been moved by those words with which I have been addressed by you for the sake of my welfare. Your statement may be for my happiness and welfare. But it is sure to go against my welfare.

## \|\| 1.19.3 \|\|

*dāsyāmi bhikṣitaṃ cāsmai viṣmave baṭurūpiṇe \|*  
*pātrībhūto hyayaṃ viṣṇuḥ sarvakarmaphaleśvaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I will surely give what has been begged of (me) to Viṣṇu in the form of a Baṭu. This Viṣṇu is the lord of the fruits of all Karmans.

## \|\| 1.19.4-6 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ hṛdi sthito viṣṇuste vai pātratamā dhruvam \|*  
*yasya nāmnā sarvamidaṃ pavitramiva cocyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yena vedāśca yajñāśca maṃtrataṃtrādayo hyamī \|*  
*sarve saṃpūrṇatāṃ yāṃti so'yaṃ viśveśvaro hariḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*āgataḥ kṛpayā medya sarvātmā harirīśvaraḥ \|*  
*uddhartuṃ māṃ na saṃdeha etajjānīhi tattvataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. Certainly, those people in whose heart Viṣṇu is stationed, are the most deserving persons. Everything seen in this world, is called holy by his name. This Hari is the lord of the universe. Vedas, Yajñas and these things beginning with Mantras, Tantras etc., become perfect and complete on account of him. Lord Hari, the soul of everyone has come here out of sympathy for me, in order to redeem me. There is no doubt about it. Understand this truthfully.”

## \|\| 1.19.7 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā cukopa ca ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*bhārgavaḥ śaptumārebhe daityeṃdraṃ dharmmavatsalam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On hearing these words of his, Bhārgava became furious. He began to curse the lord of Daityas, fond of virtue and piety:

## \|\| 1.19.8 \|\|

*mama vākyamatikramya dātumicchasyariṃdama \|*  
*viguṇo bhava re maṃda tasmāttvaṃ niḥśriko bhava \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “O suppressor of foes, you wish to offer the gift, transgressing my directives. Hence, O stupid one, become devoid of good qualities; be rid of all your glory.”

## \|\| 1.19.9 \|\|

*evaṃ śaśāpa ca tadā paramārthavijñaṃ śiṣyaṃ mahātmānamagādhabodham \|*  
*sa vai jagāmātha mahākavistvarātsvamāśramaṃ dharmmavidāṃ variṣṭhaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thus (Śukra) cursed his noble-souled disciple, conversant with the ultimate truth and possessing unfathomable knowledge and understanding. Mahā Kavi (‘the Great Śukra’), the most excellent one among those who know virtue and piety, hastened to his own hermitage.

## \|\| 1.19.10 \|\|

*gate tu bhārgave tasminbalirvirocanātmajaḥ \|*  
*vāmanaṃ cārcayitvā sa mahīṃ dātuṃ pracakrame \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When Bhārgava had departed, Bali, the son of Virocana, worshipped Vāmana and began to offer the earth,

## \|\| 1.19.11-12 \|\|

*viṃdhyāvaliḥ samāgatya balerarddhāṃgaśobhitā \|*  
*avanijya baṭoḥ pādau pradadau viṣṇave mahīm \|\| 11 \|\|*

*saṃkalpapūrveṇa tadā vidhinā vidhikovidaḥ \|*  
*saṃkalpenaiva mahatā vavṛdhe bhagavānajaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Vindhyāvalī, the resplendent better-half of Bali, came there and washed the feet of the Baṭu. He (Bali) gave the earth to Viṣṇu along with the rite of Saṃkalpa (‘ritualistic proclamation of the intention’) as he was an expert in the procedure (for holy rites). By his determination, the unborn Lord increased in size.

## \|\| 1.19.13 \|\|

*yadaikena mahī vyāptā viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*sarve svargā dvitīyena vyāptāstena mahātmanā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When the lord increased in size, the whole of the earth was covered with one of his steps by Viṣṇu who was powerful. All the Svargas (Heavens supposed to be twenty-one in number) were covered with the second step by that Supreme Soul.

## \|\| 1.19.14 \|\|

*satyalokagato viṣṇoścaraṇaḥ parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*kamaṇḍalugatenaiva aṃbhasā cāvanenije \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The foot of Viṣṇu that went as far as Satyaloka, was washed by Parameṣṭhin (i.e. Brahmā) with the water from his. Kamaṇḍalu (‘water-pot’).

## \|\| 1.19.15-16 \|\|

*tatpādasaṃparkajalācca jātā bhāgīrathī sarvasumaṃgalā ca \|*  
*yayā trilokī ca kṛtā pavitrā yayā ca sarve sagarāḥ samuddhṛtāḥ \|*  
*yayā kapardaḥ paripūrito vai śaṃbhostadānīṃ ca bhagīrathena \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tīrthānāṃ tīrthamādyaṃ ca gaṃgākhyamavatāritam \|*  
*tadviṣṇoścaraṇenaiva sametaṃ brahmaṇā kṛtam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. From the water that came in contact with his feet was born (the sacred river) Bhāgīrathī who was auspicious unto all, by whom all the three worlds were rendered sacred and pure, all the Sagaras were uplifted and the matted hair of Śaṃbhu was filled. By Bhagīratha the first and foremost of all the holy waters named Gaṅgā was made to descend. It was connected with Viṣṇu’s foot by Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.19.17 \|\|

*trivikramātparo hyātmā nāmnā trivikramo'bhavat \|*  
*trivikramakramākrāṃtaṃ trailokyaṃ ca tadā'bhavat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The greatest Ātman came to be known by the name Trivikrama, because of his three steps. Then all the three worlds were covered up by the steps taken by Trivikrama.

## \|\| 1.19.18-19 \|\|

*padadvayena vā pūrṇaṃ jagadetaccarācaram \|*  
*vihāya tatsvarūpaṃ ca devadevo janārddanaḥ \|*  
*punaśca baṭurūpo'sāvupaviśya nijāsane \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tadā devāḥ sagaṃdharvā munayaḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ \|*  
*āgatāśca baleryajñaṃ draṣṭuṃ yajñapatiṃ prabhum \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19, Or (it is better to state that) the whole of this universe including mobile and immobile beings was completely covered up by means of two steps.

Janārdana, the lord of Devas, cast off that form (i.e. the cosmic size) and again assumed the form of the Baṭu. He took his seat (as before). At that time Devas, Gandharvas, Sages, Siddhas and Cāraṇas came to the place of Bali’s Yajña in order to see the lord, the presiding deity of Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.19.20 \|\|

*tatra brahmā samāgatya stutiṃ cakre parātmanaḥ \|*  
*balestatraiva cānyena ca daityeṃdrāścāgatāstvaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Brahmā came there and eulogized the Supreme Spirit. Other leading Daityas also hastened to the place of Bali.

## \|\| 1.19.21 \|\|

*ebhiḥ sarvaiḥ parivṛto vāmano balisadmani \|*  
*upaviśyāsane so'tha uvāca garuḍaṃ prati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Vāmana sat there in the abode of Bali surrounded by all these. Then he said to Garuḍa:

## \|\| 1.19.22-23 \|\|

*daityo'sau bāliśo bhūtvā dattānena mahī mama \|*  
*tripadakramaṇenaiva gṛhītaṃ ca padadvayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*padamekaṃ pratiśrutya na dadāti hi durmatiḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvayā gṛhītavyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ padameva ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. “In his childish ignorance, sufficient ground to be covered up by three steps was offered by him to me. Two steps have been taken by me. One step that had already been promised, this evil-minded fellow does not give me. Hence the third step must be taken up by you.”

## \|\| 1.19.24 \|\|

*ityukto garuḍastena vāmanena mahātmanā \|*  
*vairocaniṃ vinirbhartsya vākyaṃ cedamuvāca ha \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On being told thus by Vāmana of great soul, Garuḍa rebuked the son of Virocana and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.19.25 \|\|

*re bale kiṃ tvayā mūḍha kṛtamasti jugupsitam \|*  
*avidyamāne hyarthe hi kiṃ dadāsi paramātmane \|*  
*audāryeṇa hi kiṃ kāryamalpakena tvayādhunā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “O stupid Bali, why is this despicable thing committed by you? When you do not have sufficient material what will you give to the Supreme Soul? Of what avail is a (show of) liberalmindedness by you, an insignificant person now?”

## \|\| 1.19.26 \|\|

*ityukto balirāviṣṭaḥ syamānaḥ khageśvaram \|*  
*vakṣyamāṇamidaṃ vākyaṃ garutmantaṃ tadā'bravīt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On being told thus, Bali was overcome (by grief) but smilingly he spoke to Garutmān, the lord of birds, the following words:

## \|\| 1.19.27-28 \|\|

*samarthosmi mahāpakṣa gṛpaṇo na bhavāmyaham \|*  
*yenedaṃ kāritaṃ sarvaṃ tasmai kiṃ pradadāmyaham \|\| 27 \|\|*

*asamartho hyahaṃ tāta kṛto'nena mahātmanā \|*  
*tadovāca baliṃ so'pi tārkṣyaputro mahāmanāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. “I am (really) capable, O (bird) of huge wings. I am not a miser. What can I give him by whom all these have been created? O dear one, I have been made incapable by this noble-souled lord.”

Then Garuḍa of noble mind spoke to Bali:

## \|\| 1.19.29 \|\|

*jānannapi ca daityeṃdra guruṇāpi nivāritaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇave'pi mahīṃ prādāstvayā kiṃ vismṛtaṃ mahat \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “Indeed you know (everything), O lord of Daityas. You were prevented by your preceptor. Yet you offered the earth to Viṣṇu. Is this important thing forgotten by you?

## \|\| 1.19.30 \|\|

*dātavyaṃ tatpadaṃ viṣṇostṛtīyaṃ yatpratiśrutam \|*  
*na dadāsi kathaṃ vīra nirayeca patiṣyasi \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. That step, the third one that has been promised to Viṣṇu must be given to him. How is it that you do not give it, O hero? You will fall into hell.

## \|\| 1.19.31 \|\|

*na dadāsi tṛtīyaṃ ca padaṃ me svāminaḥ katham \|*  
*balādgṛhṇāmi re mūḍha ityuktvā taṃ mahāsuram \|*  
*babaṃdha vāruṇaiḥ pāśairvirocana sutaṃ tadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. How is it that you do not give the third step to my master? I will take it forcibly, O foolish one.” Śaying this he bound the great Asura, the son of Virocana, by means of nooses of Varuṇa.

## \|\| 1.19.32 \|\|

*nitarāṃ niṣṭhuro bhūtvā garuḍo jayatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*baddhaṃ svapatimālokya viṃdhyāvaliḥ samabhyayāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Garuḍa, the most excellent one among conquerors, became very ruthless (and did like this). On seeing that her husband had been bound, Vindhyāvalī came there.

## \|\| 1.19.33 \|\|

*bāṇamekaṃ samāropya vāmanasyāgrataḥ sthitā \|*  
*vāmanena tadā pṛṣṭā keyaṃ cātrāgrataḥ sthitā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. She placed (her son) Bāṇa on one side and stood in front of Vāmana. It was enquired by Vāmana, “Who is this (lady) standing in front of me?”

## \|\| 1.19.34 \|\|

*tadovāca mahātejāḥ prahlādo hyasurādhipaḥ \|*  
*baleḥ patnīti tvāṃ prāptā iyaṃ viṃdhyāvalī satī \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then Prahlāda of great splendour, the lord of the Asuras, spoke: “This is Vindhyāvalī, the chaste wife of Bali. She has come to you.”

## \|\| 1.19.35 \|\|

*prahlādasya vacaḥ śrutvā vāmano vākyamabravīt \|*  
*brūhi viṃdhyāvale vākyaṃ kiṃ kāryaṃ te karomyaham \|*  
*evamuktā bhagavatā viṃdhyāvalirabhāṣata \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On hearing the words of Prahlāda, Vāmana spoke these words: “Say, O Vindhyāvalī, what shall I do for you?” On being told thus by the lord, Vindhyāvalī. spoke:

## \|\| 1.19.36 \|\|

*vindhyāvaliruvāca \|*  
*kasmādbaddho mama patirgaruḍena mahātmanā \|*  
*tatkathyatāṃ mahābhāga tvaranneva janārddana \|*  
*tadovāca mahātejā baṭuveṣadharo hiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Vindhyāvalī said:

36\. What for has my husband been bound by the noble-souled Garuḍa? Let it be explained immediately, O Janārdana of exalted fortune?

## \|\| 1.19.37 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*anenaiva pradattā me mahī tripadalakṣaṇā \|*  
*padadvayena ca mayākrāṃtaṃ trailokyamadya vai \|\| 37 \|\|*

Then Hari of great splendour, who had assumed the guise of a Baṭu said:

The Lord said:

37\. Ground measured by three steps had been offered to me by him alone. The whole of the three worlds has been covered up by me with two steps.

## \|\| 1.19.38 \|\|

*anena mama dātavyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ padameva ca \|*  
*tasmādbaddho mayā sādhvi garuḍenaiva te patiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The third step has to be given to me by this (Daitya) your husband. Hence, O chaste lady, he has been bound by me through Garuḍa.

## \|\| 1.19.39 \|\|

*śrutvā bhagavato vākyamuvāca paramaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*pratiśrutamanenaiva na dattaṃ hi tava prabho \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. On hearing the words of the lord, she spoke these great words:

“What has been promised by him, O lord, is not given to you.

## \|\| 1.19.40-41 \|\|

*krāṃtaṃ tribhuvanaṃ cādya tvayā vikramarūpiṇā \|*  
*tadasmākaṃ vijaghnīthāḥ svarge vāpyathavā bhuvi \|\| 40 \|\|*

*kiṃcinna dattā hi vibho devadeva jagatpate \|*  
*prahasya bhagavānāha tadā viṃdhyāvaliṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. All the three worlds have been covered up by you of valorous form. Therefore (everything) that we had in heaven aswell as on the earth has been hindered and obstructed by you. That was why something has not been given to you, O Lord, O Lord of the universe, O Lord of Devas.”

Then the lord laughed and said to Vindhyāvalī:

## \|\| 1.19.42 \|\|

*padāni trīṇi me cādya dātavyāni kuto'dhunā \|*  
*śīghraṃ vada viśālākṣi yatte manasi varttate \|*  
*tadovāca ca sā sādhvī hyurukramamavasthitā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. “Three steps have to be given to me today. Why (were they not given) now? Tell me quickly, O lady of large wide eyes, what have you in your mind?”

Then that chaste lady stood steady and said to Urukrama (‘one of large step’ i.e. Vāmana):

## \|\| 1.19.43 \|\|

*tvayā kuto veyamurukrameṇa krāṃtā trilokī bhuvanaikanātha \|*  
*tathaiva sarvaṃ jagadekabaṃdho deyaṃ kismābhiratulyarūpiṇe \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. “Why was the whole of the three worlds, O lord of the universe, occupied by you with large steps? Therefore, O sole kinsman of the universe, has everything to be given to you of matchless form by us?

## \|\| 1.19.44 \|\|

*tasmādvihāya tadviṣṇo tvamevaṃ kuru saṃprati \|*  
*prati śrutāni me bhartrā padāni trīṇi cādhunā \|*  
*dadāti me patistedya nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Hence leave it off, O Viṣṇu and do thus now. Three steps had been promised by my husband now. My husband will give (those promised steps) now to you. You need not worry about it.

## \|\| 1.19.45-46 \|\|

*nidhehi me padaṃ tvaṃ hi śīrṣṇi devavara prabho \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ me śiśostvaṃ hi kuru mūrdhni jagatpate \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tṛtīyaṃ ca jagannātha kuru śīrṣṇi patermama \|*  
*evaṃ trīṇi padānīśa tava dāsyāmi keśava \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Place a step on my head, O lord, the most excellent one among Devas. Place the second step, O lord of the universe, on the head of my child (Bāṇa). Place the third step, O lord of the universe, on the head of my husband. Thus I shall give you three steps, O Keśava.”

## \|\| 1.19.47 \|\|

*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā parituṣṭo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā virocanasutaṃ prati \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On hearing her words, Janārdana became delighted. He spoke these gentle and soft words to the son of Virocana:

## \|\| 1.19.48 \|\|

*bhagavānuvāca \|*  
*sutalaṃgaccha daityendra mā vilaṃbitumarhasi \|*  
*sarvaiścāsurasaṃghaiśca ciraṃ jīva sukhī bhava \|\| 48 \|\|*

The Lord said:

48\. Go to Sutala, O lord of Daityas. Do not delay. It does not behove you to delay. Live long and be happy along with all the groups of Asuras.

## \|\| 1.19.49 \|\|

*parituṣṭo'smyahaṃ tāta kiṃ kāryaṃ karavāṇi te \|*  
*sarveṣāmapi dātṝṇāṃ variṣṭho'si mahāmate \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. I am delighted and contented, O dear one. What shall I do for you? You are the most excellent one among all donors, O highly intelligent one.

## \|\| 1.19.50-51 \|\|

*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te sarvānkāmāndadāmi te \|*  
*trivikrameṇaivamukto virocanasutastadā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*vimukto hi pariṣvakto devadevena cakriṇā \|*  
*tadā baliruvācedaṃ vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Choose a boon. Welfare unto thee. I shall give you everything you wish.

On being told thus by Trivikrama, the son of Virocana was released (from bondage) and embraced by the Discus-bearing Lord of Devas. Then Bali, an expert in the use of words, spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.19.52 \|\|

*tvayā kṛtamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram \|*  
*tasmānna kāmaye kiṃcittvatpadābjaṃ vinā prabho \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. “It was by you that the whole of this universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings was created. Hence I do not wish for anything except your lotus-like feet, O Lord.

## \|\| 1.19.53 \|\|

*bhaktirastu padāṃbhoje tava deva janārdana \|*  
*bhūyobhūyaśca deveśa bhaktirbhavatu śāśvatī \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Let my devotion be to your lotus-like feet, O lord Janārdana. Let it flourish again and again, O lord of Devas. Let my devotion (unto you) be everlasting.”

## \|\| 1.19.54 \|\|

*evamabhyarthitastena bhagavānbhūtabhāvanaḥ \|*  
*uvāca paramaprīto virocanasutaṃ tadā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thus requested by him, the lord, the sanctifier of all living beings, became exceedingly pleased then and spoke to the son of Virocana:

## \|\| 1.19.55 \|\|

*bhagavānuvāca \|*  
*bale tvaṃ sutalaṃ yāhi jñātisaṃbaṃdhibhirvṛtaḥ \|*  
*evamuktastadā tena asuro vākyabravīt \|\| 55 \|\|*

The Lord said:

55\. O Bali, go to Sutala surrounded by kinsmen and relatives.

On being told thus by him the Asura spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.19.56 \|\|

*sutale kiṃ nu me kāryaṃ devadeva vadasva me \|*  
*tiṣṭhāmi tava sāṃnidhye nānyathā vaktumarhasi \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. “What have I to do in Sutala, O lord of Devas? Tell me. I shall stay near you. It does not behove you to say otherwise.”

## \|\| 1.19.57 \|\|

*tadovāca hṛṣīkeśo baliṃ taṃ kṛpayā'nvitataḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ tava samīpastho bhavāmi satataṃ nṛpa \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Then Hṛṣīkeśa, the merciful (lord), said to Bali: “O King, I shall always be near you.

## \|\| 1.19.58 \|\|

*dvāri sthitastava vibho nivāsāmi nityaṃ mā khidyatāmasuravarya bale śrṛṇuṣva \|*  
*vākyaṃ tu me vara maho varadastavādya vaikuṃṭhavāsibhipalaṃ ca bhajāmi geham \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O lord, I shall stand at the entrance to your (abode) and stay there perpetually. O Bali, the most excellent one among Asuras, be not afflicted and distressed. Listen to my clear and open statement. I shall be the bestower of boons on you. Along with the residents of Vaikuṇṭha, I shall betake myself to your abode.”

## \|\| 1.19.59 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya viṣmoratulatejasaḥ \|*  
*jagāma sutalaṃ daityau hyasuraiḥ parivāritaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. On hearing those words of Viṣṇu of matchless splendour, the Daitya went to Sutala surrounded by Asuras.

## \|\| 1.19.60 \|\|

*tadā putraśatenaiva bāṇamukhyena satvaram \|*  
*vasamāno mahābāhurdātṝṇāṃ ca parā gatiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. He stayed there along with his hundred sons, the chief (eldest) of whom was Bāṇa. The (Daitya) of great might was the greatest among all donors, their ultimate resort.

## \|\| 1.19.61 \|\|

*trailokye yācakā ye ca sarve yāṃti baliṃ prati \|*  
*dvāri sthitastasya viṣṇuḥ prayacchati yathepsitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. All the beggars and mendicants of the three worlds went to Bali. Viṣṇu who stood at the entrance to his abode, granted to them whatever they desired to get.

## \|\| 1.19.62 \|\|

*bhuktikāmāśca ye kecinmuktikāmāstathā pare \|*  
*yeṣāṃ yajñe ca te viprāstattebhyaḥ saṃprayacchati \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Some of them were desirous of worldly pleasures. Others were desirous of liberation. He gave them everything. He gave it to those persons in whose Yajñas they officiated as the Brāhmaṇa priests.

## \|\| 1.19.63-65 \|\|

*evaṃvidho balirjātaḥ prasādācchaṃkarasya ca \|*  
*purā hi kitavatvena yaddattaṃ paramātmane \|\| 63 \|\|*

*aśuciṃ bhūmimāsādya gaṃdhapuṣpādikaṃ mahat \|*  
*patitaṃ cārppitaṃ tena śivāya paramātmane \|\| 64 \|\|*

*kiṃ punaḥ parayā bhaktyā cārcayaṃti maheśvaram \|*  
*puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ te yāṃti śivasannidhim \|\| 65 \|\|*

63-65. It was by the favour of Śaṅkara that Bali became thus. In his former birth as a gambler, fragrant flowers, scents and other great things that had fallen on dirty ground were offered by him to the great Ātman. What had fallen down was dedicated to Śiva, the great spirit by him. What then in the case of those who worship Maheśvara with the greatest devotion? Those who devoutly offer sweet scents, flowers, fruits or even water go to Śiva’s presence.

## \|\| 1.19.66-67 \|\|

*śivātparataro nāsti pūjanīyo hi bho dvijāḥ \|*  
*ye hi mūkāstathāṃdhāśca paṃgavo ye jaḍāstathā \|\| 66 \|\|*

*jātihīnāśca caṃḍālāḥ śvapacā hyaṃtyajā hyamī \|*  
*śivabhaktiparā nityaṃ te yāṃti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. There is no greater (deity) worthy of being worshipped than Śiva. Those who are dumb, blind, lame and sluggish, those who are devoid of nobility of birth, Cāṇḍālas, dog-eaters and even low-born mean fellows, always attain the greatest goal if they are engaged in devotion to Śiva.

## \|\| 1.19.68 \|\|

*tasmātsadāśivaḥ pūjyaḥ sarvairevamanīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*pūjanīyo hi saṃpūjyo hyarcanīyaḥ sadāśivaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Hence Sadāśiva should be worshipped by all learned men. Sadāśiva should be worshipped, adored and venerated.

## \|\| 1.19.69 \|\|

*maheśaṃ paramārathajñāściṃtayaṃti hṛdi sthitam \|*  
*yatra jīvo bhavatyeva śivastatraiva tiṣṭhati \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Those who are aware of the ultimate truth think about Maheśa stationed in the heart. Wherever there is the individual soul, Śiva too dwells there.

## \|\| 1.19.70 \|\|

*vinā śivena yatkiṃcidaśivaṃ bhavati kṣaṇāt \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇuśca rudraśca guṇakāryakarā hyamī \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Everything without Śiva becomes inauspicious instantaneously. Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra—these carry on their activities through the Guṇas.

## \|\| 1.19.71 \|\|

*rajoguṇānvito brahmā viṣṇuḥ sattvaguṇānvitaḥ \|*  
*tamoguṇāśrito rudro guṇātīto maheśvaraḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Brahmā possesses Rajas Guṇa. Viṣṇu has Sattva Guṇa. Rudra resorts to Tamas Guṇa. Maheśvara is beyond all the Guṇas.

## \|\| 1.19.72 \|\|

*liṃgarūpo mahādevo hyarcanīyo mumukṣubhiḥ \|*  
*śivātparataro nāsti bhuktimuktipradāyakaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Mahādeva should be worshipped in the form of Liṅga by those who desire salvation. There is no greater bestower of worldly pleasures and liberation than Śiva.

## Chapter 20 - The Nirguṇatva of the Śiva Liṅga: The Manifestation of Bhavānī

## \|\| 1.20.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇuśca rudraśca saguṇāḥ kīrtitāstvayā \|*  
*liṃgarūpī tathaiveśo nirguṇo'sau kathaṃ vada \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra were mentioned by you as (deities) possessing Guṇas. Similarly Īśa has Liṅga for his form. How is he beyond Guṇas? Tell us.

## \|\| 1.20.2 \|\|

*tribhirguṇairvyāptamidaṃ carācaraṃ jaganmahadvyāpyatha vālpakaṃ vā \|*  
*māyāmayaṃ sarvamidaṃ vibhāti liṃgaṃ vinā kena kutovibhāti \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. This universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings is pervaded by the three Guṇas. Whatever is great, pervasive or small—everything is of the nature of Māyā and appears so. Whence and through what does it appear without the Liṅga?

## \|\| 1.20.3 \|\|

*yaddṛśyamānaṃ mahadalpakaṃ ca tannaśvaraṃ kṛtakatvācca sūta \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Whatever is visible whether great or small is perishable, O Sūta, because it is created.

## \|\| 1.20.4 \|\|

*tasmādvimṛśya bhoḥ sūta saṃśayaṃ chettumarhasi \|*  
*vyāsaprasādātsakalaṃ jānāsi tvaṃ na cāparaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Hence, O Sūta, it behoves you to ponder over everything, critically examine it and dispel our doubts. By the grace of Vyāsa you and none else, know everything.

## \|\| 1.20.5 \|\|

*suta uvāca \|*  
*vyāsena kathitaṃ sarvamasminnarthe śukaṃ prati \|*  
*śuka uvāca \|*  
*liṃgarūpī kathaṃ śaṃbhurnirguṇaḥ kathate tvayā \|*  
*etanme saṃśayaṃ tāta cchettumarhasyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. In this matter everything has been told (explained) by Vyāsa to Śuka.

Śuka enquired:

Śaṃbhu has Liṅga as his form. How is he described as free from Guṇas by you? O dear father, it behoves you to dispel this doubt of mine completely.

Vyāsa explained:

## \|\| 1.20.6 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*śruṇu vatsa bravīmyetatpurā proktaṃ ca naṃdinā \|*  
*agastyaṃ pṛcchamānaṃ ca yena sarvaṃ śrutaṃ śuka \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Listen, O dear one. I shall tell it. It was formerly explained by Nandī to Agastya who asked about it. O Śuka, everything was heard by him.

## \|\| 1.20.7 \|\|

*nirguṇaṃ paramātmānaṃ viddhi liṃgasvarūpiṇam \|*  
*parā śaktistathā jñeyā nirguṇā śāśvatī satī \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Know that the Great Ātman is devoid of Guṇas but it is in the form of Liṅga. Similarly Satī, the greatest and eternal Śakti, should also be known as devoid of Guṇas.

## \|\| 1.20.8 \|\|

*yayā kṛtimidaṃ sarvaṃ guṇatrayavibhāvitam \|*  
*etaccarācaraṃ viśvaṃ naśvaraṃ paramārthataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. It is by her that this ultimately perishable universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings and evolved out of the three Guṇas, has been created.

## \|\| 1.20.9 \|\|

*eka eva paro hyātmā liṃgarūpī niraṃjanaḥ \|*  
*prakṛtyā saha te sarve triguṇā vilayaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Ātman alone, the greatest unsullied Lord in the form of Liṅga (is eternal). Those three Guṇas got merged into it (the Supreme Ātman) along with Prakṛti.

## \|\| 1.20.10 \|\|

*yasminneva tato liṃgaṃ layanātkathitaṃ purā \|*  
*tasmālliṃge layaṃ prāptā parā śaktiḥ kuto'pare \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. It was hence called formerly Liṅga because of Layana (‘merging’). Even the Parā Śakti gots merged into the Liṅga. What of others?

## \|\| 1.20.11 \|\|

*līnā guṇāśca rudroktyā yairidaṃ baddhameva ca \|*  
*carācaraṃ mahābhāga tasmālliṃgaṃ prapūjayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. At the instance of Rudra, the Guṇas whereby mobile and immobile beings are bound, become merged, O highly fortunate one. Hence one should worship Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.20.12 \|\|

*liṃgaṃ ca nirguṇaṃ sākṣājjānīdhvaṃ bho drijotamāḥ \|*  
*layālliṃgasya māhātmyaṃ guṇānāṃ parikīrtyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Know, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that Liṅga is devoid of Guṇas. It is on account of the merging of the Guṇas that the Liṅga is glorified.

## \|\| 1.20.13 \|\|

*śaṃkaraḥ sukhadātā hi ucyamāno manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*sarvo hi kathyate viprāḥ sarveṣāmāśrayo hi sa \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Śaṅkara is described by learned men as the bestower of happiness. He is called Sarva, O Brāhmaṇas, as he is indeed the support of all.

## \|\| 1.20.14-15 \|\|

*śaṃbhurhi kathyate viprā yasmācca śubhasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*evaṃ sarvāṇi nāmāni sārthakāni mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tenāvṛtaṃ jagatsarvaṃ śaṃbhunā parameṣṭhinā \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. O Brāhmaṇas, he is called Śaṃbhu because he is one from whom auspiciousness originates. Thus all the names of the great Ātman are meaningful. The entire universe is enveloped by that Śaṃbhu, Parameṣṭhin (the Supreme God).

The sages enquired:

## \|\| 1.20.16-17 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadā dākṣāyaṇī cāgnau patitā yajñakarmaṇi \|*  
*dakṣasya ca mahābhāgā tirodhānagatā satī \|\| 16 \|\|*

*prādurbhūtā kadā sūta kathyatāṃ tattvayā'dhunā \|*  
*parā śaktirmaheśasya militā ca kathaṃ punaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Satī of great fortune, the daughter of Dakṣa, fell into the sacred fire of the holy rite of Yajña of Dakṣa. When did she appear again, O Sūta? Let it be described now by you. How did the greatest Śakti rejoin Maheśa?

## \|\| 1.20.18 \|\|

*etatsarvaṃ mahābhāga pūrvavṛttaṃ ca tattvataḥ \|*  
*kathanīyaṃ ca asmākaṃ nānyo vaktāsti kaścana \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. All these incidents of yore, O (Sage) of great fortune, should be described to us truthfully. There is no other person to recount it.

Sūta replied:

## \|\| 1.20.19-21 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*jajñe dākṣāyaṇī brahmanvidagdhāvayavā yadā \|*  
*vinā śaktyā maheśo'pi tatāpa paramaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*līlāgṛhītavapuṣā parvate himavadgirau \|*  
*bhṛṃgiṇā saha viśvena naṃdinā ca tathaiva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tathā caṃḍena muṃḍena tathānyairbahubhirvṛtaḥ \|*  
*daśabhiḥ koṭiguṇitairgaṇaiśca parivāritaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. O Brāhmaṇas, when Dākṣāyaṇī got her limbs (i.e. body) burnt in (the fire of) the Yajña, Maheśa was left without Śakti.

Hence he performed a great penance on the Himālaya mountain with a body playfully assumed by hiṃ He was surrounded by Bhṛṅgī, Viśva, Nandī, Caṇḍa, Muṇḍa and other Baṭus (young boys in the stage of religious students). He was surrounded by ten crores of Gaṇas (i.e. attendants).

## \|\| 1.20.22 \|\|

*gaṇānāṃ caiva koṭyā ca tathā ṣaṣṭisahasrakaiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ tatra gaṇairdeva āvṛto vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The Bull-bannered Lord was surrounded by other Gaṇas numbering one crore and sixty thousand.

## \|\| 1.20.23 \|\|

*tapo juṣāṇaḥ sahasā mahātmā himālayasyāgragatastathaiva \|*  
*gaṇairvṛto vīrabhadrapradhānaiḥ sa kevalo mūlavidyāvihīnaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The Supreme Ātman thus engaged in penance suddenly went to the top of Himālaya surrounded by his Gaṇas, the chief of whom was Vīrabhadra. He was alone, being bereft of the Mūlavidyā.

## \|\| 1.20.24-26 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare daityāḥ prādurbhūtā hyavidyayā \|*  
*viṣṇunā hi balirbaddhastathā te vai mahābalāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*jātā daityāstato viprā iṃdropadravakārakāḥ \|*  
*kālakhaṃjā mahāraudrāḥ kālakāyāstathāpare \|\| 25 \|\|*

*nivātakavacāḥ sarve ravarāvakasaṃjñakāḥ \|*  
*anye ca bahavo daityāḥ prajāsaṃhārakārakāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. In the meantime, Daityas were born of Avidyā. Bali was bound by Viṣṇu. Then those powerful Daityas became tormentors of Indra, O Brāhmaṇas. They were Kālakhañjas, the exceedingly terrible Kālakāyas (? Kālakeyas) and others. There were Nivātakavacas and those named Ravarāvakas. There were many other Daityas causing the massacre of the subjects.

## \|\| 1.20.27 \|\|

*tārako namuceḥ putrastapasā parameṇa hi \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ toṣayāmāsa brahmā tasya tutoṣa vai \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Tāraka, the son of Namuci, propitiated Brahmā by means of a great penance. Brahmā was pleased with him.

## \|\| 1.20.28 \|\|

*varāndadau yatheṣṭāṃśca tārakāya durātmane \|*  
*varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te sarvānkāmāndadāmi te \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He granted to the evil-minded Tāraka boons just according to his wish. He said: “Choose your boon. Welfare unto you. I shall give you all that your desire.”

## \|\| 1.20.29 \|\|

*tacchatvā vacanaṃ tasya brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*varayāmāsa ca tadā varaṃ lokabhayāvaham \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On hearing those words of Brahmā Parameṣṭhin, he chose a boon that instilled terror in all the worlds:

## \|\| 1.20.30 \|\|

*yadi me tvaṃ prasanna'si ajarāmaratāṃ prabho \|*  
*dehi me yadvijānāsi ajeyatvaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “If you are pleased with me, grant me freedom from old age and death and give me invincibility too as you know it.”

## \|\| 1.20.31-32 \|\|

*evamuktastadā tena tārakeṇa durātmanā \|*  
*uvāca prahasanvākyamamaratvaṃ kutastava \|\| 31 \|\|*

*jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyuretajjānīhi tattvataḥ \|*  
*prahasya tārakaḥ prāha ajeyatvaṃ ca dehi me \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. On being told thus by the evil-minded Tāraka, (Brahmā) laughingly spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.20.33 \|\|

*brahmovāca tadā daityajeyatvaṃ tavānagha \|*  
*vinārbhakeṇa dattaṃ vai hyarbhakastvāṃ vijeṣyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

“Wherefrom can you have immortality? Know it as a fact that certain indeed is death unto one who is born.” Then Tāraka laughed and said: “Then give me invincibility.”

33\. Brahmā then said to the Daitya: “Invincibility has been granted to you, O sinless one, except from an infant. An infant will defeat you.”

## \|\| 1.20.34 \|\|

*tadā sa tārakaḥ prāha brahmāṇaṃ praṇataḥ prabho \|*  
*kṛtārtho'haṃ hi deveśa prasādāttava saṃprati \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then Tāraka bowed down and said to Brahmā: “O lord, O lord of Devas, I am blessed and contented by your grace now.”

## \|\| 1.20.35 \|\|

*evaṃ labdhavaro bhūtvā tārako hi mahābalaḥ \|*  
*devānyuddhārthamāhūya yuyudhe taiḥ sahāsuraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Having acquired the boon thus, Tāraka, the Asura of great strength, challenged Devas for war and fought with them.

## \|\| 1.20.36-38 \|\|

*mucukundaṃ samāśritya devāste jayino'bhavan \|*  
*punaḥ punarvikurvāṇā devāste tārakeṇa hi \|\| 36 \|\|*

*mucukundabalenaiva jayamāpuḥsurāstadā \|*  
*kiṃ kartavyaṃ hi cāsmākaṃ yudhyamānairniraṃtaram \|\| 37 \|\|*

*bhavitavyamiti smṛtvā gatāste brahmaṇaḥ padam \|*  
*brahmaṇaścāgrato bhūtvā hyabruvaṃste savāsavāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. Resorting to Mucukunda, Devas became victorious. Although Devas were repeatedly attacked and tormented by Tāraka, they gained victory through the power of Mucukunda. ‘What is to be done by us? We are being continuously attacked and dragged into war.’ Thinking thus, Suras including Vāsava (Indra) went to Brahmā’s region. Going in front of Brahmā, they spoke thus:

## \|\| 1.20.39-40 \|\|

*devā ūcūḥ \|*  
*balinā saha pātālamāste'sau madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇuṃ vinā hi te sarve vṛṣādyāḥ patitāḥ paraiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*daityeṃdraiśca mahābhāga trātumarhasi naḥ prabho \|*  
*tadā nabhogatā vāṇī hyuvāca parisāṃtvya vai \|\| 40 \|\|*

Devas said:

39-40. Madhusūdana is staying in Pātāla along with Bali. Without Viṣṇu, all those, Vṛṣa and others have fallen on account of the enemies, the leading Daityas. O highly fortunate one, O lord, it behoves you to save us.

Then an ethereal voice spoke to them consolingly:

## \|\| 1.20.41-47 \|\|

*he devāḥ kriyatāmāśu mama vākyaṃ hi tattvataḥ \|*  
*śivātmajo yadā devā bhaviṣyati mahābalaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*yuddhe punastārakaṃ ca vadhiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yenopāyena bhagavāñchaṃbhuḥ sarvaguhāśayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*dārāparigrahī devāstathā nītirvidhīyatām \|*  
*kriyatāṃ ca paro yatno bhavadbhirnānyathā vacaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*yūyaṃ devā vijānīdhvamityuvācāśarīravāk \|*  
*paraṃ vismayamāpannā ūcurdevāḥ parasparam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*śrutvā nabhogatāṃ vāṇīmājagmuste himālayam \|*  
*bṛhaspatiṃ puraskṛtya sarve devā vaco'bruvan \|\| 45 \|\|*

*himālayaṃ mahābhāgāḥ sarve kāryārthagauravāt \|*  
*himālaya mahābhāga śrūyatāṃ no'dhunā vacaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tārakastrāsayatyasmānsāhāyyaṃ tadvadhe kuru \|*  
*tvaṃ śaraṇyo bhavāsmākaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca tapasvinām \|*  
*tasmātsarve vayaṃ yātā maheṃdrasahitā vibho \|\| 47 \|\|*

41-46a. “O Devas, let my suggestion be carried out exactly and immediately. O Devas, when an exceedingly powerful son is born to Śiva, he will undoubtedly kill Tāraka in battle. Take such a course of action that lord Śaṃbhu, dwelling in the cavity of the heart of everyone, takes a wife unto himself. Let a great effort be made by you all. These words cannot be otherwise. Know this, O ye Devas.” So said the unembodied voice. Struck with wonder, Devas spoke to one another. After hearing the ethereal voice, all the Devas of great fortune came to Himālaya keeping Bṛhaspati at their head. They spoke these words to Himālaya on account of the seriousness of the matter:

46b-47. “O Himālaya of great fortune, let our words be heard now. Tāraka terrorizes us. Render assistance in killing him. Be refuge unto us and to all the ascetics. It is for this that we have come here accompanied by Mahendra, O lord.”

## \|\| 1.20.48-51 \|\|

*lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*evamabhyarthito devairhimavāngirisattamaḥ \|*  
*uvāca devānprahasanvākyaṃ vākyavidāṃ varaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*mahendra muddiśya tadā hyupahāsasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*akṣamāśca vayaṃ sarve mahendreṇa kṛtāḥ surāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*kiṃ kurmaḥ surakāryaṃ ca tārakasya vadhaṃ prati \|*  
*pakṣayuktā vayaṃ sarve yadi syāma surottamāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tadā vayaṃ ghātayāmastārakaṃ saha bāṃdhavaiḥ \|*  
*acalohaṃ vipakṣaśca kiṃ kāryaṃ karavāṇi va \|\| 51 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

48-51. On being requested thus by Devas, Himavān, the most excellent among mountains spoke these words laughingly to Devas. Himavān, the most excellent one among those conversant with the (use of) words, was full of satirical laughter against Mahendra: “O Suras, it was by Mahendra himself that we have been made incapable of anything. What task of Suras can we do in this matter of killing Tāraka? If only we bad our wings, O excellent Suras, we would have killed Tāraka along with his kinsmen. I am an Acala (immobile; mountain). I am Vipakṣa (devoid of wings; belonging to the opposite side); what shall I do unto you all?”

## \|\| 1.20.52-53 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sarve devāstamabruvan \|*  
*sarve yūyaṃ vayaṃ caiva asamarthā vadhaṃ prati \|*  
*tārakasya mahābhāga etatkāryaṃ vicaṃtyatām \|\| 52 \|\|*

*yena sādhyo bhavecchatrustārako hi mahābalaḥ \|*  
*tadovāca mahātejā himavānsa surānprati \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. On hearing his words, all the Devas spoke to him: “All of you and all of us are incapable of killing Tāraka, O highly fortunate one. Let the means whereby Tāraka, our enemy of great power, can be brought under control, be thought off.”

Then the highly refulgent Himavān spoke to Suras:

## \|\| 1.20.54 \|\|

*kenopāyena bho devāstārakaṃ haṃtumicchatha \|*  
*kathayaṃtutvareṇaiva kāryaṃ vettuṃ mamaiva hi \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. “By what means, O Devas, do you wish to kill Tāraka? Be pleased to tell me quickly so that I can understand the matter on hand.”

## \|\| 1.20.55 \|\|

*tadā suraiḥ kathitaṃ sarvametadvāṇyā coktaṃ yatpurā kāryahetoḥ \|*  
*śrutaṃ tadā giriṇā vākyameta himavānparvato hi \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Then everything that had been previously declared by the (ethereal) voice in regard to their duty was mentioned by Suras. When it was heard by the Mountain, the Himalaya mountain spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.20.56-57 \|\|

*śivasya putreṇa ca dhīmatā yadā vadhyo daityastārako vai mahātmā \|*  
*tadā sarvaṃ suragakāryaṃ śubhaṃsyādvāṇyā coktaṃ satyametadbhavecca \|\| 56 \|\|*

*tasmāttadenatkriyatāṃ bhavadbhiryathā maheśaḥ kurute parigraham \|*  
*kanyā yathā tasya śivasya yogyā nirīkṣyatāmāśu surairidānīm \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. “When Tāraka, the Daitya of great soul, is to be slain by the intelligent son of Śiva, every objective of Suras shall be auspicious. What has been said by the ethereal voice shall become true. Hence let that be done by you, which makes Maheśa take up a wife unto himself. Who is that girl suitable to Śiva? Let that be ascertained by Suras now.”

## \|\| 1.20.58 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā prahasyocuḥ surāstadā \|*  
*janitavyā tvayā kanyā śivārthaṃ kāryasiddhaye \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On hearing his words, Suras laughed and said: “For the sake of Śiva and for accomplishing our task, a daughter has to be begotten by you.

## \|\| 1.20.59 \|\|

*surāṇāṃ ca gire vākyaṃ kuru śīghraṃ mahāmate \|*  
*ādhārastvaṃ tu devānāṃ bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O Mountain of great intellect, carry out the suggestion of Suras. You will undoubtedly become the support of Devas.”

## \|\| 1.20.60-63 \|\|

*ityukto girirājo'tha devaiḥ svagṛhamāmāviśat \|*  
*patnīṃ menāṃ ca papraccha sukāryaṃ samāgatam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*janitavyā sukanyaikā surakāryārthasiddhaye \|*  
*devānāṃ ca ṛṣīṇāṃ ca tathaiva ca tapasvinām \|\| 61 \|\|*

*priyaṃ na bhavati strīṇāṃ kanyājananaseva ca \|*  
*tathāpi janitavyā ca kanyaikā ca varānane \|\| 62 \|\|*

*prahasya menā provāca svapatiṃ ca himālayam \|*  
*yaduktaṃ bhavatā vākyaṃ śrūyatāṃ me tvayā'dhunā \|\| 63 \|\|*

60-63. On being told thus by Devas, the lord of mountains went to his house. He said to his wife Menā: “The task of Suras has become our responsibility. For the accomplishment of the task of Devas a good daughter has to be begotten. It is for the benefit of Devas, sages and ascetics. (Of course) the birth of a daughter may not be pleasing to women. Still, O lady of splendid face, a daughter has to be procreated.”

Menā laughed and spoke to her husband Himālaya: “What has been spoken by you (is true). Let my words be heard by you now.

## \|\| 1.20.64 \|\|

*kanyā sadā duḥkhakarī nṛṇāṃ pate strīṇāṃ tathā śokakarī mahāmate \|*  
*tasmādvimṛśya suciraṃ svayameva buddhyā yathā hitaṃ śailapate taducyatām \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O my lord, a daughter is the cause of misery unto men. So also, O highly intelligent one, she causes sorrow unto women. Hence ponder over this for a long time yourself with your keen intellect. Let what is conducive to our welfare be told, O lord of Mountains.”

## \|\| 1.20.65 \|\|

*himavāṃstadupaśrutyā priyāyā vacanaṃ tadā \|*  
*uvāca vākyaṃ medhāvī paropakaraṇānvitam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. On hearing the words of his wife, the intelligent Himavān spoke these words motivated by a desire to help others:

## \|\| 1.20.66 \|\|

*yenayena prakāreṇa pareṣāmupajīvanam \|*  
*bhaviṣyati ca tatkāryaṃ dhīmatā puruṣeṇa hi \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. “By an intelligent person, that whereby others can sustain themselves, should be done.

## \|\| 1.20.67 \|\|

*striyāpi caiva tatkāryaṃ paropakaraṇānvitam \|*  
*evaṃ pravartitā tena giriṇā mahiṣī tadā \|*  
*dadhāra jaṭhare kanyāṃ menā bhāgyavatī tadā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The same should be done by a woman also, viz. that which helps others.” Thus his queen was made to comply by the Mountain. Then the lucky Menā conceived a girl in her womb.

## \|\| 1.20.68 \|\|

*mahāvidyā mahāmāyā mahāmedhāsvarūpiṇī \|*  
*rudrakālī ca aṃbā ca satī dākṣāyaṇī parā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. She was the great Vidyā, the great Māyā, the embodiment of the highest intellect. She was Aṃbā, the great daughter of Dakṣa, Rudrakālī, Satī.

## \|\| 1.20.69 \|\|

*tāṃ vibhūtiṃ viśālākṣī jaṭhare paramāṃ satī \|*  
*babhāra sā mahābhāgā menā cāruvilocanā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The chaste lady of beautiful eyes and excellent fortune, Menā, bore in her womb that highest glory of large eyes.

## \|\| 1.20.70 \|\|

*stutiṃ cakrustadā devā ṛṣayo yakṣakinnarāḥ \|*  
*menāyā bhūribhāgyāyāstathā himavato gireḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Then Devas, sages, Yakṣas and Kinnaras eulogized Menā of excessive fortune and the Mountain Himavān.

## \|\| 1.20.71-74 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare jātā girijā nāma nāmataḥ \|*  
*prādurbhūtā yadā devī sarveṣāṃ ca sukhapradā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*devaduṃdubhayo nedurnanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ \|*  
*jagurgaṃdharvapatayo nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*puṣpavarṣeṇa mahatā vavṛṣurvibudhāstathā \|*  
*tadā prasannamabhavatsarvaṃ trailokyameva ca \|\| 73 \|\|*

*yadāvatīrṇā girijā mahāsatī tadaiva daityā bhayamāviśaṃste \|*  
*prāptā mudaṃ devagaṇā maharṣayaḥ sacāraṇāḥ siddhagaṇāstathaiva \|\| 74 \|\|*

71-74. In the meantime, their daughter named Girijā was born. When the goddess, the bestower of happiness on all, manifested herself, divine drums were sounded; celestial damsels danced; lords of Gandharvas sang; Siddhas and Cāraṇas eulogized (her); Devas showered plenty of flowers. Then everything, the entire unit of the three worlds became delighted. When the great Satī, Girijā, incarnated herself, Daityas became excessively frightened. The groups of Devas, the great Sages, Cāraṇas and the groups of Siddhas attained great joy.

## Chapter 21 - Pārvatī’s Penance

## \|\| 1.21.1 \|\|

*lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*varddhamānā tadā sādhvī rarāja prativāsaram \|*  
*aṣṭavarṣā yadā jātā himālayagṛhe satī \|\| 1 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

1\. The chaste girl grew up day by day and shone very much. Living in the house of Himālaya, she reached the age of eight years.

## \|\| 1.21.2 \|\|

*maheśo himavaddroṇyāṃ tatāpa paramaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*sarvairgaṇaiḥ parivṛto vīrabhadrādibhistadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. At that time Maheśa was performing a great penance in a valley of Himālaya. He was surrounded by all the groups of Gaṇas, Vīrabhadra and others.

## \|\| 1.21.3 \|\|

*etattapo juṣāṇaṃ taṃ maheśaṃ himavānyayau \|*  
*tatpādapallavaṃ draṣṭuṃ pārvatyā saha buddhimān \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Accompanied by Pārvatī, the intelligent Himavān went to Maheśa engaged in this penance, in order to see his sprout-like feet.

## \|\| 1.21.4 \|\|

*yāvatsamāgato draṣṭaṃ naṃdināsau nivāritaḥ \|*  
*dvāri sthite ca tadā kṣaṇamekaṃ sthiro'bhavat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When he arrived thus in order to see (the Lord), he was stopped by Nandin who was standing at the entrance. Then for a moment he stood steady.

## \|\| 1.21.5 \|\|

*punarvijñāpayāmāsa naṃdinā himavāngiriḥ \|*  
*vijñapto naṃdinā śaṃbhuracalo draṣṭumāgataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The mountain Himavān informed through Nandin. Śaṃbhu (he. Śiva) was informed by Nandin that the Mountain had come to see him (i.e. Śiva).

## \|\| 1.21.6 \|\|

*tadākarṇya vacastasya naṃdinaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*ānayasva giriṃ cātra naṃdinaṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On hearing his words, Parameśvara spoke these words to Nandin: “Bring the Mountain here.”

## \|\| 1.21.7 \|\|

*tatheti matvā naṃdī taṃ parvataṃ ca himācalam \|*  
*ānayāmāsa sa tathā śaṃkaraṃ lokaśaṃkaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Saying “So be it” and honouring (his words) Nandin brought the Mountain Himācala to Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds.

## \|\| 1.21.8-10 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tadānīṃ sakaleśvaraṃ prabhuṃ tapo juṣāṇaṃ vinimīlitekṣaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kaparddhinaṃ caṃdrakalāvibhūṣaṇaṃ vedāṃtavedyaṃ paramātmani sthitam \|*  
*vavaṃda śīrṣṇā ca tadā himācalaḥ parāṃ mudaṃ prāpadahīnasattvaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*uvāca vākyaṃ jagadekamaṃgalaṃ himālayo vākyavidāṃ variṣṭhaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. He saw (Śiva) the lord of everyone engaged in penance with his eyes closed. He had matted hair with the digit of the moon as an ornament. He could be understood only through the Vedānta and was stationed in the Supreme Soul. On seeing him, Mountain Himācala of unimpaired inherent strength, bent down his head and saluted him. He then attained the greatest joy. Himālaya, the foremost among those conversant with the use of words, spoke these words to the Lord who is the sole cause of auspiciousness to the universe:

## \|\| 1.21.11-13 \|\|

*sabhāgyo'haṃ mahādeva prasādāttava śaṃkara \|*  
*pratyahaṃ cāgamiṣyāmi darśanārthaṃ tava prabho \|\| 11 \|\|*

*anayā saha deveśa anujñāṃ dāturmahasi \|*  
*śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*āgaṃtavyaṃ tvayā nityaṃ darśanārthaṃ mamācala \|*  
*kumārīṃ ca gṛhe sthāpya nānyathā mama darśanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. “I am lucky, O Śaṅkara, the great lord, thanks to your grace. I shall come here everyday, O lord, to pay a visit along with this (daughter of mine). It behoves you, O lord of Devas, to grant me permission.”

On hearing his words, Maheśvara, the lord of Devas, (said): “O Mountain, you may come here everyday to meet me after keeping this girl in the house. Otherwise there would be no audience with me.”

## \|\| 1.21.14 \|\|

*acalaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ giriśaṃ natakaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*kasmānmayānayā sārddhaṃ nāgaṃtavyaṃ taducyatām \|*  
*acalaṃ ca vrīta śaṃbhuḥ prahasanvākyamabravīt \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. With his neck bent down the Mountain replied to Giriśa: “Why should I not come along with this (girl)? Let that be told.”

Śaṃbhu who was performing the holy rites, laughingly spoke these words to the Mountain:

## \|\| 1.21.15 \|\|

*iyaṃ kumārī suśroṇī tanvī cāruprabhāṣiṇī \|*  
*nānetavyā matsamīpe vārayāmi punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “This slender-bodied girl of good lips and exquisite speech should not be brought near me. I am forbidding it repeatedly.”

## \|\| 1.21.16 \|\|

*etacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya śaṃbhornirāmayaṃ niḥspṛhaniṣṭhuraṃ vā \|*  
*tapasvinoktaṃ vacanaṃ niśamya uvāca gaurī ca vihasya śaṃbhum \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. She heard Śaṃbhu’s harsh words, devoid of blemishes and free from any desire. On hearing the words uttered by that ascetic, Gaurī laughed and spoke to Śaṃbhu:

## \|\| 1.21.17-18 \|\|

*gauryuvāca \|*  
*tapaḥśaktyānvitaḥ śaṃbho karoṣi vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*tava buddhiriyaṃ jātā tapastaptuṃ mahātmanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kastvaṃ kā prakṛtiḥ sūkṣmā bhagavaṃstadvimṛśyatām \|*  
*pārvatyāstadvacaḥ śrutvā maheśo vākyamabravīt \|\| 18 \|\|*

Gaurī said:

17-18. O Śaṃbhu, you are endowed with the power of penance. You are performing a great penance. This inclination for performing penance you have because you are noble-souled. But let this be pondered over: Who are you? Who is the subtle Prakṛti, O holy lord?

On hearing those words of Pārvatī, Maheśa spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.21.19 \|\|

*tapasā parameṇaiva prakṛtiṃ nāśayāmyaham \|*  
*prakṛtyā rahitaḥ subhru ahaṃ tiṣṭhami tattvataḥ \|*  
*tasmācca prakṛte siddhair kāryaḥ saṃgrahaḥ kvacit \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “I am destroying Prakṛti by means of the greatest penance itself. In fact, O lady of good eyebrows, I will stay without Prakṛti. Hence nothing that has been evolved out of Prakṛti should be accumulated together at any time by Siddhas.”

## \|\| 1.21.20 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*yaduktaṃ parayā vācā vacananaṃ śaṃkara tvayā \|*  
*sā kiṃ prakṛti rnaiva syādatītastāṃ bhavānkatham \|\| 20 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:

20\. What has been said by you, O Śaṅkara, by means of ‘Parā’ speech, is it not Prakṛti? In that case how are you beyond it?

## \|\| 1.21.21-22 \|\|

*yacchṛṇopi yadaśrāsi yacca paśyasi śaṃkara \|*  
*vāgvādena ca kiṃ kāryamasmāke cādhunā prabho \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ prakṛteḥ kāryaṃ mithyāvādo nirrthakaḥ \|*  
*prakṛteḥ parato bhūtvā kimarthaṃ tapyate tapaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. O lord, of what avail is our disputation and argument? Whatever you hear, whatever you see and whatever you eat, O Śaṅkara, is entirely the evolute of Prakṛti. An untrue speech is meaningless. Why should penance be performed after going beyond Prakṛti?

## \|\| 1.21.23 \|\|

*tvayā śaṃbho'dhunā hyasmingirau himavati prabho \|*  
*prakṛtyā milito'si tvaṃ na jānāsi hi śaṃkara \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Lord Śaṃbhu, just now on this mountain Himālaya you have met Prakṛti. But you cannot understand it, O Śaṅkara. What have we to do with (i.e. What is the propriety of) oral dispute and argument, O Lord?

## \|\| 1.21.24 \|\|

*vāgvādena ca kiṃ kāryamasmākaṃ cādhunā prabho \|*  
*prakṛteḥ paratastvaṃ ca yadi satyaṃ vacastava \|*  
*tarhi tvayā na bhetavyaṃ mama śaṃkara saṃprati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. If your statement that you are beyond Prakṛti be true, you need not be afraid of me now, O Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 1.21.25 \|\|

*prahasya bhagavāndevo girijāṃ pratyuvāca ha \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then Lord (Śaṅkara) laughed and replied to Girijā: Mahādeva said:

## \|\| 1.21.26 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*pratyahaṃ kuru me sevāṃ girije sādhubhāṣiṇi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Serve me everyday, O Girijā of excellent speech.

## \|\| 1.21.27 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā girijāṃ maheśo himālayaṃ vākyamatho babhāṣe \|*  
*atraiva so'haṃ tapasā pareṇa carāmi bhūmyāṃ paramārthabhāvaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After saying thus to Girijā, Maheśa spoke these words to Himālaya: “Here itself, on this very ground, I shall perform a great penance with concentration on the ultimate truth.

## \|\| 1.21.28 \|\|

*tapastaptumanujñā me dātavyā parvatādhipa \|*  
*anujñayā vinā kiṃcittapaḥ kartuṃ na pāryate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Permission should be granted to me for performing the penance, O Lord of Mountains. Without (your) permission it is not possible to perform penance.”

## \|\| 1.21.29 \|\|

*etacchrutvā vacastasya devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*prahasya himavāñchaṃbhumidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On hearing these words of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas, Himavān laughed and spoke these words to Śaṃbhu:

## \|\| 1.21.30 \|\|

*tvadīyaṃ hi jagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|*  
*kimahaṃ tu mahādeva tuccho bhūtvā dadāmi te \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “The entire universe along with Devas, Asuras and human beings belongs to you. I am an insignificant person, O Mahādeva. What can I give you?”

## \|\| 1.21.31 \|\|

*evamukto himavatā śaṃkaro lokaśaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*prahasya girirājaṃ taṃ yāhīti prāha sādaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On being told thus by Himavān, Śaṅkara, the benefactor of all the worlds, laughed and respectfully said to the Lord of Mountains: “You may go.”

## \|\| 1.21.32 \|\|

*śaṃkareṇābyanujñātaḥ svagṛhaṃ himavānyayau \|*  
*sārddhaṃ girijayā so'pi pratyahaṃ darśane sthitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Permitted to go by Śaṅkara, Himavān went to his abode. Everyday he came there along with Girijā to pay a visit.

## \|\| 1.21.33-35 \|\|

*evaṃ katipayaḥ kālo gataścopāsanāttayoḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sutāpitrośca tatraiva śaṃkaro duratikramaḥ \|*  
*pārvatīṃ prati tatraiva ciṃtāmāpedire surāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*te ciṃtyamānāśca surāstadānīṃ kathaṃ maheśo girijāṃ sameṣyati \|*  
*kiṃ kāryamadyaiva vayaṃ ca kurmo bṛhaspate tatkathayasva mā ciram \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. Thus some time passed when the father and the daughter continued their visits and service. But Śaṅkara was difficult to be tackled and won over. Suras began to worry about Pārvatī. ‘How will Śaṅkara join Girijā?’ was the thought worrying the minds of Suras. They asked: “O Bṛhaspati, what should we do now? Tell us. Do not delay.”

## \|\| 1.21.36-37 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvācedaṃ maheṃdraṃ prati sadvacaḥ \|*  
*evametattvayā kāryaṃ maheṃdra śrūyatāṃ tadā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*etatkāryaṃ madanenaiva rājannānyaḥ samartho bhavitā triloke \|*  
*viplāvitaṃ tāpasānāṃ tapo hi tasmāttvarātprārthanīyo hi māraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Bṛhaspati spoke the following good words (of advice) to Mahendra: “O Mahendra, this must be done by you. Let it be heard. This task can be carried out only by Madana (the god of Love), O King. None else will be competent for it in all the three worlds. The penance of many ascetics has been upset by him. Hence Māra (god of Love) should be requested (in this matter) immediately.”

## \|\| 1.21.38 \|\|

*gurorvacanamākarṇya āhvayanmadanaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*āhvānādājagāmātha madanaḥ kāryasādhakaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On hearing the words of Guru (Bṛhaspati, the preceptor) Indra sent for Madana. Madana who accomplished (his) tasks came there on receipt of the call.

## \|\| 1.21.39 \|\|

*ratyā sametaḥ saha mādhavena sa puṣpadhanvā purataḥ sabhāyām \|*  
*maheṃdramāgamya uvāca vākyaṃ sagarvitaṃ lokamanoharaṃ ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Accompanied by Rati and Mādhava (i.e. the Spring season) the flower-armed deity came to the assembly in front of Mahendra and spoke these proud words in a manner captivating the minds of the people:

## \|\| 1.21.40 \|\|

*ahamākāritaḥ kasmādbrūhi me'dya śacīpate \|*  
*kiṃ kāryaṃ karavāṇyadya kathyatāṃ mā vilaṃbitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “Why have I been called today, O Śacīpati (i.e. Indra)? Tell me what work should I do? Do not delay.

## \|\| 1.21.41 \|\|

*mama smaraṇamātreṇa vibhraṣṭā hi tapasvinaḥ \|*  
*tvameva jānāsi hare mama vīryaparākramau \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The moment they think about me, the ascetics meet with their downfall. You do know, O Indra, my valour and prowess.

## \|\| 1.21.42 \|\|

*mama vīryaṃ ca jānāti śakteḥ putraḥ parāśaraḥ \|*  
*evaṃ cānaye ca bahavo bhṛgvādya ṛṣayo hyamī \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Parāśara, the son of Śakti, knows my power and vigour. Thus many other sages such as Bhṛgu do know it.

## \|\| 1.21.43-44 \|\|

*gururapyabhijānāti bhāryotathyasya caiva hi \|*  
*tasyāṃ jāto bharadvājo guruṇā saṃkaro hi saḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*bharadvājo mahābhāga ityuvāca gurustadā \|*  
*jānāti mama vīryaṃ ca śauryaṃ caiva prajāpatiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Bṛhaspati too knows it, as well as the wife of Utathya. Bharadvāja was born of her begotten by Guru and was thus illegitimate. Guru had then said, Bharadvāja \[‘Beat two (sons) simultaneously (conceived)’\]. Prajāpati (Brahmā) knows my heroism and powerful valour.

## \|\| 1.21.45 \|\|

*krodho hi mama baṃdhuśca mahābalaparakramaḥ \|*  
*ubhābhyāṃ drāvitaṃ viśvaṃ jaṃgamājaṃgamaṃ mahat \|*  
*brahmādistaṃbaparyaṃtaṃ plāvitaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Krodha (Anger) is my kinsman. He has great strength and valour. By both of us, this great universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings has been conquered (and liquidated,

i.e. excited and stirred up). Everything beginning with Brahmā and ending with a blade of grass, the whole world of mobile and immobile beings, has been (flooded and) overwhelmed by us.”

## \|\| 1.21.46 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*madanadvaṃ samarthosi asmāñjetuṃ sadaiva hi \|*  
*maheśaṃ prati gacchāśu surakāryārthasiddhaye \|*  
*pārvatyā sahitaṃ śaṃbhuṃ kuruṣvādya mahāmate \|\| 46 \|\|*

Devas said:

46\. O Madana, you are capable of always conquering us. (But) go immediately to Maheśa for accomplishing the task of Suras. Unite Śaṃbhu with Pārvatī, O highly intelligent one.

## \|\| 1.21.47 \|\|

*evamabhyarthito devairmadano viśvamohanaḥ \|*  
*jagāma tvarito bhūtvā apsarobhiḥ samanvitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On being requested thus by Devas, Madana, the enchanter of the universe, went away (from that place) immediately in the company of celestial damsels.

## \|\| 1.21.48 \|\|

*tato jagāmāśu mahādhanurddharo visphārya cāpaṃ kusumānvitaṃ mahat \|*  
*tathaiva bāṇāṃśca manoramāṃśca pragṛhya vīro bhuvanaikajetā \|*  
*tasminhimādrau paridṛśyamāno'vanau smaro yodhayatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. That wielder of a great bow made the twanging sound of his flowery bow. He took with him charming and fascinating arrows. That hero, the sole conqueror of the worlds, the most excellent one among warriors, Smara, was then seen on the grounds of the mountain Himavān.

## \|\| 1.21.49-50 \|\|

*tatrāgatā tadā raṃbhā urvaśī puṃjikasthalī \|*  
*sumlocā miśrakeśī ca subhagā ca tilottamā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*anyāśca vividhāḥ jātāḥ sāhāyye madanasya ca \|*  
*apsaraso gaṇairdṛṣṭā madanena sahaiva tāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Then all these celestial damsels came there, viz. Raṃbhā, Urvaśī, Puñjikasthalī, Sumlocā, Miśrakeśī, Subhagā and Tilottamā. There were others also to render different kinds of assistance to Madana. These damsels were seen by Gaṇas (attendants of Śiva) along with Madana.

## \|\| 1.21.51-53 \|\|

*sarve gaṇāśca sahasā madanena vimohitāḥ \|*  
*bhṛṃgiṇā ca tadā raṃbhā caṇḍena saha corvaśī \|\| 51 \|\|*

*menakā vīrabhadreṇa caṇḍena puṃjikasthalī \|*  
*tilottamādayastatra saṃvṛtāśca gaṇaistadā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*amattabhūtairbahubhistrapāṃ tyaktvā manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*akāle kokilā bhiśca vyāptāmāsīnmahītalam \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. All the Gaṇas were suddenly enchanted by Madana. Raṃbhā (was approached) by Bhṛṅgi, Urvaśī by Caṇḍa, Menakā by Vīrabhadra and Puñjikasthalī by Caṇḍa(?). Tilottamā and others were surrounded by the Gaṇas then, who had become mad and abandoned all shame although they were high-minded and learned.

The whole of the earth was pervaded by cuckoos, though it was not the proper season (i.e. the spring).

## \|\| 1.21.54-55 \|\|

*aśokāścaṃpakāścūtā yūthyaścaiva kadaṃbakāḥ \|*  
*nīṣāḥ priyālāḥ panasā rājavṛkṣāścarāyaṇāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*drākṣāvallayaḥ pradṛśyaṃte bahulā nāgakeśarāḥ \|*  
*tathā kadalyaḥ ketakyo bhramarairupaśobhitāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Aśoka, Caṃpaka, mangoes, Yūthīs (jasmine), Kadaṃbas (Nanclea cadamba), Nīpas (Ixora bandhucca), Priyālas (Buchamania latifolia), Panasas (jack fruit trees), Rajavṛkṣas, Carāyaṇas (?), vine creepers, and Nāgakesaras (Mesua roxburghii), plantains, Ketakīs (Pandanus odoratissimus) etc.—all these trees were in full bloom and they were rendered beautiful by bees.

## \|\| 1.21.56-58 \|\|

*mattā madanasaṃgena haṃsībhiḥ kalahaṃsakāḥ \|*  
*kareṇubhirgajāhyāsañchikhaṃḍībhiḥ śikhaṃḍinaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*niṣkāmā hyaturā hyāsañchivasaṃparkajairguṇaiḥ \|*  
*akasmācca tathābhūtaṃ kathaṃ jātaṃ vimṛśya ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

*śailādo hi mahātejā naṃdī hyamitavikramaḥ \|*  
*rakṣasaṃ vibudhānāṃ vā kṛtyamastītyaciṃtayat \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. By the contact of Madana Kalahaṃsakas (swans) became intoxicated in the company of female swans, he-elephants with she-elephants and peacocks with peahens. Though all these had been free from lust due to the qualities arising from contact with Śiva, they now became excited.

The highly refulgent Nandī, the son of Śailāda and of im-measurable (infinite) valour, pondered over this: Why have these become so all of a sudden? This must be the working of Rākṣasas or of gods.

## \|\| 1.21.59 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra madano hi dhanurddharaḥ \|*  
*paṃcabāṇānsamāropya svakīye dhanuṣi dvijāḥ \|*  
*tarośchāyāṃ samāśritya devadārugatāṃ tadā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In the meantime Maḍana took up his bow and fixed five arrows to it, O Brāhmaṇas. He resorted to the shade of a Devadāru tree.

## \|\| 1.21.60-62 \|\|

*nirīkṣya śaṃbhuṃ paramāsane stitaṃ tapo juṣāṇaṃ parameṣṭhināṃ patim \|*  
*gaṃgādharaṃ nīlatamālakaṃṭhaṃ kapardinaṃ candrakalāsametam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*bhujaṃgabhogāṃkitasarvagātraṃ paṃcānanaṃ siṃhaviśālavikramam \|*  
*karpūragaure parayānvitaṃ ca sa veddhukāmo madanastapasvinam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*durāsadaṃ dīptimatāṃ variṣṭhaṃ maheśamugraṃ saha mādhavena \|*  
*yāvacchivaṃ veddhukāmaḥ śareṇa tāvadyātā girijā viśvamātā \|*  
*sakhījanaiḥ saṃvṛtā pūjanārthaṃ sadāśivaṃ maṃgalaṃ maṃgalānām \|\| 62 \|\|*

60-62. He saw Śaṃbhu performing his penance. The Lord was seated on an excellent seat. He was the lord of all Parameṣṭhins (creators). He kept Gaṅgā (within his matted hair). His throat was blue in colour like Tamāla (dark-barked Xanthochymus pictorius). He had matted hair. He had the crescent moon (as an embellishment). All his limbs were marked by the coiled bodies of many serpents. He had five faces. His gait was in long strides like that of a lion. He was fair in complexion like camphor. He was accompanied by Parā. Maḍana was desirous of piercing the fierce ascetic Maheśa, very difficult of access and the most excellent among highly refulgent ones. In the company of Mādhava (Spring) he was about to hit Śiva with his arrow when Girijā, the mother of the universe, came there. She was surrounded by her friends. She approached Sadāśiva, the most auspicious of all auspicious ones, for the sake of worship.

## \|\| 1.21.63 \|\|

*kanakakusumamālāṃ saṃdadhe nīlakaṃṭhe sitakiraṇamanojñādurllabhā sā tadānīm \|*  
*smitavikasitanetrā cāruvaktraṃ śivasya sakalajananitrī vīkṣamāṇā babhūva \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. She placed a garland of golden flowers on Nīlakaṇṭha. At that time she had a rare splendour. She appeared very beautiful with white rays (diffused all round). The mother of all people looked (lovingly) at the handsome face of Śiva. Then her eyes bloomed and expanded widely as she smiled.

## \|\| 1.21.64 \|\|

*tāvadviddhaḥ śareṇaiva mohanākhyena catvarāt \|*  
*vidhyamānastadā śaṃbhuḥ śanairunmīlya locane \|*  
*dadarśa girijāṃ devobdhiryathā śaśinaḥ kalām \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. At that time Śaṃbhu was hit and pierced with the arrow called Mohana (‘the Enchanter’) suddenly. On being hit, Śaṃbhu opened his eyes slowly. The lord saw Girijā like the ocean viewing the digit of the moon.

## \|\| 1.21.65-67 \|\|

*cāruprasannavadanāṃ biṃboṣṭhīṃ sasmitekṣaṇām \|*  
*sudvijāmagnijāṃ tanvīṃ viśālavadanotsavām \|\| 65 \|\|*

*gaurīṃ prasannamudrāṃ ca viśvamohanamohanām \|*  
*yayā trilokaracanā kṛtā brahmādibhiḥ saha \|\| 66 \|\|*

*utpattipālanavināśakarī ca yā vai kṛtvāgrataḥ sattvarajastamāṃsi \|*  
*sā cetanena dadṛśe purato hareṇa saṃmohanī sakalamaṃgalamaṃgalaikā \|\| 67 \|\|*

65-67. She had a beautiful delightful face. Her lips were like the Biṃba fruit (Momordica monadelpha). Her eyes brightened with her smile. Her teeth were fine and excellent. She appeared as though she had come out of fire (i.e. she was resplendent). She had a slender body with a beautiful and wide face. Gaurī had all the signs of pleasure (within). She was capable of enchanting the entire universe. It was she who created the three worlds along with Brahmā and others. Making use of the qualities of Rajas, Sattva and Tamas, she caused the origin, sustenance and annihilation (of the worlds). That enchanting goddess, the sole cause of auspiciousness of all auspicious things, was seen in front by Hara who was awakened.

## \|\| 1.21.68 \|\|

*tāṃ nirīkṣya bhavo devo girijāṃ lokapāvanīm \|*  
*mumoha darśanāttasyā madanenāturīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*vismayotphullanayano babhūva sahasā śivaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. On seeing Girijā, the sanctifier of all the worlds, lord Bhava became fascinated. At her sight he was afflicted by Madana. Śiva’s eyes suddenly became expanded due to surprise.

## \|\| 1.21.69 \|\|

*evaṃ vilokamāno'sau devadevo jagatpatiḥ \|*  
*manasā dūyamānena idamāha sadāśivaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The lord of the universe, the lord of Devas (began) to look around. With the mind pained much, Sadāśiva said thus:

## \|\| 1.21.70 \|\|

*anayā mohitaḥ kasmāttapaḥstho'haṃ nirāmayaḥ \|*  
*kutaḥ kasmācca kenedaṃ kṛtamasti mamāpriyam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. “I am engaged in penance. I am devoid of blemishes. Yet how was I enchanted by this girl? Whence, why and by whom was this done causing my displeasure?”

## \|\| 1.21.71-72 \|\|

*tato vyalokayacchaṃbhurddikṣu sarvāsu sādaram \|*  
*tāvaddṛṣṭo dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi hyāttaśarāsanaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*cakrīkṛtadhanuḥ sajjaṃ cakre beddhuṃ sadāśivam \|*  
*yāvatpunaḥ saṃdhayati madano madanāṃtakam \|*  
*tāvaddṛṣṭo maheśena saroṣeṇa tadā dvijāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. Then Śaṃbhu looked in all directions earnestly. Madana was seen by him in the south with the bow lifted up. The god of Love bent his bow like a circle; kept it ready, drawn in order to pierce and wound Sadāśiva. But by the time he was able to discharge the arrow, O Brāhmaṇas, he was stared at by Maheśa angrily.

## \|\| 1.21.73 \|\|

*nirīkṣitastṛtīyena cakṣuṣā parameṇa hi \|*  
*madanastatkṣaṇādeva jvālāmālāvṛto'bhavat \|*  
*hāhākāro mahānāsīddevānāṃ tatra paśyatām \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. He was looked at with the third eye by the greatest lord. Madana was instantly encircled by clusters of flames. There was a loud wailing among Devas who stood there watching.

## \|\| 1.21.74 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva devānāṃ varado bhava \|*  
*girijāyāḥ sahāyārthaṃ preṣito madano'dhunā \|\| 74 \|\|*

Devas said:

74\. O Mahādeva, lord of Devas, be the bestower of boons on Devas. It was to help Girijā that Madana had been sent now.

## \|\| 1.21.75-81 \|\|

*vṛthā tvayātha dagdho'sau madano hi mahāprabhaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*tvayā hi kāryaṃ jagadekabaṃdho kāryaṃ surāṇāṃ parameṇa varcasā \|*  
*asyāṃ samutpatsyati deva śaṃbho tenaiva sarvaṃ bhavatīha kāryam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*tārakeṇa mahādeva devāḥ saṃpīḍitā bhṛśam \|*  
*tadarthaṃ jīvitaṃ cāsya dattvā ca girijāṃ prabho \|\| 77 \|\|*

*varayasva mahābhāga devākārye bhava kṣamaḥ \|*  
*gajāsurāttavayā trātā vayaṃ sarve divaukasaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*kālakūṭācca nūnaṃ hi rakṣitāḥ smo na cānyathā \|*  
*bhasmāsurācca sarveśa tvayā trātā na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*madanoyaṃ samāyātaḥ surāṇāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|*  
*tasmāttvayā rakṣaṇīya upakāraḥ paro hi naḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*vinā tena jagatsarvaṃ nāśameṣyati śaṃkara \|*  
*niṣkāmastvaṃ kathaṃ śaṃbho svabuddhyā ca vimṛsyatām \|\| 81 \|\|*

75-81. In vain was Madana of great lustre burned by you. It is by you alone, the sole kinsman of the universe, that the task of Suras should be carried out by means of your great splendour. O lord Śaṃbhu, (a son) will be born of her and by him alone can our objective be achieved. O Mahādeva, Devas are very much afflicted by Tāraka. For that purpose grant life unto this (Madana) and woo Girijā, O lord of exalted fortune. (Please) be capable of accomplishing the task of Devas. All of us, the heaven-dwellers, were protected by you from the demon in the shape of an elephant. Certainly we have been saved from the Kālakūṭa poison (by you), not otherwise (by anyone else). Undoubtedly we have been protected from Bhasmāsura by you, O Lord of everyone. This Madana came here for accomplishing the task of Suras. Hence he should be protected. That will be a great help to us (also). Without him, O Śaṅkara, the entire universe will be ruined. How can you also be devoid of Kāma (Love)? Let this be pondered over by your own intellect.

## \|\| 1.21.82-88 \|\|

*tadovāca ruṣāviṣṭo devānprati maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*vinā kāmena bho devā bhavitavyaṃ na cānyathā \|\| 82 \|\|*

*yadāḥkāmaṃ puraskṛtya sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*padabhraṣṭāśca duḥkhena vyāptā dainyaṃ samāśritāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*kāmo hi narakāyaiva sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ dhruvam \|*  
*duḥkharūpī hyanaṃgo'yaṃ jānīdhvaṃ mama bhāṣitam \|\| 84 \|\|*

*tārako'pi durācāro niṣkāmo'dya bhaviṣyati \|*  
*vinākāmena ca kathaṃ pāpamācarate naraḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*tasmātkāmo mayā dagdhaḥ sarveṣāṃ śāṃtihetave \|*  
*yuṣmābhiśca suraiḥ sarvairasuraiśca maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*anyaiḥ prāṇibhirevātra tapase dhīyatāṃ manaḥ \|*  
*kāmakrodhavihīnaṃ ca jagatsarvaṃ mayā kṛtam \|\| 87 \|\|*

*tasmādenaṃ pāpinaṃ duḥkhamūlaṃ na jīvayiṣyāmi surāḥ pratīkṣyatām \|*  
*nirantaraṃ cātmasukhaprabodhamānaṃdalakṣaṇamāgādhamananyarūpam \|\| 88 \|\|*

82-88. Then Maheśvara who was overwhelmed by anger, spoke to Devas: “You must all be without Kāma. It cannot be otherwise.

It was when Kāma was kept at the head, that all the Devas including Vāsava had a fall from their positions. They were overwhelmed by misery and became wretched.

Certainly Kāma is the cause of a fall into hell in the case of all living beings. This Anaṅga (‘Bodiless one’) is an embodiment of misery, understand what I say. Tāraka too whose conduct of life is very bad will be devoid of Kāma. How can a man commit a sin without Kāma? Hence for the sake of peace and calmness unto everyone, Kāma was burned by me. Let the mind be directed towards penance by you all, Suras, Asuras, the great sages and other living beings. The entire universe has been rendered by me rid of love and anger. Hence I will not resuscitate this sinner, the cause of misery, O Suras; keep waiting for that sole form which is not other than (you all), which yields spiritual pleasure and enlightenment and which is characterized by bliss. It is difficult to guage its depth.”

## \|\| 1.21.89 \|\|

*evamuktāstadā tena śaṃbhunā parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*ūcurmaharṣayaḥ sarve śakara lokaśaṃkaram \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. On being told thus by Śaṃbhu Parameṣṭhin, all the great sages spoke to Śaṅkara, the benefactor of all the worlds:

## \|\| 1.21.90 \|\|

*yaduktaṃ bhavatā śaṃbho paraṃ śreyaskaraṃ hi naḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tu vakṣyāma deveśa śrūyatāṃ cāvadhāryatām \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. “What has been said by Your Honour, O Śaṃbhu, is indeed exceedingly conducive to our welfare. But we shall say (something) which may be listened to attentively and comprehended fully.

## \|\| 1.21.91 \|\|

*yathā sṛṣṭamidaṃ viśvaṃ kāmakrodhasamanvitam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ kāmarūpaṃ hi sa kāmo na tu hanyate \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. This universe was permeated by Kāma and Krodha (anger) even while it was being created. Indeed the whole of it is in the form of Kāma. That Kāma is not killed.

## \|\| 1.21.92 \|\|

*dharmārthakāmāmokṣāśca catvāro hyekarūpatām \|*  
*nītāyena mahādeva sa kāmo'yaṃ na hanyate \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. O Mahādeva, it was by Kāma that the four (aims in life) named Dharma (Virtue), Artha (Wealth), Kāma (Love) and Mokṣa (Salvation) have been given a single (composite) form. That Kāma is not killed.

## \|\| 1.21.93 \|\|

*kathaṃ tvayā hi saṃdagdhaḥ kāmo hi duratikramaḥ \|*  
*yena saṃghaṭitaṃ viśvamābrahmasthāvarātmakam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. It was by Kāma that the universe of the nature of everything from Brahmā to an immobile being has been united together. How was that Kāma, very difficult to be tackled indeed, burned by you?

## \|\| 1.21.94 \|\|

*kāmena hīyate viśvaṃ kāmena pālyate \|*  
*kāmenotpadyate viśvaṃ tasmātkāmo mahābalaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The universe decays and declines due to Kāma. The universe is protected and sustained by Kāma. The Universe is produced by Kāma. Hence Kāma is very powerful,

## \|\| 1.21.95 \|\|

*yasmātkrodho bhavatyugro yena tvaṃ ca vaśīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasmātkāmaṃ mahādeva saṃbodhayitumarhasi \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. It is from Kāma that the fierce Krodha (anger) takes its origin. You yourself have been won over by Krodha. Hence, O Mahādeva, it behoves you to resuscitate Kāma.

## \|\| 1.21.96 \|\|

*tvayā saṃpādito deva madano hi mahābalaḥ \|*  
*samartho hi samarthatvāttatsāmarthyaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 96 \|\|*
