10-11. “Obeisance to Lord Bharga (the refulgent god), obeisance to the lord of Devas, to Mṛtyuñjaya (‘conqueror of Death’), to Rudra, to Īśāna (‘controller of the world’), to Kapardin (‘one with matted hair’). Obeisance to the blue-throated (Nīlakaṇṭha), Śarva (‘the destroyer of all’), to the lord having a form with sky as a limb. Obeisance to Kāla, the lord of Kāla; obeisance to the lord in the form of Kāla.”

## \|\| 1.31.12 \|\|

*yamena stūyamāno hi uvāca prabhurīśvaraḥ \|*  
*kimarthamāgato'si tvaṃ tatsarvaṃ kathayasva naḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On being eulogized by Yama, the lord Īśvara said: “Why have you come? Speak everything to us.”

## \|\| 1.31.13 \|\|

*yama uvāca \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ devadeveśa vākya vākyaviśārada \|*  
*tapasā parameṇaiva tuṣṭiṃ prāptosi śaṃkara \|\| 13 \|\|*

Yama said:

13\. May my words be heard, O Lord of Devas, a great expert in the use of words. Only with a great penance, O Śaṅkara, you are (propitiated and) satisfied.

## \|\| 1.31.14 \|\|

*karmaṇā parameṇaiva brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭimeti na saṃdeho varāṇāṃ hi sadā prabhuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, becomes gratified by great holy rites. There is no doubt about it that he is the lord (i.e. and bestower) of boons always.

## \|\| 1.31.15 \|\|

*tathā viṣṇurhi bhagavānvedavedyaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*yajñairanekaiḥ saṃtuṣṭa upavāsavrataistathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. So also Lord Viṣṇu who can be comprehended only through the Vedas and who is the eternal Lord, is delighted by many Yajñas, fasts and other holy rites.

## \|\| 1.31.16 \|\|

*dadāti kevalaṃ bhāvaṃ yena kaivalyamāpnuyuḥ \|*  
*narāḥ sarve mama mataṃ nānyatā hi vaco mama \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He grants Kevalabhāva (‘salvation’) whereby one is liberated. All men (conform to) my opinion. My words cannot be otherwise.

## \|\| 1.31.17 \|\|

*dadāti tuṣṭo vai bhogaṃ tathā svargādisaṃpadaḥ \|*  
*sūryo namasyayā'rogyaṃ dadātīha na cānyathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When he is pleased, he grants all worldly pleasures and the riches of heaven etc. On being bowed down and not otherwise, the Sun-god grants health.

## \|\| 1.31.18 \|\|

*gaṇeśo hi mahādeva arghyapādyādicaṃdanaiḥ \|*  
*maṃtrāvṛttyā tathā śaṃbho nirvighnaṃ ca kariṣyati \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O Śaṃbhu, the great god Gaṇeśa, if we offer Arghya, Pādya etc. and sandal paste and repeat the Mantras duly, makes our task free from obstacles.

## \|\| 1.31.19 \|\|

*tathānye lokapāḥ sarve yathāśaktyā phalapradāḥ \|*  
*yajñādhyayanadānādyaiḥ parituṣṭāśca śaṃkara \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. So also all the other Guardians of the Quarters bestow benefits in accordance with their capacity. O Śaṅkara, they are pleased with Yajñas, study of the Vedas, charitable gifts etc.

## \|\| 1.31.20 \|\|

*mahadāścarya saṃbhūtaṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināmiha \|*  
*kṛtaṃ ca tava putreṇa svargadvāramapāvṛtām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. This has caused a very great surprise to all the living beings here that the gateway to heaven has been opened wide.

## \|\| 1.31.21 \|\|

*darśanācca kumārasya sarve svargaikaso narāḥ \|*  
*pāpino'pi mahādeva jātā nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By the vision of Kumāra, O Mahādeva, even all the sinners have become heaven-dwellers. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.31.22-27 \|\|

*mayā kiṃ kriyatāṃ deva kāryākāryavyavasthitau \|*  
*ye satyaśīlāḥ śāṃtāśca vadānyā niravagrahāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*jiteṃdriyā alubdhāśca kāmarāgavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*yājñikā dharmaniṣṭhāśca vedavedāṃgapāragāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yāṃ gatiṃ yāṃti vai śaṃbho sarve sukṛtinopi hi \|*  
*tāṃ gatiṃ darśanātsarve śvapacā adhamā api \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kumārasya ca deveśa mahadāścaryakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*kārttikyāṃ kṛttikāyogasahitāyāṃ śivasya ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*śivasya tanayaṃ dṛṣṭvā te yāṃti svakulaiḥ saha \|*  
*koṭibhirbahubhiścaiva matsthānaṃ parimucya vai \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kumāradarśanātsarve śvapacā api yāṃti vai \|*  
*sadgatiṃ tvaritenaiva kiṃ kriyeta mayādhunā \|\| 27 \|\|*

22-27. What should be done by me in the matter of deciding what should be done and what should not be done? (Hitherto) only those persons of meritorious deeds, such as those who are habituated to speak the truth, the quiescent ones, liberal donors, free and independent ones, those who have conquered their sense organs, non-covetous ones, those who are devoid of lust and base attachments, the performers of Yajñas, those who abide by righteous deeds and those who have mastered the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas, attained heaven.

O Śaṃbhu, the goal attained by these meritorious persons, is now attained by base men and Cāṇḍālas by the mere vision of Kumāra of wonderfully miraculous activities. O Lord of Devas, by seeing the son of Śiva in the month of Kārttika on the day of Kṛttikā constellation, people attain the good goal along with crores of the members of their family, avoiding my region. By seeing Kumāra, even Cāṇḍālas attain good position immediately. What shall I do?

## \|\| 1.31.28 \|\|

*yamasya vacanaṃ śrutvā śaṃkaro vākyamabravīt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On hearing the words of Yama, Śaṅkara, spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.31.29 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*yeṣāṃ tvaṃtagataṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām \|*  
*viśuddhabhāvo bho dharmma teṣāṃ manasi varttate \|\| 29 \|\|*

Śaṅkara said:

29\. There are good emotions in the minds of the people of meritorious deeds whose sins have come to an end, O Dharma.

## \|\| 1.31.30 \|\|

*sattīrthagamanāyaiva darśanārthaṃ satāmiha \|*  
*vāṃchā ca mahatī teṣāṃ jāyate pūrvakāritā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. There is a great desire in them to go to a good holy spot or to visit good people. This desire is caused by previous Karmas.

## \|\| 1.31.31 \|\|

*bahūnāṃ janmanāmaṃte mayi bhāvo'nuvarttate \|*  
*prāṇināṃ sarvabhāvena janmābhyāsenabho yama \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. It is only at the end of many births and rebirths that a feeling of devotion to me is generated in the minds of living beings. O Yama, it is the result of many repeated experiences in the course of many births with all feelings.

## \|\| 1.31.32 \|\|

*tasmātsukṛtinaḥ sarve yeṣāṃ bhāvo'nuvartte \|*  
*janmajanmānuvṛttānāṃ vismayaṃ naiva kārayet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Hence all those in whom good feelings of devotion arise are meritorious ones. What has been the outcome of the repeated experiences of various births need not cause surprise.

## \|\| 1.31.33 \|\|

*strībālaśūdrāḥ śvapacādhamāśca prāgjanmasaṃskāravaśāddhi dharmma \|*  
*yoniṃ pāpiṣu varttamānāstathāpi śuddhā manujā bhavaṃti \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Women, children, Sūdras \[Śūdras?\], those who cook dog’s flesh (Cāṇḍālas) and base-born fellows who are born among sinners or stay with them become pure persons, O Dharma, due to the impressions of the previous births.

## \|\| 1.31.34-36 \|\|

*tathā sitena manasā ca bhavaṃti sarve sarveṣu caiva viṣayeṣu bhavaṃti tajjñāḥ \|*  
*daivena pūrvacaritena bhavaṃti sarve surāśceṃdrādayo lokapālāḥ prāktanena \|\| 34 \|\|*

*jātā hyamī bhūtagaṇāśca sarve hyamī ṛṣayo hyamī devatāśca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vismayo naiva karttavyastvayā vāpi kumārake \|*  
*kumāradarśane caiva dharmarāja nibodha me \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. They attain white mind (i.e. purity of mind) and through it they derive knowledge in all matters. Due to the previous actions and the working of fate, all become Suras and the Guardians of Quarters beginning with Indra. Those groups of Bhūtas (beings or goblins), these sages and these deities are born in that manner. Even in the case of Kumāra, you need not have any surprise. In connection with the seeing of Kumāra, O Dharmarāja, know from me the following things.

## \|\| 1.31.37 \|\|

*vacanaṃ karmasaṃyuktaṃ sarveṣāṃ phaladāyakam \|*  
*sarvatīrthāni yajñāśca dānāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*kāryāṇi manaḥśuddhyarthaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Words accompanied by action yield fruits to everyone. Pilgrimage to all the holy spots, Yajñas, and different kinds of charitable gifts—all these should be performed for the sake of the purity of mind. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.31.38 \|\|

*manasā bhāvito hyātmā ātmanātmānameva ca \|*  
*ātmā ahaṃ ca sarveṣaāṃ prāṇināṃ hi vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The Ātman is purified through the mind; (one must purify and redeem) the Ātman through the Ātman. I am the (immanent) Soul established in all living beings.

## \|\| 1.31.39 \|\|

*ahaṃ sadā bhāvayukta ātmasaṃstho niraṃtaraḥ \|*  
*jaṃgamājaṃgamānāṃ ca satyaṃ prati vadāmi te \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. I am stationed in the Ātman of all mobile and immobile beings perpetually. I am in yogic communion with them mentally, without anything in between. I am speaking the truth unto you.

## \|\| 1.31.40 \|\|

*dvaṃdvātīto nirvikalpo hi sākṣātsvastho nityo nityayukto nirīhaḥ \|*  
*kūṭastho vai kalpabhedapravādairbahiṣkṛto bodhabodhyo hyanantaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. I am beyond all Dvandvas (i.e. mutually opposed pairs such as pleasure, pain etc.). I am devoid of doubtful alternatives. I am abiding directly in myself. I am eternal. I am in yogic communion perpetually. I am devoid of desire. I am immutable. I am excluded from the controversies of the different Kalpas. I am infinite but can be comprehended by enlightenment.

## \|\| 1.31.41 \|\|

*vismṛtya cainaṃ svātmānaṃ kevalaṃ bodhalakṣaṇam \|*  
*saṃsāriṇo hi dṛśyaṃte samastā jīvarāśayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. All living beings are seen pursuing worldly existence because they have forgotten their Ātman which is single and characterized by enlightenment.

## \|\| 1.31.42 \|\|

*ahaṃ brahmā ca viṣṇuśca trayo'mī guṇakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭipālanasaṃhārakārakā nānyathā bhavet \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. I, Brahmā and Viṣṇu, we three are the causes of Guṇas. We are the causes of creation, sustenance and annihilation. It cannot be otherwise.

## \|\| 1.31.43-46 \|\|

*ahaṃkāravṛtenaiva karmaṇā kāritāvayam \|*  
*yūyaṃ ca sarve vibudhā manuṣyāśca khagādayaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*paśvādayaḥ pṛthagbhūtāstathānye bahavo hyamī \|*  
*pṛthakpṛthaksamīcīnā guṇavataśca saṃsṛtau \|\| 44 \|\|*

*patitā mṛgatṛṣṇāyāṃ māyayā ca vaśīkṛtāḥ \|*  
*vayaṃ sarve ca vibudhāḥ prājñāḥ paṃḍitamāninaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*parasparaṃ dūṣayaṃto mithyāvādaratāḥ khalāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

43-46. We are all caused by the Karma enveloped by Ahaṃkāra (‘Egotism’). You people, all the Devas, human beings, the birds etc., the beasts etc. and many others have separate existence because you all possess these Guṇas. You are scattered in'the ocean of worldly existence. You are fallen in a mirage and you are fascinated and subdued by Māyā. We, all the Devas, profess to be learned, scholarly and wise. We are all rogues engaged in false arguments. We blame and defame each other.

## \|\| 1.31.47 \|\|

*traiguṇā bhavasaṃpannā atattavajñāśca rāgiṇaḥ \|*  
*kāmakrodhabhayadveṣamadamātsaryasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Traiguṇas (i.e. those who come under the control of the three Guṇas) are immersed in the ocean of worldly existence. They are not aware of the reality. They are persons with deep attachment to worldly pleasures. They possess lust, anger, fear, hatred, pride and rivalry.

## \|\| 1.31.48-49 \|\|

*parasparaṃ dūṣayaṃto hyatattvajñā bahirmukhāḥ \|*  
*tasmādevaṃ viditvātha asatyaṃ guṇabhedataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*guṇātīte ca vastvarthe paramārthaikadarśanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. Not conversant with reality, they blame and defame one another. They are extroverts and do not see within themselves. Hence one should understand all these as unreal, being differentiated by Guṇas. They should see the sole ultimate reality in that object which is beyond the Guṇas.

## \|\| 1.31.50 \|\|

*yasminbhedo hyabhedaṃ ca yasminrāgo virāgatām \|*  
*krodho hyakrodhatāṃ yāti tadvāma paramaṃ śrṛṇu \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Hear that it is the greatest abode, wherein difference transforms itself into identity, attachment into absence of attachment and anger into freedom from anger.

## \|\| 1.31.51 \|\|

*na tadbhāsayate śabdaḥ kṛtakatvādyathā ghaṭaḥ \|*  
*śabdo hi jāyate dharmmaḥ pravṛttiparamo yataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Sound does not illuminate it because it is Kṛtaka (a ‘product’, that which is caused) like a Ghaṭa (pot). Indeed, O Dharma, sound is evolved (created) because it is directed towards Pravṛttī (action).

## \|\| 1.31.52 \|\|

*pravṛttiśca nivṛttiśca tathā dvaṃdvāni sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*vilayaṃ yāṃti yatraiva tatsthānaṃ śāśvataṃ matam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The place wherein natural opposite pairs (dvandvas) such as Pravṛttī and Nivṛtti (i.e. manifestation and disappearance or activity and inactivity) merge, is considered eternal.

## \|\| 1.31.53 \|\|

*niraṃtaraṃ nirguṇaṃ jñaptimātraṃ niraṃjanaṃ nirvikāśaṃ nirīham \|*  
*sattāmātraṃ jñānagamyaṃ svasiddhaṃ svayaṃprabhaṃ suprabhaṃ bodhagamyam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. It has nothing intervening in between. It is devoid of Guṇas. It is Jñapti (i.e. pure knowledge) alone. It is unsullied. It is free from aberrations. It is devoid of desires. It is pure existence. It is to be understood only through knowledge. It is self-established, self-luminous, refulgent and comprehensible through enlightenment.

## \|\| 1.31.54 \|\|

*etajjñānaṃ jñānavido vadaṃti sarvātmabhāvena nirīkṣayaṃti \|*  
*sarvātītaṃ jñānagamyaṃ viditvā yena svasthāḥ samabuddhyā caraṃti \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Those who are endowed with perfect knowledge speak of this as Jñāna (‘knowledge’). They observe it in the form of their own self in everyone. After understanding it as something beyond all and comprehensible only through perfect knowledge, they establish themselves in their own self and impartially.

## \|\| 1.31.55 \|\|

*atītya saṃsāramanādimūlaṃ māyāmayaṃ māyayā durvicāryam \|*  
*māyāṃ tyaktvā nirmamā vītarāgā gacchaṃti te pretarāṇinarvikalpam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. They go beyond the worldly existence which has no beginning, which is caused by Māyā and which cannot be deliberated on because of Māyā. O king of the dead ones, after abandoning Māyā they attain the state of freedom from doubts. They are rid of the sense of my-ness and are devoid of attachment.

## \|\| 1.31.56 \|\|

*saṃsṛtiḥ kalpanāmūlaṃ kalpanā hyamṛtopamā \|*  
*yaiḥ kalpanā parityaktā te yāṃti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The worldly existence has (unreal) fictitiousness or fancy (Kalpanā) as its root. Indeed Kalpanā (fictitiousness) is comparable to untruth. Those by whom Kalpanā is eschewed attain the ultimate goal.

## \|\| 1.31.57 \|\|

*śuktyāṃ rajatabuddhiśca rajjubuddhiryarthoraṇe \|*  
*marīcau jalabuddhiśca mithyā mithyaiva nānyathā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The notion of silver (presumed) in an oyster shell, the notion of a rope in a serpent, the notion of water in a mirage—all these are definitely unreal, not otherwise.

## \|\| 1.31.58 \|\|

*siddhiḥ svacchaṃdavarttitvaṃ pārataṃtryaṃ hi vai mṛṣā \|*  
*baddho hi parataṃtrākhyo muktaḥ svātaṃtryabhāvanaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Siddhi (‘spiritual attainment’) is the ability to act as one desires. The unreal thing is dependence. One who is bound is called Paratantra (‘dependent on another’). One who is liberated has the sense of freedom.

## \|\| 1.31.59-62 \|\|

*eko hyātmā viditvātha nirmamo niravagrahaḥ \|*  
*kutasteṣāṃ baṃdhanaṃ ca yathākhe puṣpameva ca \|\| 59 \|\|*

*śaśaviṣāṇamevaitajtrānaṃ saṃsāra eva ca \|*  
*kiṃ kāryaṃ bahunoktena vacasā niṣphalena hi \|\| 60 \|\|*

*mamatāṃ ca nirākṛtya prāptukāmāḥ paraṃ padam \|*  
*jñāninaste hi vidvāṃso vītarāgā jiteṃdriyāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*yaistyakto mamatābhāvo lobhakopau nirākṛtau \|*  
*te yāṃti paramaṃ sthānaṃ kāmakrodhavivarjitāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

59-62. Whence can be bondage to those who, having realized that soul is one, have eschewed the sense of myness and have no external restraints? The bondage (is fictitious and non-existent) like the sky-flower, or the horn of a rabbit. So the worldly existence is unreal. Of what avail is much talk? Of what avail is fruitless blabbing?

Those who are desirous of attaining the greatest region avoid Mamatā (feeling of my-ness or possession). They are the wise ones, the learned ones. They are devoid of attachment and have conquered their sense organs.

Those who have cast off mamatā, those who have eschewed covetousness and anger, attain the greatest region, (as) they are devoid of love and anger.

## \|\| 1.31.63 \|\|

*yāvatkāmaśca lobhaśca rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau \|*  
*nāpnuvaṃti ca tāṃ siddhiṃ śabdamātraikabodhakāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. As long as lust and greed, attachment and hatred persist, they do not attain spiritual beatitude. They will know only the words (of the scriptures).

## \|\| 1.31.64 \|\|

*yama uvāca \|*  
*śabdācchabdaḥ pravartteta niḥśabdaṃ jñānameva ca \|*  
*anityatvaṃ hi śabdasya kathaṃ proktaṃ tvayā prabho \|\| 64 \|\|*

Yama said:

64\. Word comes out of sound; but knowledge is devoid of word (sound). How then was it said by you, O lord, that word is non-eternal?

## \|\| 1.31.65 \|\|

*akṣaraṃ brahmaparamaṃ śabdo vai hyarātmakaḥ \|*  
*tasmācchabdastvayā prokto nirīkṣaka iti śrutam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The greatest Brahman is Akṣara (‘Imperishable’). Word is of the nature of Akṣara (‘syllable’). Hence it is heard that ‘word’ is mentioned by you as Nirīkṣaka (?) (‘that which observes’).

## \|\| 1.31.66 \|\|

*pratipādyaṃ hi yatkiṃcicchabdenaiva vinā katham \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ kathyatāṃ śaṃbho kāryākāryavyavasthitau \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Whatever has to be explained can be explained only through words. How can it be explained without words? Let all these be recounted, O Śaṃbhu, in the matter of deciding what should be done and what should not be done.

Śaṅkara explained:

## \|\| 1.31.67 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*śrṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā paramārdhayutaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*yasya śravaṇamātreṇa jñātavyaṃ nāvaśiṣyate \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Listen attentively to these truthful words (of great meaning). By hearing this nothing that should be known remains (unknown).

## \|\| 1.31.68 \|\|

*jñānapravādinaḥ sarva ṛṣayo vītakalmaṣāḥ \|*  
*jñānābhyāsena varttaṃte jñānaṃ jñānavido viduḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. All the sages expound knowledge. They are devoid of sins. They repeatedly practise knowledge. Those who are conversant with knowledge know what is knowledge.

## \|\| 1.31.69-70 \|\|

*jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ jñātvā ca parigīyate \|*  
*kathaṃ kena ca jñātavyaṃ kiṃ tadvaktuṃ vivakṣitam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*etatsarvaṃ samāsena kathayāmi nibodha me \|*  
*eko hyanekadhā caiva dṛśyate bhedabhāvanaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. It is only after knowing the three (things), viz. (i) knowledge, (ii) object of knowledge and that (iii) which is comprehended and attained, that it can be described how and by whom it should be known and what is it that was intended to be spoken. I shall explain these things succinctly. Understand it from me. The only and single one (i.e. Brahman) appears to be many in the light of difference.

## \|\| 1.31.71 \|\|

*yathā bhramarikādṛṣṭā bhramyate ca mahī yama \|*  
*tathātmā bhedabuddhyā ca pratibhāti hyanekadhā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Just as the ground viewed from a Bhramarikā (‘merry-go-round’) appears to be whirling, O Yama, so also the Ātman appears to be many, due to the idea of difference.

## \|\| 1.31.72-73 \|\|

*tasmādvimṛśya tenaiva jñātavyaḥ śravaṇena ca \|*  
*maṃtavyaḥ suprayogeṇa mananena viśeṣataḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*nirddhārya cātmanātmānaṃ sukhaṃ baṃdhātpramucyate \|*  
*māyājālamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagadetaccārācaram \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. Hence after critically examining it, it should be known through Śravaṇa (‘listening attentively’); it should be meditated upon through close application of the process of Manana (‘deliberation’) in particular.

After comprehending the Ātman, one can easily be released from bondage. This entire universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings is a network of magical delusion.

## \|\| 1.31.74 \|\|

*māyāmayo'yaṃ saṃsāro mamatālakṣaṇo mahān \|*  
*mamatāṃ ca bahiḥ kṛtvā sukhaṃ baṃdhātpramucyate \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. This great extensive worldly existence is full of Māyā characterized by Mamatā (‘sense of my-ness’). After driving out Mamatā one is liberated from bondage easily.

## \|\| 1.31.75 \|\|

*ko'haṃ kastvaṃ kutaścānye mahāmāyāvalaṃbinaḥ \|*  
*ajāgalastanasyeva prapaṃco'yaṃ nirarthakaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Who am I? Who are you? Whence are the others? All these are based on the great Māyā. Just like the fleshy protuberance from the neck of a goat, the entire world is worthless and aimless.

## \|\| 1.31.76 \|\|

*niṣphalo'yaṃ nirābhāso niḥsāro dhūmaḍaṃbaraḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena ātmānaṃ smara vai yama \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. (All) this is fruitless and devoid of permanent appearance. It is a showy mass of smoke without any essence. Hence with all effort, remember the Ātman, O Yama.

## \|\| 1.31.77 \|\|

*lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ pracoditastena śaṃbhunā pretarāṭsvayam \|*  
*buddho bhūtvā yamaḥ sākṣādātmabhūto'bhavattadā \|\| 77 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

77\. Directed thus by Śaṃbhu, the king of the dead ones became enlightened himself and realized the Ātman.

## \|\| 1.31.78 \|\|

*karmmaṇāṃ hi ca sarveṣāṃ śāstā karmānusārataḥ \|*  
*babhūva ḍaṃbaro nṝṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ ca samāhitaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. He became famous as the dispenser absorbed in dispensing the fruits of the Karmas of all men and living beings.

Sages enquired:

## \|\| 1.31.79 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*hatvā tu tārakaṃ yuddhe kumāreṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*ata ūrdhvaṃ kathyatāṃ bhoḥ kiṃ kṛtaṃ mahadadbhutam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. It may be described what highly wonderful feat was accomplished by the noble-souled Kumāra after killing Tāraka in the battle.

Sūta replied:

## \|\| 1.31.80 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*hate tu tārake daitye himavanpramukhādrayaḥ \|*  
*kārttikeyaṃ samāgatya gīrbhī ramyābhiraiḍayan \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. When the Daitya Tāraka was killed, Mountains, the chief of whom was Himavān, approached there and eulogized Kārttikeya with sweet words.

The Mountains prayed:

## \|\| 1.31.81 \|\|

*giraya ūcuḥ \|*  
*namaḥ kalyāṇarūpāya namaste viśvamaṃgala \|*  
*viśvabaṃdho namaste'stu namaste viśvabhāvana \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Obeisance to the lord of auspicious form. We salute you, the cause of auspiciousness unto the universe. Hail to you, O kinsman of the universe; obeisance to you, the sanctifier of the universe.

## \|\| 1.31.82 \|\|

*varīṣṭhāḥ śvapacā yena kṛtā vai darśanāttvayā \|*  
*tvāṃ namāmo jagadbaṃdhuṃ tvāṃ vayaṃ śaraṇāgatāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. We bow down to you by whom, merely through your sight, Cāṇḍālas have been made excellent ones. We seek refuge in you, the sole kinsman of the universe.

## \|\| 1.31.83 \|\|

*namaste pārvatīputra śaṃkarātmaja te namaḥ \|*  
*namaste kṛttikāsūno agnibhūta namostu te \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Hail to you, O son of Pārvatī. Obeisance to you, O son of Śaṅkara. Obeisance to you, O son of Kṛttikās. Obeisance to you who are born of the Fire-god.

## \|\| 1.31.84 \|\|

*namostu te devavaraiḥ supūjya namo'stu te jñānavidāṃ variṣṭha \|*  
*namo'stu te devavara prasīda śaraṇya sarvārtivināśadakṣa \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Obeisance to you, O lord worthy of being worshipped very well by the excellent Devas. Obeisance to you, O lord, the most excellent one among the possessors of perfect knowledge. Obeisance to you, O most excellent one among Devas. Be pleased, O lord worthy of being sought refuge in and competent to destroy all agonies, O Lord.

## \|\| 1.31.85 \|\|

*evaṃ stuto giribhiḥ kārttikeyo hyumāsutaḥ \|*  
*tāngirīnsuprasannātmā varaṃ dātuṃ samutsukaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. On being praised thus by Mountains, Kārttikeya, the son of Umā, was pleased in his mind and became eager to grant them a boon.

## \|\| 1.31.86 \|\|

*kārttikeya uvāca \|*  
*bhobho girivarā yūyaṃ śrṛṇudhvaṃ madvaco'dhunā \|*  
*karmibhirjñānibhiścaiva sevyamānā bhaviṣyatha \|\| 86 \|\|*

Kārttikeya said:

86\. O excellent Mountains, listen to my words now. You will be served (resorted to) by both Karmins (i.e. those who are devoted to holy rites) and Jñānins (i.e. those who are devoted to the path of knowledge).

## \|\| 1.31.87 \|\|

*bhavatsveva hi varttate dṛṣado yatnasevitāḥ \|*  
*punaṃtu viścaṃ vacanānmama tā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Stones served with great effort are found only in you. At my instance, let them purify the universe. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.31.88 \|\|

*parvatīyāni tīrthāni bhaviṣyaṃti na cānyathā \|*  
*śivālayāni divyāni divyānyāyatanāni ca \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. All mountain regions will become holy spots and not otherwise. They will become divine temples of Śiva and other holy shrines.

## \|\| 1.31.89 \|\|

*ayanāni vicitrāṇi śobhanāni mahāṃti ca \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃti na saṃdehaḥ parvatā vacanānmama \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. There is no doubt that at my instance they will become splendid and great pilgrim-spots of various forms.

## \|\| 1.31.90 \|\|

*yo'yaṃ mātāmaho me'dya himavānparvatottamaḥ \|*  
*tapasvināṃ mahābhāgaḥ phalado hi bhaviṣyati \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. This excellent Mountain Himavān who is my maternal grandfather and is highly fortunate, will be the bestower of fruits on ascetics.

## \|\| 1.31.91-94 \|\|

*meruśca girirājo'yamāśrayo hi bhaviṣyati \|*  
*lokāloko girivara udayādrirmahāyaśaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*liṃgarūpo hi bhagavānbhaviṣyati na cānyathā \|*  
*śrīśailo hi maheṃdraśca tathā sahyācalogiriḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*mālyavānmalayo vindhyastathāsau gaṃdhamādanaḥ \|*  
*śvetakūṭastrikūṭo hi tathā darduraparvataḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

*ete cānye ca bahavaḥ parvatā liṃgarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*mama vākyādbhaviṣyaṃti pāpakṣayakarā hyamī \|\| 94 \|\|*

91-94. Mem, this lord of Mountains, will be the support (of all). The excellent Mountain Lokāloka and the Mountain of the Rising Sun, of great fame, will become the lord himself in the form of a Liṅga and not otherwise. The following Mountains will be the destroyers of sins: Śrīśaila, Mahendra, Sahyācala, Mālyavān, Malaya, Vindhya, Gandhamādana, Śvetakūṭa, Trikūṭa and Mountain Dardura. These and many other Mountains are the embodiments of Liṅga. At my instance these will become the destroyers of sins.

## \|\| 1.31.95 \|\|

*evaṃ varaṃ dadau tebhyaḥ parvatebhyaśca śāṃkariḥ \|*  
*tato naṃdīhyuvācātha sarvāgamapuraskṛtam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Thus the son of Śaṅkara granted boons to those Mountains. Then Nandin spoke (to the lord) honoured by all the Āgamas:

## \|\| 1.31.96 \|\|

*naṃdyuvāca \|*  
*tvayā kṛtā hi girayo liṃgarūpiṇa eva te \|*  
*śivālayāḥ kathaṃ nātha pūjyāḥ syuḥsarvadaivataiḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

Nandin said:

96\. O Lord, the Mountains have been made embodiments of Liṅga by you. How should the shrines of Śiva be worshipped by all the Devas?

## \|\| 1.31.97 \|\|

*kumāra uvāca \|*  
*liṃgaṃ śivālayaṃ jñeyaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*sarvairnṛbhirdaivataiśca brahmādibhiratāṃdritaiḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

Kumāra said:

97\. Liṅga should be known as the shrine of Śiva, the trident-bearing lord of Devas. (It should be worshipped) by all human beings and Devas beginning with Brahmā, diligently without any lethargy.

## \|\| 1.31.98-101 \|\|

*nīlaṃ muktā pravālaṃ ca vaiḍūryaṃ caṃdrameva ca \|*  
*gomedaṃ padmarāgaṃ ca mārataṃ kāṃcanaṃ tathā \|\| 98 \|\|*

*rājataṃ tāmramāraṃ ca tathā nāgamayaṃ param \|*  
*ratnadhātumayānyeva liṃgāni kathitāni te \|\| 99 \|\|*

*pavitrāṇyeva pūjyāni sarvakāmapradāni ca \|*  
*eteṣāmapi sarveṣāṃ kāśmīraṃ hi viśiṣyate \|\| 100 \|\|*

*aihikāmuṣmikaṃ sarvaṃ pūjākartuḥ prayacchati \|\| 101 \|\|*

98-101. Liṅgas made of sapphire, pearls, coral, lapis lazuli, lunar stone, Gomeda, ruby, emeralds, gold, silver, copper, brass and zinc, Liṅgas made of precious stones and metal have been described to you. Only the pure ones should be worshipped. They are the bestowers of all desired objects. Among all these (that made in) Kāśmīra is the most excellent one. It gives all pleasures of this world and the next one to the devotee who worships.

## \|\| 1.31.102 \|\|

*naṃdyuvāca \|*  
*liṃgānāmapi pūjyaṃ syādbāṇaliṃgaṃ tvayā katham \|*  
*kathitaṃ cottamatvena tatsarvaṃ vadasuvrata \|\| 102 \|\|*

Nandī said:

102\. How is it that you have told that Bāṇa-liṅga is the most excellent and worthy of being worshipped? Explain everything, O Lord of holy rites.

## \|\| 1.31.103 \|\|

*kumāra uvāca \|*  
*revāyāṃ toyamadhye ca dṛśyaṃte dṛṣado hi yāḥ \|*  
*śivaprasādāttāstu syurliṃgarūpā na cānyathā \|\| 103 \|\|*

Kumāra said:

103\. The stones that are seen in the waters in the middle of the river Revā, shall be in the form of Liṅga, by the favour of Śiva and not otherwise.

## \|\| 1.31.104-106 \|\|

*ślakṣṇamūlāśca kartavyāḥ piṃḍikopari saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*pūjanīyāḥ prayatnena śivadīkṣāyutena hi \|\| 104 \|\|*

*piṃḍīyuktaṃ ca śāstreṇa vidhinā ca yajecchivam \|*  
*varado hi jagannāthaḥ pūjakasya na cānyathā \|\| 105 \|\|*

*paṃcākṣarī yasya mukhe sthitā sadā cetonivṛttiḥ śivaciṃtane ca \|*  
*bhūteṣuḥ sāmyaṃ parivādamūkatā ṣaṃḍhatvameva parayoṣitāsu \|\| 106 \|\|*

104-106. Their roots should be made smooth and placed over the Piṇḍikā (‘pedestal’). They should be scrupulously worshipped by one who has the initiation called Śīvadīkṣā.

One shall worship Śiva joined to the Piṇḍī in accordance with the injunctions of the scriptures.

The Lord of the universe should bestow boons on the worshipper, not otherwise.

The five-lettered Mantra should always be in the mouth (of the worshipper); the mind should be directed towards the contemplation on Śiva; he must have impartiality towards all living beings. He should be dumb in giving expression to slander. He should be an impotent fellow in regard to other men’s wives.

## Chapter 32 - The Burning of Kāla

## \|\| 1.32.1 \|\|

*\| lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ te śivadharmāśca kathitāstena vai dvijāḥ \|*  
*saviśeṣāḥ pāśupatāḥ prasādāccaiva vistarāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: This chapter illustrates Śiva’s kindness and alertness in protecting his devotees. Kāla, the supreme destroyer of the world, was burnt down by Śiva in order to protect his devotee, King Śveta, and he was resuscitated at the request of the victim-King.

Lomaśa said:

1\. Thus all the rites pertaining to the worship of Śiva (Śiva-dharmāḥ) were narrated by him, O Brāhmaṇas. It was out of grace that the Pāśupata doctrines were explained in details in particular.

## \|\| 1.32.2 \|\|

*anekāgamasaṃvītā yathātattvamudāhṛtāḥ \|*  
*kāpālikānāṃ bhedāśca proktā vyāsasamāsataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Doctrines enshrined in various Āgamas were declared truthfully in accordance with the principles. The different sects of Kāpālikas were described succinctly as well as in details.

## \|\| 1.32.3 \|\|

*dharmā nānāvidhāḥ proktā naṃdinaṃ prati vai tadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Various kinds of holy rites were recounted to Nandin then.

## \|\| 1.32.4 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*śrutaṃ kumāracaritamaviśeṣaṃ sumaṃgalam \|*  
*asmābhiśca mahābhāgakiṃcitpṛcchāmahe vayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:

4\. The highly auspicious story of Kumāra which has nothing to surpass it, has been completely heard by us, O highly fortunate one. We shall enquire of something more.

## \|\| 1.32.5 \|\|

*śvetasya rājasiṃhasya caritaṃ paramādbhutam \|*  
*yena saṃtoṣito rudraḥ śivo bhaktyā'prameyayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The narrative of the leonine king Śveta is wonderfully mysterious. By means of his boundless devotion, Śiva-Rudra has been gratified by him.

## \|\| 1.32.6 \|\|

*te bhaktāste mahātmāno jñāninaste ca karmiṇaḥ \|*  
*ye'rcayaṃti mahāśaṃbhuṃ devaṃ bhaktyā samāvṛtāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Those who worship Lord Mahāśaṃbhu devoutly, are great devotees of noble souls. They are experts both in the path of spiritual knowledge (Jñāna) and of religious rites (Karman),

## \|\| 1.32.7 \|\|

*tasmātpṛcchāmahe sarve caritaṃ śaṃkarasya ca \|*  
*vyāsaprasādātsarvaṃ yajjānāsi tvaṃ na cāparaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence all of us enquire of you about the story of Śaṅkara as you and none else know everything through the favour of Vyāsa.

## \|\| 1.32.8 \|\|

*niśamya vacanaṃ teṣāṃ munīnāṃ lomaśo'bravīt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On hearing the words of those sages, Lomaśa said:

## \|\| 1.32.9 \|\|

*lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*ākarṇyatāṃ mahābhāgāścaritaṃ paramādbhutam \|*  
*tasya rājño hi bhajato rājabhogāṃśca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*matirddhirme samutpannā śvetasya ca mahātmanaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

9\. Let that wonderful anecdote be listened to, O highly fortunate ones. Even as that king was enjoying all sorts of royal pleasures, the mind of that noble-souled Śveta was directed towards virtue and piety.

## \|\| 1.32.10 \|\|

*pṛthivīṃ pālayāmāsa prajā dharmeṇa pālayan \|*  
*brahmaṇyaḥ satyavākchūraḥ śivabhakto niraṃtaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He protected the subjects righteously and ruled the earth. He was heroic and truthful in speech. He was well-versed in the Vedas. He was a constant and faithful devotee of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.32.11 \|\|

*rājyaṃ śaśāsātha sa śaktito nṛpo bhaktyā tadā caiva samarcayatsadā \|*  
*śaṃbhuṃ pareśaṃ paramaṃ parātparaṃ śāṃtaṃ purāṇaṃ paramātmarūpam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. That king administered the kingdom in accordance with his capacity. With devotion, he always worshipped Śaṃbhu, the great lord, the Supreme Being, greater than the greatest, the quiescent one, the ancient lord in the form of the Supreme Spirit.

## \|\| 1.32.12-14 \|\|

*āyustasya parikṣīṇamarcataḥ parameśvaram \|*  
*athaitacca mahābhāga caritaṃ śrūyatāṃ mama \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vāṇī śivakathāyuktā paramāścaryasaṃyutā \|*  
*na vā'dhayo hi tasyaiva vyādhayo hi mahīpateḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tasya rājño na bādhaṃte tathā copadravāstvamī \|*  
*nirītiko jano hyāsīnnirupadrava eva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. His whole life was spent in worshipping the Supreme Lord. Let the story of this highly fortunate (king) be listened to. My words cover Śiva’s story and are full of wonders. Neither mental agonies nor physical ailments harassed the king. No natural calamity afflicted him. The people were free from all the Ītis (i.e. abnormal calamitous phenomena such as excessive rain, drought etc.) and were devoid of afflicting distresses.

## \|\| 1.32.15 \|\|

*akṛṣṭapacyauṣadhayastasya rājño'bhavanbhuvi \|*  
*tapasvino brāhmaṇāśca varṇāśramayutā janāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In the realm of that king medicinal herbs grew naturally without being cultivated. Ascetics and Brāhmaṇas and common people adhered to the discipline of the four castes and stages of life.

## \|\| 1.32.16 \|\|

*na putramaraṇe duḥkhaṃ nāpamānaṃ na mārakāḥ \|*  
*na dāridryaṃ ca te sarve prāpnuvanti kadācana \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. No one had, at any time, the misery due to the death of a son. No one was insulted. There were no deadly (diseases). No one ever suffered from poverty.

## \|\| 1.32.17 \|\|

*evaṃ bahutaraḥ kālastasya rājño mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*gato hi saphalo viprāḥ śivapūjāratasya vai \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thus a great deal of time passed even as that noble-souled king successfully engaged himself in the worship of Śiva, O Brāhmaṇās.

## \|\| 1.32.18-19 \|\|

*ekadā pūjamānaṃ taṃ śaṃkaraṃ paramārthadam \|*  
*yamo hi preṣayāmāsa yamadūtānnṛpaṃ prati \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vacanāccitraguptasya śveta ānīyatāmiti \|*  
*tatheti matvā te dūtā āgatāḥ śivamaṃdiram \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Once, Yama sent his messengers to that king who was worshipping Śaṅkara, the bestower of the greatest aim in life (i.e. salvation). At the instance of Citragupta, the messengers were deputed and instructed, “Let Śveta be brought.” Thinking that it should be so, the messengers came to the temple of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.32.20 \|\|

*rājānaṃ netukāmāste pāśahastā mahābhayāḥ \|*  
*yāvatsamāgatā yāmyā rājānaṃ dadṛśustvarāt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Desirous of taking the king away, the messengers of Yama who had nooses in their hands and were very frightful, came there and looked for the king hurriedly.

## \|\| 1.32.21-23 \|\|

*na cakrire tadā dūtā ājñāṃ dharmasya caiva hi \|*  
*jñātvā sarvaṃ yamaścaiva āgataḥ svayameva hi \|\| 21 \|\|*

*uddhṛtya daṃḍaṃ sahasā netukāmastadā nṛpam \|*  
*dadarśa ca mahābāhuḥ śivadhyānaparāyaṇam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śivabhaktiyutaṃ śāṃtaṃ kevalaṃ jñānasaṃyutam \|*  
*yamo'pi dṛṣṭvā rājānaṃ paraṃ kṣobhamupāgamat \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Then the messengers could not carry out the command of Dharma. After knowing this, Yama himself came there. He suddenly lifted up his baton and was desirous of taking the king away. The deity of great arms saw the king engaged in the meditation of Śiva. He was endowed with great devotion to Śiva. He was qui escent and possessed of pure spiritual knowledge. On seeing the king, Yama became highly excited.

## \|\| 1.32.24-26 \|\|

*citrastho hyabhavatsdyaḥ pretarājo'tivihvalaḥ \|*  
*kālarūpaśca yo nityaṃ prajānāṃ kṣayakārakaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*āgatastatkṣaṇādeva nṛpaṃ prati ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*khaḍgena sitadhāreṇa carmaṇā paramema hi \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tāvattaṃ dadṛśe so'pi sthitaṃ dvāri bhayāvṛtam \|*  
*uvāca kālo hi tadā yamaṃ vaivasvataṃ prati \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. Immediately the king of dead ones became excessively agitated and remained (motionless) as though he was painted in a picture.

The deity who in the form of Kāla, caused perpetual destruction of the subjects, came very furiously to that king at that very same instant. (He was armed) with a sword of very sharp edge and a big shield.

He (Yama) overwhelmed by fear was standing at the entrance. Kāla spoke to Yama, the son of the Sun:

## \|\| 1.32.27-28 \|\|

*kasmāttvayā dharamarāja no nīto'yaṃ nṛpo mahān \|*  
*yama dūtasahāyaśca bhītavatpratibhāsi me \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kālātyayo na karttavyo vacanānmama suvrata \|*  
*kālenoktastadā dharma uvāca prastutaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. “Why was this great king not taken away by you, O Dharmarāja? O Yama, (though) you are assisted by your messengers, you appear to me to be frightened. Do not delay, O deity of good holy rites. At my instance do everything quickly).”

On being told thus by Kāla, Dharma spoke these words befitting the occasion:

## \|\| 1.32.29 \|\|

*tavājñāṃ ca kariṣyāmi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*asau huratyayo'smākaṃ śivabhakto niraṃtaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “I shall do according to your command. There is no doubt about this. This devotee of Śiva caṇnot be tackled by us.

## \|\| 1.32.30 \|\|

*citrasthā iva tiṣṭhāma bhayāddevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*yamasya vacanaṃ śrutvā kālaḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*rājānaṃ haṃtumārebhe tvaritaḥ khaḍgamādade \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Due to fear from the Trident-bearing Lord, we stand (motionless) as though painted in a picture.”

On hearing Yama’s words, Kāla became infuriated. Hurriedly he took up the sword intending to kill the king.

## \|\| 1.32.31-36 \|\|

*triguṇāṣṭākrasaṃkāśaṃ praviveśa śivālayam \|*  
*yāvatkopena mahatā tāvaddṛṣṭaḥ pinākinā \|*  
*svabhaktaṃ haṃtukāmosau śvetarājānamuttamam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*dhyānasthitaṃ cātmani taṃ viśuddhajñānapradīpena viśuddhacittam \|*  
*ātmānamātmātmatayā niraṃtaraṃ svayaṃprakāśaṃ paramaṃ purastāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

*evaṃvidhaṃ taṃ prasamīkṣya kālaṃ saṃciṃtyamānaṃ manasā'calena \|*  
*śaivaṃ padaṃ yatparamārtharūpaṃ kaivalyasāyujyakaraṃ svarūpataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sadāśivena dṛṣṭo'sau kālaḥ kālāṃtakena ca \|*  
*ucchṛṃkhalaḥ khalo darpādviśamāno nijāṃtike \|\| 34 \|\|*

*naṃdikeśvaramadhyastho yāvaddṛṣṭo nijāṃtike \|*  
*śivena jagadīśena bhaktavatsalabaṃdhunā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nirīkṣitastṛtīyena cakṣuṣā parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*svabhaktaṃ rakṣamāṇena bhasmasādabhavatkṣaṇāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

31-36. As he furiously entered the temple of Śiva, resembling twenty-four Suns, he was seen by Śiva, the Pināka-bearing Lord (who thought): ‘This (deity) is desirous of killing my devotee, the excellent king Śveta. He is absorbed in his own soul by way of meditation. His mind has become purified by the bright light of pure knowledge. Without any differentiation he meditates upon his Ātman in the form of the innermost Ātman. He is self-luminous. He is greater than the greatest standing in front of him. The king is thinking about the foot of Śiva who is of the nature of the Supreme Being, the cause of salvation and complete identity in form.’ Kāla was rushing at him and was seen by Sadāśiva, the slayer of Kāla. The rogue was approaching him undeterred arrogantly. When he was seen midway between himself and Nandikeśvara by Śiva, the lord of the universe, the affectionate kinsman of devotees, he was stared at with the third eye by the great Lord who wanted to protect his devotee. He became reduced to ash in an instant.

## \|\| 1.32.37 \|\|

*dadāha taṃ kālamanekavarṇaṃ vyāttānanaṃ bhīmabahūgrarūpam \|*  
*jvālāvalībhiḥ paridahyamānamatipracaṃḍaṃ bhuvanaikabhakṣaṇam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He burned Kāla who had many colours, who had opened his month very wide, whose form was extremely terrible and frightening, whose sole food was the universe and who was very fierce. He was burned by a series of flames.

## \|\| 1.32.38-40 \|\|

*dadarśire devagaṇāḥ sametāḥ sayakṣagaṃdharvapiśācaguhyakāḥ \|*  
*siddhāpsaraḥsarvakhagāśca pannagāḥ patatriṇo lokapālāstathaiva \|\| 38 \|\|*

*jvālāmālāvṛtaṃ kālamīśvarasyāgrataḥ sthitam \|*  
*labdhasaṃjñastadā rājā kālaṃ svaṃ haṃtumāgatam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*punaḥ punarddadarśātha dahyamānaṃ kṛśānunā \|*  
*prārthayāmāsa sa vyagro rudraṃ kālāgnisannibham \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. The groups of Devas who had gathered together along with Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Piśācas, Guhyakas, Siddhas, groups of celestial damsels, all the sky-walkers, serpents, birds and the Guardians of Quarters, saw Kāla enveloped in flames and stationed in front of Īśvara.

The king then regained consciousness and looked again and again at Kāla who had come to kill him and who was then being burnt by fire. Without being excited, he prayed to Rudra who resembled the fire of Kāla:

## \|\| 1.32.41 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*namo rudrāya śāṃtāya svajyotsnāyātmavedhase \|*  
*niraṃtarāya sūkṣmāya jyotiṣāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

The king said:

41\. Obeisance to Rudra the quiescent one, who is the moonlight unto himself, is the creator of himself, who is perpetual and subtle. I bow to the lord of the luminaries.

## \|\| 1.32.42 \|\|

*trātā tvaṃ hi jagannātha pitā mātā suhṛtsakhā \|*  
*tvameva baṃdhuḥ svajano lokānāṃ prabhurīśvaraḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. You alone are indeed the saviour, O Lord of the universe. You are the father, mother, friend and comrade. You alone are the kinsman and relative. You are Īśvara, the lord of people and of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.32.43 \|\|

*kiṃ kṛtaṃ hi tvayā śaṃbho ko'sau dagdho mamāgrataḥ \|*  
*na jānāmi ca kiṃ jātaṃ kṛtaṃ kena mahattaram \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. What has been done by you, O Śaṃbhu? Who is this who has been burned in front of me? I do not know what has taken place here; what great thing has been carried out and by whom.

## \|\| 1.32.44 \|\|

*evaṃ prārthayatastasya śrutvā ca paridevanam \|*  
*uvāca śaṃkaro vākyaṃ bodhayanniva taṃ nṛpam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On hearing this expression of the pain of that (king) who was praying thus, Śaṅkara spoke these words enlightening that king:

## \|\| 1.32.45 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*mayā dagdho hyayaṃ kālastavārthe ca tavāgrataḥ \|*  
*dahyamāno hi dṛṣṭaste jvālā mālākulo mahān \|\| 45 \|\|*

Rudra said:

45\. This Kāla was burnt by me in front of you for your sake. He was seen being burnt and overwhelmed by a great mass of flames.

## \|\| 1.32.46 \|\|

*evamuktastadā tena śaṃbhunā rājasattamaḥ \|*  
*uvāca praśrito bhūtvā vacanaṃ śivamagrataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On being told thus by Śaṃbhu that excellent king became humble before Śiva and spoke these words to him:

## \|\| 1.32.47 \|\|

*kimanena kṛtaṃ śaṃbho akṛtyaṃ vada tattvataḥ \|*  
*ya imāṃ prāptito'vasthāṃ prāṇātyayakarīṃ bhava \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “What misdeed has been committed by this (Kāla), O Śaṃbhu? Tell me exactly. O Bhava, what for has he been reduced to this plight, ending with his death?”

## \|\| 1.32.48 \|\|

*evaṃ vijñāpitastena hyuvāca parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*bhakṣako'yaṃ mahārāja sarveṣāṃ prāṇināmiha \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On being requested by him the Supreme Lord said: “O great king, he is one who swallows all living beings.

## \|\| 1.32.49 \|\|

*bhakṣaṇārthaṃ tava vibho so'yaṃ krūro'dhunā'gataḥ \|*  
*mamāṃtikaṃ mahārāja tasmāddagdho mayā vibho \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O lord, it was for the purpose of swallowing you that this cruel one had come near me now. Hence, O lord, O great king, he was burnt by me.

## \|\| 1.32.50-51 \|\|

*bahūnāṃ kṣemamanvicchaṃstavārthe'nhaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*ye pāpino hyadharmiṣṭhā lokasaṃhārakārakāḥ \|*  
*pāṣaṃḍavādasaṃyuktā vadhyāste mama caiva hi \|*  
*vākyaṃ niśamya rudrasya śveto vacanamabravīt \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Desiring the welfare of many persons, I have killed him particularly.

Those who are sinners, those who engage themselves in unrighteous activities, those who cause the annihilation of the worlds and those who propagate heretic doctrines—all these are to be killed by me.”

Oṇ hearing the words of Rudra, Śveta spoke thus:

## \|\| 1.32.52-53 \|\|

*kālenaiva hi loko'yaṃ puṇyamācarate sadā \|*  
*dharmaniṣṭhāśca kecittu bhaktyā paramayā yutāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*upāsanāratāḥ kecijjñānino hi tathā pare \|*  
*kecidadhyātmasaṃyuktāścānye muktāśca kecana \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. “It is on account of Kāla that the whole world always performs meritorious deeds: Some abide by righteous activities; some are endowed with great devotion; some are engaged in Upāsanas (‘devotional rites’); others become Jñānins (‘possessors of knowledge’); some practise spiritual pursuits; and some are liberated,

## \|\| 1.32.54 \|\|

*kālo hi hartā ca carācarāṇāṃ tathā hyasau pālako'pyadvitīyaḥ \|*  
*sa sraṣṭā vai prāṇināṃ prāṇabhūtastasmādenaṃ jīvayasvāśu bhūyaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Indeed Kāla is the annihilator of all mobile and immobile beings. Similarly, he is the matchless protector too (of all). He is the creator as well of the vital air of all living beings. Hence revive him back to life.

## \|\| 1.32.55-56 \|\|

*yadi sṛṣṭiparo'si tvaṃ kālaṃ jīvaya satvaram \|*  
*yadi saṃhārabhūto'si sarveṣāṃ prāṇināmiha \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tarhyevaṃ kuru śaṃbho tvaṃ kālasya ca mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*vinā kālena yatkiṃcidbhaviṣyati na śaṃkara \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. If you are intent on creation, resuscitate Kāla quickly. If you are inclined to annihilate all living beings, then (revive him) and give this work, O Śaṃbhu, to the noble-souled Kāla. Without Kāla nothing will take place, O Śaṅkara.”

## \|\| 1.32.57 \|\|

*iti vijñāpitastena rājñā śaṃbhuḥ pratāpinā \|*  
*cakāra vacanaṃ tasya bhaktasya ca cikīrṣitam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On being requested thus by that valorous king, Śaṃbhu carried out his suggestion. He did what his devotee desired (him) to do.

## \|\| 1.32.58 \|\|

*śaṃbhuḥ prahasyātha tadā maheśaḥ saṃjīvayāmāsa pinākapāṇiḥ \|*  
*cakāra rūpaṃ ca yathā purāsīdāliṃgatosau yamadūtamadhye \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Śaṃbhu, the great Pināka-bearing Lord, resuscitated him and made his form as it had been before. He was then fixed by him in his place, in the middle of the messengers of Yama.

## \|\| 1.32.59 \|\|

*upasthito'sau tvatha lajjamānastuṣṭāva devaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajaṃ tam \|*  
*natvā puraḥsthāgnimayaṃ hi kālaḥ savismayo vākyamidaṃ babhāṣe \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Approaching (the Lord) with shyness, he eulogized the Bull-bannered Lord. After bowing down to the fire stationed in front, this Kāla spoke these words in great dismay:

## \|\| 1.32.60 \|\|

*kāla uvāca \|*  
*kālāṃtaka tripureśa tripurāṃtakara prabho \|*  
*madano hi tvayā deva kṛto'naṃgo jagatpate \|\| 60 \|\|*

Kāla said:

60\. O slayer of Kāla, O lord of Tripura, O destroyer of the three Puras. Indeed Madana was made Anaṅga (bodiless) by you, O lord of the universe.

## \|\| 1.32.61-62 \|\|

*dakṣayajñavināśaśca kṛto hi paramādbhutaḥ \|*  
*kālakūṭaṃ duḥprasahaṃ sarveṣāṃ kṣayakṛnmahat \|\| 61 \|\|*

*grasitaṃ tattvayā śaṃbho anyeṣāmapi durddharam \|*  
*liṃgarūpeṇa mahatā vyāptamāsījjagattrayam \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. A very wonderful feat was perfromed by you in destroying the sacrifice (Yajña) of Dakṣa. Kālakūṭa, the poison, unbearable to everyone, the great poison that caused destruction of all, was swallowed by you, O Śaṃbhu, as it was unbearable to all. The whole range of the three worlds was pervaded in the form of Liṅga by the great lord.

## \|\| 1.32.63 \|\|

*layanālliṃgamityuktaṃ sarvairapi surā suraiḥ \|*  
*yasyāṃtaṃ na vidurddevā brahmaviṣṇupurogamāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. It is called Liṅga by all the Suras and Asuras because it absorbs the world within it. Devas with Brahmā and Viṣṇu at their head do not know its limits and extremities.

## \|\| 1.32.64 \|\|

*liṃgasya devadevasya mahimānaṃ parasya ca \|*  
*namaste parameśāya namaste viśvamaṃgala \|*  
*namaste śitikaṇṭhāya namastasmai kapardine \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. They do not know the greatness of the Liṅga as well as the great lord of Devas.

Hail to you, the Supreme Lord. Obeisance to you, O cause of the auspiciousness of the universe. I bow to you, the blue-throateded one; I salute that lord with matted hair.

## \|\| 1.32.65 \|\|

*namonamaḥ kāraṇakāraṇāya te namonamo maṃgalamaṃgalātmane \|*  
*jñānātmane jñānavidāṃ manīṣiṇāṃ tvamādidevo'si pumānpurāṇaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Repeated obeisance to you, the cause of causes. Salutations to you, the auspicious soul of all auspicious things. Obeisance to the lord in the form of knowledge of all the learned ones conversant with knowledge. You are the primordial God. You are the ancient Puruṣa.

## \|\| 1.32.66 \|\|

*tvameva sarvaṃ jagadevabaṃdho vedāṃtavedyo'si mahānubhāvaḥ \|*  
*mahānubhāvaiḥ parikīrttanīyastvameva viśveśvara viśvamānyaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. You are everything, O sole kinsman of the universe. You can be comprehended only through the Vedāntas; you are of exalted magnanimity; you are worthy of being glorified by all magnanimous persons. You alone are honoured by the whole universe, O lord of the universe.

## \|\| 1.32.67 \|\|

*tvaṃ pāsi luṃpasi jagattritayaṃ maheśa sraṣṭāsi bhūtapatireva na kaścidanyaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. You protect; you annihilate all the three worlds, O great lord. You are the creator. You and none else, are the lord of all living beings.

## \|\| 1.32.68 \|\|

*iti stutastadā tena kālena jagadīśvaraḥ \|*  
*uvāca kālo rājānaṃ śvetaṃ saṃbodhayanniva \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Thus the lord of the universe was eulogized by Kāla.

Kāla then said to king Śveta enlightening him as it were:

## \|\| 1.32.69 \|\|

*kāla uvāca \|*  
*manuṣyaloke sakale nānyastvatto hi vidyate \|*  
*yena tvayā jito devo hyajeyo bhuvanatraye \|\| 69 \|\|*

Kāla said:

69\. In the whole of the mortal world, there is no one greater than you by whom the lord who is invincible in all the three worlds, has been conquered.

## \|\| 1.32.70 \|\|

*mayā hatamidaṃ viśvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram \|*  
*jetāhaṃ sarvadevānāṃ sarveṣāṃ duratikramaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. This universe of the mobile and immobile beings has been killed by me. I am the conqueror of all the Devas. I cannot be transgressed by anyone.

## \|\| 1.32.71 \|\|

*sa hi te cānugo jāto mahārāja prayaccha me \|*  
*abhayaṃ devadevācca śūlinaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. I have now become your follower, O great king. Grant me protection from fear of the trident-bearing Parameṣṭhin, the lord of the Devas.

## \|\| 1.32.72 \|\|

*evamuktastadā tena śvetaḥ kālena caiva hi \|*  
*uvāca prahasanvācā meghanādagabhīrayā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. On being addressed thus by Kāla, Śveta laughingly spoke in a voice as majestic as the sound of clouds:

## \|\| 1.32.73 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*śivasya paramaṃ rūpaṃ tvameko nāsti saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kālastvamasi bhūtānāṃ sthitisaṃhārarūpavān \|\| 73 \|\|*

The King said:

73\. There is no doubt about this that you are the greatest form of Śiva. You are Kāla in the form of sustenance and annihilation of all living beings.

## \|\| 1.32.74 \|\|

*tasmātpūjyatamo'si tvaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca niyāmakaḥ \|*  
*tvadbhayātkṛtinaḥ sarve śaraṇaṃ parameśvaram \|*  
*vrajaṃti vividhairbhārvairātmalakṣaṇatatparāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Hence you are the most adorable of all. You are the controller of all. It is on account of their fear of you that all those who perform rites seek refuge in Parameśvara with various emotional feelings, desirous of dedicating themselves.

## \|\| 1.32.75-76 \|\|

*suta uvāca \|*  
*tenaivaṃ rakṣitataḥ kālo rājñā paramadharmiṇā \|*  
*śivaprasādamātreṇa labdhasaṃjño babhūvaha \|\| 75 \|\|*

*tadā yamena stavito mṛtyunā yamadūtakaiḥ \|*  
*śivaṃ praṇamya saṃstutya śvetaṃ rājānameva ca \|*  
*yayau svamālayaṃ viprā mene svaṃ janitaṃ punaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

Sūta said:

75-76. Kāla who was thus saved by the excessively righteous king regained consciousness by the grace of Śiva alone. The lord was eulogized by Yama in the company of Mṛtyu and messengers of Yama.

After bowing down and praising Śiva and the king Śveta, (Kāla) went to his abode, O Brāhmaṇas. He considered himself as born once again.

## \|\| 1.32.77 \|\|

*māyayā saha patnyā ca śivasya caritaṃ mahat \|*  
*anusaṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya vismayaṃ paramaṃ yayau \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. In the company of his wife Māyā, he frequently recollected the great story of Śiva and became surprised more and more-

## \|\| 1.32.78-79 \|\|

*kathayāmāsa sarveṣāṃ dūtānāṃ svayameva hi \|*  
*ākarṇyatāṃ mama vaco he dūtāstvaritena hi \|\| 78 \|\|*

*karttavyaṃ ca prayatnena nānyathā mama bhāṣitam \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. He said to all the messengers himself: “O messengers, let my words be heard quickly; what I suggest in my speech should be carried out scrupulously. It should not be otherwise.”

Kāla instructed:

\[2\]

## \|\| 1.32.80-83 \|\|

*kāla uvāca \|*  
*ye tripuṇḍraṃdhārayaṃti tathā ye vai jaṭādharāḥ \|*  
*ye rudrākṣadharāścaiva tathā ye śivanāminaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*upajīvanahetośca bhiyā ye hyapi mānavāḥ \|*  
*pāpino'pi durācārāḥ śivaveṣadharā hyamī \|\| 81 \|\|*

*nānetavyā bhavadbhiśca mama lokaṃ kadācana \|*  
*varjyāste hi prayatnena pāpino'pi sadaiva hi \|\| 82 \|\|*

*anyeṣāṃ kā kathā dūtā ye'rcayaṃti sadāśivam \|*  
*bhaktyā paramayā śaṃbhuṃ rudrāste nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

80-83. The following persons should never be brought to my region: Those who apply Tripuṇḍra (upon their forehead); those who have matted hair; those who wear Rudrākṣa; those who are called by the names of Śiva; those who assume the guise of the men of Śaiva cult either for the sake of livelihood or out of fear; even men who have committed sins or practised evil conduct if they are wearing Śaiva garments. All these should never be brought to my region by you. They should be scrupulously avoided even if they are always sinful. What then about others, O messengers—others who worship Sadāśiva, Śaṃbhu, with great devotion? They are undoubtedly Rudras themselves.

## \|\| 1.32.84 \|\|

*rudrākṣamekaṃ śirasā bibharti yastathā tripuṃḍraṃ ca lalāṭamadhyake \|*  
*paṃcākṣarīṃ ye prajapaṃti sādhavaḥ pūjya bhavadbhiśca na cānyathā kvacit \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. He who wears even a single Rudrākṣa on his head and the Tripuṇdra mark in the middle of the forehead, the good persons who repeat the five-syllabled Mantra—these are to be honoured by you all and never otherwise.

## \|\| 1.32.85 \|\|

*yasminrāṣṭro'tha vā deśe grāme cāpi vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*śivabhakto na dṛśyeta smaśānāttu viśiṣyate \|*  
*tadrāṣṭraṃ deśamityāhuḥ satyaṃ prativadāmi vaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The nation, the country or the village where no wise devotee of Śiva is seen—is it different from a cremation ground? They (may) call that nation (rāṣṭra) deśa—a small place. I speak the truth unto you.

## \|\| 1.32.86 \|\|

*yasminna saṃti nityaṃ hi śivabhaktisamanvitāḥ \|*  
*tadgramasthā janāḥ sarve śāsanīyā na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. The persons in that village where there exist no persons who practise devotional rites of Śiva, should be chastised well.

## \|\| 1.32.87 \|\|

*evamājñāpayāmāsa yamo'pi nijakiṃkarān \|*  
*tatheti matvā te sarve tūṣṇī māsansuvismitāḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Thus Yama commanded his servants. Thinking that it should be so, they remained quiet on being much surprised.

## \|\| 1.32.88 \|\|

*evaṃvidho'yaṃ bhuvanaikabhartā sadāśivo lokaguruḥ sa ekaḥ \|*  
*dātā prahartā nijabhāvayuktaḥ sanātano'yaṃ jagadekabaṃdhuḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Such is Sadāśiva, the sole lord of the worlds, the sire of the worlds. He is one and only one. He is the bestower and the chastiser, possessor of his supreme powers (Bhāva), emotional feelings. He is eternal, the sole kinsman of the universe.

## \|\| 1.32.89-90 \|\|

*dagdhvā kālaṃ mahādevo nirbhayaṃ ca dadau vibhuḥ \|*  
*śvetasya rājarājasya mahīpālavarasya ca \|\| 89 \|\|*

*tadā nirbhayamāpannaḥ śvetarājo mahāmanāḥ \|*  
*bhaktyā ca parayā mukto babhūva kṛtaniścayaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. After burning Kāla, lord Mahādeva granted freedom from fear to Śveta, the king of kings, the most excellent one among the rulers of the earth.

Having attained freedom from fear, the lofty-minded king Śveta resolved (to strive for salvation) and by means of supreme devotion became liberated.

## \|\| 1.32.91 \|\|

*tadā devaiḥ pūjyamāna ṛṣibhiḥ pannagaistathā \|*  
*śvato rājanyavaryo'sau śivasāyujyamāptavān \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. On being honoured by Devas, sages and Serpents, this Śveta, the most excellent one among kings, attained Sāyujya (identity) with Śiva.

## \|\| 1.32.92 \|\|

*evaṃ bhaktiparāṇāṃ ca maheśe ca jagadgurau \|*  
*siddhiḥ karatale teṣāṃ satyaṃ prativadāmi vaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Thus Siddhi (liberation) is within the palm (i.e. within the reach) of those persons who are devoted to Maheśa, the Sire of the universe. I am speaking the truth unto you.

## \|\| 1.32.93 \|\|

*śvapaco'pi variṣṭhaḥ syātprasādācchaṃ karasya ca \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena pūjanīyo hi śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Even a Cāṇḍāla can become an excellent man by the favour of Śaṅkara. Hence Śaṅkara should be worshipped with all efforts.

## \|\| 1.32.94-95 \|\|

*bahūnāṃ janamanāmaṃte śivabhaktiḥ prajāyate \|\| 94 \|\|*

*jñānināṃ kṛtabuddhīnāṃ janmajanmaniśaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*kiṃ mayā bahunoktena pūjanīyaḥ sadāśivaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. It is only after the end of many births that devotion to Śiva is born in Jñānins with great intellect. Śaṅkara should be worshipped in every birth. Of what avail is too much talk on my part? Sadāśiva should be worshipped.

## \|\| 1.32.96 \|\|

*atraivodāharaṃtīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*kirātena kṛtaṃ vrataṃ ca paramādbhutam \|*  
*yenaiva tāritaṃ viśvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. In this context they cite this ancient mythological legend in regard to the wonderful hoīy rite performed by a Kirāta (forester) by whom the whole universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings was redeemed.

## Chapter 33 - The Greatness of Śivarātri Vrata

## \|\| 1.33.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kinnāmā ca kirāto'bhūtkiṃ tena vratamāhitam \|*  
*tattvaṃ kathaya vipreṃdra paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. What was the name of that Kirāta? What holy rite was performed by him? O great Brāhmaṇa, narrate it. We are very eager.

## \|\| 1.33.2 \|\|

*tatsarvaṃ śrotumicchāmo yāthātathyena kathyatām \|*  
*na hyanyo vidyate loke tvadvinā vadatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*tasmātkatha bho vipra sarvaṃ śuśrūṣatāṃ hi naḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. We wish to hear everything. Let it be described exactly. Excepting you, there is no one else, O foremost one among eloquent people. Hence recount everything, O lord of Brāhmaṇas, to us who wish to hear.

## \|\| 1.33.3 \|\|

*evamuktastadā tena śaunakena mahātmanā \|*  
*kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ puṣkasena kṛtaṃ yat \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On being told thus by the noble-souled Śaunaka, (Lomaśa) narrated every thing done by the Puṣkasa (? Forester).

## \|\| 1.33.4 \|\|

*lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*āsītpurā mahāraudraścaḍonāma durātmavān \|*  
*krūrasaṃgo niṣkṛtiko bhūtānāṃ bhayavāhakaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

4\. Once there was an excessively terrible vicious man named Caṇḍa. He used to associate with cruel people. He was roguish and of bad conduct. He used to terrorize all living beings.

## \|\| 1.33.5-6 \|\|

*jālena matsyānduṣṭātmā ghātayatyaniśaṃ khalu \|*  
*bhallairmṛgāñchāpadāṃśca kṛṣṇasārāṃśca śallakān \|\| 5 \|\|*

*khaḍgāṃścaiva ca duṣṭātmā dṛṣṭvā kāṃścicca pāpavān \|*  
*pakṣiṇo'ghātayatkruddho brāhmaṇāṃśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. With a net that evil-minded one used to capture and kill fish incessantly. That wicked fellow killed different kinds of deer, beasts of prey and porcupine as well as rhinoceros by means of arrows. Sometimes he furiously killed birds. The sinner killed Brāhmaṇas in particular. The forester of great sins was wicked himself and was a favourite of all wicked people. The wife of that Puṣkasa was also very terrible, like him.

## \|\| 1.33.7-8 \|\|

*lubdhako hi mahāpāpo duṣṭo duṣṭajanapriyaḥ \|*  
*bhāryā tathāvidhaā tasya puṣkasasya mahābhayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*evaṃ viharatastasya bahukālotyavartata \|*  
*gate bahutithekāle pāpaughaniratasya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Even as he amused himself thus, many years passed by. He continued to be engaged in those sinful activities and much time passed.

## \|\| 1.33.9 \|\|

*niṣaṃge jalamādāya kṣutpipāsārddito bhṛśam \|*  
*ekadā niśi pāpīyācchrīvṛkṣopari saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*kolaṃ haṃtuṃ dhanuṣpāṇirjāgraccānimiṣeṇa hi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Once that sinful fellow sat on a Bilva tree at night with the bow in his hand. He wanted to kill a wild boar and he kept awake even without winking. He had stored some water in his quiver, lest he should be distressed due to hunger and thirst.

## \|\| 1.33.10 \|\|

*māghamāse'sitāyāṃ vai caturdaśyāmathāgrataḥ \|*  
*mṛgamārgavilokārthī bilvapatrāṇyapātayat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. It was the fourteenth day in the dark fortnight of the month of Māgha (January-February). He was looking in front for the animal and unintentionally he (plucked and) made many Bilva (Aegle marmelos) leaves fall down.

## \|\| 1.33.11-15 \|\|

*śrīvṛkṣaparṇāni bahūni tatra sa cchedayāmāsa ruṣānvitopi \|*  
*śrīvṛkṣamūle parivartamāne liṃgaṃ tasyoparidṛṣṭabhāvaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vavarṣa gaṃḍūṣajalaṃ durātmā yadṛcchayā tāni śive pataṃti \|*  
*śrīvṛkṣaparṇāni ca daivayogājjātaṃ ca sarvaṃ śivapūjanaṃ tat \|\| 12 \|\|*

*gaṃḍūṣavāriṇā tena snapanaṃ ca kṛtaṃ mahat \|*  
*bilvapatrairasaṃkhyātairarcanaṃ mahatkṛtam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ajñānenāpi bho viprāḥ puṣkasena durātmanā \|*  
*māghamāse'site pakṣe caturdaśyāṃ vidhūdaye \|\| 14 \|\|*

*puṣkaso'tha durācāro vaॉkṣādavatatāra saḥ \|*  
*āgatya jalasaṃkāśaṃ matsyānhaṃtuṃ pracakrame \|\| 15 \|\|*

11-15. Sometimes in anger he plucked a number of Bilva leaves and dropped them down. Wafted (by the wind) they fell upon a Liṅga that was at the root of the Śrīvṛkṣa (Bilva tree). Sometimes that wicked fellow gargled and that water fell on the Śivaliṅga. The leaves of the Bilva tree also fell. In such a manner, by sheer good luck and happy coincidence the action of that forester became a worship of Śiva.

With mouthfuls of water the great rite of bathing was performed; with the numerous leaves of the Aegle marmelos the great rite of worshipping too was carried out in ignorance, O Brāhmaṇas, by that evil-minded Puṣkasa. On the fourteenth day in the black fortnight of the month of Māgha when the crescent moon was about to rise (at dawn), that Puṣkasa of evil conduct got down from the tree. Coming near the water-pond he began to catch (and kill) fish.

## \|\| 1.33.16 \|\|

*lubdha kasyāpi bhāryābhūnnāmnā caiva ghanodarī \|*  
*duṣṭā sā pāpaniratā paradravyāpahāriṇī \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The wife of that Puṣkasa was known by the name Ghanodarī. She was vicious and she used to steal other people’s wealth. She was engaged in committing sins.

## \|\| 1.33.17 \|\|

*gṛhānnirgatya sāyāhne puradvārabahiḥ sthitā \|*  
*vanamārgaṃ prapaśyaṃtī patyurāgamanecchayā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the evening she started from her house and stood outside the city gates. Desirous of meeting her husband on his arrival, she was watching the road to the forest.

## \|\| 1.33.18-22 \|\|

*cirādbhartarī nāyāte cintayāmāsa lubdhakī \|*  
*adya sāyāhnavelāyāmāgatāḥ sarvalubdhakāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tamaḥ stomena saṃchannāścatasro vidiśo diśaḥ \|*  
*rātrau yāmadvayaṃ yātaṃ kiṃ mataṃgaḥ samāgataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kiṃ vā kesaralobhena siṃhenaiva vidāritaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ bhujaṃgaphaṇāratnahārī sarpaviṣārditaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*kiṃ vā varāhadaṃṣṭrāgraghātaiḥ paṃcatvamāgataḥ \|*  
*madhulobhena vṛkṣāgrātsa vai prapatito bhuvi \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kvānveṣayāmi pṛcchāmi kva gacchāmi ca kaṃ prati \|*  
*evaṃ vilapya bahudhā nivṛttā svaṃ gṛhaṃ prati \|\| 22 \|\|*

18-22. When even after a long time her husband did not return, the huntress began to think:

‘All the other hunters and fowlers have returned in the evening today. The four cardinal points and the intermediate quarters have been covered with mass of darkness. Two Yāmas (2x3 = 6 hours) have gone by in the night. Has the forester come yet? Was he torn to pieces by a lion because he had coveted the mane? Was he tortured and afflicted by the poison of serpents because he was about to remove the gems and jewels from the hoods of serpents? Did he meet death on being hit and struck by the tips of the curved teeth of boars? Did he fall down on the ground from the top of a tree which he climbed up because he coveted honey? Where shall I enquire? Whom shall I ask? To whom shall I go?’

After lamenting thus in various ways, she returned to the house.

## \|\| 1.33.23 \|\|

*naivānnaṃ no jalaṃ kiṃcinna bhuktaṃ taddine tayā \|*  
*ciṃtayaṃtī patiṃ cāpi lubdhakī tvayanniśām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Throughout that day, nothing was eaten by her. Even water was not taken in. The fowler’s wife spent the whole of the night thinking about her husband.

## \|\| 1.33.24 \|\|

*atha prabhāte vimale puṣkasī vanamāyayau \|*  
*aśanārthaṃ ca tasyānnamādāya tvaritā satī \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. At dawn when everything was free from impurities (i.e. darkness), the Puṣkasī went to the forest in a hurry, taking with her food for him to eat.

## \|\| 1.33.25 \|\|

*bhramamāṇāvane tasmindadarśa mahatīṃ nadīm \|*  
*tasyāstīre samāsīnaṃ svapatiṃ prekṣya harṣitā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Wandering in the forest, she saw a big river. On seeing her own husband seated on its bank, she became delighted.

## \|\| 1.33.26 \|\|

*tadannaṃ kūlanaḥ sthāpya nadīṃ tartuṃ pracakrame \|*  
*nirīkṣya cātha matsyānsa jālaprotānsamānayat \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. She placed the food on the bank and began to cross the river. On seeing (her), he brought the fish caught in his net.

## \|\| 1.33.27 \|\|

*tāvattayoktaścaṇḍo'sāvehi śīghraṃ ca bhakṣaya \|*  
*annaṃ tvadarthamānītamupoṣya divasaṃ mayā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. By that time, Caṇḍa was told by her: “Come quickly. Take your food. I have observed fast throughout the day and food has been brought for your sake.

## \|\| 1.33.28 \|\|

*kṛtaṃ kimadya re maṃda gate'hani ca kiṃ kṛtam \|*  
*nā'śitaṃ ca tvayā mūḍha laṃghitenādya pāpinā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. What has been done by you today? What was done yesterday, O dull-witted one? Was not anything taken in by you, O stupid fellow? You sinner, did you refrain from taking food?”

## \|\| 1.33.29-30 \|\|

*nadyāṃ snātau tathā tau ca dampatī ca śuci vratau \|*  
*yāvadgataśca bhoktuṃ sa tāvacchvā svayamāgataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tena sarvaṃ bhakṣitaṃ ca tadannaṃ svayameva hi \|*  
*caṃḍī prakupitā caiva śvānaṃ haṃtumupasthitā \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. That couple of pure holy rites took their bath in the river. When he went (to the other bank) for taking his food a dog came that way. All the food was eaten by it. The fierce woman became infuriated and proceeded to kill the dog.

## \|\| 1.33.31 \|\|

*āvayorbhakṣitaṃ cānnamanenaiva ca pāpinā \|*  
*kiṃ ca bhakṣayase mūḍha bhavitādya vubhukṣitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “Our food has been eaten by this sinful wretch. What will you eat, O dull-witted one? You will have to remain hungry now.”

## \|\| 1.33.32-35 \|\|

*evaṃ tayoktaścaṇḍo'sau babhāṣe tāṃ śivapriyaḥ \|*  
*yacchunā bhakṣitaṃ cānnaṃ tenāhaṃ paritoṣitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kimanena śarīreṇa naśvareṇa gatāyuṣā \|*  
*śarīraṃ durlabhaṃ loke pūjyate kṣaṇabhaṃguram \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ye puṣṇaṃti nijaṃ dehaṃ sarvabhāvena cāhatāḥ \|*  
*mūḍhāste pāpino jñeyā lokadvayabahiṣkṛtāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tasmānmānaṃ parityajya krodhaṃ ca duravagraham \|*  
*svasthā bhava vimarśena tattvabuddhyā sthirā bhava \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. On being (reproachfully) told thus by her, Caṇḍa who had become a favourite (devotee) of Śiva, spoke to her: “I have been gratified by the food that has been eaten by the dog- Of what avail is this perishable body bereft of long life? This ill-fated body of momentary existence is being worshipped in the world. Those who are overwhelmed by emotional attachments and go on nourishing their body, are foolish ones. They should be known as sinners, excluded from both the worlds. Hence abandon false pride and unrestrained anger. Be composed by means of discrimination (between good and evil). Be steady by means of the intellect based on reality (i.e. through knowledge of reality).”

## \|\| 1.33.36 \|\|

*bodhitā tena caṃḍī sā puṣkasena tadā bhṛśam \|*  
*jāgarādi ca saṃprāptaḥ puṣkaso'pi caturdaśīm \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. That fierce woman was extremely enlightened by the Puṣkasa then. That Puṣkasa had carried out the rite of keeping awake on the Caturdaśī night.

## \|\| 1.33.37 \|\|

*śivarātriprasaṃgācca jāyate yaddhyasaṃśayam \|*  
*tajjñānaṃ paramaṃ prāptaḥ śivarātriprasaṃgataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In view of the connection with Śivarātri, he attained that perfect knowledge which is undoubtedly produced at the time of Śivarātri.

## \|\| 1.33.38 \|\|

*yāmadvayaṃ ca saṃjātamamāvāsyāṃ tu tatra vai \|*  
*āgatāśca gaṇāstatra bahavaḥ śivanoditāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Two Yāmas (i.e. six hours) passed and Amāvāsyā started. Many Gaṇas deputed by Śiva came there.

## \|\| 1.33.39 \|\|

*vimānāni bahūnyatra āgatāni tadaṃtikam \|*  
*dṛṣṭāni tena tānyeva vimānāni gaṇāstathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Many aerial chariots also came there near him. Those aerial chariots and the Gaṇas were seen by him.

## \|\| 1.33.40 \|\|

*uvāca parayā bhaktyā puṣkaso'pi ca tānprati \|*  
*kasmātsamāgatā yūyaṃ sarve rudrākṣadhāriṇaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The Puṣkasa spoke to them with great devotion: “From where have you come? All of you wear Rudrākṣa beads.

## \|\| 1.33.41 \|\|

*vimānasthāśca kecicca vṛṣārūḍhāśca kecana \|*  
*sarve sphaṭikasaṃkāśāḥ sarve caṃdrārddhaśekharāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Some of you are riding in aerial chariots. Some have mounted bulls. All of you resemble the crystal. All of you have the crescent moon as coronet.

## \|\| 1.33.42 \|\|

*kaparddinaścarmaparītavāsaso bhujaṃgabhogaiḥ kṛtahārabhūṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*śriyānvitā rudrasamānavīryā yathātathaṃ bho vadatātmanocitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. All of you have matted hair. Hides are your garments. (Bodies of) serpents have been worn as ornaments. You are equipped with all glorious features. Your heroism is like that of Rudra. Explain specifically and exactly what is proper unto you.”

## \|\| 1.33.43 \|\|

*puṣkasena tadā pṛṣṭā ūcuḥ sarve ca pārpadāḥ \|*  
*rudrasya devadevasya saṃnamrāḥ kamalekṣaṇāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On being asked by Puṣkasa, then, all the lotus-eyed Pārṣadas (attendants) of Rudra, the lord of Devas, said very humbly:

## \|\| 1.33.44 \|\|

*gaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*preṣitāḥ smo vayaṃ caṃḍa śivena parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*āgaccha tvarito bhutvā sastrīko yā namāruha \|\| 44 \|\|*

Gaṇas said:

44\. O Caṇḍa, we have been sent by the great god Śiva. Come on. Hurry up. Get into the vehicle along with your wife.

## \|\| 1.33.45 \|\|

*liṃgārccanaṃ kṛtaṃ yacca tvayā rātrau śivasya ca \|*  
*tena karmavipākena prāpto'si śivasannidhim \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The worship of the Liṅga of Śiva has been performed by you at night. As a result of that good rite you have attained Siva’s presence.

## \|\| 1.33.46 \|\|

*tathokto vīrabhadreṇa uvāca prahasanniva \|*  
*puṣkaso'pi svayā buddhyā prastāvasadṛśaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Told thus by Vīrabhadra, the Puṣkasa too laughingly said the following words relevant to the occasion, in accordance with his own intellect.

## \|\| 1.33.47 \|\|

*puṣkasa uvāca \|*  
*kiṃ mayā kṛtamadyaiva pāpinā hiṃsakena ca \|*  
*mṛgayārasikenaiva puṣkasena durātmanā \|\| 47 \|\|*

The Puṣkasa said:

47\. What (good) has been done today by me who have been a sinner, a violent tormentor, an evil-minded Puṣkasa interested in hunting?

## \|\| 1.33.48 \|\|

*pāpācāro hyahaṃ nityaṃ kathaṃ svargaṃ vrajāmyaham \|*  
*kathaṃ liṃgārcanamidaṃ kṛtamasti taducyatām \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. I have been perpetually committing sins. How can I go to heaven? How was the worship of Liṅga performed? "Let it be explained

## \|\| 1.33.49 \|\|

*paraṃ kautukamāpannaḥ pṛcchāmi tvāṃ yathātatham \|*  
*kathayasva mahābhāga sarvaṃ caiva yathāvidhi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. My curiosity has been roused much. I am asking you for the exact state (of affairs). Explain, O deity of great fortune, everything in due order.

## \|\| 1.33.50 \|\|

*ityevaṃ pṛcchatastasya puṣkasasya yathāvidhi \|*  
*kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ śivadharma mudānvitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. As the Puṣkasa put these questions properly, (Vīra-bhadra) described the Śaiva rites entirely with great joy.

## \|\| 1.33.51 \|\|

*vīrabhadra uvāca \|*  
*devadevo mahādevo devānāṃ patirīśvaraḥ \|*  
*parituṣṭo'dya he caṃḍa sa maheśa umāpatiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

Vīrabhadra said:

51\. Mahādeva, the lord of Devas, Īśvara, the lord of refulgent ones, Maheṣa, the consort of Umā, is delighted today, O Caṇḍa.

## \|\| 1.33.52 \|\|

*prāsaṃgikatayā māghe kṛtaṃ liṃgārcanaṃ tvayā \|*  
*śivatuṣṭikaraṃ cādya pūto'si tvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*śivarātryāṃ prasaṃgena kṛtamarcanameva ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. In the month of Māgha, the worship of Liṅga was performed by you incidentally. It is the cause of the delight of Śiva. Undoubtedly you have become sanctified today. The worship was incidentally performed on the Śivarātri night.

## \|\| 1.33.53 \|\|

*kolaṃ nirīkṣamāṇena bilvapatrāṇi caiva hi \|*  
*ccheditāni tvayā caṃḍa patitāni tadaiva hi \|*  
*liṃgasya mastake tāni tena tvaṃ sukṛtī prabho \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O Caṇḍa, the leaves of the Bilva tree were plucked by you who were on the lookout for a wild boar. At the same time, they fell on the head of the Liṅga. Hence you have become full of merits, O holy lord.

## \|\| 1.33.54 \|\|

*tataśca jāgaro jāto mahānvṛkṣopari dhruvam \|*  
*tenaiva jāgareṇaiva tutoṣa jagadīśvaraḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Similarly the great rite of keeping awake was performed by you on the tree. The Lord of the universe is delighted at that keeping awake.

## \|\| 1.33.55 \|\|

*chalenaiva mahābhāga kolasaṃdarśanena hi \|*  
*śivarātridine cātra svapnaste na ca yoṣitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Under the pretext of watching (the arrival) of a wild boar, you had no sleep on the Śivarātri night. Nor did your wife sleep.

## \|\| 1.33.56 \|\|

*tenopavāsena ca jāgareṇa tuṣṭo hyasau devavaro mahātmā \|*  
*tava prasādāya mahānubhāvo dadāti sarvānvarado mahāṃśca \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The noble-souled lord, the most excellent one among Devas, is delighted on account of that fast and keeping the vigil. In order to please you, the lord of great magnanimity, the bestower of boons, granted you all festivities.

## \|\| 1.33.57-60 \|\|

*evamuktastadā tena vīrabhadreṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*puṣkaso'pi vimānāgryamāruhoha ca paśyatām \|\| 57 \|\|*

*gaṇānāṃ devatānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ prāṇināmapi \|*  
*tadā duṃdubhayo nedurbheryastūryāṇyanekaśaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*vīṇāveṇumṛdaṃgāni tasya cāgre gatāni ca \|*  
*jagurgaṃdharvapatayo nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*vidyādharagaṇāḥ sarve tuṣṭuvuḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ \|*  
*cāmaraivarvījyamāno hi cchatraiśca vividhairapi \|*  
*mahotsavena mahatā ānīto gaṃdhamādanam \|\| 60 \|\|*

57-60. On being told thus by the intelligent Vīrabhadra, the Puṣkasa got into the excellent aerial chariot even as the Gaṇas, Devas and all living beings were watching. Dundubhi-drums were sounded. Bherīs and many musical instruments were played. The instruments like lutes, flutes and Mṛdaṅgas went ahead of him. The lords of Gandharvas sang; groups of celestial damsels danced. All the groups of Vidyādharas, Siddhas and Cāraṇas eulogized. The Puṣkasa was being fanned with chowries. He was honoured with various kinds of umbrellas. He was brought to Gandhamādana with great festivities and celebrations.

## \|\| 1.33.61 \|\|

*śivasānnidhyamāgaccaṃḍosau tena karmaṇā \|*  
*śivarātryupavāsena paraṃ sthānaṃ samāgamat \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. This Caṇḍa attained the presence of Śiva on account of that holy rite. By fasting on the Śivarātri night, he attained the greatest region.

## \|\| 1.33.62-63 \|\|

*puṣkaso'pi tathā prāptaḥ prasaṃgena sadāśivam \|*  
*kiṃ punaḥ śraddhayā yuktāḥ śivāya paramātmane \|\| 62 \|\|*

*puṣpādikaṃ phalaṃ gaṃdhaṃ tāṃbūlaṃ bhakṣyamṛddhimat \|*  
*ye prayacchaṃti loke'sminrudrāste nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. Even a Puṣkasa and that too by means of an incidental (holy rite) attained Sadāśiva. What then in the case of those who have great faith in attaining Śiva, the great Ātman?

There is no doubt about this that those who offer flowers etc., fruits, scents, betel leaves and rich foodstuffs in this world to god Śiva are Rudras themselves.

## \|\| 1.33.64 \|\|

*caṃḍena vai puṣkasena saphalaṃ tasya cābhavat \|*  
*prasaṃgenāpi tenaiva kṛtaṃ taccālpabuddhinā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Everything was incidentally performed by Caṇḍa, a Puṣkasa, who was of insignificant intellect. Still his action was fruitful.

The sages enquired:

## \|\| 1.33.65 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ phalaṃ tasya coddeśaḥ kena caiva punā kṛtam \|*  
*kasmādvratamidaṃ jātaṃ kṛtaṃ kena purā vibho \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. What is the benefit? What is its purpose? By whom was it performed formerly? Wherefrom did this Vrata originate? By whom was it laid down, O holy lord, formerly?

## \|\| 1.33.66 \|\|

*lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*yadā sṛṣṭaṃ jagatsarvaṃ brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*kālacakraṃ tadā jātaṃ purā rāśimanvitām \|\| 66 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

66\. When the entire universe was created by Brahmā Parameṣṭhin, the wheel of Time also was evolved formerly a long with the zodiacs.

## \|\| 1.33.67 \|\|

*dvādaśa rāśayastatra nakṣatrāṇi tathaiva ca \|*  
*saptaviṃśatisaṃkhyāni mukhyāni siddhaye \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. There are twelve zodiacs and the main constellations are twenty-seven in number, for the sake of achieving the objectives.

## \|\| 1.33.68 \|\|

*ebhiḥ sarvaṃ pracaṃḍaṃ ca rāśibhiruḍubhistathā \|*  
*kālacakrānvitaḥ kālaḥ krīḍayansṛjate jagat \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The Wheel of Time is very fierce with these zodiacs and constellations. Accompanied by this Kālacakra (‘Wheel of Time’), Kāla sportively creates this universe.

## \|\| 1.33.69 \|\|

*ābrahmastaṃbaparyaṃtaṃ sṛjatya vati haṃti ca \|*  
*nibaddhamasti tenaiva kālenaikena bho dvijāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Kāla creates, protects and destroys everything from Brahmā down to a blade of grass, O Brāhmaṇas. Everything is connected with Kāla.

## \|\| 1.33.70 \|\|

*kālo hi balavāṃlloke eka eva na cāparaḥ \|*  
*tasmātkālātmakaṃ sarvamidaṃ nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Indeed Kāla is very powerful. It is the only one (of its kind). (There is) nothing else than Kāla. Hence all these (visible worlds) are of the nature of Kāla. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.33.71 \|\|

*ādau kālaḥ kālanācca lokanāyakanāyakaḥ \|*  
*tato lokā hi saṃjātāḥ sṛṣṭiśca tadanaṃtaram \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The leader of all the leaders of the world is Kāla at the outset because of Kālana (calculation?). The worlds are born therefrom. The creation comes next.

## \|\| 1.33.72 \|\|

*sṛṣṭerlavo hi saṃjāto lavācca kṣaṇameva ca \|*  
*kṣaṇācca nimiṣaṃ jātaṃ prāṇināṃ hi niraṃtaram \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. From the creation, Lava (i.e. the smallest unit of time) is born. From Lava, Kṣaṇa (moment) is born; from Kṣaṇa, Nimiṣa (i.e. winking time) is born. This occurs continuously in all living beings.

## \|\| 1.33.73 \|\|

*nimiṣāṇāṃ ca ṣaṣṭyā vai phala ityabhidhīyate \|*  
*paṃcadaśyā ahorātraiḥ pakṣaityabhidhīyate \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Sixty Nimiṣas make one Pala. Fifteen days and nights make one Pakṣa (fortnight).

## \|\| 1.33.74 \|\|

*pakṣābhyāṃ māsa eva syānmāsā dvādaśa vatsaraḥ \|*  
*taṃ kālaṃ jñātukāmena kāryaṃ jñānaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Two Pakṣas make one Māsa (month); twelve Māsas make one Vatsara (year). Knowledge should be acquired from experts by a person desirous of knowing Kāla.
