## \|\| 2.22.40 \|\|

*bhajasva putrīṃ jagatī mamāpi ca tavāpi ca \|*  
*puṃduḥkhanakāttrātrī putrī te bhāvinī tviyam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. ‘Accept this daughter. The universe is mine as well as yours. This will be your daughter saving you from the miserable hell named Puṃ.’

## \|\| 2.22.41 \|\|

*evamukto mayā dakṣaḥ putrītve pari kalpitām \|*  
*rudrāya dattavānbhaktyā nāma dattvā satīti yat \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. On being told thus by me, Dakṣa adopted her as his daughter. After giving her the name Satī, he devoutly gave her to Rudra.

## \|\| 2.22.42 \|\|

*tataḥ kāle caṃ kasmiṃścidavamene ca tāṃ pitā \|*  
*mumūrṣuḥ pāpasaṃkalpo durātmā kulakajjalaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On a certain occasion, the father insulted her. He was a person of sinful resolve, a stigma on the family, a person of suicidal activities, a wicked soul.

## \|\| 2.22.43 \|\|

*ye rudraṃ naiva manyaṃte te sphuṭaṃ kulakajjalāḥ \|*  
*piśācāste durātmāno bhavaṃti brahmarākṣasāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Those who do not honour Rudra are clearly blots on the family. They are Piśācas (‘Ghosts’). They become wicked souls and Brahma-Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 2.22.44 \|\|

*avamānena tasyāpi yathā devī jahau tanum \|*  
*yathā yajñaḥ sa ca dhvasto bhavena viditaṃ hi te \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On account of insult from him (Dakṣa), the goddess cast off her body. The Yajña was destroyed by Bhava. These and (subsequent things) are known to you.

## \|\| 2.22.45 \|\|

*adhunā himaśailasya bhavitrī duhitā ca sā \|*  
*maheśvaraṃ patiṃ sā ca punaḥ prāpsyati niścitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Now she will be born as the daughter of Himālaya. Certainly, she will attain Maheśvara as her husband.

## \|\| 2.22.46 \|\|

*tadidaṃ ca tvayā kāryaṃ menāgarbhe praviśya ca \|*  
*tasyāśchaviṃ kuru kṛṣṇāṃ yathā kālī bhavettu sā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Therefore, this is the job to be carried out by you. Enter the womb of Menā and turn her complexion black so that she will be Kālī (‘dark-complexioned’).

## \|\| 2.22.47-49 \|\|

*yadā rudropahasitā tapastapsyati sā mahat \|*  
*samāptaniyamā devī yadā cogrā bhaviṣyati \|\| 47 \|\|*

*svayameva yadā rūpaṃ sugauraṃ pratipatsyate \|*  
*viraheṇa haraścāsyā matvā śūnyaṃ jagattrayam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*tasyaiva himaśailasya kaṃdare siddhasevite \|*  
*pratīkṣamāṇastāṃ devīmugraṃ saṃtapsyate tapaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. On being laughed at by Rudra, she will perform a great penance. After concluding her holy observances the goddess herself will become fierce and formidable. Then she will herself regain the extremely fair complexion. Being separated from her, he will consider the entire space of the three worlds a void.

He will perform a severe penance waiting for the goddess, in a cave of the same (Himālaya) mountain which is frequented by Siddhas.

## \|\| 2.22.50 \|\|

*tayoḥ sutaptatapasorbhavitā yo mahānsutaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati sa daityasya tārakasya nivārakaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The great son born to them who have performed great penances, will be the annihilator of Daitya Tāraka.

## \|\| 2.22.51 \|\|

*tapaso hi vinā nāsti siddhiḥ kutrāpi śobhane \|*  
*sarvāsāṃ karmasiddhīnāṃ mūlaṃ hi tapa ucyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O splendid lady, without penance there can never be any achievement anywhere. Penance is called the root of all Siddhis (‘miraculous powers’),

## \|\| 2.22.52 \|\|

*tvayāpi dānavo devi dehanirgatayā tadā \|*  
*caṃḍamuṃḍapurogāśca haṃtavyā lokadurjayāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O goddess, the Dānavas whose leaders will be Caṇḍa and Ṃuṇḍa and who cannot be vanquished by the whole world should be killed by you after coming out of the body (of Pārvatī).

## \|\| 2.22.53 \|\|

*yasmāccaṃḍaṃ ca muṃḍaṃ ca tvaṃ devi nihaniṣyasi \|*  
*cāmuṃḍeti tato loke khyātā devi bhaviṣyasi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O goddess, since you will kill Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, you will become famous by the name Cāmuṇḍā in the world.

## \|\| 2.22.54 \|\|

*tatastvāṃ varade devī lokaḥ saṃpūjayiṣyati \|*  
*bhederbahuvidhākāraiḥ sarvagāṃ kāmasādhanīm \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thereupon, O goddess. O bestower of boons, the world will worship you in different forms and ways. You who can go wherever you like, will accomplish their desires.

## \|\| 2.22.55-56 \|\|

*oṃkāravaktrāṃ gāyatrīṃ tvāmarcaṃti dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*ūrjitāṃ baladāṃ pāpi rājānaḥ sumahābalāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*vaiśyāśca bhūtimityeva śivāṃ śūdrāstathā śubhe \|*  
*kṣāṃtirmunīnāmakṣobhyā dayā niyamināmapi \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. Excellent Brāhmaṇas worship you as Gāyatrī with Oṃkāra as her face. Kings of very great power (will worship you) as Ūrjitā (‘having great power and potentiality’) and bestower of strength. Vaiśyas worship (you) as Bhūti (‘prosperity’). Similarly, O splendid one, Śūdras worship as Śivā.

You are Kṣānti (‘forbearance’) of the sages, which cannot be agitated. You are Dayā (mercy) of those who have holy observances and restraints.

## \|\| 2.22.57-59 \|\|

*tvaṃ mahopāya sandohā nītirnayavisarpiṇām \|*  
*paristhitistvamarthānāṃ tvamaho prāṇikā matā \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tvaṃ yuktiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tvaṃ gatiḥ sarvadehinām \|*  
*ratistvaṃ raticittānāṃ prītistvaṃ hṛdyadarśinām \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tvaṃ kāṃtiḥ śubharūpāṇāṃ tvaṃ śāṃti śubhakarmiṇām \|*  
*tvaṃ bhrāṃtirmūḍhacittānāṃ tvaṃ phalaṃ kratuyājinām \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-59. You are Nīti (‘policy’) of those who make strategic movements. You have the great collection of Upāyas (’expedients’). You are the environment of wealth and riches. You are considered as the vital air. You are the Yukti (‘device’) of all the living beings. You are the Gati (‘goal’) of all embodied ones. You are Rati (‘pleasure’) of those who are inclined towards pleasure. You are Prīti (‘affection’) of those who see things dear to the heart. You are Kānti (‘lustre’) of those who have splendid forms. You are Śānti (‘peace’) of those who perform auspicious holy rites. You are Bhrānti (‘delusion’) of those who have deluded minds. You are the fruit (i.e. merit) of those who perform Kratus (‘sacrifices’).

## \|\| 2.22.60 \|\|

*jaladhīnāṃ mahāvelā tvaṃ ca līlā vilāsinām \|*  
*saṃbhūtistvaṃ padārthānāṃ sthitistvaṃ lokapālinī \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. You are the great foreshore of the oceans. You are Līlā (‘dalliance’) of those who lead graceful romantic lives. You are Saṃbhūti (‘origin and existence’) of the objects. You are the Sthiti (‘preservation’) protecting the worlds.

## \|\| 2.22.61 \|\|

*tvaṃ kālarātrirniḥśeṣa bhuvanāvalināśinī \|*  
*priyakaṃṭhagrahānandadāyinī tvaṃ vibhāvarī \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. You are the night of destruction (at the end of the world), the destroyer of all the groups of the worlds. You are Vibhāvarī (‘night’), the bestower of the pleasure of the beloved’s embrace.

## \|\| 2.22.62 \|\|

*prasīda praṇatānasmānsaumyadṛṣṭyā vilokaya \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Be pleased with us. We have bowed down. Look at us with gracious eyes.

## \|\| 2.22.63 \|\|

*iti stuvaṃto ye devi pūjayiṣyaṃti tvāṃ śubhe \|*  
*te sarvakāmānāpsyaṃti niyatā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Those who eulogize you, O auspicious one, in this manner and worship you, will invariably attain all their desires. There is no doubt about this.”

## \|\| 2.22.64 \|\|

*ityuktā tu niśādevī tathetyuktvā kṛtāñjaliḥ \|*  
*jagāma tvaritā pūrvaṃ gṛhaṃ himagirermahat \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. On being told thus the goddess Niśā joined her palms in reverence. Saying “So be it” she hurriedly went, at the outset, to the great abode of Himālaya.

## \|\| 2.22.65 \|\|

*tatrā'sīnāṃ mahāharmye ratnabhittisamāśraye \|*  
*dadarśa menāmāpāṃḍucchavivaktrasaroruhām \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. There in a great mansion with gem-studded walls, she saw Menā with pale yellowish white complexion and lotus-like face.

## \|\| 2.22.66 \|\|

*kiṃcicchayāmamukhodagrastanabhāgāvanāmitām \|*  
*mahauṣadhigaṇabaddhamaṃtrarājaniṣevitām \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. She was seated with a slight bend to one side where the breasts protruded with the nipples somewhat dark in colour. Medicinal herbs had been tied to her limbs after being charged with excellent Mantras.

## \|\| 2.22.67-68 \|\|

*tataḥ kiṃcitpramilite menānetrāṃbujadvaye \|*  
*āviveśamukhaṃ rātrirbrahmaṇo vacanāttadā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*janmadāyā jaganmātuḥ krameṇa jaṭharāṃtaram \|*  
*araṃjayacchaviṃ devyā guhamāturvibhāvarī \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. When the pair of lotus-like eyes of Menā closed slightly, the goddess of Night, at the instance of Brahmā, entered the mouth of the mother of the mother of the universe and gradually entered her stomach. The goddess Vibhāvarī (‘Night’) coloured the complexion of the goddess, mother of Guha.

## \|\| 2.22.69 \|\|

*tato jaganmaṃ galadā menā himagireḥ priyā \|*  
*brāhme muhūrte subhage prāsūyata śubhānanām \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Thereafter, in the excellent Brāhma Muhūrta (i.e. early dawn), Menā, the bestower of auspiciousness on the universe, the beloved wife of Himagiri, gave birth (to a daughter) of splendid face.

## \|\| 2.22.70 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tu jāyamānāyāṃ jaṃtavaḥ sthāṇujaṃgamāḥ \|*  
*abhavansukhinaḥ sarve sarvalokanivāsinaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. When she was born, all the living beings, the mobile as well as the immobile ones, became happy. All the residents of all the worlds were joyful.

## \|\| 2.22.71 \|\|

*abhavatkrūrasattvānāṃ cetaḥ śāṃtaṃ ca dehinām \|*  
*jyotiṣāmapi tejastvamabhavatsutarāṃ tadā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The minds of cruel animals and embodied beings became calm. The refulgence of all the luminaries was enhanced.

## \|\| 2.22.72 \|\|

*vanāśritāścauṣadhayaḥ svādavaṃti phalāni ca \|*  
*gaṃdhavaṃti ca mālyāni vimalaṃ ca nabho'bhavat \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The plants and the medicinal herbs of the forest yielded tasty fruits and fragrant flowers. The sky became devoid of cloudiness and clear.

## \|\| 2.22.73 \|\|

*mārutaśca sukhasparśo diśaśca sumanoharāḥ \|*  
*vismṛtā ni ca śāstrāṇi prādurbhāvaṃ prapedire \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The wind was very pleasing to the touch. The quarters were very charming. All the scriptures that had been forgotten became manifest.

## \|\| 2.22.74-76 \|\|

*prabhāvastīrthamukhyānāṃ tadā puṇyatamo'bhavat \|*  
*satye dharme cādhyayane yajñe dāne tapasyapi \|\| 74 \|\|*

*sarveṣāmabhavacchraddhā janmakāle guhāraṇeḥ \|*  
*aṃtarikṣemarāścāpi praharṣotphullalocanāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*haribrahmamaheṃdrārkavāyuvahnipurogamāḥ \|*  
*puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ pramumucustasminmenāgṛhe śubhe \|\| 76 \|\|*

74-76. At that time the power of important holy spots became highly meritorious. Everyone had faith in truth, virtue, study of the Vedas, Yajña, charitable gifts and penance at the time of the birth of Guha’s mother.

In the firmament, the immortal ones with their eyes blooming with delight, showered flowers. Devas, the chiefs of whom were Hari, Brahmā, Mahendra, the Sun, the Wind and the Fire gods released showers of flowers over the splendid abode of Menā.

## \|\| 2.22.77-80 \|\|

*meruprabhṛtayaścāpi mūrtimaṃto mahānagāḥ \|*  
*tasminmahotsave prāptā vīrakāṃsyopaśobhitāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*sāgarāḥ saritaścaiva samājagmuśca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*himaśailo'bhavalloke tadā sarvaiścarācaraiḥ \|*  
*sevyaścāpyabhigamyaśca pūjanīyaśca bhārata \|\| 79 \|\|*

*anubhūyotsavaṃ te ca jagmuḥ svānālayāṃstadā \|\| 80 \|\|*

77-80. The great mountains beginning with Meru assumed physical forms and took part in that great festival. They were rendered splendid by means of Vīrakāṃsyas (i.e. bell metal plates to hold Nīrājana lamps during waving ceremony). Oceans and Rivers also came from all sides. At that time Himavān became worthy of being served, worshipped and approached by all the mobile and immobile beings in the world, O descendant of Bharata. After enjoying the great festival all of them went back to their respective abodes.

## Chapter 23 - Himavān Consoled

## \|\| 2.23.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*tataśca śailajā devī cikrīḍa subhagā tadā \|*  
*devagaṃdharvakanyābhirnagakiṃnarasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*munīnāṃ cāpi yāḥ kanyāstābhiḥ sārdhaṃ ca śobhanā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. Thereafter the goddess born of the Mountain played and sported. That goddess of good fortune and exalted magnificence, the splendid lady, played along with the girls of Devas and Gandharvas, the ladies of Mountains and of Kinnara families and the daughters of acetics.

## \|\| 2.23.2 \|\|

*kadācidatha merustho vāsavaḥ pāṃḍunaṃdana \|*  
*sasmārā māṃ yayau cāhaṃ saṃsmṛto vāsavaṃ tadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Once, O son of Pāṇḍu, Vāsava (i.e. Indra) who was staying on Meru, remembered me. On being remembered I went to Vāsava.

## \|\| 2.23.3 \|\|

*māṃ dṛṣṭvā ca sahasrākṣaḥ samutthāyātiharṣitaḥ \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa tāṃ pūjāṃ pratigṛhyāhamabruvam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing me the Thousand-eyed Lord became extremely delighted. He got up and worshipped me. After receiving his adoration I said:

## \|\| 2.23.4 \|\|

*mahāsura mahonmādakālānala divaspate \|*  
*kuśalaṃ vidyate kaccicca naṃdasi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. “O deadly fire of annihilation destroying the intensively mad arrogance of great Asuras, I hope you are hale and hearty and are delighted (too).”

## \|\| 2.23.5-8 \|\|

*pṛṣṭastvevaṃ mayā śakraḥ provāca vacanaṃ smayan \|*  
*kuśalasyāṃkurastāvatsaṃbhūto bhuvanatraye \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tatphalodayasaṃpattau tadbhavānsaṃsmṛto mune \|*  
*vetsi sarvamataṃ tvaṃ vai tathāpi parinodakaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*nirvṛtiṃ paramāṃ yāti nivedyārthaṃ suhṛjjane \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tadbhavāñchailajāṃ devīṃ śailaṃdraṃ śailavallabhām \|*  
*haraṃ saṃbhāvaya varaṃ yannānyaṃ rocayaṃti te \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. On being asked by me thus, Śakra smilingly spoke these words: “The sprout of welfare of the three worlds has come out. With regard to the outcome of its fruit, you have been remembered, O Sage. You know everything thought by everyone. Still I (act as) one who reminds and urges. If one confides matters to a friend, one attains great pleasure. Therefore, you (meet) the Lord of Mountains, the beloved wife of the Mountain and the goddess born of the Mountain and make them take Hara as the bridegroom. (See) that they do not approve of anyone elṣe.”

## \|\| 2.23.9 \|\|

*tatastadvākyamākarṇya gato'haṃ śailasattamam \|*  
*oṣadhiprasthanilayaṃ sākṣādiva divaspatim \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thereafter, on hearing his words I went to the excellent Mountain whose abode was in Oṣadhiprastha (‘land of medicinal herbs’). He (shone) like the lord of the heavenly world himself.

## \|\| 2.23.10 \|\|

*tatra haime svayaṃ tena mahābhaktyā nivedite \|*  
*mahāsane pūjitohamupaviṣṭo mahāsukham \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. I was honoured by him. A golden seat was offered to me with great devotion by himself. I sat on it with great pleasure.

## \|\| 2.23.11 \|\|

*gṛhītārghyaṃ tato māṃ ca papraccha ślakṣṇayā girā \|*  
*kuśalaṃ tapasaḥ śailaḥ śanaiḥ phullānanāṃbujaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. As I accepted his respectful reception (arghya) the Mountain with his face beaming like a full-blown lotus slowly enquired about my happiness and the progress of penance in sweet smooth words.

## \|\| 2.23.12-21 \|\|

*ahamapyasya tatprocya pratyavocaṃ girīśvaram \|*  
*tvayā śaileṃdra pūrvāṃ vāpyaparāṃ ca diśaṃ tathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*avagāhya sthitavatā kriyate prāṇipālanā \|*  
*aho dhanyosi vipreṃdrāḥ sāhāyyena tavācala \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tapojapavratasnānauḥ sādhyaṃtyātmanaḥ param \|*  
*yajñāṃgasādhanaiḥ kāṃścitkaṃdādiphaladānataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tvaṃ samuddharasi viprānkimataḥ procyate tava \|*  
*anye'pi jīva bahudhātvāmupāśritya bhūdhara \|\| 15 \|\|*

*muditāḥ prativartaṃte gṛhasthamiva prāṇinaḥ \|*  
*śītamātapavarṣāṃśca kleśānnānāvidhānsahan \|\| 16 \|\|*

*upākaroṣi jaṃtūnāmevaṃrūpā hi sādhavaḥ \|*  
*kimataḥ procyate tubhyaṃ dhanyastvaṃ pṛthivīdhara \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kaṃdaraṃ yasya cādhyāste svayaṃ tava maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*ityuktavati vākyaṃ ca yathārthaṃ mayiphālguna \|\| 18 \|\|*

*himaśailasya mahiṣī menā āgāddidṛkṣayā \|*  
*anuyātā duhitrā ca svalpāśca paricārikāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*lajjayānatasarvāṃgī praviveśa sado mahat \|*  
*tato māṃ śailamahiṣī vavaṃde praṇipatya sā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vastranirgūḍhavadanā pāṇipadmakṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*tāmahaṃ satyarūpābhirāśīrbhiḥ samavardhayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

12-18a. I too enquired about his well-being and then replied to the Lord of the Mountains: “O Lord of the Mountains, you occupy the eastern and the western cardinal points and protect the living beings. Oh, you are blessed indeed, O Mountain! With your assistance, leading Brāhmaṇas achieve everything they require through penance, holy rites and sacred ablutions. You support some Brāhmaṇas through the materials required for Yajñas and some, by offering them fruits, bulbous roots etc. What then need be said about you? O Mountain, other living beings too resort to you in various ways and rejoice in the same manner as the living beings resorting to a householder. You suffer the rigours of chillness, sunshine and heavy downpour. You bear patiently different kinds of sufferings and help other creatures. Good people are like this. What then need be said more than this about you? You are blessed, O Mountain, because Maheśvara himself occupies a cave in you.”

18b-21. O Phālguna, when I spoke these truthful words, the queen of Himālaya, Menā, came there desirous of seeing me. She was followed by her daughter. A few servant-maids too followed. She entered the great assembly with her face bent down and all the limbs (covered decently). Thereafter, the queen of the Mountain bowed down to me and saluted me with her face covered with a cloth (veil) and with palms of the lotus-like hands joined in reverence. With truthful blessings I offered my benedictions to her.

## \|\| 2.23.22 \|\|

*pativratā śubhācārā subagā vīrasūḥ śubhe \|*  
*sadā vīravatī cāpi bhava vaṃśonnatiprada \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “O splendid lady, always be chaste, well-behaved, fortunate mother of heroes and attended by heroes, O lady, the bestower of the progress of the family.”

## \|\| 2.23.23 \|\|

*tato'haṃ vismitākṣīṃ ca himavadgiriputrikām \|*  
*mṛduvāṇyā pratyavocamehi bāle mamāṃtikam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then I spoke in sweet gentle words to the daughter of Himālaya Mountain, whose surprise was evident in her eyes: “Come, girl, near me.”

## \|\| 2.23.24 \|\|

*tato devī jaganmātā bālabāvaṃ svakaṃ mayi \|*  
*darśayaṃtī svapitaraṃ kaṃṭhe gṛhyāṃkamāvi śat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then the goddess, the mother of the universe, exhibiting her childhood to me clasped her father’s neck and slipped down in his lap.

## \|\| 2.23.25-26 \|\|

*uvāca vācaṃ tāṃ maṃdaṃ muniṃ vaṃdaya putrike \|*  
*muneḥ prasādato'vaśyaṃ patimāpsyasi saṃmatam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ityuktā sā tato bālā vastrāṃtapi hitānanā \|*  
*kiṃcitsahuṃkṛtotkaṃpaṃ procya novāca kiṃcana \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The father gently spoke these words to her, “O daughter, salute the sage. Thanks to the grace of the sage, you will certainly get a well-approved husband.”

On being told thus, the lass covered her face with the end of her garment. With a slight quiver and a muffled hum, she whispered something and thereafter did not say anything.

## \|\| 2.23.27-32 \|\|

*tato vismitacittohamupacāravidāṃvaraḥ \|*  
*pratyavocaṃ punardevīmehi dāsyāmi te śubhe \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ratnakrīḍanakaṃ ramyaṃ stāpitaṃ suciraṃ mayā \|*  
*ityuktā sā tadotthāya pituraṃkātsavegataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vaṃdamānā ca me pādau mayā nītāṃka mātmanaḥ \|*  
*manyatā tāṃ jagatpūjyāmuktaṃ bāle tavocitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*na tatpaśyāmi yattubhyaṃ dadmyāśīḥ kā tavocitā \|*  
*ityukte mātṛvātsalyācchailendra mahiṣī tadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*nodayāmāsa māṃ maṃdamānaśīḥśaṃkitā tadā \|*  
*bhagavanvetsi sarvaṃ tvamatītānāgataṃ prabho \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tadahaṃ jñātumicchāmi kīdṛśo'syāḥ patirbhavet \|*  
*śrutveti sasmitamukhaḥ prāvocaṃ narmavallabhaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

27-32. I was surprised then. Being the most excellent one among those who are conversant with courteous behaviour, I said to the goddess once again, “O splendid girl, come. I shall give you a gem-set toy kept by me for long.”

On being told thus, she got up from her father’s lap speedily and saluted my feet. She was taken in my lap by me. Considering that she would be worthy of being worshipped by the universe I said, “O lass, I do not see anything befitting you. I do not know what blessing should I offer. What is the blessing suitable unto you?”

When this was spoken by me, the queen of the Lord of Mountains, out of motherly affection, became afraid that I would not bless her. She urged me slowly:

“O Holy Lord, you know everything, the past and the future. Therefore, I wish to know of what nature will her husband be.”

On hearing this my face was covered with smiles. Witty and humorous that I am, I said thus:

## \|\| 2.23.33-34 \|\|

*na jāto'syāḥ patirbhadre vartate ca kulakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*nagno'tinirdhanaḥ krodhīvṛtaḥ krūraiśca sarvadā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śrutveti saṃbhramāviṣṭo dhvastavīryo himācalaḥ \|*  
*māṃ tadā pratyuvācedaṃ sāśrukaṇṭho mahāgiriḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. “O gentle lady, her husband is one who is not born. He is one with evil characteristics. He is naked. He is absolutely devoid of wealth. He is furious (by nature). He is always surrounded by cruel persons.”

On hearing this, Himācala became extremely excited and bewildered as well as bereft of all energy. With his throat choked with tears, the great Mountain spoke to me:

## \|\| 2.23.35 \|\|

*aho vicitraḥ saṃ sāro durvedyo mahatāmapi \|*  
*pravarastvapi śaktyā yo nareṣu na kṛpāyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. “Oh! this world is extremely mysterious. It is incomprehensible even to great men. He who is the most excellent one due to his efficiency, does not show mercy to men.

## \|\| 2.23.36 \|\|

*yatnena mahatā tāvatpuṇyairbahuvidhairapi \|*  
*sādhayatyātmano loko mānuṣya matidurlabham \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. It is with very great effort, by means of many kinds of meritorious deeds that people attain the rare state of being a human being.

## \|\| 2.23.37-40 \|\|

*adhruvaṃ taddhravatve ca kathaṃcitparikalpyate \|*  
*tatrāpi durlabhānāma samānavratacāriṇī \|\| 37 \|\|*

*sādhvī mahākulotpannā bhāryāyā syātpativratā \|*  
*tatrāpi durlabhaṃ yacca tayā dharmaniṣevaṇam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*saha vedapurāṇoktaṃ jagattrayahitāvaham \|*  
*etatsudurlabhaṃ yacca tasyāṃ caiva prajāyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tadapatyamapatyārthaṃ saṃsāre kila nārada \|*  
*eteṣāṃ durlabhānāṃ hi kiṃcitprāpnoti puṇyavān \|\| 40 \|\|*

37-39a. Though it is unstable, somehow with very great difficulty it is considered to be stable. There too, rare indeed is a chaste wife who follows (her husband in) similar holy rites, who is born of a great family and who will adhere to her husband.

There again, it is rare to be able to practise pious rites along with her, as laid down in the Vedas, in a manner conducive to the welfare of the three worlds.

39b-40. Again it is very rare that one is born to her. That child is for the sake of its child (continuation of the race?) in the world, O Nārada. It is the meritorious one who gets something from among these rare things.

## \|\| 2.23.41 \|\|

*sarvametadavāpnoti sa kopi yadivā na vā \|*  
*kiṃcitkenāpi hi nyūnaṃ saṃsāraḥ kurute naram \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Someone may or may not desire all these things. The worldly existence (Saṃsāra) makes a mān deficient and wanting in something or the other.

## \|\| 2.23.42 \|\|

*atha saṃsāriko doṣaḥ svakṛtaṃ yatra bhujyate \|*  
*gārhasthyaṃ ca praśaṃsaṃti vedāḥ sarve'pi nārada \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. It is a defect in the worldly existence that one has to experience the fruit of one’s own (past) actions.

All the Vedas praise the stage of a householder.

## \|\| 2.23.43 \|\|

*neti kecittatra punaḥ kathaṃ te yadi no gṛhī \|*  
*ato dhātrā ca śāstreṣu sutalābhaḥ praśaṃsitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Some say that it is not so. How can they (survive) if there is no householder? Therefore, the acquisition of a son is praised by Brahmā in the scriptures.

## \|\| 2.23.44 \|\|

*punaścasṛṣṭivṛddhyarthaṃ narakatrāṇanāya ca \|*  
*tatra strīṇāṃ samutpattiṃ vinā sṛṣṭirna jāyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. That is for the sake of further increase in the creation and to save (one) from hell. There, the creation is not possible without the birth of women.

## \|\| 2.23.45 \|\|

*sā ca jātiprakṛtyaiva kṛpaṇā dainyabhāginī \|*  
*tāsāmupari māvajñā bhavediti ca vedhasā \|*  
*śāstreṣūktamasaṃdigdhaṃ vākyametanmahātphalam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. That species is by nature wretched and victim of ill-luck and dejection. Lest there should be disrespect to them, the following statement of great effect has been distinctly made by Brahmā in the scriptures:

## \|\| 2.23.46 \|\|

*daśaputrasamā kanyā daśaputrānpravarddhayan \|*  
*yatphalaṃ labhate martyastallabhyaṃ kanyayaikayā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. ‘A daughter is equal to ten sons. The merit that one derives by bringing up ten sons is obtainable by bringing up one daughter.’

## \|\| 2.23.47-50 \|\|

*tasmātkanyā pituḥ śocyā sadā duḥkhavivardhinī \|\| 47 \|\|*

*yāpi syātpūrṇasarvārthā patiputradhanānvitā \|*  
*tvayoktaṃ ca kṛte hyasyāstadvākyaṃ mama śokadam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kena doṣeṇa me putrī na yogyā āśiṣāmatā \|*  
*na jāto'syāḥ patiḥ kasmādvartate vā kulakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*nirdhanaśca mune kasmātsarveṣāṃ sarvadaḥ kutaḥ \|*  
*iti durghaṭavākyaṃ te mano mohayatīva me \|\| 50 \|\|*

47-50. Hence a daughter becomes deplorable to the father. She increases his misery always even if she happens to be wholly endowed with all objects, even if she possesses sons, a husband and ample wealth. The statement that has been made by you in regard to this (daughter of mine) causes me grief. For what fault was my daughter considered not worthy of benediction? How is it that her husband is one who is not born? How is he one with evil characteristics? How is he devoid of wealth, O sage? How is it that he is the bestower of all on all? This impossible statement of yours bewilders my mind as it were.”

## \|\| 2.23.51 \|\|

*iti taṃ putravātsalyātsabhāryaṃ śokasaṃplutam \|*  
*ahamāśvāsayaṃ vāgbhiḥ satyābhiḥ pāṃḍunaṃdana \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. As he was overwhelmed by sorrow along with his wife owing to the affection for his daughter, O son of Pāṇḍu, I consoled him with truthful words:

## \|\| 2.23.52 \|\|

*mā śucaḥ śailarāja tvaṃ harṣasthāne'tipuṇyabhāk \|*  
*śrṛṇu tadvacanaṃ mahyaṃ yanmayoktaṃ ca hyarthavat \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. “Do not be sad, O king of Mountains, on this occasion of delight. You are highly meritorious. Listen to my statement which is meaningful.

## \|\| 2.23.53 \|\|

*jaganmātā tviyaṃ bālā putrī te sarvasiddhidā \|*  
*purā bhave'bhavadbhāryā satīnāmnā bhavasya yā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. This girl, your daughter, is the mother of this universe, the bestower of all Siddhis. In her former birth she had been the wife of Bhava under the name Satī.

## \|\| 2.23.54 \|\|

*tadasyāḥ kimahaṃ dadmi raverdīpamivālpakaḥ \|*  
*saṃciṃtyeti mahādevyā nāśiṣaṃ dattavānaham \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. ‘What shall I give her—an insignificant fellow giving a lamp to the Sun?’ It was thinking thus that I did not offer any benediction to the great goddess.

## \|\| 2.23.55 \|\|

*na jāto'bhavadbhāryā patiśceti vartate ca bhavo hi saḥ \|*  
*na sa jāto mahādevo bhūtabhavyabhavodbhavaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Her husband is one who is not born, because Bhava is (always) present. That great Lord, the source of all the creatures past, present and future, is one who is not born.

## \|\| 2.23.56-57 \|\|

*śaraṇyaḥ śāśvataḥ śāstā śaṃkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*sarve devā yatpadamāmanaṃti vedaiśca sarvairapi yo na labhyaḥ \|*  
*brahmādiviśvaṃ nanu yasya śaila bālasya vā krīḍanakaṃ vadaṃti \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. Śaṅkara, the supreme Īśvara is the refuge, is eternal, and the chastiser.

All the deities meditate upon him as the goal. He is not obtained even through all the Vedas. O Mountain, the entire universe beginning with Brahmā, they say, is like a toy in the hand of a boy.

## \|\| 2.23.58 \|\|

*sa cāmaṃgalyaśīlo'pi maṃgalāṃ yatano haraḥ \|*  
*nirdhanaḥ sarvadaścāsau veda svaṃ svayameva saḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Though his activities may not be auspicious, Hara is an abode of all auspiciousness. Though he is devoid of wealth, he is the bestower of all. He alone knows himself.

## \|\| 2.23.59 \|\|

*sa ca devo'calaḥ sthāṇurmahādevo'jaro haraḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati patiḥ so'syāstatkimarthaṃ tu śocasi \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. That Lord is permanent, steady, the great Lord, the unageing Hara. He will become her husband. Then why do you feel sorry?”

## Chapter 24 - Kāma is Burned

## \|\| 2.24.1-2 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ śrutvā sabhāryaḥ sa pramodaplutamānasaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya māmiti prāha yadyevaṃ puṇyavānaham \|\| 1 \|\|*

*punaḥ kiṃcitpravakṣyāmi putryā me dakṣiṇaḥ karaḥ \|*  
*uttānaḥ kāraṇaṃ kiṃ tacchrotumicchāmi nārada \|\| 2 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1-2. On hearing this along with his wife, he became highly delighted in his mind. After bowing down to me he said, “If it is so, I am (really) meritorious. I will tell you something more. The right hand of my daughter is spread out (as in offering a thing and thus) faces upwards. What is the reason thereof? O Nārada, I wish to hear about it.”

## \|\| 2.24.3-6 \|\|

*iti pṛṣṭo'smi śailena prāvocaṃ kāraṇaṃ tadā \|*  
*sarvadaiva karo hyasyāḥ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ prati \|\| 3 \|\|*

*abhayasya pradātā'sāvuttānastu karastataḥ \|*  
*eṣā bhāryā jagadbharturvṛṣāṃkasya mahīdhara \|\| 4 \|\|*

*jananī sarvalokasya bhāvinī bhūtabhāvinī \|*  
*tadyathā śīghramevaiṣā yogaṃ yātu pinākinā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tvayā vidheyaṃ vidhivattathā śailendrasattama \|*  
*astyatra sumahatakāryaṃ devānāṃ himabhūdhara \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. On being asked thus by the Mountain, I told the reason then: “Her hand is always in the position of offering freedom from fear to all the living beings. Therefore, the hand faces upwards. O Mountain, she is the wife of the Bull-emblemed Lord of the universe. She is the future mother of all the worlds. She is the sanctifier of all living beings. Hence steps should be duly taken by you, O most excellent one among the leading Mountains, so that she can be immediately united with the Pināka-bearing Lord quickly. In this, O Himālaya, a great task of Devas is involved.”

## \|\| 2.24.7-8 \|\|

*iti procya tamāpṛcchya prāvocaṃ vāsavāya tat \|*  
*mama bhūyastu kartavyaṃ tanmayā kṛtameva hi \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kiṃ tu paṃcaśaraḥ preryaḥ kāryaśeṣe'tra vāsava \|*  
*ityādiśya gataścāhaṃ tārakaṃ prati phālguna \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. After saying this to Himālaya I took leave of him and informed Vāsava too: “Greater part of my duty has been accomplished by me. But the Five-arrowed one (i.e. Madana, the god of Love) should be induced (and sent) for the remaining part of the task.” After directing him thus, O Phālguna, I went to Tāraka.

## \|\| 2.24.9-11 \|\|

*kalipriyatvāttasyainamarthaṃ kathayituṃ sphuṭam \|*  
*himādrirapi me vākyapreritaḥ pārvatīṃ prati \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhavasyārādhanāṃ kartuṃ sasakhīmādiśattadā \|*  
*sā taṃ paricacāreśaṃ tasyā dṛṣṭvā suśīlatām \|\| 10 \|\|*

*puṣpatoyaphalādyāni niyuktā pārvatī vyadhāt \|*  
*mahendropi ca madvākyātsmaraṃ sasmāra bhārata \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. I am fond of quarrels and hence I went to him for intimating this matter to him clearly. Urged by my suggestion, Himādri directed Pārvatī along with her friends to propitiate Bhava (i.e. Śiva). She served that Lord. On seeing her good conduct, Pārvatī was employed (by god Śiva) (to fetch) flowers, water, fruits etc. She duly carried out (the task assigned to her). At my instance, Mahendra remembered Smara (god of Love), O descendant of Bharata.

## \|\| 2.24.12 \|\|

*sa ca tatsmaraṇaṃ jñātvā vasaṃtaratisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*cūtāṃkurāstraḥṛ sahasā prādurāsīnmanobhavaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On coming to know that he was being remembered, (the mind-born god of Love) whose missile was the sprout of Mango tree, appeared immediately in the company of Rati and Vasanta (i.e. the spring season).

## \|\| 2.24.13-16 \|\|

*tamāha ca vaco dhīmānsmaranniva ca taṃ spṛśan \|*  
*upadeśena bahunā kiṃ tvāṃ prati ratipriya \|\| 13 \|\|*

*citte vasasi tena tvaṃ vetsi bhūtamanogatam \|*  
*tathāpi tvāṃ vadiṣyāmi svakāryaparatāṃ smaran \|\| 14 \|\|*

*mamaikaṃ sumahatkāryaṃ kartumarhasi manmatha \|*  
*maheśvaraṃ kṛpānāthaṃ satībhāryāviyojitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*saṃyojaya punardevyā himādrigṛhajātayā \|*  
*devī devaśca tuṣṭau te kariṣyata ihepsitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. The intelligent one (i.e, Indra) touched him (gently) smilingly and spoke to him these words: “O lover of Ṛati, of what avail is much advice to you? You live in the mind. Hence you know what is in the mind of all living beings. Still, I will tell you (something) remembering my eagerness for my own task. It behoves you, O Manmatha, to carry out a great task of mine. Maheśvara, the lord of compassion, is separated from his wife Satī. Unite him with the goddess born in the house of Himādri. When the goddess and the Lord are satisfied, they will carry out whatever you wish.”

## \|\| 2.24.17-20 \|\|

*madana uvāca \|*  
*alīkametaddevendra sa hi devasya poratiḥ \|*  
*nānyāsādayitavyāni tejāṃsi munarabravīt \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vedānteṣu ca māṃ viprā garhasaṃyati punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*mahāśano mahāpāpmā kāmo'yama nalo gahān \|\| 18 \|\|*

*āvṛtaṃ jñānametena jñānināṃ nityavairiṇā \|*  
*tasmādayaṃ sadā tyājyaḥ kāma'hiriva sattamaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*evaṃ śīlasya me kasmātpratuṣyati maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*madyapasyeva pāpasya vāsudevo jagadguraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Madana said:

17-20. This is not true, O Lord of Devas. Indeed that Lord has taken pleasure in penance. As Manu has said, magnificence and refulgence cannot be attained by other means (than penance). In the Vedāntas, the Brāhmaṇas censure and insult me every now and then: “This Kāma (Lust) is a great fire of great appetite, a great sinner. Spiritual knowledge is enveloped by this eternal enemy of wise men. Hence this Kāma should be abandoned always by excellent men, as though it is a serpent.” How will Maheśvara be delighted with me of such a nature? Just as Vāsudeva, the preceptor of the universe, is not pleased with a sinner addicted to drinking liquor, (so is Maheśvara not delighted with me).

## \|\| 2.24.21-25 \|\|

*iṃdra uvāca \|*  
*maivaṃ brūhi mahābhāga tvāṃ vinākaḥ pumānbhuvi \|*  
*dharmamarthaṃ tathā kāmaṃ mokṣaṃ vā prāptumīśvaraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yatkiṃcitsādhyate loke mūlaṃ tasya ca kāmanā \|*  
*kathaṃ kāmaṃ viniṃdati tasmātte mokṣasādhakāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*satyaṃ cāpi śrutervākyaṃ tava rūpaṃ tridhāgatam \|*  
*tāmasaṃ rājasaṃ caiva sāttvikaṃ cāpi manmatha \|\| 23 \|\|*

*amuktitaḥ kāmanayā rūpaṃ tattāmasaṃ tava \|*  
*sukhabuddhyā spṛhā yā ca rūpaṃ tadrājasaṃ tava \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kevalaṃ yāvadarthārthaṃ tadrūpaṃ sāttvikaṃ tava \|*  
*tatte rūpatrayamidaṃ brūhi nopāsate hi ke \|\| 25 \|\|*

Indra said:

21-25. Do not say so, O highly fortunate one. Without you, which man on the earth is competent to attain (the four aims in life, viz.) Dharma, Artha, Kāma and Mokṣa? Whatever is achieved in the world has Kāmanā (Desire) at its root. How is it then that those who aspire after salvation censure Kāma? True indeed is the statement in the Veda that your form is threefold, O Manmatha, viz. Tāmasa, Rājasa and Sāttvika. If the desire is not for liberation(?) it is your Tāmasa form. A mere desire for something, with the intention of having some pleasure, is your Rājasa form. The desire of a simple nature for some object is your Sāttvika form. Who is it, tell me, who does not resort to one of these three forms?

## \|\| 2.24.26-27 \|\|

*tvaṃ sākṣātparamaḥ pūjyaḥ kuru kāryamidaṃ hi naḥ \|*  
*atha vā pīḍitāndṛṣṭvā sāmānyānapi paṃḍitāḥ \|*  
*svaprāṇairapi trāyāṃti parametanmahāphalam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*iti saṃciṃtya kāryaṃ tvaṃ sarvathā kuru tatsphuṭam \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. You are the Great Being itself worthy of being worshipped. Carry out this task of ours. On seeing even ordinary persons afflicted learned men save them even at the cost of their own lives, while this (task) is great and has great outcome. Thinking thus, you make that task clearly manifest in every respect.

## \|\| 2.24.28 \|\|

*ityā karṇya tathetyuktvā vasaṃtaratisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*pikādisainyasaṃpanno himādriṃ prayayau smaraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On hearing this and saying “So be it”, Smara (i.e. Madana) went to Himādri. He was accompanied by Rati and Vasanta. He was richly (endowed) (supplied) with cuckoo and other parts of his army.

## \|\| 2.24.29 \|\|

*tatrāpaśyata śaṃbhoḥ sa puṇyamāśramamaṃḍalam \|*  
*nānāvṛkṣasamākīrṇaṃ śāṃtasattvasamākulam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. There he saw the holy region of the hermitage of Śaṃbhu. It was full of many kinds of trees and was teeming with animals which were quiescent therein.

## \|\| 2.24.30 \|\|

*tatrāpaśyattrinetrasya vīrakaṃnāma dvārapam \|*  
*yathā sākṣānmaheśānaṃ gaṇaāṃścāyutaśo'sya ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. There he saw the gatekeeper of the Three-eyed Lord, named Vīraka as if Lord Maheśāna incarnate, and ten thousands of his Gaṇas.

## \|\| 2.24.31-32 \|\|

*dadarśa ca maheśānaṃ nāsāgrakṛtalocanam \|*  
*devadārudrumacchāyāvedikā madhyamāśritam \|*  
*samākāyaṃ sukhāsīnaṃ samādhisthaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

*nistaraṃgaṃ vinirgṛhya sthitamiṃdriyagocarān \|*  
*ātmānamātmanā devaṃ praviṣṭaṃ tapaso nidhim \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. He saw Maheśāna with the eyes fixed on the tip of the nose. He was seated in the middle of an altar under the shade of a Devadāru tree. His body was straight and erect. He was seated motionless, comfortably engaged in meditation. Maheśvara had controlled all the sense organs and had entered the Supreme Ātman through (his) Ātman. He was a storehouse of penance.

## \|\| 2.24.33 \|\|

*taṃ tathāvidhamālokya soṃtarbhedāya yatnavān \|*  
*bhramaradhvanivyājena viveśa madano manaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On seeing him in that posture, Madana tried to enter within him. Under the pretext of the humming (of the) bee, he entered the mind (of Śiva).

## \|\| 2.24.34 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devo vikāsitavilocanaḥ \|*  
*sasmāra nagarājasya tanayāṃ raktamānasaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. In the meantime the Lord with the eyes opened and the mind affected with love, remembered the daughter of the king of Mountains.

## \|\| 2.24.35 \|\|

*niveditā vīrakeṇa viveśa ca gireḥ sutā \|*  
*tasminkāle mahābhāgā sadā yadvadupaiti sā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. (Ushered in and) announced by Vīraka, the daughter of the Mountain entered. At that time the highly fortunate girl entered in the same manner as she used to do usually.

## \|\| 2.24.36 \|\|

*tatastasyāṃ manaḥ svīyamanuraktamavekṣya ca \|*  
*nigṛhya līlayā devaḥ svakaṃ pṛṣṭhamavaikṣata \|*  
*tāvadāpūrṇadhanuṣamapaśyata ratipriyam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The Lord found that his mind had become enamoured of her. He sportingly curbed (the feeling) and looked behind. There he saw the Lover of Rati (Madana) with the bow fully bent.

## \|\| 2.24.37 \|\|

*tannāśakṛpayā devo nānāsthāneṣu so'gamat \|*  
*tāvatpasyati pṛṣṭhastamākṛṣya dhanuṣaḥ śaram \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. With the compassionate feeling of destroying (that feeling of love), the Lord went to various places. Everywhere he saw Madana standing behind with the arrow fully drawn on the bow.

## \|\| 2.24.38 \|\|

*sa nadīḥ parvatāścaiva āśramānsarasīstathā \|*  
*paribhramanmahādevaḥ pṛṣṭhasthaṃ tamavaikṣata \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Mahādeva wandered over rivers, mountains, hermitages and lakes. But he saw him always behind him.

## \|\| 2.24.39 \|\|

*jagattrayaṃ paribhramya punarāgātsvamāśramam \|*  
*pṛṣṭhasthameva taṃ vīkṣya niḥśvāsaṃ mumuce haraḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After wandering over all the three worlds, he came back to his hermitage once again. On seeing him still stationed behind, Hara released a deep breath.

## \|\| 2.24.40 \|\|

*tatastṛtīyanetrotthavahninā nākavāsinām \|*  
*krośatāṃ gamitaḥ kāmo bhasmatvaṃ pāṃḍunaṃdana \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Thereafter, O son of Pāṇḍu, Kāma was reduced to ash by the fire emanating from the third eye even as the heaven-dwellers were lamenting.

## \|\| 2.24.41 \|\|

*sasa tu taṃ bhasmasātkṛtvā haranetrodbhavo'nalaḥ \|*  
*vyajṛṃbhata jagaddagdhuṃ jvālāpūritadiṅmukhaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. After reducing him to ash, the fire that arose from the eyes of Hara increased in size in order to burn the entire universe. It filled the faces of all cardinal points with its flames.

## \|\| 2.24.42-43 \|\|

*tato bhavo jagaddhetorvyabhajajjātavedasam \|*  
*sāhaṃkāre jane caṃdre sumanassu ca gītake \|\| 42 \|\|*

*bhṛṃgeṣu kokilāsyeṣu vihāreṣu smarānalam \|*  
*tatprāptau snehasaṃyuktaṃ kāmināṃ hṛdayaṃ kila \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. Thereafter, for the sake of the people of the universe Bhava divided that fire of Smara among proud people, the moon, flowers, songs, bees, the beaks of the cuckoo and sporting grounds. Indeed when one is near them, the heart of lovers becomes more affectionate.

## \|\| 2.24.44-45 \|\|

*jvālayatyaniśaṃ so'gnirduścikitsyo'sukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*vilokya haraniḥśvāsajvālābhasmīkṛtaṃ smaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

*vilalāpa ratirddīnā madhunā baṃdhunā saha \|*  
*vilapaṃtī subahuśo madhunā parisāṃtvitā \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45a. That fire gets enkindled eternally. It is very difficult to be cured and is conducive to unhappiness.

On seeing Smara reduced to ash by the flames of the fiery breaths of Hara, pitiable Rati cried and lamented along with (her) friend Madhu (‘Spring’).

45b. She who was thus crying was consoled by Madhu in various ways:

## \|\| 2.24.46 \|\|

*ratyāḥ pralāpamākarṇya devadevo vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|*  
*kṛpayā parayā prāha kāmapatnīṃ nirīkṣya ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On hearing the lamentations of Rati, the Bull-emblemed Lord of Devas looked at Kāma’s wife with great compassion and said:

## \|\| 2.24.47 \|\|

*amūrto'pi hyayaṃ bhadre kāryaṃ sarvaṃ patistava \|*  
*ratikāle dhruvaṃ bāle kariṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “O gentle lass, though he has no body, your husband will do everything necessary at the time of amorous dalliance. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 2.24.48 \|\|

*yadā viṣṇuśca bhavitā vasudevātmajo vibhuḥ \|*  
*tadai tasya suto yaḥ syātsapatiste bhaviṣyati \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. When Lord Viṣṇu incarnates as the son of Vasudeva, he who will be born as his son, will be your husband.”

## \|\| 2.24.49 \|\|

*sā praṇamya tato rudramiti proktā ratistataḥ \|*  
*jagāma svecchayā gatyā vasaṃtādibhiranvitā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. On being told thus, Rati bowed down to Rudra and went away as she pleased in the company of Vasanta and others.

## Chapter 25 - Mahādeva Meets Pārvatī: Eagerness for Marriage with Pārvatī

## \|\| 2.25.1-3 \|\|

*arjuna uvāca \|*  
*devarṣe varṇyate ceyaṃ kathā pīyūṣasodarā \|*  
*punaretanmune brūhi yadā vetti maheśvaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*bhagavānsvāṃ satīṃ bhāryāṃ vadhārthaṃ cāpi tārakam \|*  
*satyāśca virahāttapyandadāha kimasau smaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tvayaivoktaṃ sa virahātsatyāstapyati vai tapaḥ \|*  
*himādrimāsthito devastasyāḥ saṃgamavāṃchayā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Arjuna said:

1-3. O celestial sage, the story that is being narrated (by you) is (life-giving) just like Nectar. O sage tell me further. Lord Maheśvara knows Satī as his own wife and the task of the slaying of Tāraka. He was performing the penance due to the bereavement of Satī. (In spite of all these) why did he burn Smara (Kāma)? You had also said that he performed penance due to the separation from Satī and that the Lord occupied Himādri because of his desire to have union with her.

Nārada narrated:

## \|\| 2.25.4-9 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*satyametatpurā pārtha bhavasyedaṃ manīṣitam \|*  
*ataptatapasā yogo na kartavyo mayā'nayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tapo vinā śuddhadeho na kathaṃcana jāyate \|*  
*asuddhadehena samaṃ saṃyogo naiva daihikaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mahatkarmāṇi yānīha teṣāṃ mūlaṃ sadā tapaḥ \|*  
*nātaptatapasāṃ siddhirmahatkarmāṇi yāṃti vai \|\| 6 \|\|*

*etasmātkāraṇāddevo darpitaṃ taṃ dadāha tu \|*  
*tato dagdhe smare cāpi pārvatīmapi vrītitām \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vihāya sagaṇo devaḥ kailāsaṃ samapadyata \|*  
*devī ca paramodvignā praskhalaṃtī padepade \|\| 8 \|\|*

*jīvitaṃ svaṃ viniṃdaṃtī babhrāmetastataścasā \|*  
*himādrirapi sve śrṛṃge rudatīṃ pṛṣṭavānratim \|\| 9 \|\|*

4-9. It is true, O son of Pṛthā, that this was the desire of Bhava at the outset: “I must not be united with her before performing the penance. Without a penance, one does not become pure in body. Bodily contact with one of impure body is not (proper). Penance is the root cause of all great acts. The achievement of those who have not performed penance does not reach (the level of) great men’s deeds. It is for this reason that the Lord burned that arrogant one (i.e. Kāma).

When Smara was burned, the Lord left off Pārvatī (standing) there bashfully. Accompanied by the Gaṇas, the Lord reached Kailāsa.

The goddess got very much dejected and faltered at every step. Cursing her own life, she wandered here and there.

Himādri asked Rati who was lamenting on his peak:

## \|\| 2.25.10 \|\|

*kāsi kasyāsi kalyāṇi kimarthaṃ cāpi rodiṣi \|*  
*pṛṣṭā sā ca ratiḥ sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “Who are you, O auspicious lady? To whom do you belong? Why do you cry?” On being asked, Rati recounted everything as it happened.

## \|\| 2.25.11 \|\|

*nivedite tathā ratyā śailaḥ saṃbhrāṃtamānasaḥ \|*  
*prāpya svāṃ tanayāṃ pāṇāvādāyāgātsvakaṃ puram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When it was reported thus by Rati, the Mountain became agitated in his mind. He reached the place (of Pārvatī), took his daughter by hand and went to his own city.

## \|\| 2.25.12 \|\|

*sā tatra pitarau prāha sakhīnāṃ vadanena ca \|*  
*durbhagena śarīreṇa kimanena hi kāraṇam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Through the mouth of her friends, she informed her parents thus: “Of what use is this wretched unfortunate body?

## \|\| 2.25.13 \|\|

*dehavāsaṃ parityakṣye prāpsye vābhimataṃ patim \|*  
*asādhyaṃ cāpyabhīṣṭaṃ ca kathaṃ prāpyaṃ tapo vinā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I will either get the husband desired (by me) or cast off this body. If the desired object is impossible to be achieved, how can it be obtained without penance?

## \|\| 2.25.14 \|\|

*niyamairvividhaistasmācchoṣayiṣye kalevaram \|*  
*anujānīta māṃ tatra yadi vaḥ karuṇā mayi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Hence I will dry up my physical body by means of different kinds of restraints. If you both have kindness towards me, permit me for this.”

## \|\| 2.25.15 \|\|

*śrutveti vacanaṃ mātā pitā ca prāha tāṃ śubhām \|*  
*u meti capale putri na kṣamaṃ tāvakaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On hearing these words, the mother and father said to that auspicious (girl), “U-MĀ” (‘Oh, do not’)! O excessively frail daughter, your body is not capable of enduring the pain and rigour of penance.

## \|\| 2.25.16-17 \|\|

*soḍhuṃ kleśātmarūpasya tapasaḥ saumyadarśane \|*  
*bhāvīnyapyani vāryāṇi vastūni ca sadaiva tu \|\| 16 \|\|*

*bhāvinorthā bhavaṃtyeva narasyānicchatopi hi \|*  
*tasmānna tapasā te'sti bāle kiṃcitprayojanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. O girl of gentle appearance, the future events and objects cannot be avoided at any time. Even if a man does not wish for them, the future events do take place. Hence O girl, no purpose will be served by means of penance.”

Śrīdevī replied.

## \|\| 2.25.18 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*yadidaṃ bhavato vākyaṃ na samyagiti me matiḥ \|*  
*kevalaṃ na hi daivena prāptumartho hi śakyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. My opinion is that this statement of yours is not correct. It is not through destiny alone that objects, are achieved.

## \|\| 2.25.19 \|\|

*tkiṃciddaivāddhaṭhātkiṃcitkiṃcideva svabhāvataḥ \|*  
*puruṣaḥ phalamāpnoti caturthaṃ nātra kāraṇam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A man acquires fruit partly by means of fate, partly by means of force (efforts) and partly as a natural sequence. There is no fourth means (for acquisition of fruit).

## \|\| 2.25.20 \|\|

*brahmaṇā cāpi brahmatvaṃ prāptaṃ kilatapobalāt \|*  
*anyairapi ca yallabdhaṃ tannasaṃkhyātumutsahe \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. It is said that Brahmāhood was acquired by Brahmā by the power of penance. I do not wish to count what has been acquired by others.

## \|\| 2.25.21 \|\|

*adhruveṇa śarīreṇa yadyabhīṣṭaṃ na sādhyate \|*  
*paścātsa śocyate maṃdaḥ patite'smiñcharīrake \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If the desired thing is not accomplished through the body which is unstable (i.e. perishable), a foolish fellow will regret later when the body falls off (i.e. passes away).

## \|\| 2.25.22 \|\|

*yasya dehasya dharmo'yaṃ kvacijjāyetkvacinmriyet \|*  
*kvacidgarbhagataṃ naśyejjātamātraṃ kvacittathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. This is the nature of this body. It is born in some place and it dies in another place. In some cases, it dies in the womb and in some cases it dies as soon as it is born.

## \|\| 2.25.23 \|\|

*bālye ca yauvane cāpi vārdhakyepi vinaśyati \|*  
*tena caṃcaladehena ko'rthaḥ svārtho na cedbhavet \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. It perishes in childhood, in youth or in old age. Of what use is this fickle body, if one’s own purpose is not achieved?

## \|\| 2.25.24 \|\|

*ityuktvā svasakhīyuktā pitṛbhyāṃ sāśru vīkṣitā \|*  
*śrṛṃgaṃ himavataḥ puṇyaṃ nānāścaryaṃ jagāma sā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. After saying this, she went to the peak of Himālaya, the holy peak of many miracles and mysteries. She was accompanied by her friends and was tearfully looked at by her parents.

## \|\| 2.25.25 \|\|

*tatrāṃ barāṇi saṃtyajya bhūṣaṇāni ca śailajā \|*  
*saṃvītā valkalairdivyaistapo'tapyata saṃyatā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. There, the daughter of the Mountain cast off her (costly) robes and ornaments. She wore divine bark garments and performed penance with great restraint.

## \|\| 2.25.26 \|\|

*īśvaraṃ hṛdi saṃsthāpya praṇavābhyasanādṛtā \|*  
*munīnāmapya bhūnmānyā tadānīṃ pārtha pārvatī \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Installing Īśvara in the heart and enthusiastically reciting Praṇava (i.e. Oṃkāra), Pārvatī became one worthy of being honoured even by sages and was then so honoured (even by them), O son of Pṛthā.

## \|\| 2.25.27-31 \|\|

*trisnātā pāṭalāpatrabhakṣakābhūcchataṃ samāḥ \|*  
*śaṃta ca bilvapatreṇa śīrṇona kṛtabhojanā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*jalabhakṣā śataṃ cābhūcchataṃ vai vāyubhojanā \|*  
*tato niyamamādāya pādāṃguṣṭhasthitābhavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nirāhārā tatastāpaṃ prāpustattapaso janāḥ \|*  
*tato jagatsamālokya tadīyatapasorjitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*harastatrāyayau sākṣādbrahmacārivapurddharaḥ \|*  
*vasāno valkalaṃ divyaṃ rauravājinasaṃvṛtaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sulakṣaṇāṣāḍhadharaḥ sadvṛttaḥ prati bhānavān \|*  
*tatastaṃ pūjayāmāsustatsakhyo bahumānataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

27-31. She used to take holy baths thrice a day. For a hundred years she used to eat only a leaf of Pāṭala (trumpet flower-tree). For another hundred years, she ate only a withered Bilva leaf. For another hundred years, she drank water only and for still another hundred years she lived on air only. Thereafter practising restraints she stood on the big toes of her feet. Then she remained without any food. On account of her penance, people became scorched. Then on seeing the universe energized (Scorched?) by her penance, Hara personally came there in the guise of a Brahmacārin (‘religious student’). He wore divine bark garments and covered himself with the hide of Ruru deer. He held a staff having the requisite good characteristics. He had presence of mind and decent behaviour. There upon, with great respect her friends received him and adored him.

## \|\| 2.25.32-36 \|\|

*vaktumicchuḥ śailaputrīṃ sakhībhiriti coditaḥ \|*  
*brahmanniyaṃ mahābhāgā gṛhītaniyamā śubhā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*muhūrtapaṃcamātreṇa niyamo'syāḥ samāpyate \|*  
*tatpratīkṣasva taṃ kālaṃ paścādasmatsakhīsamam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*nānāvidā dharmavārtāḥ prakariṣyasi brāhmaṇa \|*  
*ityuktvā vijayādyāstā devīcaritavarṇanaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*aśrumukhyo dvijasyāgre ninyuḥ kālaṃ ca taṃ tadā \|*  
*tataḥ kāle kiṃcidūne brahmacārī mahāmatiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vilokanamiṣeṇāgādāśramopasthitaṃ hradam \|*  
*nipapāta ca tatrāsau cukrośātitarāṃ tataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

32-36. When he expressed his desire to speak to the daughter of the Mountain, he was urged (to wait) thus by (her) friends:

“O holy Brāhmaṇa, this splendid girl of great fortune has taken up holy observances and restraints. In another five Muhūrtas (i.e. four hours) her holy observances will be concluded. Therefore, wait till that time. Thereafter, O Brāhmaṇa, you will carry on a dialogue with our friend on various topics relating to virtue, piety and devotion.”

After saying this, those friends, Vijayā and others, spent their time in front of the Brāhmaṇa describing the activities of the goddess with tears on their faces (eyes).

A little before the close of the stipulated period, the highly intelligent Brāhmacārin, under the pretext of a general survey (of the premises) went to a deep pool of water situated near her hermitage. He fell down into it and therefore cried extremely aloud.

## \|\| 2.25.37-39 \|\|

*ahamatra nimajjāmi ko'pi māmuddhareta bhoḥ \|*  
*iti tāreṇa krośaṃtaṃ śrutvā taṃ vijayādikāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ājagmustvarayā yuktā dadustasmai karaṃ ca tāḥ \|*  
*sa cukrośa tato gāḍhaṃ dūredūre punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*nāhaṃ spṛśāmyasaṃsiddhāṃ mriye vā nānṛtaṃ tvidam \|*  
*tataḥ samāptaniyamā pārvatī svayamāyayau \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. “I am drowning here. One of you, kindly lift me up.” On hearing him cry aloud in a shrill voice thus, Vijayā and others came there and offered him their hands. Thereupon he sank deeper and deeper and went farther and farther crying louder and louder. “I would rather die than touch a girl without spiritual achievement. This is not a lie.” Thereupon, Pārvatī herself came there after concluding her holy observances.

## \|\| 2.25.40-41 \|\|

*savyaṃ karaṃ dadāvasya taṃ cāsau nābhyanandata \|*  
*bhadre yacchuci naiva syādyaccaivāvajñayā kṛtam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sadoṣeṇa kṛtaṃ yacca tadādadyānna karhicit \|*  
*savyaṃ cāśuci te hastaṃ nāvalaṃbāmi karhicit \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. She offered him her left hand but he did not approve of it. “O gentle lady, one shall not accept what is not at all clean, what has been done contemptuously and what has been performed by one with some defects. Your left hand is unclean and I will never hold it.”

## \|\| 2.25.42-43 \|\|

*ityuktā pārvatī prāha nāhaṃ dattaṃ ca dakṣiṇam \|*  
*dadāmi kasyacidvipra devadevāya kalpitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇaṃ me karaṃ devo grahītā bhava eva ca \|*  
*śīryate cogratapasā satyametanmayoditam \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. On being told thus, Pārvatī said: “I will not offer my right hand to anyone, O Brāhmaṇa, as it has been allotted to the Lord of the Devas. Lord Bhava alone will hold my right hand, even if it were to be shattered by severe penance. What has been said by me is true.”

## \|\| 2.25.44-48 \|\|

*vipra uvāca \|*  
*yadyevamavalepaste gamanaṃ kena vāryate \|*  
*yathā tava pratijñeyaṃ mamāpīyaṃ tathācalā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*rudrasyāpi vayaṃ mānyāḥ kīdṛśaṃ te tapo vada \|*  
*viṣamasthaṃ yatra vipraṃ mriyamāṇamupekṣasi \|\| 45 \|\|*

*avajā nāsi viprāṃstvaṃ tacchīghraṃ vraja darśanāt \|*  
*yadi vā manyase pūjyāṃstato'bhyuddhara nānyathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tato vicārya bahudhā iti ceti ca sā śubhā \|*  
*viprasyoddharaṇaṃ sarvadharmebhyo'manyatādhikam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tataḥ sā dakṣiṇaṃ dattvā karaṃ taṃ projjahāra ca \|*  
*naraṃ nārī proddharati sajjantaṃ bhavavāridhau \|*  
*etatsandarśanārthāya tathā cakre bhavodbhavaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

44-48. If your pride is of this sort, by whom can (my) departure be prevented? Just like your vow, my vow too is unshakable. We (Brāhmaṇas) are worthy of respect of even Rudra. Of what nature is your penance, tell me, whereby you neglect a distressed Brāhmaṇa who is on the point of death. If you disrespect Brāhmaṇas go away from (the path of) my vision. If you consider them worthy of being worshipped, lift me up. Otherwise not.

Thereupon, after pondering upon the pros and cons in various ways, the splendid lady considered the uplift of the Brāhmaṇa superior to all the other Dharmas. Then she offered him her right hand and lifted him up. It was to demonstrate that a woman redeems a man drowning in the ocean of worldly existence, that the Lord, the source of the world of existence, did so.

## \|\| 2.25.49 \|\|

*proddhṛtya ca tataḥ snātvā baddhva yogāsanaṃ sthitā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. After lifting him up she took her bath and seated herself in a yogic posture.

## \|\| 2.25.50 \|\|

*brahmacārī tataḥ prāha prahasankimidaṃ śubhe \|*  
*kartukāmāsi tanvaṃgi dṛḍhayogāsanasthitā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The religious student then said laughingly: “O splendid lady, what is it that you wish to do that you have adopted a firm yogic posture? O lady of slender limbs!”

## \|\| 2.25.51 \|\|

*devī prāha jvālayiṣye śarīraṃ yogavahninā \|*  
*mahādevakṛtamatirucchiṣṭāhaṃ yato'bhavam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The goddess replied: “With the Yogic fire I shall burn this body, since I have become Ucchiṣṭa (i.e. left over, spoilt) though my mind was fixed in Mahādeva.”

## \|\| 2.25.52 \|\|

*brahmacārī tataḥ prāha kāścidbrāhmaṇakāmyayā \|*  
*kṛtvā vārtāstataḥ svīyamabhīṣṭaṃ kuru pārvati \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The Brahmacārin then said: “O Pārvatī! After speaking a few words (on some topic) as desired by a Brāhmaṇa you may do as you please.

## \|\| 2.25.53 \|\|

*nopahanyāṃ kadācidvi sādhubhirviprakāmanā \|*  
*dharmamenaṃ manyase cenmuhūrtaṃ brūhi pārvati \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. A desire of a Brāhmaṇa should never be disregarded by good people. If you accept this as Dharma, O Pārvatī, speak (with me) for a short while.”

## \|\| 2.25.54 \|\|

*devī prāha brūhi vipra muhūrtaṃ saṃsthitā tvaham \|*  
*tataḥ svayaṃ vratī prāha devīṃ tāṃ svasakhīyutām \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The goddess said, “O Brāhmaṇa, speak, I shall wait for a Muhūrta (i.e. 48 minutes).”

Then the holy observer of rites himself said to the goddess accompanied by her friends:

## \|\| 2.25.55 \|\|

*kimarthamiti rambhoru nave vayasi duścaram \|*  
*tapastvayā samārabdhaṃ nānurūpaṃ vibhāti me \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. “What for, O beautiful lady, is this penance begun in the fresh bloom of your youth? It does not appear to me to be befitting.

## \|\| 2.25.56 \|\|

*durlabhaṃ prāpya mānuṣyaṃ girirājagṛhe'dhunā \|*  
*bhogāṃśca durlabhāndevi tyaktvā kiṃ kliśyate vapuḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. You have obtained the rare birth as a human being in the abode of the king of Mountains. Why do you, O gentle lady, forsake all worldly pleasures of very rare nature and subject your body to torture?

## \|\| 2.25.57 \|\|

*atīva dūye vīkṣya tvāṃ sukumāratarākṛtim \|*  
*atyugratapasā kliṣṭā padminīva himarditā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. I am much pained on seeing you—a girl of excessively delicate frame—having become extremely afflicted like a lotus plant smitten by frost.

## \|\| 2.25.58 \|\|

*idaṃ cānyattva śubhe śiraso rogadaṃ mama \|*  
*yaddehaṃ tyaktukāmā tvaṃ prabuddhā nāsi bālike \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O splendid lady, this is another thing concerning you that gives me a great headache that you are desirous of giving up your body. O girl, you are not enlightened.

## \|\| 2.25.59 \|\|

*vāmaḥ kāmo manuṣyeṣu satyametadvaco yataḥ \|*  
*spṛhaṇīyāsi sarveṣāmevaṃ pīḍayase vapuḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The statement that the god of Love is vile and crooked in regard to human beings is indeed true, because although you are lovable to all, you are subjecting your body to pains this way.

## \|\| 2.25.60 \|\|

*avijñātānvayo nagnaḥ śūlī bhūtagaṇādhipaḥ \|*  
*śmaśānanilayo bhasmoddhūlano vṛṣavāhanaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. (The one whom you desire) is naked. His antecedents and family background are unknown. He is a bearer of a trident. He is the Lord of the groups of goblins. His abode is cremation ground. His vehicle is a bull. He smears his body with ash.

## \|\| 2.25.61 \|\|

*gajājino dvijihvādyalaṃkṛtāṃgo jaṭādharaḥ \|*  
*virūpākṣaḥ kathaṃkāraṃ nirguṇaḥ syāttavocitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. He covers himself with the hide of an elephant. His limbs are adorned with serpents etc. He wears matted locks of hair. He is deformed in the eyes. He is devoid of Guṇas (‘qualities’). How can he be suitable unto you?

## \|\| 2.25.62 \|\|

*guṇā ye kulaśīlādya varāṇāmuditā budhaiḥ \|*  
*teṣāmeko'pi naivāsti tasmiṃstannocitaḥ sa te \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Nobility of birth, good conduct and other qualities have been spoken by learned men as the qualities in a bridegroom. Not even one among them finds a place in him. Hence he is not suitable unto you.

## \|\| 2.25.63 \|\|

*śocanīyatamā pūrvamāsītpārvati kaumudī \|*  
*tvaṃ saṃvṛttā dvitīyāsi tasyāstatsaṃgamāśayā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Formerly the moon-light (the moon’s digit) was worthy of being pitied on account of its desire to be in contact with him, O Pārvatī. Now you have become a second one wishing his company.

## \|\| 2.25.64 \|\|

*tapodhanāḥ sarvasamā vayaṃ yadyapi pārvati \|*  
*dunotyeva tavāraṃbhaḥ śūlāyāṃ yūpasatkriyā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Although we ascetics view everyone equally, O Pārvatī, this enterprise on your part pains me. It is like having Śūla (i.e. stake for impaling criminals) for consecration as Yūpa (i.e. sacrificial post).

## \|\| 2.25.65 \|\|

*vṛṣabhārohaṇaṃ vāsaḥ śmaśāne pāṇisaṃgrahaḥ \|*  
*savyālapāṇinā kṣaumagajatvagbaṃdhanaḥ katham \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. How can you have (he endure) all these things, viz. riding on a bull, residence in cremation ground, being hand in hand with one who has serpents round his arms and silken cloth tied with elephant hide?

## \|\| 2.25.66 \|\|

*janahāsyakaraṃ sarvaṃ tvayārabdhamasāṃpratam \|*  
*strībhāvādbhūtisaṃparkkaḥ kathaṃ cābhimatastava \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Everything provoking the derisive laughter of the common people, and everything irrelevant has been begun by you. Being a woman, how was a contact with Bhūti (ash, riches) desired by you?

## \|\| 2.25.67 \|\|

*nivartaya manastasmādasmātsarvavirodhinaḥ \|*  
*mṛgākṣi madanārātermarkaṭākṣasya prārthanāt \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Hence retract your mind from this (i.e. Śiva), the enemy of Madana, the antagonist of everyone. O fawn-eyed one, desist from wooing the monkey-eyed one.”

## \|\| 2.25.68 \|\|

*viruddhavādinaṃ caivaṃ brahmacāriṇamīśvaram \|*  
*niśamya kupitā devī prāha vācā sagadgadam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. On hearing the Brahmacārin who was Īśvara himself and who was speaking against Īśvara, the goddess became infuriated and said in words faltering (due to emotion):

## \|\| 2.25.69 \|\|

*mā mā brāhmaṇa bhāṣiṣṭhā viruddhamiti śaṃkare \|*  
*mahattamo yāti pumāndevadevasya niṃdayā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. “O Brāhmaṇa, do not, do not speak against Śaṅkara thus. A man enters dense darkness through the contemptuous insult of the Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 2.25.70 \|\|

*na samyagabhijānāsi tasya devasya ceṣṭitam \|*  
*śrṛṇu brāhmaṇa tvaṃ pāpādyathāsmātparimucyase \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. You do not understand the activities of the Lord properly. Listen, O Brāhmaṇa, so that you shall be absolved of this sin.

## \|\| 2.25.71 \|\|

*sa ādiḥ sarvajagatāṃ kosya vedānvayaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ jagadyasya rūpaṃ digvāsāḥ kīrtyate tataḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. He is the primordial cause of all the worlds. Therefore, who can know his family? He is glorified as Digvāsas (i.e. having the cardinal points for his garments) because the entire universe is his form.

## \|\| 2.25.72 \|\|

*guṇatrayamayaṃ śūlaṃ śūlī yasmādbibhārte saḥ \|*  
*abaddhāḥ sarvato muktā bhūtā eva ca tatpatiḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. He is called Śūlin because he bears the Śūla—the trident in the form of the three Guṇas. The Bhūtas are those who are not in bondage, those who are liberated in every respect. He is the Lord of those Bhūtas.

## \|\| 2.25.73 \|\|

*śmaśānaṃ cāpi saṃsārastadvāsī kṛpayārthinām \|*  
*bhūtayaḥ kathitā bhūtistāṃ bibharti sa bhūtibhṛt \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The cremation ground (is symbolic of) the whole world. He stays there because he is compassionate towards the suppliants. Bhūti (‘prosperity’) constitutes riches and he bears it. Hence he is called Bhūtibhṛt.

## \|\| 2.25.74 \|\|

*vṛṣo dharma iti proktastamārūḍhastato vṛṣī \|*  
*sarpāśca doṣāḥ krodhādyāstānbibharti jaganmayaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Dharma is called by the name Vṛṣa (bull). He rides on it. Therefore he is called Vṛṣī. Serpents are the defects beginning with anger. The Lord identical with the universe holds them (under control).

## \|\| 2.25.75-78 \|\|

*nānāvidhāḥ karmayogā jaṭārūpā bibharti saḥ \|*  
*vedatrayī trinetrāṇi tripuraṃ triguṇaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*bhasmīkaroti taddevastripuradhnastataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*evaṃvidha mahādevaṃ vidurye sūkṣmadarśinaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*kathaṃkāraṃ hi te nāma bhajaṃte naiva taṃ haram \|*  
*atha vā bhītasaṃsārāḥ sarve vipra yato janāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*vimṛśya kurvate sarvaṃ vimṛśyaitanmayā kṛtam \|*  
*śubhaṃ vāpyaśubhaṃ vāstu tvamapyenaṃ prapūjaya \|\| 78 \|\|*

75-78. Different kinds of holy rites (Karmayogas) are the matted locks of hair he wears. The three Vedas are the three eyes. The three Puras means the physical body having the three Guṇas. The Lord reduces it to ash. Therefore, he is remembered as Tripuraghna. How can those people with subtle vision who understood Mahādeva of such a nature remain without worshipping Hara. Or, O Brāhmaṇa, since all people are afraid of worldly existence, they do everything after thinking and pondering upon everything. This has been done by me too after thinking deeply. Whether he is auspicious or inauspicious, you too do worship him.”

## \|\| 2.25.79 \|\|

*iti bruvaṃtyāṃ tasyāṃ tu kiṃcitprasphuritādharam \|*  
*vijñāya tāṃ sakhīmāha kimapyeṣa vivakṣukaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. When she said thus, the lips of the Brāhmaṇa quivered slightly. On coming to know of it, she said to the friend: “He is desirous of saying something.

## \|\| 2.25.80 \|\|

*vāryatāmiti vipro'yaṃ mahaddūṣaṇabāṣakaḥ \|*  
*na kevalaṃ pāpabhāgī śrotā vai syānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Let this Brāhmaṇa be prevented. He speaks disparagingly about great men. It is not only he who speaks thus but he who beats the same also will be a sharer in the sin.

## \|\| 2.25.81 \|\|

*atha vā kiṃ ca naḥ kāryaṃ vādena saha brāhmaṇaiḥ \|*  
*karṇau pidhāya yāsyāmo yathā yaḥ syāttatāstu saḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Or what have we to do with an argument with the Brāhmaṇa? We shall close our ears and go away. Let him be whatever he is.”

## \|\| 2.25.82 \|\|

*ityuktvotthāya gacchaṃtyāṃ pidhāya śravaṇāvubhau \|*  
*svarūpaṃ samupāśritya jagṛhe vasanaṃ haraḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. When, after saying thus she got up, closed her ears and was about to go, Hara assumed his real form and caught hold of her garment.

## \|\| 2.25.83 \|\|

*tato nirīkṣya taṃ devaṃ saṃbhrāṃtā parameśvarī \|*  
*praṇipatya maheśānaṃ tuṣṭāvāvanatā umā \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. On seeing the Lord, the great goddess became agitated. Umā bowed down to Maheśāna with bent (head) and eulogized (him).

## \|\| 2.25.84 \|\|

*prāha tāṃ ca mahādevo dāso'smi tava śobhane \|*  
*tapodravyeṇa krītaśca samādiśa yathepsitam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Mahādeva spoke to her: “O splendid lady, I am your slave. I have been bought by you with the wealth in the form of peṇance. Command me as you please.”

## \|\| 2.25.85 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*manasastvaṃ prabhuḥ śaṃbho dattaṃ tacca mayā tava \|*  
*vapuṣaḥ pitarāvīśau tau sammānayitumarhasi \|\| 85 \|\|*

The goddess said:

85\. O Śaṃbhu, you are the Lord of my mind. That has been already given to you by me. My parents are the lords of my body. It behoves you to honour them.

## \|\| 2.25.86-87 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*pitrā hi te parijñātaṃ dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ rūpaśālinīm \|*  
*bālāṃ svayaṃvaraṃ putrī mahaṃ dāsyāmi nānyathā \|\| 86 \|\|*

*tattasya sarvamevāstu vacanaṃ tvaṃ himācalam \|*  
*svayaṃvarārthaṃ suśroṇi preraya tvāṃ vṛṇe tataḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

Mahādeva said:

86-87. On seeing you endowed with beauty, your father took a vow: “I will give my daughter only in a Svayaṃvara and not otherwise.” Hence let his words be so. O lady with excellent buttocks, you urge Himācala to conduct a Svayaṃvara. I shall accept you therein.

## \|\| 2.25.88 \|\|

*ityuktvā tāṃ mahādevaḥ śuciḥ śuciṣado vibhuḥ \|*  
*jagāmeṣṭaṃ tadā deśaṃ svapuraṃ prayayau ca sā \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. After saying this to her, Lord Mahādeva, the pure one seated among the pure ones, went to the place he wished to go. She went back to her city.

## \|\| 2.25.89-94 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā devīṃ tadā hṛṣṭo menayā sahito'calaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*āliṃgyāghrāya papraccha sarvaṃ sā ca nyavedayat \|*  
*duhiturdevadevena ājñaptaṃ tu himācalaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

*svayaṃvaraṃ pramuditaḥ sarvalokeṣvaghoṣayat \|*  
*aśvino dvādaśādityā gandharvaruḍoragāḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*yakṣāḥ siddhāstathā sādhyā daityāḥ kiṃpuruṣā nagāḥ \|*  
*samudrādyāśca ye kecittrailokyapravarāsca ye \|\| 92 \|\|*

*trayastriṃśatsahasrāṇi trayastriṃśacchatāni ca \|*  
*trayastriṃśacca ye devāstrayastriṃśacca koṭayaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

*jagmurgirīndraputryāstu svayaṃvaramanuttamam \|*  
*āmaṃtritastathā viṣṇurmerumāha hasanniva \|\| 94 \|\|*

89-94. On seeing the goddess, the Mountain along with Menā was delighted. After embracing her and sniffing at her head, he asked and she said everything. Himācala announced the Svayaṃvara of his daughter as commanded by the Lord of Devas. He announced it with great delight in all the worlds. The two Aśvins, the twelve Ādityas, Gandharvas, Garuḍa, Serpents, Yakṣas, Siddhas, Sādhyas, Daityas, Kiṃpuruṣas, Mountains, Oceans etc., nay all those who were the most excellent ones in the three worlds, all the thirty-three crore, thirty-three thousand, thirty-three hundred and thirty-three Devas, went to the excellent Svayaṃvara of the daughter of Lord of Mountains. On being invited, Viṣṇu laughingly said to Meru:

## \|\| 2.25.95-97 \|\|

*tātāsmākaṃ ca sā devī mero gaccha namāmi tām \|*  
*atha śailasutā devī haimamāruhya śobhanam \|\| 95 \|\|*

*vimānaṃ sarvatobhadraṃ sarvaratnairalaṃkṛtam \|*  
*apsarobhiḥ pranṛtyadbhiḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā \|\| 96 \|\|*

*gaṃdharvasaṃghairvividhaiḥ kiṃnaraiśca suśobhanaiḥ \|*  
*baṃdibhiḥ stūyamānā ca vīrakāṃsyadharā sthitā \|\| 97 \|\|*

95-97. “Dear one, she is our goddess. Go. I shall bow down to her.”

The daughter of the Mountain, the goddess, got into a splendid aerial chariot made of gold and beautified by all gems. It was guarded from all sides. She was bedecked in all ornaments. She was eulogized by the dancing celestial damsels, different groups of Gandharvas, splendid Kinnaras and bards. She stood there holding the Vīrakāṃsya (i.e. bell-metal vessel for the hero).

## \|\| 2.25.98 \|\|

*sitātapatraratnāṃśumiśritaṃ cāvahattadā \|*  
*śālinī nāma pārvatyāḥ saṃdhyāpūrṇedumaṃḍalā \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. (A maid) of Pārvatī named Śālinī, with face resembling the full disc of the moon at dusk held the white umbrella, radiating rays of precious stones mixed (studded,) in it.

## \|\| 2.25.99 \|\|

*cāmarāsaktahastābhirdivyastrībhiśca saṃvṛtā \|*  
*mālāṃ pragṛhya sā tasthau suradrumasamudbhavām \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. She was surrounded by the divine ladies with chowries in their hands. She had a garland (in her hand) made of flowers coming from the celestial tree.

## \|\| 2.25.100-101 \|\|

*evaṃ tasyāṃ sthitāyāṃ tu sthite lokatraye tadā \|*  
*śiśurbhūtvā mahādevaḥ krīḍārthaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*utsaṃgatalasaṃgupto babhūva bhagavānbhavaḥ \|*  
*jayeti yatpadaṃ khyātaṃ tasya satyārthamīśvaram \|\| 101 \|\|*

100-101. While she was standing thus, while all the three worlds were present there, the bull-emblemed Mahādeva, for the sake of sport, became a small child. Lord Bhava was then held and guarded in the lap of a certain person named Jaya. To him of course he was the Lord of the truthful meaning(?)

## \|\| 2.25.102 \|\|

*atha dṛṣṭvā śiśuṃ devāstasya utsaṃgavartinaḥ \|*  
*koyamatreti saṃmaṃtrya cukruśurbhṛśaroṣitāḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. On seeing that child in his lap, gods enquired one another, “Who is this?” Infuriated much they shouted loudly.

## \|\| 2.25.103 \|\|

*vajramāhārayattasya bāhumudyamya vṛtrahā \|*  
*sa bāhurudyatastasya tathaiva samatiṣṭhata \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. The slayer of Vṛtra raised his hand and lifted up the thunderbolt (to strike him). That hand of his so lifted up ramained in that position.

## \|\| 2.25.104 \|\|

*staṃbhitaḥ śiśurūpeṇa devadevena līlayā \|*  
*vajraṃ kṣeptuṃ na śaknoti bāhuṃ cālayituṃ tadā \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. It was paralysed sportingly by the Lord of Devas in the form of a child. He not only could not discharge the thunderbolt but also could not move his hand.

## \|\| 2.25.105 \|\|

*vahniḥ śaktiṃ tadā kṣeptuṃ na śaśāka tathotthitaḥ \|*  
*yamo'pi daṃḍaṃ khaḍgaṃ ca nirṛtistaṃ śiśuṃ prati \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Towards that child Vahni (‘Fire-god’) could not hurl his Śakti, though he stood up (for the same). Yama could not discharge his baton. Nirṛti could not send the sword against the child.

## \|\| 2.25.106 \|\|

*pāśaṃ ca varuṇo rājā dhvajayaṣṭiṃ samīraṇaḥ \|*  
*somo guḍaṃ dhaneśaśca gadāṃ sumahatīṃ dṛḍhām \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. King Varuṇa could not send his noose. Nor was Samīraṇa (‘Wind-god’) able to hurl his flag-staff. Soma could not discharge Guḍa (i.e. elephant’s armour) nor could Dhaneśa hurl his great and strong iron club.

## \|\| 2.25.107 \|\|

*nānāyudhāni cādityā musalaṃ vasavastathā \|*  
*mahāghorāṇi śastrāṇi tārakādyāśca dānavāḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. The Ādityas could not hurl different weapons nor could the Vasus discharge the threshing rod (i.e. pestle). Dānavas beginning with Tāraka could not discharge their extremely terrible weapons.

## \|\| 2.25.108-111 \|\|

*staṃbhitā devadevena tathānye bhuvaneṣu ye \|*  
*pūṣā daṃtāndaśandaṃrbālamaikṣata mohitaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

*tasyāpi daśanāḥ peturdṛṣṭamātrasya śaṃbhunā \|*  
*bhagaśca netre vikṛte cakāra sphuṭite ca te \|\| 109 \|\|*

*balaṃ tejaśca yogāṃśca sarveṣāṃ jagṛhe prabhuḥ \|*  
*atha teṣu sthiteṣveva manyumatsu sureṣvapi \|\| 110 \|\|*

*brahmā dhyānamupāśritya bubodha haraceṣṭitam \|*  
*so'bhigamya mahādevaṃ tuṣṭāva prayato vidhiḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

108-111. These as well as others in the worlds were rendered motionless by the Lord of Devas. Pūṣan gnashed his teeth. In his deluded state, he looked at the child, immediately after being seen by Śaṃbhu, his teeth fell down. Bhaga made his eyes deformed (i.e. he viewed with a distorted vision). His eyes split. The Lord took away the strength, the splendour and the Yogic power of everyone.

Even as those Suras stood thus with great fury Brahmā meditated on it and understood the act of Hara. Hence Vidhi (i.e. Brahmā) approached Mahādeva and eulogized him with great purity.

## \|\| 2.25.112-114 \|\|

*paurāṇaiḥ sāmasaṃgītairvedikairguhyanāmabhiḥ \|*  
*namastubhyaṃ mahādeva mahādevyai namonamaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*prasādāttava buddhyādirjagadetatpravartate \|*  
*mūḍhāśca devatāḥ sarvā nainaṃ budhyata śaṃkaram \|\| 113 \|\|*

*mahādevamihāyātaṃ sarvadevanamaskṛtam \|*  
*gacchadhvaṃ śaraṇaṃ śīghraṃ yadi jīvitumicchata \|\| 114 \|\|*

112-114. Brahmā eulogized through the secret names from Purāṇas, Sāman-songs, and the Vedas:

“Obeisance to you, O Mahādeva, obeisance, obeisance to the great goddess, it is by your grace that Buddhi etc. and the entire universe function. All the Devas are dull and stupid; they have not recognised Śaṅkara, the great Lord who is saluted by all the Devas and who has come here. O Devas, seek refuge in him immediately, if you wish to live.”

## \|\| 2.25.115-118 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃbhrama saṃpannāstuṣṭuvuḥ praṇatāḥ surāḥ \|*  
*namonamo mahādeva pāhipāhi jagatpate \|\| 115 \|\|*

*durācārānbhavānasmānātmadrohaparāyaṇān \|*  
*aho paśyata no mauḍhyaṃ jānaṃtastava bhāvinīm \|\| 116 \|\|*

*bhāryāmumāṃ mahādevīṃ tathāpyatra samāgatāḥ \|*  
*yuktametadyadasmākaṃ rājyaṃ gṛhyeta cāsuraiḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

*yeṣāmevaṃvidhābuddhirasmābhiḥ kiṃ kṛtaṃ tvidam \|*  
*atha vā no na doṣo'sti paśavo hi vayaṃ yataḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

115-118. Then the Suras who were highly excited bowed down and eulogized the Lord:

“Obeisance, obeisance, O great Lord. Save us, save us, O Lord of the universe, (though) we are of bad conduct and we have engaged ourselves in self-injury. Oh! See our stupidity. Though we know that Umā, the great goddess, will be your wife, we have gathered here. It is proper if our kingdom is taken away by Asuras because our intellect (has gone astray) thus. What has been done! Or this is not our fault since we are Paśus (brutes, or Jīvas).

## \|\| 2.25.119 \|\|

*tvayaiva patinā sarve preritāḥ kurmahe vibho \|*  
*īśvaraḥ sarva bhūtānāṃ patistvaṃ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. O Lord, we do everything on being impelled by you, the Pati (‘Lord’). You are Īśvara, the Lord of all Jiving beings, the Supreme Lord.

## \|\| 2.25.120 \|\|

*bhrāmayasyakhilaṃ viśvaṃ yantrārūḍhaṃ svamāyayā \|*  
*yena vibhrāmitā mūḍhāḥ samāyātāḥ svayaṃvaram \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. You whirl the entire universe as though it has been, placed on a machine. You whirl it through your Māyā. We have been deluded thereby and it was so that we have come to the Svayaṃvara.

## \|\| 2.25.121 \|\|

*tasmai paśunāṃ pataye namastubhyaṃ prasīda naḥ \|*  
*atha teṣāṃ prasanna'bhūddevadevāstriyaṃbakaḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Obeisance to that Lord of the Paśus; obeisance to you. Be pleased with us.” Thereupon, the three-eyed Lord of Devas, became pleased with them.

## \|\| 2.25.122 \|\|

*yathāpūrvaṃ cakāraitānsaṃstavādbrahmaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*tārakapramukhā daityāḥ saṃkruddhāstatra procire \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. On being eulogized by Brahmā, the Lord made all of them as before (by removing their paralysed state).

Thereupon, Daityas, the chief of whom was Tāraka, became infuriated and spoke thus:

## \|\| 2.25.123 \|\|

*koyamaṃga mahādevo na manyāmo vayaṃ ca tam \|*  
*tataḥ prahasya bālo'sau huṃkāraṃ līlayā vyadhāt \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. “Who is this Mahādeva? We do not worship or honour him”. Thereupon the boy laughed and sportingly made a Huṃkāra (i.e. loud humming sound).

## \|\| 2.25.124 \|\|

*huṃkāreṇaiva te daityāḥ svameva nagaraṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*vismṛtaṃ sakalaṃ teṣāṃ svayaṃvaramukhaṃ ca tat \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Merely because of that Huṃkāra those Daityas went (i.e. were thrown back) to their own city. Everything connected with that Svayaṃvara celebration was forgotten by them.

## \|\| 2.25.125-129 \|\|

*mahādevaprabhāvena daityānāṃ ghorakarmaṇām \|*  
*evaṃ yasya prabhāvo hi devadaityeṣu phālguna \|\| 125 \|\|*

*kathamīśvaravākyārthastasmādanyatra mucyate \|*  
*asaṃśayaṃ vimuḍhāste paścāttāpaḥ purā mahān \|\| 126 \|\|*

*īśvaraṃ bhuvanasyāsya ye bhajaṃte na tryaṃbakam \|*  
*tataḥ saṃstūyamānaḥ sa suraiḥ padmabhuvādibhiḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

*vapuścakāra deveśastryaṃbakaḥ paramādbhutam \|*  
*tejasā tasya devāste seṃdracaṃdradivākarāḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

*sabrahmakāḥ sasādhyāśca vasurviśve ca devatāḥ \|*  
*sayamāśca sarudrāśca cakṣuraprārthayanprabhum \|\| 129 \|\|*

125-129. It was due to the power of Mahādeva that the Daityas of terrible activities became so.

O Phālguna, such is the power of Śiva over Devas and Daityas. How then can the meaning of the word Īśvara be applied to anyone other than he (Śiva). Undoubtedly, those who do not worship the Three-eyed Lord of this universe, are deluded and stupid. Their regret later on will be great.

Thereafter, on being eulogized by the Suras beginning with the Lotus-born Lord, the Three-eyed Lord of Devas assumed an excessively wonderful body. All the Devas became dazzled by his refulgence. Therefore, all the Devas including Indra, the Moon and the Sun, Brahmā, Sādhyas, Vasus, Viśvedevas, Yama and Rudra requested the Lord for (a divinely powerful) vision.

## \|\| 2.25.130 \|\|

*tebhyaḥ paratamaṃ cakṣuḥ svavapurdraṣṭumuttamam \|*  
*dadāvambāpatiḥ śarvo bhavānyāścālasya ca \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Śarva, the husband of Aṃbā, granted them as well as to Bhavānī and the Mountain the most excellent vision in order īo see his own excellent physical body.

## \|\| 2.25.131 \|\|

*labdhvā rudraprasādena divyaṃ cakṣuranuttamam \|*  
*sabrahyakāstadā devāstamapaśyanmaheśvaram \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. After obtaining the divine and the most excellent vision by the favour of Rudra, the Devas including Brahmā saw Maheśvara.

## \|\| 2.25.132 \|\|

*tato jaguśca munayaḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ ca khecarāḥ \|*  
*mumucuśca tadā nedurdevaduṃdubhayo bhṛśam \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Thereupon the sages sang, the sky-walkers showered flowers and the divine Dundubhi drums were sounded loudly.

## \|\| 2.25.133 \|\|

*jagugadharvamukhyāśca nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ \|*  
*mumudurgaṇapāḥ sarve mumodāṃbā ca pārvatī \|\| 133 \|\|*
