133\. The chiefs of Gandharvas sang; the groups of the celestial damsels danced; all the lords of the Gaṇas rejoiced. Pārvatī, Aṃbā too rejoiced.

## \|\| 2.25.134-136 \|\|

*brahmādyā menire pūrṇāṃ bhavānīṃ ca girīśvaram \|*  
*tasya devī tato hṛṣṭā samakṣaṃ tridivaukasām \|\| 134 \|\|*

*pādayoḥ sthāpayāmāsa mālāṃ divyāṃ sugaṃdhinīm \|*  
*sādusādhviti saṃprocya tayā taṃ tatra carcitam \|\| 135 \|\|*

*saha devyā namaścakruḥ śirobhirbhūtalāśritaiḥ \|*  
*sarve sabrahmakā devā jayeti ca mudā jaguḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

134-136. Brahmā and others considered Bhavānī and Īśvara complete (on their being united). In the presence of the heaven-dwellers, the delighted goddess placed the divine fragrant garland at his feet. They said, “Well done! Well done!” With their heads touching the ground they bowed down to him worshipped by and accompanied by the goddess. All the Devas including Brahmā joyously sang, “Be victorious”.

## Chapter 26 - The Marriage of Hara and Gaurī Celebrated

## \|\| 2.26.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*atha brahmā mahādevamabhivādya kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*udvāhaḥ kriyatāṃ deva ityuvāca maheśvaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. Brahmā then saluted Mahādeva. With palms joined in reverence, he said to Maheśvara, “O Lord, let the marriage be celebrated.”

## \|\| 2.26.2-40 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā prāhedaṃ bhagavānharaḥ \|*  
*parādhīnā vayaṃ brahmanhimādrestava cāpi yat \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yadyuktaṃ kriyatāṃ taddhi vayaṃ yuṣmadvaśe'dhunā \|*  
*tato brahmā svayaṃ divyaṃ puraṃ ratnamayaṃ śubham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*udvāhārthaṃ maheśasya tatkṣaṇātsamakalpayat \|*  
*śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ prāsādaśataśobhitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*puretasminmahādevaḥ svayameva vyatiṣṭhata \|*  
*tataḥ saptamunīndevaściṃtitābyāgatānpuraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prāhiṇodaṃbikāyāśca sthirapatrārthamīśvaraḥ \|*  
*sāruṃdhatīkāste tatra hlādayaṃto himācalam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sabhāryāmīśvaraguṇaiḥ sthirapatrāṇi cādadhuḥ \|*  
*tataḥ saṃpūjitāstena punarāgamya te'calāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

*nyavedayaṃsryaṃbakāya sa ca tānabhyanaṃdata \|*  
*udvāhārthaṃ tato devo viśvaṃ sarvaṃ nyamaṃtrayat \|\| 8 \|\|*

*samāgataṃ ca tatsava vinā daityairdurātmabhiḥ \|*  
*sthāvaraṃ jaṃgamaṃ yacca viśvaṃ viṣṇupurogamam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sabrahyakaṃ purārātermahimānamavardhayat \|*  
*tatastaṃ vidhirāhedaṃ gandhamādanaparvate \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pure sthitaṃ vivāhasya deva kālaḥ pravartate \|*  
*tatastasya jaṭājūṭe caṃdrakhaṃḍaṃ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*babaṃdha praṇayodāravisphāritavilocanaḥ \|*  
*kaparddaṃ śobhanaṃ viṣṇuḥ svaya cakre'sya harṣataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kapālamālāṃ vipulāṃ cāmuṇḍā mūrdhnyabaṃdhata \|*  
*uvāca cāpi giriśaṃ putraṃ janaya śaṃkara \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yo daityeṃdrakulaṃ hatvā māṃ raktaistarpayiṣyati \|*  
*sūryo jvalacchikhāraktaṃ bhābāsitajagattrayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*babaṃdha devadevasyaca svayameva pramodataḥ \|*  
*śeṣavāsukimukhyāśca jvalaṃtastejasā śubhāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ bhūṣaṇasthāne svayaṃ te cakrurīśvare \|\|*  
*vāyavaśca tatastīkṣṇaśrṛṃgaṃ himagiriprabham \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vṛṣaṃ vibhūṣayāmāsurnānāratnopapattibhiḥ \|*  
*śakro gajajinaṃ gṛhya svayamagre vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vinā bhasma samādhāya kapāle rajataprabham \|*  
*manujāsthimayīṃ mālāṃ pretanāthaśca vandanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vahnistejomayaṃ divyamajinaṃ pradadau sthitaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ vibhūṣitaḥ sarvairbhṛtyairīśo babhau bhṛśam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tato himādreḥ puruṣā vīrakaṃ procire vacaḥ \|*  
*mā bhūtkālātyayaḥ śīghraṃ bhavasyaitannivedyatām \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tato devaṃ praṇamyāha vīrakaḥ karasaṃpuṭī \|*  
*tvarayaṃti maheśānaṃ himādreḥ puruṣāstvamī \|\| 21 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vaco devaḥ śīghramityeva cābravīt \|*  
*sapta vāridhayastasya cakrurdarpaṇadarśanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tatraikṣata mahādevaḥ svarūpaṃ sa jaganmayam \|*  
*tato baddhāṃjalirdhīmānsthāṇuṃ provāca keśavaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*devadeva mahādeva tripurāṃtaka śaṃkara \|*  
*śobhase'nena rūpeṇa jagadānaṃdadāyinā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*maheśvara yathā sākṣādaparastvaṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tataḥ smayanmahādevo jayeti bhuvane śrutaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*karamālaṃbya viṣṇośca vṛṣabhaṃ ruruheśanaiḥ \|*  
*tataśca vasavo devāḥ śūlaṃ tasya nyavedayan \|\| 26 \|\|*

*dhanado nidibhiryuktaḥ samīpasthastato'bhavat \|*  
*sa śūlapāṇirviśvātmā saṃcacāla tato haraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*devaduṃdubhinādaiśca puṣpāsāraiśca gītakaiḥ \|*  
*nṛtyadbhirapsarobhiśca jayeti ca mahāsvanaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*savyadakṣiṇasaṃsthānau brahmaviṣṇūtu jagmatuḥ \|*  
*haṃsaṃ ca garuḍaṃ caiva samāruhya mahāprabhau \|\| 29 \|\|*

*athāditirditiḥ sā ca danuḥ kadrūḥ suparṇajā \|*  
*paulomī surasā caiva siṃhikā surabhirmuniḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*siddhirmāyā kṣamā durgā devī svāhā svadhā sudhā \|*  
*sāvitrī caiva gāyatrī lakṣmīḥ sā dakṣiṇā dyutiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*spṛhāmatirdhṛtirbuddhirmaṃthirṛddhiḥ sarasvatī \|*  
*rākā kuhūḥ sinīvālī devī bhānumatī tathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dharaṇī dhāraṇī velā rājñī cāpi ca rohiṇī \|*  
*ityetāścānyadevānāṃ mātaraḥ patnayastathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*udvāhaṃ devadevasya jagmuḥ sarvā mudānvitāḥ \|*  
*uragā garuḍā yakṣā gaṃdharvāḥ kiṃnarā narāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sāgarā girayo meghā māsāḥ saṃvatsarāstathā \|*  
*vedā maṃtrāstathā yajñāḥ śrautā dharmāśca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*huṃkārāḥ praṇavāścaiva itihāsāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*koṭiśaśca tathā devā maheṃdrādyāḥ savāhanāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*anujagmurmahādevaṃ koṭiśo'rbudaśaśca hi \|*  
*gaṇāśca pṛṣṭhato jagmuḥ śaṃkhavarṇāśca koṭiśaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*daśabhiḥ kekarākhyāśca vidyuto'ṣṭābhireva ca \|*  
*catuḥṣaṣṭyā viśākhāśca navabhiḥ pāriyātrikāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ṣaḍbhiḥ sarvāṃtakaḥ śrīmāṃstathaiva vikṛtānanaḥ \|*  
*jvālākeśo dvādaśabhiḥ koṭibhiḥ saṃvṛto yayau \|\| 39 \|\|*

*saptabhiḥ samadaḥ śrīmānduṃdubhoṣṭhābhireva ca \|*  
*paṃcabhiśca kapālīśaḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ saṃhrādakaḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

2-4 On hearing his words, Lord Hara said thus: “O Brahmā, we are dependent upon you and Himādri. Whatever is proper and relevant may be done. We are under your control now.” Thereupon, for the sake of the marriage of Maheśa, Brahmā instantaneously himself created a divine city, splendidly set with gems and jewels. It extended to a hundred Yojanas and it was rendered beautiful with hundreds of mansions.

## \|\| 2.26.5-8 \|\|

*puretasminmahādevaḥ svayameva vyatiṣṭhata \|*  
*tataḥ saptamunīndevaściṃtitābyāgatānpuraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prāhiṇodaṃbikāyāśca sthirapatrārthamīśvaraḥ \|*  
*sāruṃdhatīkāste tatra hlādayaṃto himācalam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sabhāryāmīśvaraguṇaiḥ sthirapatrāṇi cādadhuḥ \|*  
*tataḥ saṃpūjitāstena punarāgamya te'calāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

*nyavedayaṃsryaṃbakāya sa ca tānabhyanaṃdata \|*  
*udvāhārthaṃ tato devo viśvaṃ sarvaṃ nyamaṃtrayat \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. Mahādeva himself stayed in that city. The Lord thought of the Seven Sages. When they arrived, he sent them to offer the letter of confirmation regarding Aṃbikā. Accompanied by Arundhatī, they went to Himācala and delighted him and his wife by mentioning the good qualities of the Lord. They gave him the letter of confirmation. They were duly honoured and entertained by him. They returned from the Mountain and intimated everything to the Three-eyed Lord. He congratulated them. Thereafter, the Lord invited the entire universe for the marriage.

## \|\| 2.26.9-12 \|\|

*samāgataṃ ca tatsava vinā daityairdurātmabhiḥ \|*  
*sthāvaraṃ jaṃgamaṃ yacca viśvaṃ viṣṇupurogamam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sabrahyakaṃ purārātermahimānamavardhayat \|*  
*tatastaṃ vidhirāhedaṃ gandhamādanaparvate \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pure sthitaṃ vivāhasya deva kālaḥ pravartate \|*  
*tatastasya jaṭājūṭe caṃdrakhaṃḍaṃ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*babaṃdha praṇayodāravisphāritavilocanaḥ \|*  
*kaparddaṃ śobhanaṃ viṣṇuḥ svaya cakre'sya harṣataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

9-12. Excepting Daityas of wicked nature, ail of them came, the entire universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings. The universe with Viṣṇu as the leader and including Brahmā, proclaimed the greatness- of the enemy of the Puras. Brahmā said to him stationed in front on the Gandhamādana, “O Deva, it is time for the marriage ceremony.”

Thereafter, the grandfather, with his eyes distended on account of excessive love, tied the Crescent Moon to his matted locks of hair. With great delight, Viṣṇu himself made his matted hair splendid.

## \|\| 2.26.13-19 \|\|

*kapālamālāṃ vipulāṃ cāmuṇḍā mūrdhnyabaṃdhata \|*  
*uvāca cāpi giriśaṃ putraṃ janaya śaṃkara \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yo daityeṃdrakulaṃ hatvā māṃ raktaistarpayiṣyati \|*  
*sūryo jvalacchikhāraktaṃ bhābāsitajagattrayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*babaṃdha devadevasyaca svayameva pramodataḥ \|*  
*śeṣavāsukimukhyāśca jvalaṃtastejasā śubhāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ bhūṣaṇasthāne svayaṃ te cakrurīśvare \|\|*  
*vāyavaśca tatastīkṣṇaśrṛṃgaṃ himagiriprabham \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vṛṣaṃ vibhūṣayāmāsurnānāratnopapattibhiḥ \|*  
*śakro gajajinaṃ gṛhya svayamagre vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vinā bhasma samādhāya kapāle rajataprabham \|*  
*manujāsthimayīṃ mālāṃ pretanāthaśca vandanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vahnistejomayaṃ divyamajinaṃ pradadau sthitaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ vibhūṣitaḥ sarvairbhṛtyairīśo babhau bhṛśam \|\| 19 \|\|*

13-19. Cāmuṇḍā, tied to his head a large garland of skulls and said to Giriśa, “Beget a son, O Śaṅkara, who will kill the family of the leading Daitya and offer libations unto me with blood.”

The Sun himself with great delight fixed a red jewel with blazing fiery sparks and illuminating the three worlds with its refulgence, to the tuft of the Lord of Devas. The chief (Serpents) Śeṣa, Vāsuki etc., the splendid ones, sparkling with their splendour, offered themselves to īśvara in the place of ornaments. With different kinds of jewel-fittings, the Vāyus (i.e. Wind-gods) decorated the bull that had sharp pointed horns and also the lustre of the Himālaya mountain. Śakra held the elephant’s hide himself and stood in front.

Pretanātha saluted and offered a garland of human bones without ash of silver lustre on the skull. Vahni (i.e. Fire-god) gave a refulgent divine hide of deer. The Lord who was adorned thus by all the attendants shone well.

## \|\| 2.26.20 \|\|

*tato himādreḥ puruṣā vīrakaṃ procire vacaḥ \|*  
*mā bhūtkālātyayaḥ śīghraṃ bhavasyaitannivedyatām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then the officials of Himādri spoke these words to Vīraka, “Let there not be delay. Let Bhava be informed of this.”

## \|\| 2.26.21 \|\|

*tato devaṃ praṇamyāha vīrakaḥ karasaṃpuṭī \|*  
*tvarayaṃti maheśānaṃ himādreḥ puruṣāstvamī \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. With his hands joined together in reverence, Vīraka bowed down to the Lord and said: “These officials of Himādri want Maheśāna to hurry up.”

## \|\| 2.26.22 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vaco devaḥ śīghramityeva cābravīt \|*  
*sapta vāridhayastasya cakrurdarpaṇadarśanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On hearing these words, the Lord said, “Yes, soon.” The Seven Oceans showed him the mirror.

## \|\| 2.26.23 \|\|

*tatraikṣata mahādevaḥ svarūpaṃ sa jaganmayam \|*  
*tato baddhāṃjalirdhīmānsthāṇuṃ provāca keśavaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. There, the great Lord saw his own form identical with the universe. Then, with palms joined in reverence, the intelligent Keśava spoke to Sthāṇu (i.e. Śiva):

## \|\| 2.26.24-26 \|\|

*devadeva mahādeva tripurāṃtaka śaṃkara \|*  
*śobhase'nena rūpeṇa jagadānaṃdadāyinā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*maheśvara yathā sākṣādaparastvaṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tataḥ smayanmahādevo jayeti bhuvane śrutaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*karamālaṃbya viṣṇośca vṛṣabhaṃ ruruheśanaiḥ \|*  
*tataśca vasavo devāḥ śūlaṃ tasya nyavedayan \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. “O Mahādeva, Lord of Devas, O Śaṅkara, slayer of Tripura, you shine with this form that delights the universe, O Maheśvara, like another Maheśvara (‘Lord of festivals’).” Then the smiling Mahādeva was hailed saying, “Be victorious in all the worlds”. Taking hold of Viṣṇu’s hand, he slowly mounted the Bull. Thereafter, Vasus and Devas handed him the trident.

## \|\| 2.26.27 \|\|

*dhanado nidibhiryuktaḥ samīpasthastato'bhavat \|*  
*sa śūlapāṇirviśvātmā saṃcacāla tato haraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Dhanada accompanied by all the treasures stood nearby. Then Hara, the immanent soul of the universe, moved ahead with the trident in his hand.

## \|\| 2.26.28-29 \|\|

*devaduṃdubhinādaiśca puṣpāsāraiśca gītakaiḥ \|*  
*nṛtyadbhirapsarobhiśca jayeti ca mahāsvanaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*savyadakṣiṇasaṃsthānau brahmaviṣṇūtu jagmatuḥ \|*  
*haṃsaṃ ca garuḍaṃ caiva samāruhya mahāprabhau \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. With the sounds of the divine Dundubhi drums, showers of flowers, music, the dances of the celestial damsels and others, and the Loud shouts of “Victory”, the Lord went ahead. Brahmā and Viṣṇu of great lustre rode on the Swan and Garuḍa and went ahead keeping to the left and right sides of the Lord.

## \|\| 2.26.30-37 \|\|

*athāditirditiḥ sā ca danuḥ kadrūḥ suparṇajā \|*  
*paulomī surasā caiva siṃhikā surabhirmuniḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*siddhirmāyā kṣamā durgā devī svāhā svadhā sudhā \|*  
*sāvitrī caiva gāyatrī lakṣmīḥ sā dakṣiṇā dyutiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*spṛhāmatirdhṛtirbuddhirmaṃthirṛddhiḥ sarasvatī \|*  
*rākā kuhūḥ sinīvālī devī bhānumatī tathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dharaṇī dhāraṇī velā rājñī cāpi ca rohiṇī \|*  
*ityetāścānyadevānāṃ mātaraḥ patnayastathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*udvāhaṃ devadevasya jagmuḥ sarvā mudānvitāḥ \|*  
*uragā garuḍā yakṣā gaṃdharvāḥ kiṃnarā narāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sāgarā girayo meghā māsāḥ saṃvatsarāstathā \|*  
*vedā maṃtrāstathā yajñāḥ śrautā dharmāśca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*huṃkārāḥ praṇavāścaiva itihāsāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*koṭiśaśca tathā devā maheṃdrādyāḥ savāhanāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*anujagmurmahādevaṃ koṭiśo'rbudaśaśca hi \|*  
*gaṇāśca pṛṣṭhato jagmuḥ śaṃkhavarṇāśca koṭiśaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

30-37a. The following persons then went behind the Lord: Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadru, Suparṇajā, Paulomī, Surasā, Siṃhikā, Surabhi, Muni, Siddhi, Māyā, Kṣamā, the goddess, Durgā, Svāhā, Svadhā, Sudhā, Sāvitrī, Gāyatrī, Lakṣmī, Dakṣiṇā, Dyuti, Spṛhā, Mati, Dhṛti, Buddhi, Manthi(?), Ṛddhi, Sarasvatī, Rākā, Kuhū, Sinīvālī, Devī Bhanumatī, Dharaṇī, Dhāraṇī, Velā, the queen Rohiṇī etc. The mothers and wives of other Devas went to the marriage of the Lord of Devas. All of them rejoiced. Serpents, Garuḍas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Naras (human beings), Oceans, Mountains, Cloud, Months, Years, the Vedas, Mantras, Yajñas, all the Vedic Dharmas, Huṃkāras, Praṇavas, the thousands of Itihāsas, crores of the Devas beginning with Mahendra and their vehicles too followed Mahādeva. There were crores and thousand billions of these.

37b. Innumerable lords of Gaṇas came there. Billions and trillions of Gaṇas followed behind (the Lord). Gaṇas having the colour of conch-shell were crores in number.

## \|\| 2.26.38-39 \|\|

*daśabhiḥ kekarākhyāśca vidyuto'ṣṭābhireva ca \|*  
*catuḥṣaṣṭyā viśākhāśca navabhiḥ pāriyātrikāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ṣaḍbhiḥ sarvāṃtakaḥ śrīmāṃstathaiva vikṛtānanaḥ \|*  
*jvālākeśo dvādaśabhiḥ koṭibhiḥ saṃvṛto yayau \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Gaṇas called Kekaras numbered ten crore; Vidyuts eight crore; Viśākhas sixty-four crore; Pāriyātrikas nine crore; glorious Sarvāntaka and Vikṛtānana went with six crores; Jvālākeśa went surrounded by twelve crores.

## \|\| 2.26.40 \|\|

*saptabhiḥ samadaḥ śrīmānduṃdubhoṣṭhābhireva ca \|*  
*paṃcabhiśca kapālīśaḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ saṃhrādakaḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The glorious Samada with seven crores; Dundubha with eight crores; Kapālīśa with five crores; the splendid Saṃhlādaka with six crores.

## \|\| 2.26.41 \|\|

*koṭikoṭibhirevaikaḥ kuṃḍakaḥ kuṃbhakastathā \|*  
*viṣṭaṃbho'ṣṭābhireveha gaṇapaḥ sarvasattamaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Kundaka and Kuṃbhaka each with a crore. Viṣṭaṃbha, the chief of the Gaṇas, the most excellent of all, went with eight crores.

## \|\| 2.26.42 \|\|

*pippalaśca sahasreṇa sannādaśca tathā balī \|*  
*āveśanastathāṣṭābhiḥ saptabhiścaṃdratāpanaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Pippala with a thousand; the powerful Sannāda too like that; Āveśana with eight; Candratāpana with seven crores.

## \|\| 2.26.43 \|\|

*mahākeśaḥ sahasreṇa naṃdirdvādaśabhistathā \|*  
*nagaḥ kālaḥ karālaśca mahākālaḥ śatena ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Mahākeśa with a thousand; Nandi with twelve crores; Nāga, Kāla, Karāla and Mahākāla (each) with a hundred.

## \|\| 2.26.44 \|\|

*agnikaḥ śatakoṭyā vai koṭyāgnimukha eva ca \|*  
*ādityamūrdhā koṭyā ca koṭyā caiva dhanāvahaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Agnika with a hundred crores. Agnimukha with a crore. Ādityamūrdhā and Dhanāvaha each with a crore.

## \|\| 2.26.45 \|\|

*sannāgaśca śatenaiva kumudaḥ koṭibhistribhiḥ \|*  
*amoghaḥ kokilaścaiva koṭikoṭyā sumaṃtrakaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Sannāga with a hundred; Kumuda with three crores. Amogha, Kokila and Sumantraka each with a crore.

## \|\| 2.26.46 \|\|

*kākapādastatā ṣaṣṭyā ṣaṣṭyā saṃtānako gaṇaḥ \|*  
*mahābalaśca navabhirmadhupiṃgaśca piṃgalaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Kākapāda with six crores; the Gaṇa called Santānaka with six crores; Mahābala, Madhupiṅga and Piṅgala (each) with nine crores.

## \|\| 2.26.47 \|\|

*nīlo navatyā saptatyā caturvaktraśca pūrvapāt \|*  
*vīrabhadraścaścatuḥṣaṣṭyā karaṇo bālakastathā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Nīla with ninety; Caturvaktra and Pūrvapāt each with seventy; Vīrabhadra, Karaṇa and Bālaka each with sixty-four.

## \|\| 2.26.48 \|\|

*paṃcākṣaḥ śatamanyuśca meghamanyuśca viṃśatiḥ \|*  
*kāṣṭhakoṭiścatuḥṣaṣṭyā sukośo vṛṣabhastathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Pañcākṣa, Śatamanyu and Meghamanyu each with twenty crores; Kāṣṭhakoṭi, Sukeśa and Vṛṣabha each with sixty-four.

## \|\| 2.26.49-50 \|\|

*viśvarūpastālaketuḥ paṃcāśacca sitānanaḥ \|*  
*īśāno vṛddhadevaśca dīptātmā mṛtyuhā tathā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*viṣādo yamahā caiva gaṇo bhṛṃgariṭistathā \|*  
*aśanī hāsakaścaiva catuḥṣaṣṭyā sahasrapāt \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Viśvarūpa, Tālaketu and Sitānana each with fifty; Īśāna, Vṛddhadeva, Dīptātmā, Mṛtyuhā, Viṣāda, Yamahā and Bhṛṅgiriṭi, Aśanī and Hāsaka as well as Sahasrapāt each with sixty-four.

## \|\| 2.26.51 \|\|

*ete cānye ca gaṇapā asaṃkhyātā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*sarve sahasrahastāśca jaṭāmukuṭadhārīṇaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. These and other leaders of the Gaṇas followed. They were innumerable and all of them were very powerful. All of them had a thousand hands. They wore matted locks of hair and crowns.

## \|\| 2.26.52 \|\|

*caṃdralekhāvataṃsāśca nīlakaṃṭhāstrilocanāḥ \|*  
*hārakuṃḍalakeyūramukuṭādyairalaṃkṛtāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. They had the crescent moon for an ornament. They were blue-throated and three-eyed. They were adorned with necklaces, ear-rings, armlets, crowns and other ornaments.

## \|\| 2.26.53 \|\|

*aṇimādiguṇairyuktāḥ śaktāḥ śāpaprasādayoḥ \|*  
*sūryakoṭipratīkāśāstatrājagmurgaṇeśvarāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. They were endowed with Aṇimā and other qualities (Siddhis). They were competent to curse as well as to bless. Leading chiefs of Gaṇas resembling crores of Suns came there.

## \|\| 2.26.54-55 \|\|

*pātālāṃbarabhūmisthāḥ sarvalokanivāsinaḥ \|*  
*tuṃbururnārado hāhā hūhūścaiva tu sāmagāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*taṃtrīmādāya vādyāṃścā'vādayañchaṃkarotsave \|*  
*ṛṣayaḥ kṛtsnaśaścaiva vedagītāṃstapodhanāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. The Gaṇas stationed in the nether worlds, sky and the earth (came there); the residents of all the worlds too came there.

Tuṃburu, Nāraḍa, Hāhā, Hūhū and the Sāmagas took up stringed instruments and played on them in the festival of Śaṅkara. All the sages and ascetics sang Vedic songs of great sacred nature.

## \|\| 2.26.56-57 \|\|

*puṇyānvaivāhikānmaṃtrāñjeṣuḥ saṃhṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ pratasthegiriśo vījyamānaśca gaṃgayā \|\| 56 \|\|*

*tathā yamunayā cāpāṃpatinā dhṛtacchatrayā \|*  
*strībhirnānāvidhālāpailājābhiścānumoditaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. They were delighted in their minds and repeated the sacred Mantras pertaining to marriage rites. Thus started Giriśa. He was fanned by Gaṅgā and Yamunā, while the Lord of the Waters held the umbrella. He was cheered and humoured by the different groups of women showering fried grains and holding various kinds of talks.

## \|\| 2.26.58-59 \|\|

*mahotsavena deveśo giristhānaṃ viveśa saḥ \|*  
*prabhāsatsvarṇakalaśaṃ toraṇānāṃ śatairyutam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*vaiḍūryabaddhabhūmisthaṃ ratnajaiśca gṛhairyutam \|*  
*tatpraviśya stūyamāno dvāramabhyāsasāda ha \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. With great festivity, the Lord of Devas entered the abode of the Mountain, where golden domes shone. It was fitted with hundreds of arched gateways; there all the floors had been paved with lapis lazuli. It had a number of houses built of gems and jewels. While entering he was being eulogized.

## \|\| 2.26.60 \|\|

*tato himācalastatra dṛśyate vyākulākulaḥ \|*  
*ādiśadātmabhṛtyānāṃ mahādeva upasthite \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Then Himācala was seen there extremely excited. When Mahādeva approached he began giving orders to his servants.

## \|\| 2.26.61 \|\|

*tato brahmāṇamacalo gurutve prārthayattadā \|*  
*kṛtyānāṃ sarvabhāreṣu vāsudevaṃ ca buddhimān \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Then the Mountain requested Brahmā to accept the office of the preceptor. The intelligent (Mountain) entrusted Vāsudeva (Viṣṇu) with the entire burden of all the duties.

## \|\| 2.26.62-63 \|\|

*pratyāha ca vivāha'sminkumārībhrātaraṃ vinā \|*  
*bhaviṣyati kathaṃ viṣṇo lājahomādikarmasu \|\| 62 \|\|*

*suto hi mama mainākaḥ sa praviṣṭo'rṇave sthitaḥ \|*  
*iti ciṃtāviṣaṇṇaṃ taṃ viṣṇurāhamahāmatiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. He said to him, “In this marriage, O Viṣṇu, how can the rites of Lājāhoma (‘offerings of the fried grain’) etc. take place, without the brother of the bride? Indeed my son Maināka is inside the sea.” Viṣṇu of great intellect spoke to him as he was in a predicament due to worry:

## \|\| 2.26.64 \|\|

*atra ciṃtā na kartavyā girirāja kathaṃcana \|*  
*ahaṃ bhrātā jaganmāturetade vaṃ ca nānyathā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. “In this matter, O Lord of Mountains, you need not worry at all. I am the brother of the mother of the universe. It is so and not otherwise,”

## \|\| 2.26.65 \|\|

*tataḥ pramuditaḥ śailaḥ pārvatīṃ ca svalaṃkṛtām \|*  
*sakhībhiḥ koṭisaṃkhyābhirvṛtāṃ praveśayatsadaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Then the Mountain was delighted. He brought the well-adorned Pārvatī to the assembly-hall surrounded by crores of friends.

## \|\| 2.26.66-67 \|\|

*tato nīlamayastaṃbhaṃ jvalatkāṃcanakuṭṭimam \|*  
*muktājālapariṣkāraṃ jvalitau ṣadhidīpitam \|\| 66 \|\|*

*ratnāsanasahasrāḍhyaṃ śatayojanavistṛtam \|*  
*vivāhamaṃḍapaṃ śarvo viveśānucarāvṛtaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. Surrounded by his attendants, Śarva entered the marriage Pandal, the columns of which were made of sapphire, the shining ground of which had been paved with gold. It had been beautified with clusters of pearls and was illuminated with blazing medicinal herbs; it contained thousands of gem-set seats and was extended to a hundred Yojanas.

## \|\| 2.26.68 \|\|

*tataḥ śailaḥ sapatnīkaḥ pādau prakṣālya harṣitaḥ \|*  
*bhavasya tena toyena siṣice svaṃ jagattathā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Then, the Mountain accompanied by his wife, became delighted while washing the feet of Bhava. He sprinkled the water on himself and on all the people (present there).

## \|\| 2.26.69 \|\|

*pādyamācamanaṃ dattvā madhuparkaṃ ca gāṃ tathā \|*  
*pradānasya prayogaṃ ca saṃciṃtayaṃti brāhmaṇāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. After giving Pādya, Ācamana, Madhuparka and a cow (as gift) the Brāhmaṇas began to ponder upon the procedure of Pradāna (‘giving the daughter in marriage’).

## \|\| 2.26.70 \|\|

*dauhitrīṃ kavyavāhānāṃ dadmi putrīṃ svakāmaham \|*  
*ityuktvā tasthivāñchailo na jānāti harasya saḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. “I am giving you my daughter, the granddaughter of Kavyavāhas (Pitṛs).” After saying this the Mountain stood (silent). He did not know the particulars of Hara.

## \|\| 2.26.71-73 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvānapṛcchatsa kulaṃ ko'pi na veda tat \|*  
*tato viṣṇuridaṃ prāha pṛchyaṃte'nye kimarthataḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*ajñātakulatāṃ tasya pṛchyatāmayameva ca \|*  
*ahireva aheḥ pādānvetti nānyo himācala \|\| 72 \|\|*

*svagotraṃ yadi na brūte na deyā bhaginī mama \|*  
*tato hāsastadā jajñe sarveṣāṃ sumahāsvanaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

71-73. Then he asked everyone about the family (of Śiva). No one knew that. Then Viṣṇu said this: “Why are the others being asked? He is of unknown family and parentage. Let him alone be asked. It is only the serpent that knows the feet of serpents, O Himācala. If he does not mention his Gotra (‘Lineage’), my sister should not be given.” Thereat all of them laughed loudly.

## \|\| 2.26.74-75 \|\|

*nivṛttaśca kṣaṇādbhūyaḥ kiṃ vakṣyati harastviti \|*  
*tato vimṛśya bahudhā kiṃcidbhītānano yatā \|\| 74 \|\|*

*lajjājaḍaḥ smitaṃ cakre tataḥ pārtha sa vai haraḥ \|*  
*tato viśiṣṭā bruvati śīghraṃ kālo'tivartate \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. Within a moment all the laughter subsided. Everyone awaited what Hara would say. Then Hara pondered in various ways. He appeared to be a bit afraid—‘they may not give Pārvātī in marriage if I (Śiva) do not tell them my Gotra.’ He remained dumb, speechless due to bashfulness. O son of Pṛthā, he smlied. Then the leading persons said, “Be quick. The time is up.”

## \|\| 2.26.76 \|\|

*hariḥ prāha maheśānaṃ bibhyadāvedmayahaṃ tava \|*  
*mātāmahaṃ ca pitaraṃ prayogaṃ śrṛṇu bhūdhara \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Hari spoke to Maheśāna who was afraid, “I shall name your grandfather and father.” “Listen, O mountain, to the procedure.”

## \|\| 2.26.77 \|\|

*ātmaputrāya te śaṃbho ātmadauhitrakāya te \|*  
*ityukte viṣṇunā sarve sādhusādhviti te jaguḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. “O Śambhu, to you the son of Ātman, to the grandson of Ātman”.

When this was said by Viṣṇu, all of them said, “Well-done! Well-done!”

## \|\| 2.26.78-79 \|\|

*devo'pyudāharedvuddhiṃ sarvebhyo'pyadhikāṃ varām \|*  
*tataḥ śailastathā coktvā dattvā devīṃ ca sodakam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ cāpi devāya pradadau sodakaṃ nagaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sarve tuṣṭuvustaṃ vivāhaṃ vismayānvitāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. The Lord too exhibited an intelligence more excellent than that of all others. Then the Mountain mentioned it and gave the goddess along with the formal libation of water. He dedicated himself to the Lord. The Mountain offered himself with water to the Lord, Then all of them were surprised. They praised the marriage rite.

## \|\| 2.26.80 \|\|

*dātā mahībhṛtāṃ nātho hotā devaścaturmukhaḥ \|*  
*varaḥ paśupatiḥ sākṣātkanyā viśvaraṇistathā \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The giver is the Lord of all Mountains. The presiding priest is the Four-faced Lord. The bridegroom is Paśupati himself and the bride is the Mother of the universe.

## \|\| 2.26.81 \|\|

*tataḥ stuvatsu muniṣu puṣpavarṣe mahatyapi \|*  
*nadatsu devatūryeṣu karaṃ jagrāha tryambakaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. When the sages eulogized, when the great shower of flowers was being scattered and while the celestial musical instruments were being played, the Three-eyed Lord (formally) grasped the hand (of the goddess),

## \|\| 2.26.82 \|\|

*devo devīṃ samālokya salajjāṃ himaśailajām \|*  
*na tṛpyati na cāhlādatsā ca devāṃ vṛṣadhvajam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. On glancing at the bashful goddess, the daughter of the Himālaya Mountain, the Lord was not satiated. Nor did she delight the Bull-bannered Lord to satiation.

## \|\| 2.26.83 \|\|

*tatra brahmādimunayo devīmadbhutarūpiṇīm \|*  
*paśyaṃtaḥ śaraṇaṃ jagmurmanasā parameśvaram \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The sages beginning with Brahmā gazed at the goddess of wonderful form and mentally sought refuge in Parameśvara (Śiva).

## \|\| 2.26.84 \|\|

*mā muhyāma pārvatīṃ ca yathā nāradaparvatau \|*  
*tatastathaiva taccakre sarveṣāmīpsitaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. “Let us not lose sense over Pārvatī, like Nārada and Parvata (over Śrīmatī).” Thereupon, he carried out the desire of everyone.

## \|\| 2.26.85 \|\|

*tato devaiśca munibhiḥ saṃstutaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*praviveśa śubhāṃ vedīṃ mūrtimajjvalanāśritām \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Then, Parameśvara was eulogized by the Devas and sages. He entered the auspicious altar containing the Fire-god in an embodied form.

## \|\| 2.26.86-89 \|\|

*vedhāḥ śrutīritairmaṃ trairmūrtimadbhirupasthitaiḥ \|*  
*mūrtamagniṃ juhāva triḥ parikramya ca taṃ haraḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*lājāhoma umābhrātā prāha taṃ sasmitaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*bahavo militāḥ saṃti lokāḥ saṃmarda īśvara \|\| 87 \|\|*

*sāvadhānena rakṣyāṇi bhūṣaṇāni tvayā hara \|*  
*tato haraśca taṃ prāha svajane mā'tigopaya \|\| 88 \|\|*

*kiṃcitprārthaya dāsyāmi prāha viṣṇustato varam \|*  
*tvayi bhaktirdṛḍhā me'stu sa ca taddurlabhaṃ dadau \|\| 89 \|\|*

86-89. By means of the Mantras prescribed in the Vedas, who were bodily present (there), he performed the Homa in the Agni of an embodied form. Hara circumambulated the fire three times and performed Lājā Homa (i.e. offering of the fried grains in the fire). Hari, the brother of Umā, smilingly said to him, “O Īśvara, many people have gathered. The pressure of the crowd of people is great. O Hara, all the ornaments should be guarded well with careful attention by you.” Then Hara said to him, “Do not over-guard it even from your own people. Request for something. I shall give you.” Then Viṣṇu said, “It is good, let my devotion to you be firm.” He granted that rare (boon).

## \|\| 2.26.90 \|\|

*dadatuḥ sṛṣṭisaṃrakṣāṃ brahmaṇe dakṣiṇāmubhau \|*  
*agnaye yajñabhāgāṃśca prītau harajanārdanau \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Then both of them, Hara and Janārdana, who were pleased, gave as Dakṣiṇā Brahmā the protection of the creation; to Agni they gave shares in the Yajñas.

## \|\| 2.26.91-94 \|\|

*bhṛgvādīnāṃ tato dattvā śrutirakṣaṇadakṣiṇām \|*  
*tato gītaiśca nṛtyaiśca bhojanaiśca yathepsitaiḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*mahotsavairanekaiśca vismayaṃ samapadyata \|*  
*visṛjya lokaṃ taṃ sarvaṃ kimicchādānakairbhavaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*sarasvatyā ca pitarau devyāścā'śvāsya duḥkhitau \|*  
*āmaṃtrya himaśaileṃdraṃ brahmaṇaṃ ca sakeśavam \|\| 93 \|\|*

*jagāma maṃdaragiriṃ giriṇā yānugorcitaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

91-94. To Bhṛgu and others, he gave as Dakṣiṇā, the protection of the Vedas. Then there was a wonderfully pleasant time with songs, dances and feastings as they pleased and many kinds of festivities. After giving them gifts as they desired, he bade farewell to the whole world. Bhava then consoled the parents of the goddess who had been miserable. He consoled them with sweet words. He took leave of Himācala, Brahmā and Keśava and went to Mandara mountain. He was duly worshipped along with his followers by the Mountain.

## \|\| 2.26.95-96 \|\|

*tato gate bhagavati nīlalohite sahomayā girimamalaṃ hi bhūdharaḥ \|*  
*sabāṃdhavo ruditi hi kasya no mano visaṃṣṭhaṃlaṃ jagati hi kanyakāpituḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*imaṃ vivāhaṃ girirājaputryāḥ śrṛṇoti cādhyeti ca yo naraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*viśeṣataścāpi vivāhamaṃgale sa maṃgalaṃ vṛddhimavāpnute ciram \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96. When Lord Nīlalohita had gone along with Umā to his pure mountain, the Mountain Himavān began to cry. Who is that father of a girl whose mind is not agitated and excited?

The man who listens to, and studies this (description of the) marriage of the daughter of the King of Mountains with great purity, especially in the course of a marriage festival, attains auspiciousness and perpetual prosperity.

## Chapter 27 - Pārvatī Enraged: The Origin of Gaṇeśa

## \|\| 2.27.1 \|\|

*\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*tato nirupamaṃ divyaṃ sarvaratnamayaṃ śubham \|*  
*īśānanirmitaṃ sākṣātsaha devyāviśadgṛham \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. Then along with the goddess the Lord entered the abode that had been directly built by Īśāna and was matchlessly divine. It was splendid and was set with all sorts of gems and jewels.

## \|\| 2.27.2 \|\|

*tatrāsau maṃdaragirau saha devyā bhagākṣahā \|*  
*prāsāde tatra codyāne reme saṃhṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There, the destroyer of the vision of Bhaga sported with the goddess on the Mandara mountain, in the palace and in the park. He was delighted in his mind.

## \|\| 2.27.3 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devāstārakeṇātipīḍitāḥ \|*  
*protsāhitena cātyarthaṃ mayā kalicikīrṣuṇā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the meantime Devas had been excessively harassed by Tāraka, urged to a great extent by me who was desirous of bringing about a quarrel.

## \|\| 2.27.4-6 \|\|

*āsādya te bhavaṃ devaṃ tuṣṭuburbahudhā stavaiḥ \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare devī prodvartayata gātrakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*udvartanamalenātha naraṃ cakre gajānanam \|*  
*devānāṃ saṃstavaiḥ puṇyaiḥ kṛpayābhipariplutā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*putretyuvāca taṃ devī tataḥ saṃhṛṣṭamānasā \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare śarvastatrāgatya vaco'bravīt \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. They came to Lord Bhava and eulogized him with many hymns. In the meantime the goddess cleansed her person and applied perfumes and unguents over her body. With the dirt of the cleansing therefrom she created a human body with elephantine face. On being moved with compassion by the holy eulogies of Devas the goddess spoke to him addressing “O son” with delighted mind. In the meantime Śarva came there and spoke these words:

## \|\| 2.27.7-10 \|\|

*putrastavāyaṃ girije śrṛṇu yādṛgbhaviṣyati \|*  
*vikrameṇa ca vīryeṇa kṛpayā sadṛśo mayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yathāhaṃ tādṛśaścāsau putraste bhavitā guṇaiḥ \|*  
*ye ca pāpā durācārā vedāndharmaṃ dviṣaṃti ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*teṣāmāmaraṇāṃtāni vighnānyeṣa kariṣyati \|*  
*ye ca māṃ naiva manyaṃte viṣṇuṃ vāpi jagadgurum \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vighnitā vighnarājena te yāsyaṃti mahattamaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ gṛheṣu kalahaḥ sadā naivopasāmyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. “O daughter of the Mountain, listen; of what nature would he be? By means of his exploits, prowess and compassion he will be on a par with me. Your son will be just like me in qualities. Those sinners of evil conduct who hate the Vedas and Virtue (Dharma) will be harassed by him with obstacles throughout their lives till death. Those who do not honour me or Viṣṇu, the preceptor of the universe, will be hindered by Vighnarāja (Gaṇapati). They will enter great darkness. There will be perpetual quarrel in their houses. It will never subside.

## \|\| 2.27.11-14 \|\|

*putrasya tava vighnena samūlaṃ tasya naśyati \|*  
*yeṣāṃ na pūjyāḥ pūjyaṃte krodhāsatyaparāśca ye \|\| 11 \|\|*

*raudrasāhasikā ye ca teṣāṃ vighnaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*śrutidharmāñjñātidharmānpālayaṃti gurūṃśca ye \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kṛpālavo gatakrodhāsteṣāṃ vighnaṃ hariṣyati \|*  
*sarve dharmāśca karmāṇi tathā nānāvidhāni ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*savighnāni bhivaṣyaṃti pūjayāsya vinā śubhe \|*  
*evaṃ śrutvā umā prāha evamastviti śaṃkaram \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. By the obstacles caused by your son, everything connected with them will perish to the very root.

He will cause obstacles to those by whom persons worthy of adoration are not respected duly, those who are excessively prone to anger and untruth and those who are terribly venturesome.

He will remove the obstacles of those persons who abide by the Dharma of Śrutis (i.e. holy rites laid down in the Śrutis) and those who keep up the customs and conventions of their kinsmen and society, those who are merciful and those who are devoid of anger.

O splendid lady, without his worship all pious deeds and holy rites of various kinds will be hindered and obstructed.”

On hearing this Umā said to Śaṅkara, “Let it be so.”

## \|\| 2.27.15 \|\|

*tato bṛhattanuḥ so'bhūttejasā dyotayandiśaḥ \|*  
*tato gaṇaiḥ samaṃ śarvaḥ surāṇāṃ pradadau ca tam \|*  
*yāvattāra kahaṃtā vo bhavettāvadayaṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. His body increased in size and he brightened the quarters. Thereupon, Śarva gave him to Suras along with Gaṇas (saying), “This is your Lord till the advent of the slayer of Tāraka.”

## \|\| 2.27.16 \|\|

*tato vighnapatirdevaiḥ saṃstutaḥ pramatārtihā \|*  
*cakāra teṣāṃ kṛtyāni vighnāni ditijanmanām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Since then, Vighnapati (‘Lord of obstacles’), the destroyer of the agony of those who bow down, was eulogized by Devas. He made their activities obstacle-free and put obstacles in the activities of Daityas.

## \|\| 2.27.17 \|\|

*pārvatī ca punardevī putratve parikalpya ca \|*  
*aśokasyāṃkuraṃ vārbhiravarddhayata svādṛtaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Afterwards goddess Pārvatī adopted a sapling of Aśoka as her own son and nurtured it with waters brought by herself.

## \|\| 2.27.18 \|\|

*saptarṣīnatha cāhūya saṃskāramaṃgalaṃ taroḥ \|*  
*kārayāmāsa tanvaṃgī tatastāṃ munayo'bruvan \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. She invited the Seven Sages and made them perform the auspicious and consecratory rites of the tree. Then the Sages spoke to that lady of slender body:

## \|\| 2.27.19 \|\|

*tvayaiva darśite mārge maryādāṃ kartumarhasi \|*  
*kiṃ phalaṃ bhavitā devi kalpitaistaruputrakaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “O goddess, it behoves you to fix a rule for the path pointed out by you alone. What will be the benefit in adopting trees as sons?”

## \|\| 2.27.20-23 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*yo vai nirudake grāme kūpaṃ kārayate budhaḥ \|*  
*yāvattoyaṃ bhavetkūpe tāvatsvarge sa modate \|\| 20 \|\|*

*daśakūpasamāvāpī daśavāpī samaṃ saraḥ \|*  
*daśasaraḥsamā kanyā daśakanyāsamaḥ kratuḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*daśakratusamaḥ putro daśaputrasamo drumaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*eṣaiva mama maryādā niyatā lokabhāvinī \|*  
*jīrṇoddhāre kṛte vāpi phalaṃ taddviguṇaṃ matam \|\| 23 \|\|*

The goddess said:

20-23. If a learned man digs a well in a village without water, he will rejoice in heaven as long as there is water in that well.

A tank is on a par with ten wells. A lake is on a par with ten tanks. A girl is on a par with ten lakes. A sacrifice is on a par with ten girls (daughters). A son is on a par with ten sacrifices and a tree is on a par with ten sons. This is ray rule. It is invariable and it sanctifies the worlds. When the ruins are repaired the benefit is considered to be twofold.

Thus the origin of Gaṇeśa (has been recounted).

## \|\| 2.27.24-27 \|\|

*iti gaṇeśotpattiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kadācidbhagavānumayā saha maṃdare \|*  
*maṃdire harṣajanane kaladhautamaye śubhe \|\| 24 \|\|*

*prakīrṇakusumāmodamahālikulakūjite \|*  
*kiṃnarodgītasaṃgīta pratiśabditamadhyake \|\| 25 \|\|*

*krīḍāmayūrairhasaiśca śrutaiścaivābhinādite \|*  
*mauktikairvividha ratnairvinirmitagavākṣake \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tatra puṇyakathābhiśca krīḍato rubhayostayoḥ \|*  
*prādurabhūnmahāñchabdaḥ pūritāṃbaragocaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. Thereafter, once, the Lord was sporting with Umā on the Mandara mountain. In a splendid silver mansion that delighted (everyone) both of them sported and had pleasant and meritorious talks. Flowers had been scattered here and there. Hence bees were humming and hovering round in great numbers for the sake of the fragrance of those flowers. The middle portion (of the mansion) reverberated with the loud songs of Kinnaras. There was also the pleasant sound of peacocks kept as pets for the sake of sports, as well as of swans. The windows were made and beautified with different kinds of pearls and gems and jewels. While they were thus engaged, a loud sound was heard. It filled the entire sky.

## \|\| 2.27.28 \|\|

*taṃ śrutvā kautukāddevī kimetaditi śaṃkaram \|*  
*paryapṛcchacchubhatanūrharaṃ vismayapūrvakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On hearing it the goddess became curious. The goddess of splendid body asked Śaṅkara with great surprise, “What is this?”

## \|\| 2.27.29 \|\|

*tāmāha devīṃ giriśo dṛṣṭapūrvāstu te tvayā \|*  
*ete gaṇā me krīḍaṃti śaile'smiṃstvatpriyāḥ śubhe \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Giriśa spoke to the goddess, “They have already been seen by you. These are my Gaṇas, O splendid lady. They play about on this mountain. They are fond of you.

## \|\| 2.27.30 \|\|

*tapasā brahmacaryeṇa kleśena kṣetrasādhanaiḥ \|*  
*yairahaṃ toṣitaḥ pṛthvyāṃ ta ete manujottamāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. They had been excellent men on the earth and I had been propitiated by them by means of penance, vow of celibacy, various kinds of physical sufferings in visiting holy spots etc.

## \|\| 2.27.31 \|\|

*matsamīpamanuprāptā mama lokaṃ varānane \|*  
*carācarasya jagataḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhāraṇakṣamāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. They have come near me in my world, O lady of excellent face. They are capable of creating and annihilating the universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings.

## \|\| 2.27.32 \|\|

*vinaitānnaiva me prītirnaibhirvirahito rame \|*  
*ete ahamahaṃ caite tānetānpasya pārvati \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Without them I am not at all happy. I do not feel joy without these. I am they and they are me. O Pārvatī, see them.”

## \|\| 2.27.33 \|\|

*ityuktā vismitā devī dadṛśe tāngavākṣake \|*  
*sthitā padmapalāśākṣī mahādevena bhāṣitā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On being told thus, the goddess became surprised. The goddess with her eyes resembling lotus petals and addressed thus by Mahādeva, saw them through the window.

## \|\| 2.27.34 \|\|

*kecitkṛśā hrasvadīrghāḥ kecitsthūlamahodarāḥ \|*  
*vyāghrebhameṣājamukhā nānāprāṇimahāmukhāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Some of them were lean, some short, some tall. Some of them were very stout with large bellies. They had the faces of tiger, elephant, sheep and goat. They had the faces of different kinds of living beings.

## \|\| 2.27.35 \|\|

*vyāghracarmaparīdhānā nagnā jvālāmukhāḥ pare \|*  
*gokarṇā gajakarṇāśca bahupādamukhekṣaṇāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Some wore the hides of tigers. Others were naked. Others had faces with flames coming out of their mouths. Some had the ears of cows and some (had those) of elephants. They had many feet, faces and eyes.

## \|\| 2.27.36 \|\|

*vicitravāhanāścaiva nānāyudhadharāstathā \|*  
*gītavāditratattvajñāḥ sattvagītarasapriyāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Some had very strange vehicles. They wielded various kinds of weapons. Some were conversant with the principles of vocal music and instrumental music. They were fond of sweet songs of all living beings.

## \|\| 2.27.37 \|\|

*tāndṛṣṭvā pārvatī prāha katisaṃkhyābhidhāstvamī \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On seeing them Pārvatī said, “How many are these and what are their names?”

## \|\| 2.27.38 \|\|

*śrīśaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*asaṃkhye yāstvamī devī asaṃkhyeyābhidhāstathā \|*  
*jagadāpūritaṃ sarvametairbhīmairmahābalaiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

Śrī Śaṅkara said:

38\. O gentle lady, these are innumerable. They have innumerable names as well. The entire universe is filled with these terrible beings of great strength.

## \|\| 2.27.39-40 \|\|

*siddhakṣetreṣu rathyāsu jīrṇodyāneṣu veśmasu \|*  
*dānavānāṃ śarīreṣu bāleṣūnmattakeṣu ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

*ete viśati muditā nānāhāravihāriṇaḥ \|*  
*ūṣmapāḥ phenapāścaiva dhūmrapā madhupāyinaḥ \|*  
*madāhārāḥ sarvabhakṣyāstathānye cāpyabhojanāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. These enter Siddha-kṣetras (i.e. holy places of Siddhas), streets, dilapidated parks, houses, the bodies of Dānavas, children, maddened persons etc. They rejoice with different kinds of food and sports. Some are heat-imbibers, some foam-imbibers, some smoke-imbibers and some honey-imbibers. The diet of some is ichor. Others eat everything and some eat no food at all.

## \|\| 2.27.41 \|\|

*gītanṛtyopahārāśca nānāvādyaravapriyāḥ \|*  
*anaṃtatvādamīṣāṃ ca vaktuṃ śakyā na vai guṇāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. They engage themselves in singing and dancing and other simple activities. They are fond of the sound of different kinds of musical instruments. They are infinite in number. Their qualities cannot be described.

## \|\| 2.27.42 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*manaḥśilena kalkena ya eṣa cchuritānanaḥ \|*  
*tejasā bhāskarākāro rūpeṇa sadṛśastava \|\| 42 \|\|*

The goddess (Śrī Devī) said:

42\. Who is this one who has coated his face with powdered red arsenic, who has the form of the Sun in refulgence and who resembles you in features.

## \|\| 2.27.43 \|\|

*ākarṇyākarṇya te deva gaṇairgītānmahāguṇān \|*  
*muhurnṛtyati hāsyaṃ ca vidadhāti muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On hearing your great qualities sung about by the Gaṇas, O Lord, he repeatedly dances and makes humorous gestures.

## \|\| 2.27.44 \|\|

*sadāśivaśivetyevaṃ vihvalo vakti yo muhuḥ \|*  
*dhanyo'mīdṛśī yasya bhaktistvayi maheśvare \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In great excitement, he repeats ‘Sadāśiva’, ‘Śiva’. Blessed indeed is he because he has so much devotion to you, O Maheśvara.

## \|\| 2.27.45-47 \|\|

*enaṃ vijñātumicchāmi kiṃnāmāsau gaṇastava \|*  
*śrīśaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*sa eṣa vīraka devī sadā medrisute priyaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*nānāścaryaguṇādhāraḥ pratīhāro matoṃ'bike \|*  
*devyuvāca \|*  
*īdṛśasya sutasyāpi mamo'kaṃṭhā purāṃtaka \|\| 46 \|\|*

*kadāhamīdṛśaṃ putraṃ lapsyāmyānaṃdadāyakam \|*  
*śarva uvāca \|*  
*eṣa eva sutastestu yāvadīdṛkparo bhavet \|\| 47 \|\|*

45a. I wish to know him. What is the name of this Gaṇa of yours?

Śrī Śaṅkara replied:

45b-47. O gentle lady, daughter of the Mountain, he is Vīraka, a permanent favourite of mine. He has many mysterious features and good qualities. O Aṃbikā, he is considered to be my gatekeeper.

## \|\| 2.27.48 \|\|

*ityuktā vijayāṃ prāha śīghramānaya vīrakam \|*  
*vijayā ca tato gatvā vīrakaṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 48 \|\|*

Devī said:

O Slayer of the Puras, I have great yearning and craving for a son like him. When will I get a son. like him, the bestower of delight?

Śarva said:

Let him alone be your son till there is another one like him.

48\. On being told thus, she told Vijayā, “Bring Vīraka quickly.” Vijayā went to Vīraka and spoke these words:

## \|\| 2.27.49 \|\|

*ehi vīraka te devī girijā toṣitā śubhā \|*  
*tvamamāhvayati sā devī bhavasyānumate svayam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. “Come on, Vīraka, the splendid goddess is pleased with you. That goddess calls you with the permission of Bhava himself.”

## \|\| 2.27.50 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ saṃbhramayuto mukhaṃ saṃmārjya pāṇinā \|*  
*devyāḥ samīpamāgacchajjayayā'nugataḥ śanaiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On being told thus, he became greatly agitated. He wiped his face with his hand. Slowly he came near the goddess followed by Vijayā.

## \|\| 2.27.51 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā girijā prāha girāmadhuravarṇayā \|*  
*ehyehi putra dattastvaṃ bhavena mama putrakaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. On seeing him, the daughter of the Mountain said in a sweet voice, “Come, Come, dear Son. You are given to me by Bhava as my son.”

## \|\| 2.27.52 \|\|

*ityukto daṃḍavaddevīṃ praṇamyāvasthitaḥ puraḥ \|*  
*mātā tatastamāliṃgya kṛtvotsaṃge ca vīrakam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. On being told thus, he prostrated before the goddess falling down like a staff. Then he stood up as before. The mother then embraced him and placed Vīraka in her lap.

## \|\| 2.27.53 \|\|

*cucuṃba ca kapole taṃ gātrāṇi ca pramārjayat \|*  
*bhūṣayāmāsa divyaistaṃ svayaṃ nānāvibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. She kissed him in the cheek and stroked his limbs. She herself adorned him with different kinds of ornaments,

## \|\| 2.27.54 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃkalpya taṃ putraṃ lālayitvā umāciram \|*  
*uvāca putra krīḍeti gaccha sārdhaṃ gaṇairiti \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. After considering him as her son and after fondling him for a long time, Umā said, “So, go and play along with the Gaṇas.”

## \|\| 2.27.55 \|\|

*tataścikrīḍa madhye sa gaṇānāṃ pārvatīsutaḥ \|*  
*muhurmuhuḥ svamanasi stuvanbhaktiṃ sa śāṃkarīm \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thereupon, that son of Pārvatī played amidst the Gaṇas eulogizing the devotion to Śaṅkara repeatedly in his mind.

## \|\| 2.27.56 \|\|

*praṇamya sarvabhūtāni prārthayāmyasmi duṣkaram \|*  
*bhaktyā bhajadhvamīśānaṃ yasyā bhakteridaṃ phalam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. ‘I bow down unto all living beings and request them to do something very difficult to do. Worship Īśāna with devotion. This is the benefit of that devotion.’

## \|\| 2.27.57 \|\|

*krīḍituṃ vīrake yāte tato devī ca pārvatī \|*  
*nānākathābhiscikrīḍa punareva jaṭābhṛtā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. When Vīraka went out to play, goddess Pārvatī sported with (the Lord) wearing matted locks of hair, recounting various kinds of stories.

## \|\| 2.27.58 \|\|

*tato girisutākaṇṭhe kṣiptabāhurmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tapasastu viśeṣārthaṃ narma devīṃ kilābravīt \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Then Maheśvara placed his arms round the neck of the daughter of the Mountain. In order to make her perform a special penance, he made the following witty remarks to the

goddess:

## \|\| 2.27.59 \|\|

*sa hi gauratanuḥ śarvo viśeṣācchaśiśobhitaḥ \|*  
*raṃjitā ca vibhāvaryā devī nīlotpalacchaviḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Indeed Śarva had a white-complexioned body. He shone particularly like the moon. The goddess had the complexion of blue lotus, coloured (as it were) by the night.

## \|\| 2.27.60 \|\|

*śarva uvāca \|*  
*śarīre mama tanvaṃgī site bhāsyasitadyutiḥ \|*  
*bhujaṃgīvāsitā śubhre saṃśliṣṭā candane tarau \|\| 60 \|\|*

Śarva said:

60\. On my white body, O slender-bodied lady, you with your black colour shine like a black serpent maiden coiling round a fair sandalwood tree.

## \|\| 2.27.61 \|\|

*caṃdrajyotsnābhisaṃpṛktā tāmasī rajanī yathā \|*  
*rajanī vā site pakṣe dṛṣṭidoṣaṃ dadāsi me \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. You are like the dark night mixed with the moonlight. You give me the defect of vision like the night in the dark half (of the lunar month).

## \|\| 2.27.62 \|\|

*ityuktā girijā tena kaṇṭhaṃ śarvādvimucya sā \|*  
*uvāca koparaktākṣī bhṛkuṭīvikṛtānanā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On being addressed thus, the daughter of the Mountain got her neck released from (the grip of) Śarva. With the eyes reddened due to anger and with the face deformed by the knitting of the eyebrows she said:

## \|\| 2.27.63 \|\|

*svakṛtena janaḥ sarvo janena paribhūyate \|*  
*avaśyamarthī prāpnoti khaṇḍanāṃ śaśikhaṃḍabhṛt \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “O Crescent-bearing one, that all the people are assailed by other people is because of their own deeds. A suppliant of necessity meets with frustration?

## \|\| 2.27.64 \|\|

*tapobhirdīptacaritairyattvāṃ prārthitavatyaham \|*  
*tasya me niyamasyaivamavamānaḥ padepade \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. I sought you with various kinds of severe austerities and brilliant activities. (Unfortunately) at every step that holy observance of mine is being insulted.

## \|\| 2.27.65 \|\|

*naivāhaṃ kuṭilā śarva viṣamā na ca dhūrjaṭe \|*  
*svadoṣaistvaṃ gataḥ kṣāṃtiṃ tathā doṣākaraśriyaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O Śarva, I am not crooked nor am I adverse and odd and deformed, O Dhūrjaṭī. You have attained forbearance, because of your own faults as well as of the faults of the splendour of Doṣākara (i.e. the Moon, also one who is a mine of defects).

## \|\| 2.27.66 \|\|

*nāhaṃ muṣṇāmi nayane netrahaṃtā bhavānbhava \|*  
*bhagastatte vijānāti tathaivedaṃ jagattrayamā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. I do not deprive (others) of eyes. You alone are a destroyer of eyes (eye-sight). Bhaga knows this (aspect) of yours. So also the entire three worlds.

## \|\| 2.27.67 \|\|

*mūrdhni śūlaṃ janayase svairdoṣairmāmadikṣipan \|*  
*yattvaṃ māmāha kṛṣṇeti mahākālo'si viśrutaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. You create a headache in me reviling me with your own defects. For you called me Kṛṣṇā (black) but you are called Mahākāla (‘extremely black or a great annihilator’).

## \|\| 2.27.68 \|\|

*yāsyāmyahaṃ parityaktumātmānaṃ tapasā girim \|*  
*jīvaṃtyā nāsti me kṛtyaṃ dhūrtena paribhūtayā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. I am going to the mountain in order to abandon myself by means of penance. I have nothing to do with my being continuously alive because I have been insulted by a rogue.”

## \|\| 2.27.69 \|\|

*niśamya tasyā vacanaṃ kopatīkṣṇākṣaraṃ bhavaḥ \|*  
*uvācātha ca saṃbhrāṃto durjñeyacarito haraḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. On hearing her words which had been very sharp on account of anger, Bhava, Hara whose conduct was inscrutable said in great excitement:

## \|\| 2.27.70 \|\|

*na tattvajñāsi girije nāhaṃ niṃdāparastava \|*  
*cāṭūktibuddhyā kṛtavāṃsta vāhaṃ narmakīrtanam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. ‘O daughter of the Mountain, you are not conversant with the reality. I am not censuring or reviling you. With the intention of uttering some coaxing words I engaged myself in this diversion of amusing words.

## \|\| 2.27.71 \|\|

*vikalpaḥ svacchacitteti girijaiṣā mama priyā \|*  
*prāyeṇa bhūtiliptānāmanyathā ciṃtitā hṛdi \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. It was a mistake on my part (to have thought) that the daughter of the Mountain had a dean mind about her being my beloved. Generally the way of thinking of persons in great prosperity is peculiar (i.e. other than the ordinary).

## \|\| 2.27.72 \|\|

*asmādṛśānāṃ kṛṣṇāṃgi pravartaṃte'nyathā giraḥ \|*  
*yadyevaṃ kupitā bhīru na te vakṣyāmyahaṃ punaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O lady of dark limbs, the words of people like us act (i.e. imply) otherwise. If you are angry, O timid lady, I will not say like this again to you.

## \|\| 2.27.73 \|\|

*narmavādī bhaviṣyāmi jahi kopaṃ sucismite \|*  
*śirasā praṇataste'haṃ racitaste mayāñjaliḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. I shall be a sycophant—a flatterer saying amusing words. O lady of pure smiles, give up your anger; I bow down my head before you. I pray to you with the palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 2.27.74 \|\|

*dīnenāpyapamānena niṃditā nami vikriyām \|*  
*varamasmi vinamro'pi na tvaṃ devi guṇānvitā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. I do not undergo any perturbation even though I am censured with mean insult. It is better that I am extremely humble. Still, O goddess, you do not thereby become endowed with good qualities.”

## \|\| 2.27.75 \|\|

*ityanekaiścāṭuvākyaiḥ sūktairdevena bodhitā \|*  
*kopaṃ tīvraṃ na tatyāja satī marmaṇi ghaṭṭitā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Although she was advised and urged by means of many words of flattery and good words by the Lord, the chaste lady did not give up her intense anger, because she had been wounded in a vulnerable spot.

## \|\| 2.27.76 \|\|

*avaṣṭabdhāvatha kṣiptvā pādau śaṃkarapāṇinā \|*  
*viparyastālakā vegādgantumaicchata śailajā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. She shook off her feet held by the hands of Śaṅkara. With her forelocks thrown back, the daughter of the Mountain wished to go away in a hurry.

## \|\| 2.27.77 \|\|

*tasyāṃ vrajantyāṃ kopena punarāha purāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ sarvairavayavaiḥ suteti sadṛśī pituḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. As she went off in fury, the Slayer of the Puras (Śiva) said, “It is true that the daughter is on a par with her father in her limbs.

## \|\| 2.27.78 \|\|

*himācalasya śrṛṃgaistairmeghamālākulairmanaḥ \|*  
*tathā duravāgāhyo'sau hṛdayebhyastavāśayaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Your mind is like the peak of Himācala encircled and obscured by the clusters of clouds. Your mind is very difficult to be fathomed.

## \|\| 2.27.79 \|\|

*kāṭhinyaṃ kaṣṭamasmiṃste vanebhyo bahudhā gatam \|*  
*kuṭilatvaṃ nadībhyaste duḥsevyatvaṃ himādapi \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. You have acquired hardness from the forests of Himācala, crookedness from the rivers and impossibility of being resorted to from the snow.

## \|\| 2.27.80 \|\|

*saṃkrāṃtaṃ sarvamevaitattava devī himācalāt \|*  
*ityuktā sā punaḥ prāha giriśaṃ sailajā tadā \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. All these things, O goddess have come over to you from Himācala.”

On being told thus, the daughter of the Mountain said to Giriśa once again:

## \|\| 2.27.81 \|\|

*kopakaṃpitadhūmrāsyā prasphuraddaśanacchadā \|*  
*mā śarvātmopamānena niṃda tvaṃ guṇino janān \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. With her face fuming and shaking with anger and the lips throbbing she said: “O Śarva, do not censure people with good qualities. You are viewing everyone in comparison with, you.

## \|\| 2.27.82 \|\|

*tavāpi duṣṭasaṃparkātsaṃkrāṃtaṃ sarvamevahi \|*  
*vyālebhyo'nekajihvatvaṃ bhasmanaḥ snehavandhyatā \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Because of your contact with the wicked ones, everything has come over to you: Ths stats of being many-tongued from the serpents, the lack of Sneha (affection, glossiness) from the ash (which you apply to your psrson).

## \|\| 2.27.83 \|\|

*hṛtkāluṣyaṃ śaśāṃkātte durbodhatvaṃ vṛṣādapi \|*  
*athavā bahunoktena alaṃ vācā śrameṇa me \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. (You have got) turbidness of the heart from the moon; Durbodhatva (inability to understand) from the bull. Or enough of speaking too much. Why should I talk and strain myself?

## \|\| 2.27.84 \|\|

*śmaśānavāsa āsīstvaṃ nagnatvānna tava trapā \|*  
*nirghṛṇatvaṃ kapālitvādevaṃ kaḥ śaknuyāttavaṃ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. You were a resident of cremation ground. You have no sense of shame because of your nudity. You are devoid of mercy because you are a skull-bearer. Who can (enumerate your faults)?”

## Chapter 28 - Pārvatī Goes to the Mountain for Penance

## \|\| 2.28.1 \|\|

*\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*vrajaṃtī girijā'paśyatsakhīṃ māturmahāprabhām \|*  
*kusumāmodinīṃnāma tasya śailasya devatām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. After saying thus, the daughter of Himādri went out of the mansion. As she proceeded ahead, the Gaṇas made a hue and cry.

## \|\| 2.28.2 \|\|

*sāpi dṛṣṭvā girisutāṃ snehaviklavamānasā \|*  
*kvapunargacchasītyuccairāliṃgyovāca devatā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. “Where are you going, mother?”, saying this and crying loudly, they ran forward. Vīraka grasped the feet of the goddess and said in a faltering voice choked with tears:

## \|\| 2.28.3-4 \|\|

*sā cāsyai sarvamācakhyau śaṃkarātkopakāraṇam \|*  
*punaścovāca girijā devatāṃ mātṛsaṃmatām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*nityaṃ śailādhirājasya devatā tvamaniṃdite \|*  
*sarvaṃ ca sannidhānaṃ ca mayi cātīva vatsalā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. “O Mother, what is this? Where are you going in great fury? Why are you hurrying away? I will follow you, my mother, very affectionate towards me. If I am forsaken by you, I will not be able to bear the harshness of Giriśa. A son will always be the victim of the harshness of his father if he has no mother.”

## \|\| 2.28.5-10 \|\|

*tadahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yadvidheyaṃ tavādhunā \|*  
*athānya strīpraveśe tu samīpe tu pinākinaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tvayākhyeyaṃ mama śube yuktaṃ paścātkaromyaham \|*  
*tathetyukte tayā devyā yayau devī giriṃ prati \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ramye tatra mahāśṛṃge nānāścaryopaśobhite \|*  
*vibhūṣaṇādi sanyasya vṛkṣavalkaladhāriṇī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tapastepe girisutā putreṇa paripālitā \|*  
*grīṣme paṃcāgnisaṃtaptā varṣāsu ca jaloṣitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yathā na kācitpraviśedyoṣidatra harāṃtike \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā parāṃ striyaṃ cātra vadethā mama putraka \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śīghrameva kariṣyāmi tato yuktamanaṃtaram \|*  
*evamastviti tāṃ devīṃ vīrakaḥ prāha sāṃpratam \|\| 10 \|\|*

5-10. With her right hand, the mother lifted up his face and said to Vīraka: “O son, do not feel sorry. (If bereaved of the mother) It is not proper to fall down from the top of the mountain. It is not justifiable for you to go with me. I shall tell you, my son, a befitting job; listen. I have been called Kṛṣṇā (‘Black’) by Hara and censured. I was treated with contempt. I shall therefore perform a penance and acquire white complexion. This (Lord) is enamoured of women of white complexion. After I have gone, you must guard the entrance continuously looking for even the smallest aperture. See that no women enters and approaches Hara. If you happen to see any other woman here, tell me, dear son. Thereupon I shall do what is suitable.” Vīraka, the son devoid of ailments and delighted in every limb said, “Let it be so” (i.e. your order is proper, I shall abide by it).

## \|\| 2.28.11 \|\|

*māturājñā suto hlāda plāvitāṃgo gatajvaraḥ \|*  
*jagāma tryakṣaṃ saṃdraṣṭuṃ praṇipatya ca mātaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He had his person dipped in the pond of nectar in the form of the mother’s order. His fever (i.e. heated feelings) got subsided. After paying obeisance to his mother, he went to see the Three-eyed god.

## \|\| 2.28.12-14 \|\|

*gajavaktraṃ tataḥ prāha praṇamya samavasthitam \|*  
*sāśrukaṃṭhaṃ prayācaṃtaṃ naya māmapi pārvati \|\| 12 \|\|*

*gajavaktraṃ hi tvāṃ bāla māmivopahasiṣyati \|*  
*tadāgaccha mayā sārdhaṃ yā gatirme tavāpi sā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*parābhavāddhi dhūrtānāṃ maraṇaṃ sādhu putraka \|*  
*evamuktvā samādāya himādriṃ prati sā yayau \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. When the Elephant-faced One bowed down and stood there with the throat choked with tears requesting, “O Pārvatī, take me too,” she said, “O boy, since you are elephantfaced, he will laugh at you as at me. Hence come along with me. Let my state or fate be that of yours too. Death is better than discomfiture at the hands of knaves, dear son”. Saying thus and taking (the Elephant-faced One) with her, she went to the mountain Himādri.

## Chapter 29 - Kumāra Becomes Commander-in-chief of the Deva Army

## \|\| 2.29.1 \|\|

*\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*vrajaṃtī girijā'paśyatsakhīṃ māturmahāprabhām \|*  
*kusumāmodinīṃnāma tasya śailasya devatām \|\| 1 \|\|*

(i) Legend of Arbuda.

Nārada said:

1\. As she was going ahead, the daughter of the Mountain saw a friend of her mother. She had great refulgence. She was the deity of the Mountain. Her name was Kusumāmodinī.

## \|\| 2.29.2 \|\|

*sāpi dṛṣṭvā girisutāṃ snehaviklavamānasā \|*  
*kvapunargacchasītyuccairāliṃgyovāca devatā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. That deity looked at the daughter of the Mountain with her mind agitated and overcome with affection. After embracing her, she asked her loudly, “Where are you going?”

## \|\| 2.29.3 \|\|

*sā cāsyai sarvamācakhyau śaṃkarātkopakāraṇam \|*  
*punaścovāca girijā devatāṃ mātṛsaṃmatām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. She told her everything regarding the cause of her anger with Śaṅkara. Thereafter the daughter of the Mountain mentioned this to that deity honoured by her mother:

## \|\| 2.29.4-6 \|\|

*nityaṃ śailādhirājasya devatā tvamaniṃdite \|*  
*sarvaṃ ca sannidhānaṃ ca mayi cātīva vatsalā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tadahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yadvidheyaṃ tavādhunā \|*  
*athānya strīpraveśe tu samīpe tu pinākinaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tvayākhyeyaṃ mama śubhe yuktaṃ paścātkaromyaham \|*  
*tathetyukte tayā devyā yayau devī giriṃ prati \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. “O uncensured (i.e. praise-worthy) one, you are the presiding deity of the Lord of the Mountains. You have always been present here and you have been greatly affectionate to me. Therefore, I shall tell you what should be done now. If any other lady were to enter the premises of the Pināka-bearing Lord, O splendid lady, you must mention it to me. I shall later on do what is befitting in that respect.” When that deity said, “So be it”, the goddess went towards the Mountain (her father).

## \|\| 2.29.7-11 \|\|

*ramye tatra mahāśṛṃge nānāścaryopaśobhite \|*  
*vibhūṣaṇādi saṃnyasya vṛkṣavalkaladhāriṇī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tapastepe girisutā putreṇa paripālitā \|*  
*grīṣme paṃcāgnisaṃtaptā varṣāsu ca jaloṣitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sthaṃḍilasthā ca hemaṃte nirāhārā tatāpa sā \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare daityo hyaṃdhakasya suto balī \|\| 9 \|\|*

*jñātvā gatāṃ girisutāṃ piturvairamanusmaran \|*  
*āḍirnāma bakabhrātā rahasyāṃtaraprekṣakaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*jite kilāṃdhake daitye giriśenāmaradviṣi \|*  
*āḍiścakāra vipulaṃ tapo harajigīṣayā \|\| 11 \|\|*

7-8a. Renouncing her ornaments and other things, the daughter of the Mountain put on bark-garments. There on the great beautiful peak which was rendered extremely splendid with various mysterious features, she performed penance while her son protected her.

8b-11. During summer, she scorched herself in the midst of the Five Fires. During rainy season, she spent the time in water. During Hemanta (i.e. early winter) she sat (and slept) on bare ground. She performed the penance without any intake of food.

In the meantime, a powerful Daitya, son of Andhaka named Āḍi, the brother of Baka, performed an extensive penance, because he wished to defeat Hara. He did not forget the old enmity, because Daitya Andhaka, the enemy of the immortal beings, had been defeated by Giriśa. He was on the lookout for an opportunity (to take revenge) in secret. He knew that the daughter of the Mountain had gone away.

## \|\| 2.29.12 \|\|

*tamāgatyābravīdbrahmā tapasā paritoṣitaḥ \|*  
*brūhi kiṃ vāsuraśreṣṭha tapasā prāptumicchasi \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Brahmā who was delighted with his penance came to him and said, “O excellent one among Asuras, tell me, what you wish to acquire by means of penance?”

## \|\| 2.29.13-14 \|\|

*brahmāṇamāha daityastu nirmṛtyutvamahaṃ vṛṇe \|*  
*brahmovāca \|*  
*na kaścicca vinā mṛtyuṃ jaṃturāsura vidyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yatastato'pi daityeṃdra mṛtyuḥ prāpyaḥ śarīriṇā \|*  
*ityuktastaṃ tathetyāha tuṣṭaḥ kamalasaṃbhavam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The Daitya said to Brahmā, “I choose exemption from death.”

## \|\| 2.29.15 \|\|

*rūpasya parivarto me yadā syātpadmasaṃbhava \|*  
*tadā mṛtyurmama bhavedanyathā tvamaro hyaham \|\| 15 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

O Asura, there is no living creature without death. O lord of Daityas, an embodied being has to meet with his death from one cause or other.

On being told thus, the lion-like Daitya spoke thus to the Lotus-born Lord:

15\. “When my form is changed, O Lotus-born Lord, let my death take place. Otherwise, I should be immortal.”

## \|\| 2.29.16 \|\|

*ityuktastaṃ tathetyāha tuṣṭaḥ kamalasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*ityukto'maratāṃ mene daityarājyasthito'suraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On being told thus, the delighted Lotus-born Lord said, “So be it”. On being told thus, the Asura, established in the kingdom of Daityas, considered it to be immortality itself.

## \|\| 2.29.17 \|\|

*ājagāma sa ca sthānaṃ tadā tripuraghātinaḥ \|*  
*āgato dadṛśe taṃ ca vīrakaṃ dvāryavasthitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He came to the abode of the Slayer of the Tripuras. On arrival, he saw Vīraka stationed at the entrance.

## \|\| 2.29.18 \|\|

*taṃ cāsau vaṃcayitvā ca āḍiḥ sarpaśarīrabhṛt \|*  
*avārito vīrakeṇa praviveśa harāṃtikam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Āḍi assumed the form of a serpent and deceived him. Unhindered by Vīraka, he entered the place near Hara.

## \|\| 2.29.19 \|\|

*bhujaṃgarūpaṃ saṃtyajya babhūvātha mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*umārūpī chalayituṃ giriśaṃ mūḍhacetanaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He forsook the form of the serpent. Deluded in his mind, the great Asura, in the guise of Umā, wanted to deceive Giriśa.

## \|\| 2.29.20-21 \|\|

*kṛtvomāyāstato rūpamapratarkyamanoharam \|*  
*sarvāvayavasaṃpūrṇaṃ sarvābhijñānasaṃvṛtam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*cakre bhagāṃtare daityo daṃtānvajropamāndṛḍhān \|*  
*tīkṣṇāgrānbuddhimohena giriśaṃ haṃtumudyataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. He assumed the form of Uraā, very exquisite and unbelievably beautiful. It was perfect in every limb and it contained many signs and symbols of recognition (of being Umā). On account of the delusion of his intellect, he attempted to kill Giriśa. For that purpose the Daitya had kept within the vaginal passage some hard adamantine teeth with sharp points.

## \|\| 2.29.22-25 \|\|

*kṛtvomārūpamevaṃ sa sthito daityo harāṃtike \|*  
*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā giriśastuṣuṭaḥ samāliṃgya mahāsuram \|\| 22 \|\|*

*manyamāno girisutāṃ sarvai ravayavāṃtaraiḥ \|*  
*apṛcchatsādhu te bhāvo giriputrī hyakṛtrimā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yā tvaṃ madaśayaṃ jñātvā prāpteha varavarṇini \|*  
*tvayā virahitaḥ śūnyaṃ manyosminbhuvanatraye \|\| 24 \|\|*

*prāptā prasannā yā tvaṃ māṃ yuktamevaṃvidhaṃ tvayi \|*  
*ityukte gūhayaṃśceṣṭāmumārūpyasuro'bravīt \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25. After assuming the form of Umā thus, the Daitya stationed himself near Hara. On seeing that great Asura, Giriśa was delighted and he embraced him thinking him to be the daughter of the Mountain (due to similarity) in every limb. He asked him (her), “Oh, your feelings are perfectly genuine. You are not a fake (i.e. impersonation of the) daughter of the Mountain. O lady of excellent complexion, you have understood my desire and come here. Separated from you, I feel all the three worlds a void. You have come back to me in a delighted (mood). This is but proper.”

On being told thus, the Asura in the guise of Umā concealed his activities and spoke:

## \|\| 2.29.26 \|\|

*yātāsmi tapasaścartuṃ kālīvākyāttavātulam \|*  
*ratiśca tatra me nābhūttataḥ prāptā tavāṃtikam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “I went away to perform penance at your calling me ‘Kālī’ (black). But I did not have any pleasure in the same. Therefore, I have come near you.”

## \|\| 2.29.27-32 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ śaṃkaraḥ śaṃkāṃ kiṃcitprāpyavadhārayat \|*  
*kupitā mayi tanvaṃgī pratyakṣā ca dṛḍhavratā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*aprāptakāmā saṃprāptā kimetatsaṃśayo mama \|*  
*rahasīti viciṃtyātha abhijñānādvicārayan \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nāpaśyadvāmapārśve tu tasyāṃkaṃ padmalakṣaṇam \|*  
*lomnāmāvartacaritaṃ tato devaḥ pinākadhṛk \|\| 29 \|\|*

*buddhā tāṃ dānavīṃ māyāṃ kiṃcitprahasitānanaḥ \|*  
*meḍhre raudrāstramādhāya cakre daityamanoratham \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sa rudanbhairavājrāvānavasādaṃ gato'suraḥ \|*  
*abudhyadvīrako naitadasureṃdraniṣūdanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*hate ca mārutenāśugāminā nagadevatā \|*  
*aparicchinnatattvārthā śailaputryāṃ nyavedayat \|\| 32 \|\|*

27-32- On being told thus, Śaṅkara had some doubt and he thought thus: ‘The lady of slender body became angry with me directly. She is steadfast in holy observances. But without realizing her desired object, she has came back. What is this? I am doubtful about it.’ He thought this in secret. Then he thought about the various signs of recognition. He did not see the scar in the shape of a lotus on the left side, nor the curly hair over the folded skin. Thereupon the Pināka-bearing Lord understood that it was the magical deception of the Dānava. With a slight smile on his face, he fixed the terrible Rudra missile in his penis and did everything to fulfil the desire of the Daitya. The Asura cried aloud making (piteous and) terrible shrieks. He became utterly dead.

Vīraka did not know about this killing of the leading Asura. When the Daitya was killed, the deity of the Mountain was informed of the fact by the Wind-god, that went there quickly. She intimated this to the daughter of the Mountain.

## \|\| 2.29.33 \|\|

*śrutvā vāyumukhāddevī krodharaktātilocanā \|*  
*apasyadvīrakaṃ putraṃ hṛdayena vidūyatā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The goddess heard the same from the Wind-god. Due to anger, her eyes became excessively red. She saw her son Vīraka with an afflicted heart.

## \|\| 2.29.34-35 \|\|

*mātaraṃ māṃ parityajya yasmāttvaṃ snehavihvalām \|*  
*vihitāvasaraḥ strīṇāṃ śaṃkarasya rahovidhau \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tasmātte paruṣā rūkṣā jaḍā hṛdaya varjitā \|*  
*gaṇeśākṣarasadṛśā śilā mātā bhaviṣyati \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. “You have abandoned me, your mother, agitated due to affection. Thereby you provided an opportunity for women (to go in) for Śaṅkara’s secret activities. Hence your (?) mother will be rough, hard, insentient, devoid of heart, rock and similar to the syllables Gaṇeśa (Gaṇeśākṣarasadṛśa?)

## \|\| 2.29.36 \|\|

*evamutsṛṣṭaśāpāyā giriputryāstvanaṃtaram \|*  
*nirjagāma mukhātkrodhaḥ siṃharūpī mahābalaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. When the daughter of the Mountain uttered this curse, (her) anger came out of her mouth in the form of a lion of great strength.

## \|\| 2.29.37-40 \|\|

*paścāttāpaṃ samaśritya tayā devyā visarjitaḥ \|*  
*sa tu siṃhaḥ karālāsyo mahākesarakaṃdharaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*proddhūtabalalāṃgūladaṃṣṭrotkaṭa guhāmukhaḥ \|*  
*vyāvṛtāsyo lalajjihvaḥ kṣāmakukṣiścikhādiṣuḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tasyāsye vartituṃ devī vyavasyata satī tadā \|*  
*jñātvā manogataṃ tasyā bhagavāṃścaturānanaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*ājagāmāśramapaṃda saṃpadāmāśrayaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*āgamyovāca tāṃ brahmā girijāṃ mṛṣṭayā girā \|\| 40 \|\|*

37-40. Afterwards the goddess regretted and let off the lion of terrible jaw with great mane round the neck. He continued to shake his strong tail. His mouth was fierce like a cave with terrible curved teeth. The tongue was lolling from the gaping mouth. His belly was thin (in size). He was desirous of eating.

Then the chaste gentle lady endeavoured to be stationed (i.e. enter) in its mouth.

After realizing the mental inclination of the goddess, the Four-faced Lord came to the hermitage that was an abode of riches. After coming, Brahmā spoke to Girijā in polished speech:

## \|\| 2.29.41 \|\|

*kiṃ devī prāptukāmāsi kimalabhyaṃ dadāmi te \|*  
*tacchrutvovāca girijā gurugauravagarbhitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “O goddess, what are you desirous of obtaining? What rare thing can I give you?”

On hearing it, the daughter of the Mountain said with due reverence to elders:

## \|\| 2.29.42-43 \|\|

*tapasā duṣkareṇāptaḥ patitve śaṃkaro mayā \|*  
*sa māṃ śyāmalavarṇeti bahuśaḥ proktavānbhavaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*syāmahaṃ kāṃcanākārā vāllabhyena ca saṃyutā \|*  
*bharturbhūtapateraṃge hyekato nirviśaṃkitā \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. “Śaṅkara has been obtained by me through the extremely difficult process of penance, as my husband. Bhava called me many times ‘black-complexioned one’. I shall be golden-complexioned with his love secured. I must be able to be on one side of the Lord of goblins, my husband, without any hesitation, whatsoever.”

## \|\| 2.29.44 \|\|

*tasyāstadbhāṣitaṃ śrutvā provāca jalajāsanaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ bhavatu bhūyastvaṃ bharturdehārdhadhāriṇī \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On hearing her words, the Lotus-seated Lord spoke: “Let it be so. Further you will be the occupant of half of the body of your husband.”

## \|\| 2.29.45-46 \|\|

*tatastasyāḥ śarīrāttu strī sunīlāṃbujatviṣā \|*  
*nirgatā sābhavadbhīmā ghaṃṭāhastā trilocanā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*nānābharaṇapūrṇāṃgī pītakauśeyavāsinī \|*  
*tāmabravīttato brahmā devīṃ nīlāṃbujatviṣam \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. There upon a lady of the bright lustre of a blue lotus came out of her body. She was very terrible. She had three eyes. She had a bell in her hand. There were many kinds of ornaments covering (i.e. decorating) (her) limbs. She had put on a yellow silken robe. Thereupon, Brahmā spoke to the goddess of the lustre of the blue lotus:

## \|\| 2.29.47-50 \|\|

*asmādbhūdharajā radehasaṃparkāttvaṃ mamājñayā \|*  
*saṃprāptā kṛtakṛtyatvamekānaṃśā purākṛtiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ya eṣa siṃhaḥ prodbhūto devyāḥ krodhādvarānane \|*  
*sa testu vāhano devī ketau cāstu mahābalaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*gaccha viṃdhyācale tatra surakāryaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*atra śuṃbhaniśuṃbhau ca hatvā tārakasainyapau \|\| 49 \|\|*

*pāṃcālonāma yakṣo'yaṃ yakṣalakṣapadānugaḥ \|*  
*dattaste kiṃkaro devī mahāmāyāśatairyutaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

47-50. “At my bidding and through the contact of the body of this daughter of the Mountain, you have attained blessedness of satisfaction, You are single (entire) without parts(?) You have the previous form(?).

Let this lion that has come out of the anger of the goddess, O lady of excellent face, be your powerful vehicle as well as the emblem in your flag. Go to the Vindhya mountain. There you will perform the task of Devas, after killing Śuṃbha and Niśuṃbha, the commanders of the army of Tāraka. This Yakṣa, named Pāñcāla, has been given to you, O goddess, as your servant. He has a hundred thousand Yakṣas as his followers and attendants. He has hundreds of great Māyās.”

## \|\| 2.29.51-59 \|\|

*ityuktā kauśikī devī tatetyāha pitāmaham \|*  
*nirgatāyāṃ ca kauśikyāṃ jātā svairāśritā guṇaiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*sarvaiḥ pūrvabhavopāttaistadā svayamupastitaiḥ \|*  
*umāpi prāptasaṃkalpā paścāttāpaparāyaṇā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*muhuḥ svaṃ pariniṃdaṃtī jagāma giriśāṃtikam \|*  
*saṃprayāṃtīṃ ca tāṃ dvārī apavārya samāhitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*rurodha vīrako devīṃ hemavetralatādharaḥ \|*  
*tāmuvāca ca kopena tiṣṭha tiṣṭha kva yāsi ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

*prayojanaṃ na te'stīha gaccha yāvanna bhartsyase \|*  
*devyā rūpadharo daityo devaṃ vaṃcayituṃ tviha \|\| 55 \|\|*

*praviṣṭo na ca dṛṣṭo'sau sa ca devena ghātitaḥ \|*  
*ghātite cāhamākṣipto nīlakaṇṭhena dhīmatā \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kāpi strī nāpi moktavyā tvayā putreti sādaram \|*  
*tasmāttvamatra dvāristhā varṣapūgānyanekaśaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyasi na cāpyatra praveśaṃ lapsyase vraja \|*  
*ekā me praviśedatra mātā yā snehavatsalā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*nagādhirājatanayā pārvatī rudravallabhā \|*  
*ityuktā tu tato devī ciṃtayāmāsa cetasā \|\| 59 \|\|*

51-59. On being told thus, the goddess Kauśikī said to Brahmā, “Let it be so.” After Kauśikī had gone, all the good qualities that she had acquired in her previous birth, came to her by themselves. They resorted to her.

After realizing her ambitious desire, Umā regretted the same. Censuring herself, she went near Giriśa. As she was going in, Vīraka who held a gold (-topped) staff, stopped her with great care. He said to her angrily, “Stop. Stop. Where are you going? You have no business here. Go away, lest I should rebuke you. A Daitya who had assumed the form of the goddess, entered (this abode) in order to deceive the Lord. He was not seen (by me). He was killed by the Lord. After he had been killed, I was rebuked by the intelligent Nīlakaṇṭha. I have been commanded earnestly: ‘Dear son, nobody should be allowed to go in by you.’ Hence, even if you were to be standing at the entrance for many years, you will not gain entry. Go away, only one shall enter (this abode) (i.e.) my mother who is very affectionate towards me. She is the daughter of the Lord of Mountains, Pārvatī, the beloved of Rudra.”

On being told thus, the goddess thought in her mind:

## \|\| 2.29.60-62 \|\|

*na sā nārī tu daityo'sau vāyornaivāvabāsata \|*  
*vṛthaiva vīrakaḥ śapto mayā krodhaparītayā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*akāryaṃ kriyate mūḍhaiḥ prāyaḥ krodhasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*krodhena naśyate kīrtiḥ krodho haṃti sthirāṃ śriyam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*aparicchinnasarvārthā putraṃ śāpitavatyaham \|*  
*viparītārthaboddhṝṇāṃ sulabhā vipado yataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

60-62. ‘Oh, that was not a woman! It had been a Daitya! The Wind-god did not see him clearly. In vain was Vīraka cursed by me, overwhelmed by anger. What should not be done is being done generally by the deluded (stupid) persons overwhelmed by anger. Reputation is destroyed by anger; Anger destroys stable prosperity and glory. Without understanding all the facts I cursed my son. Mishaps easily befall those who misunderstand facts.’

## \|\| 2.29.63 \|\|

*saṃciṃtyaivamuvācedaṃ vīrakaṃ prati śailajā \|*  
*adho lajjāvikāreṇa vadanenāṃbujatviṣā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. After thinking thus, the daughter of the Mountain had her face lowered due to shame, her face that had the lustre of lotus. She spoke to Vīraka thus:

## \|\| 2.29.64 \|\|

*ahaṃ vīraka te mātā mā te'stu manaso bhramaḥ \|*  
*śaṃkarasyāsmi dayitā sutā tu himabhūbhṛtaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. “Q Vīraka, I am your mother. Let not your mind be confused. I am the beloved wife of Śaṅkara, the daughter of Himālaya mountain.

## \|\| 2.29.65 \|\|

*mama gātrasthitibhrāṃtyā mā śaṃkāṃ putra bhāvaya \|*  
*tuṣṭena gauratā dattā mameyaṃ padmayoninā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O son, do not entertain any doubt because of your error in noting the present state of my body. This whiteness of ray complexion has been granted to me by the Lotus-born Lord who had been propitiated.

## \|\| 2.29.66 \|\|

*mayā śapto'syavidite vṛttāṃte daityanirmite \|*  
*jñātvā nārīpraveśaṃ tu śaṃkare rahasi stite \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. You have been cursed by me because the events brought about by the Daitya had not been known. It was thought that a woman entered (the place) while Śaṅkara was seated there alone.

## \|\| 2.29.67 \|\|

*na nivartayituṃ śakyaḥ śāpaḥ kiṃ tu bravīmi te \|*  
*mānuṣyāṃ tu śilāyāṃ tvaṃ śilādātsaṃbhaviṣyasi \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. It is impossible to revoke the curse, but I shall tell you this. You will be born of Śilāda in a rock of human shape.

## \|\| 2.29.68-73 \|\|

*puṇye cāpyarbudāraṇye svargamokṣaprade nṛṇām \|*  
*acaleśvaraliṃgaṃ tu vartate yatra vīraka \|\| 68 \|\|*

*vārāṇasyāṃ viśvanāthasamaṃ tatphaladaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*prabhāsasya ca yātrābhirdaśabhiryatphalaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tadekayātrayā proktamarbudasya mahāgireḥ \|*  
*yatra taptvā tapo martyā dehadhātūnvihāya ca \|\| 70 \|\|*

*saṃsārī na punarbhūyānmaheśvaravaco yathā \|*  
*arbudo yadi labhyeta sevituṃ janmaduḥkhitaiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*vārāṇasīṃ ca kedāraṃ kiṃ smaraṃti vṛthaiva te \|*  
*tatrārādhya bhavaṃ devaṃ bhavānnandīti nāmabhṛt \|\| 72 \|\|*

*śīghrameṣyasi cātraiva pratīhāratvamāpsyasi \|*  
*evamukte hṛṣṭaromā vīrakaḥ praṇipatya tām \|\| 73 \|\|*

68-73. In the holy forest of Arbudāraṇya which yields heavenly pleasures and liberation unto men, O Vīraka, there is the Liṅga called Acaleśvaraliṅga. It yields the same benefit unto men as the Viśvanātha liṅga at Vārāṇasī. Its benefit is equivalent to that of ten pilgrimages to Prabhāsa. It is said that by taking one trip to the great mountain Arbuda, the same can be acquired. By performing penance in this place and by casting off the essential ingredients of the body (i.e. by dying) in this place, men will never become Saṃsārin (i.e. subjected to births and deaths), as Maheśvara himself has uttered. If (a pilgrimage to) Arbuda could be (performed) by persons who are miserable due to frequent births and they can resort to it, why should they remember Vārāṇasī and Kedāra? It is not necessary. There you shall propitiate Lord Bhava. Bearing the name Nandin, you will come here quickly and will attain the status of gatekeeper.”
