*sevinastvāṃ prarohaṃtu bharitā vividhaiḥ phalaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. May the celestial trees beginning with Kalpaka growing in the divine gardens, serve you and thereby grow laden with different kinds of fruits.

## \|\| 3.2.35 \|\|

*divyauṣadhigaṇāssarve siṃhādyā mṛgajātayaḥ \|*  
*praśāṃtāḥ parivarttaṃtā pāpakalmaṣanāśanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Let the groups of the celestial medicinal herbs (be so). Let the animal species beginning with lions become calm and move about. Let there be washing off of the dirt of sins.

## \|\| 3.2.36 \|\|

*ayanadvayabhinnena gamanenāpi saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*na laṃghayiṣyati raviḥ śṛṃgaṃ liṃgatanostava \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Though he has two different types of transit, the Sun will not transgress your peak while you are in the form of a Liṅga.

## \|\| 3.2.37 \|\|

*divya duṃdubhiśaṃkhānāṃ ghoṣaiḥ puṣpaughavṛṣṭibhiḥ \|*  
*sevito bhava deva tvamapsaronṛtyagītibhiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Lord, be served through the dances and songs of celestial damsels, the sounds of the divine Dundubhi drums and conchs and showers of flowers.

## \|\| 3.2.38 \|\|

*amaratvaṃ ca siddhatvaṃ rasasiddhīśca nirvṛtim \|*  
*labhaṃtāṃ mānuṣā nityaṃ tvatsaṃnidhimupāgatāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Let the human beings who come to your presence, obtain immortality, Siddhahood, skill in alchemy and extreme bliss.

## \|\| 3.2.39 \|\|

*īśatvaṃ ca vaśitvaṃ ca saubhāgyaṃ kālavaṃcanam \|*  
*tvāmāśritya narāssarve labhaṃtāmaruṇācala \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O Aruṇācala, may all men resorting to you obtain Īśitva (i.e. mastery over everything), Vaśitva (he. ability to win over others), Saubhāgya (i.e. good fortune) and Kālavañcana (i.e. ability to defy death).

## \|\| 3.2.40 \|\|

*sarvāvayavadānena sarvavyādhivināśanāt \|*  
*sarvābhīṣṭapradānena dṛśyo bhava mahītale \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Be visible on the earth through blessings granting all limbs, destroying all ailments and bestowing everything desired.”

## \|\| 3.2.41 \|\|

*tatheti varadaṃ devamaruṇādripatiṃ śivam \|*  
*praṇamya kamalānāthaḥ prārthayannidamabravīt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The Lord of Kamalā (i.e. Viṣṇu) too prayed in the same manner to Lord Śiva, the bestower of boons, the Lord of the Aruṇa mountain. He bowed down and spoke thus:

## \|\| 3.2.42 \|\|

*prasīda karuṇāpūrṇa śoṇaśaileśvara prabho \|*  
*maheśa sarvalokānāṃ hitāya prakaṭodaya \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. “Be pleased, O Lord of Śoṇa-Śaila (i.e. Aruṇācala), full of mercy. O Maheśa, you have manifested yourself for the sake of the welfare of all the worlds.

## \|\| 3.2.43 \|\|

*yadāhaṃ tvāmupāśritya jagadrakṣaṇadakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*śrīpatitvamanuprāptastadā bhaktā bhavaṃtu te \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Just as I, by resorting to you, became capable of protecting the universe and acquired the husbandhood of Lakṣmī, so also let your devotees be so.

## \|\| 3.2.44 \|\|

*nālpapuṇyairupāsyeta tvadrūpaṃ mahadadbhutam \|*  
*mayā ca brahmaṇā caivamadṛṣṭapadaśekharaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Your great and wonderful form cannot be adored by the persons of insufficient merits, O Lord whose foot and crest have not been seen by me and by Brahmā.

## \|\| 3.2.45 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇānamaskārairnṛtyagītaiśca pūjanaiḥ \|*  
*tvāmarcayaṃti ye martyāḥ kṛtārthāste gatāṃhasaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Those men who worship you by means of circumambulations, obeisances, dances, songs and adorations are blessed with all their sins gone.

## \|\| 3.2.46 \|\|

*upavāsairvrataiḥ satrairupahāraistathārcanaiḥ \|*  
*tvāmarcayaṃti manujāḥ sārvabhaumā bhavaṃtu te \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Let those human beings who worship you by observing fasts, performing holy rites, sacrifices, offerings as well as adorations, become emperors.

## \|\| 3.2.47 \|\|

*ārāmaṃ maṃḍapaṃ cāpi kūpaṃ vidhiviśodhanam \|*  
*kurvatāmaruṇādrīśa saṃnidhāne punarbhava \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Lord of Aruṇācala, be in the vicinity of those who build and maintain parks, platforms, sacrificial halls and wells for freedom from adverse fate.

## \|\| 3.2.48-50 \|\|

*aṃgapradakṣiṇaṃ kurvannaṣṭaiśvaryasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*aśeṣapātakaiḥ sadyo vimukto nirmalāśayaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*āvāmapyavimuṃcaṃtau sadā tvatpādapaṃkajam \|*  
*dhyātavyaṃ manujaiḥ sarvaistava saṃnidhimāgataiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tathāstviti varaṃ dattvā viṣṇave caṃdraśekharaḥ \|*  
*bharuṇācalarūpeṇa prāptaḥ sthāvaraliṃgatām \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. May a man who circumambulates you rolling on the ground, become endowed with all the eight Aiśvaryas (‘superhuman powers’). Let him be immediately liberated from all sins. Let him be pure in mind. Let us both not leave off your lotuslike feet that should be meditated upon by all men who come to your vicinity.”

After granting the boon saying “So be it” to Viṣṇu, the Moon-crested Lord assumed the state of an immobile Liṅga in the form of Aruṇācala.

## \|\| 3.2.51 \|\|

*taijasaṃ liṃgametaddhi sarvalokaikakāraṇam \|*  
*aruṇādririti khyātaṃ dṛśyate vasudhātale \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Indeed this Liṅga which is well-known as Aruṇādri and is seen on the surface of the earth, is Taijasa (i.e. of fiery or effulgent nature) and the sole cause of all the worlds.

## \|\| 3.2.52 \|\|

*yugāṃtasamaye kṣubdhaiścaturbhirapi sāgaraiḥ \|*  
*api nirmagnalokāṃtairaspṛṣṭāṃtikabhūtalam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The ground near it is not at all touched by the four oceans that become agitated at the close of the Yuga and that have the extremities of the worlds submerged in them.

## \|\| 3.2.53 \|\|

*gajapramāṇaiḥ pṛṣataiḥ pūrayaṃto jagattrayam \|*  
*puṣkarādyā mahāmeghā viśrāṃtā yasya sānuni \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The great clouds beginning with Puṣkara fill the three worlds with drops of water of the size of elephants. They take rest on its ridge.

## \|\| 3.2.54 \|\|

*pravṛtte bhūtasaṃhāre prakṛtau pratisaṃcare \|*  
*bhaviṣyatsarvabījāni niṣeduryatra niścayam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. When the annihilation of all living beings takes place, when all created things are reabsorbed into Prakṛti, all the future seeds are certainly deposited there.

## \|\| 3.2.55 \|\|

*mayā cāhūyamānebhyaḥ pralayānaṃtaraṃ punaḥ \|*  
*yatpādaseviviprebhyo vedādhyayanasaṃgrahaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Brāhmaṇas who resort to the foot of that mountain are called again by me (i.e. Brahmā) after the deluge and I make them study the Vedas and make the collections thereof.

## \|\| 3.2.56 \|\|

*sarvāsāmapi vidyānāṃ kalānāṃ śāstrasaṃpadām \|*  
*āgamānāṃ ca vedānāṃ yatra satyavyavasthitiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. All the lores, arts, wealth of scriptures, Āgamas and the Vedas are truthfully well arranged there.

## \|\| 3.2.57 \|\|

*yadguhāgahvarāṃtassthā munayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ \|*  
*jaṭinaḥ saṃprakāśaṃte koṭisūryāgnitejasaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Sages of well-praised holy observances and rites, who abide within the caves of that mountain, shine with their matted hair. They have the refulgence of a crore of suns and fires.

## \|\| 3.2.58 \|\|

*paṃcabrahmamayairmaṃtraiḥ paṃcākṣaravapurdharaiḥ \|*  
*akārapīṭhikārūḍho nādātmā yaḥ sadāśivaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Sadāśiva who is of the nature of Nāda (i.e. the divine sound) is seated on the Akārapīṭhikā (i.e. the pedestal of the letter ‘A’) along with the five Vedic Mantras that assume the forms of the five syllables (i.e. namaḥ śivāya).

## \|\| 3.2.59 \|\|

*aṣṭabhiśca sadā liṃgairaṣṭadikpālapūjitaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamūrttitayā yo'yamaṣṭasiddhipradāyakaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. He is worshipped by the Guardians of the eight quarters always by means of the eight Liṅgas.

Having the eight physical forms,\[2\] he bestows the eight Siddhis (‘superhuman powers’).

## \|\| 3.2.60 \|\|

*yatra siddhāstathā lokānsvānsvānmuktvā sureśvarāḥ \|*  
*apekṣaṃte sthitā muktiṃ vihāya kanakācalam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Siddhas leave off their own respective worlds and leading Suras abandon the Meru mountain and stay there (i.e. in Aruṇācala) waiting for their salvation.

## \|\| 3.2.61 \|\|

*evaṃ vasuṃdharāpuṇyaparipākasamuccayaḥ \|*  
*aruṇādririti khyāto bhaktabhaktivarapradaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thus the entire collection of the ultimate fruits of all the merits of the earth is well-known as Aruṇācala. It yields devotion to devotees as a boon.

## \|\| 3.2.62 \|\|

*kailāsānmeruśikharādāgatairdevasaṃcayaiḥ \|*  
*pūjyate śoṇaśailātmā śaṃbhuḥ sarvavarapradaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Śaṃbhu, the bestower of all boons, of the nature of Śoṇaśaila (i.e. Aruṇācala) is worshipped by the groups of Devas coming from Kailāsa and the summit of Meru.

## \|\| 3.2.63 \|\|

*iti kamalajavaktrapadmajāṃ taṃ muditamanāḥ sanako niśamya bhaktyā \|*  
*viracitavinayaḥ praṇamya putraḥ pitaramapṛcchadaśeṣavedasāram \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. After hearing devoutly these words orally transmitted by the Lotus-born Lord, Śaṅkara became delighted in his mind. The son humbly bowed down to the father and asked him the essence of the Veda.

## Chapter 3 - Pārvatī Goes to Kāñcī for Penance

## \|\| 3.3.1 \|\|

*sanaka uvāca \|*  
*bhagavannaruṇādrīśa māhātmyamidamadbhutam \|*  
*śrutaṃ śivaprasādena dayayā te jagadguroḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanaka said:

1\. O Lord, this wonderful greatness of the Lord of Aruṇācala has been heard by Śiva’s grace as well as the favour shown by you, the preceptor of the universe.

## \|\| 3.3.2 \|\|

*āścaryametanmāhātmyaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam \|*  
*ārādhayanpunaḥ ke vā varadaṃ śoṇaparvatam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. This greatness is very wonderful. It is conducive to the destruction of all sins. Who are those who worshipped and propitiated the Śoṇa mountain, the bestower of boons?

## \|\| 3.3.3 \|\|

*anādiraṃtarahitaḥ śivaḥ śoṇacalākṛtiḥ \|*  
*yuvayostapasā deva varadānāya saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Śiva who has neither the beginning nor the end, has assumed the form of Śoṇācala. O "Lord, it is on account of the penance of you both that he has been abiding here for offering boons.

## \|\| 3.3.4 \|\|

*sakṛtsaṃkīrtite nāmni śoṇādririti muktide \|*  
*sannidhiḥ sarvakāmānāṃ jāyate cāghanāśanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When the name Śoṇādri that yields salvation is uttered even once, all the desired objects come to one’s presence. It is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 3.3.5-9 \|\|

*śivaśabdāmṛtāsvādaḥ śivārcanakathākramaḥ \|*  
*iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā devadevaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*uvāca karuṇāmūrtiraruṇādrīśamānaman \|*  
*brahmovāca \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ vatsa pārvatyāścaritaṃ yatpurātanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*aruṇādrīśamāśritya yathā sā nirvṛtābhavat \|*  
*āsasāda mahādevaḥ kadācitpārvatīpatiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ratnasiṃhāsanaṃ divyaṃ ratnatoraṇasaṃyutam \|*  
*ratnapuṣpaphalopeta kalpadrumamanoharam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*parārdhya dṛṣadāstīrṇaṃ baddhamuktāvitānakam \|*  
*vimuktapuṣpaprakaradivyadhūporusaurabham \|\| 9 \|\|*

5a. The word Śiva has the taste of nectar. Let the procedure of the worship of Śiva and the story thereof (be described).

5b-6a. On hearing these words, Brahmā, the Lord of Devas, who is Mercy itself incarnate, spoke after bowing down to the Lord of Aruṇācala.

Brahmā said:

6b-9. O dear one, let the ancient legend of Pārvatī, how she resorted to the Lord of Aruṇācala and became happy, be heard.

Once Mahādeva, the Lord of Pārvatī, came to his divine gem-set throne fitted with festoons. It was as charming as the Kalpa-tree laden with gems as its fruit and flowers. It was covered with precious stones. It had a canopy bedecked with pearls. It was full of fragrance due to the clusters and nosegays of flowers and divine incense.

## \|\| 3.3.10 \|\|

*pralaṃbamālikājālaninadadbhṛṃgasaṃkulam \|*  
*divyatūryaghanārāvapranṛtyadguhavāhanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Swarms of bees from the hanging clusters of garlands hummed and hovered around it. The vehicle of Guha (i.e. the peacock) danced (near it) at the sound of the divine instruments of music, taking it for the sound of thunder.

## \|\| 3.3.11-12 \|\|

*pārvatīsiṃhasaṃcāraparitrastamahāgajam \|*  
*apsarobhiḥ pranarttābhirgāyaṃtībhiśca kevalam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*āsevitapuroraṃgaṃ dikpālakaniṣevitam \|*  
*ṛgyajuḥsāmajairmaṃtraiḥ stuvadbhirmunipuṃgavaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Great elephants were afraid as the lion of Pārvatī moved (up and down). The stage (i.e. space) in front of it was resorted to exclusively by the dancing and singing celestial damsels. It was frequented by the Guardians of the Quarters. It was surrounded by prominent ascetics and Brāhmaṇa sages eulogizing (the Lord) with Mantras (selected) from the Ṛg(-), Yajur(-) and Sāma-Vedas and by gods, Siddhas and saintly kings.

## \|\| 3.3.13-33 \|\|

*brahmarṣibhistathā devaiḥ siddhai rājarṣibhivṛtam \|*  
*gaṇaiśca vividhākārairbhasmālaṃkṛtavigrahaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*rudrākṣadhārasubhagairāpūrṇaṃ śivatatparaiḥ \|*  
*vīṇāveṇumṛdaṃgāditauryatrikajanisvanaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ghaṃṭāṭaṃkārasubhagairvedadhvanivimiśritaiḥ \|*  
*manoharaṃ mahādivyamāsanaṃ pārvatīsakhaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*alaṃcakāra bhagavanbhaktānugrahakāmyayā \|*  
*āsthāya vimalaṃ rūpaṃ sarvatejomayaṃ śivam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*aṃbikāsahitaḥ śrīmānvijahāra dayānidhiḥ \|*  
*saṃgītena kathābhedairdyūtakrīḍāvikalpanaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*gaṇānāṃ vikaṭairnṛtyai ramayāmāsa pārvatīm \|*  
*visṛjya sakalāndevānṛṣīṃścāpi sabhāsadaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*varānpradāya vividhānbhaktalokāya vāñchitān \|*  
*āgameṣu vicitreṣu sarvartukusumeṣu ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vijahāromayā sārddhaṃ ratnaprāsādapaṃktiṣu \|*  
*vāpikāsu manojñāsu ratnasopānapaṃktiṣu \|\| 20 \|\|*

*keliparvataśṛṃgeṣu hemaraṃbhāvanāṃtare \|*  
*gaṃgātaraṃgaśītena phullapaṃkajagaṃdhinā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vātena maṃdagatinā vihāravihataśramaḥ \|*  
*svakāmataḥ svayaṃ devaḥ preyasīmabhyanandayat \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ratirūpāṃ śivāṃ devīṃ sarvasaubhāgyasundarīm \|*  
*kadācidrahasi prītā nijājñāvaśavarttinam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*ramaṇaṃ jānatī mugdhā paścādabhyetya sādaram \|*  
*karābhyāṃ kamalābhābhyāṃ triṇetrāṇi jagadguroḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*pidadhe līlayā śaṃbhoḥ kimetaditi kautukāt \|*  
*candrādityāgnirūpeṇa pihiteṣvakṣiṣu kramāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

*andhakāro'bhavattatra cirakālaṃ bhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*nimiṣārddhena devasya jagmurvatsarakoṭayaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*devīlīlāsamutthena tamasābhūjjagatkṣayaḥ \|*  
*tamasā pūritaṃ viśvamapāreṇa samantataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*śūnyaṃ jyotiḥ pracāreṇa vināśaṃ pratyapadyata \|*  
*na vyajṛṃbhata vibudhā na ca vedāścakāśire \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nāpi jīvāḥ samabhavannavyaktaṃ kevalaṃ sthitam \|*  
*jagatāmapi sarveṣāmakāle vīkṣya saṃkṣayam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tapasā labdhasphūrtīnāṃ vicāraḥ samapadyata \|*  
*kimetattamaso janma bhuvanakṣayakāraṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*bhagavānapi sarvātmā na nūnaṃ kālamākṣipat \|*  
*devī vinodarūpeṇa pidhatte purajiddṛśaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tenedamakhilaṃ jātaṃ nistejo bhuvanatrayam \|*  
*akālatamasā vyāpte sakale bhuvanatraye \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kā gatirlabdharājyānāṃ tapaso devajanmanām \|*  
*na yajñāḥ saṃpravartaṃte na pūjyante surā bhuvi \|\| 33 \|\|*

13-17a. It was filled with the Gaṇas of different forms and sizes, whose bodies were adorned with sacred ash. They appeared handsome as they wore Rudrākṣa beads and were devoted to Śiva. It was fascinating with the tinkling sound of bells and the sounds of three types of musical instruments such as lute, flute, drum etc., mixed with the sounds of Vedic Mantras. With a desire to bless devotees, the Lord, the consort of Pārvatī, graced the great divine seat. Adopting the pure and auspicious form full of splendour, the glorious Lord, the storehouse of mercy, sported along with Aṃbikā.

17b-23a. He delighted Pārvatī by means of music, diverse kinds of tales, different sorts of games at dice and the hideous dances of the Gaṇas. After bidding farewell to all the Devas, sages and the members of his court, and after granting different kinds of boons to devout people as desired by them, be sported about along with Umā in the parks of variegated and wonderful features abounding in flowers blossoming in all seasons, in rows and studded with gems and jewels; in the fascinating tanks with rows of steps studded with gems; on the peaks of the mountains of sports and pastime and in the groves of golden plantain trees. His fatigue due to these sports was dispelled by the gentle breeze that was cool (as it blew from) the waves of Gaṅgā and fragrant due to the full blown lotuses. In accordance with his desire, the Lord delighted goddess Śivā, his beloved one, the beautiful lady endowed with all felicity, the splendid one in the form of Rati.

23b-28a. The delighted goddess (like) a young girl of youthful simplicity, once thought her lover to be under her absolute control. So once, she went stealthily behind him. With her hands of lotus-like (tenderness and lustre) she sportingly closed the three eyes of Śaṃbhu, the sire of the world, just out of curiosity to know what it was.

When the eyes in the forms of the moon, the sun and the fire respectively were dosed, there appeared a terrible darkness of a very long duration. With half a moment of the Lord crores of (human) years passed by. The universe came to its destruction on account of the darkness caused by the playful sport of the goddess. The universe was filled all over with boundless darkness. Being deprived of the movement of the luminaries, the universe met with its destruction.

28b-33. Devas did not flourish nor did the Vedas shine. No living beings existed. Only the Uṇmanifest (i.e. Prakṛti) remained by itself.

On seeing this untimely destruction of the worlds, it occurred to those (venerable persons) who through their penance had gained a flash of inspiration in their minds: ‘(What) is the source of this darkness causing destruction of the worlds. Certainly, the Lord, the immanent soul of everyone, has not impelled the god of Death. Playfully the goddess has closed the eyes of the conqueror of Tripura. Therefore, the entire unit of the three worlds has become deprived of light. If the three worlds have been pervaded by untimely darkness, what course is left to those of divine origin (i.e. gods) who have acquired their realms by means of penance? Yajñas are not being performed on the earth. Suras are not being worshipped.’

## \|\| 3.3.34 \|\|

*iti niścitya manasā vīkṣya te jñānacakṣuṣā \|*  
*nityāste sūrayo bhaktyā śaṃbhumāgamya tuṣṭuvuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On determining this by their mental powers and observing this through their vision born of knowledge, those eternal Sūris (i.e. persons of spiritual wisdom) devoutly bowed down to Śaṃbhu and prayed:

## \|\| 3.3.35 \|\|

*namaḥ sarvajagatkartre śivāya paramātmane \|*  
*māyayā śaktirūpeṇa pṛthagbhāvamupeyuṣe \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. “Obeisance to Śiva, the Supreme Soul, the maker of the entire universe, who has assumed separate forms in the nature of Śaktis through Māyā.

## \|\| 3.3.36 \|\|

*avinābhāvinī śaktirādyaikā śivarūpiṇī \|*  
*līlayā jagadutpattirakṣāsaṃhṛtikāriṇī \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The inevitable one primordial Śakti in the form of Śiva is the cause of creation, sustenance and annihilation in a sportful manner.

## \|\| 3.3.37 \|\|

*ardhāṃgī sā tava deva śivaśaktyātmakaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*eka eva mahādevo na pare tvadvinā vibho \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. She is half of your body, O Lord, Your body is in the form of Śiva and Śakti. Mahādeva is one and only one (without a second). O Lord, without you none else exists.

## \|\| 3.3.38 \|\|

*līlayā tava lokoyamakāle pralayaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*karuṇā tava nirvyājā varddhatāṃ lokavarddhanī \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thanks to your sporting activity, this world has met with untimely destruction. May your genuine mercifulness making the worlds flourish, increase.

## \|\| 3.3.39 \|\|

*bhavato nimiṣārddhena tejasāmupasaṃhṛteḥ \|*  
*gatānyanekavarṣāṇi jagatāṃ nāśahetave \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Due to the withdrawal of lights for the duration of half a winking of yours, innumerable years of the worlds have gone by causing their destruction.

## \|\| 3.3.40 \|\|

*tataḥ prasīda karuṇāmūrtte kāla sadāśiva \|*  
*virama praṇayārabdhādamuṣmāllokasaṃkṣayāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Therefore, be pleased, O Sadāśiva, the embodiment of mercifulness; O Kāla (i.e. god of Death), stop this destruction of the worlds initiated through love’s sport.”

## \|\| 3.3.41 \|\|

*iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā bhaktānāṃ siddhiśālinām \|*  
*visṛjākṣoṇi gaurīti karuṇāmūrttirabravīt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. On hearing these words of those devotees endowed with Siddhis the Lord, the embodiment of mercifulness, said, “O Gaurī, leave off my eyes.”

## \|\| 3.3.42 \|\|

*visasarja ca sā devī pidhānaṃ haracakṣuṣām \|*  
*somasūryāgnirūpāṇāṃ prakāśamabhavajjagat \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The goddess desisted from continuing the closure of the eyes of Hara in the form of the moon, the sun and the fire. The universe became bright and brilliant.

## \|\| 3.3.43 \|\|

*kiyānkālo gataśceti pṛṣṭaiḥ siddhaiśca vai nataiḥ \|*  
*uktaṃ tvannimiṣārddhena jagmurvatsarakoṭayaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On being asked “How much time has passed?”, Siddhas bowed down and said, “Along with your half a winking crores of (human) years have elapsed.”

## \|\| 3.3.44 \|\|

*atha devaḥ kṛpāmūrttirālokya vihasanpriyām \|*  
*abravītparamodāraḥ paraṃ dharmārthasaṃgraham \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Looking smilingly at his beloved, the exceedingly liberal-minded Lord, the embodiment of mercy, spoke about a few points of great piety and righteousness:

## \|\| 3.3.45-47 \|\|

*avicārya kṛtaṃ mugdhe bhuvanakṣayakāraṇāt \|*  
*ayuktamiha paśyāmi jaganmātustavaiva hi \|\| 45 \|\|*

*ahamapyakhilāṃllokānsaṃhariṣyāmi saṃkṣaye \|*  
*prāpte kāle tvayā maugdhyādakāle pralayaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*keyaṃ vā tvādṛśī kuryādīdṛśaṃ sadvigarhitam \|*  
*karma narmaṇyapi sadā kṛpāmūrtirna bādhate \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. “O pretty girl of youthful simplicity! You have done this thoughtlessly as it caused the destruction of the world. I regard it improper on your part, you being the mother of the universe. I too destroy all the worlds when the proper time of dissolution comes. On account of your immaturity the worlds have met with destruction at the most improper time.

Which lady (in a position) like you will commit this sort of improper action despised by good people, even for fun? A person who is an embodiment of sympathy and mercy does not harass (others).”

## \|\| 3.3.48 \|\|

*iti śambhorvacaḥ śrutvā dharmalopabhayākulā \|*  
*kiṃ kariṣyāmi tacchāṃtyā ityapṛcchatsma taṃ priyā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On hearing these words of Śaṃbhu she became agitated, because she was afraid of the loss of Dharma. The beloved wife of the Lord asked him, “What shall I do in order to countervail it?”

## \|\| 3.3.49 \|\|

*atha devaḥ prasannātmā vyājahāra dayānidhiḥ \|*  
*devyāstenānutāpena bhaktyā ca toṣitaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Being pleased at that repentance and devotion of the goddess, Lord Śiva, the storehouse of sympathy, spoke:

## \|\| 3.3.50 \|\|

*manmūrtestava keyaṃ vā prāyaścittirihocyate \|*  
*athāpi dharmamārgoyaṃ tvayaiva paripālyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. “You constitute my own person. Hence what expiation is to be suggested? Still, this path of virtue is being maintained by you.

## \|\| 3.3.51-52 \|\|

*śrutismṛtikriyākalpā vidyāśca vibudhādayaḥ \|*  
*tvadrūpametadakhilaṃ mahadarthosmi tanmayaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*mānyayābhinnayā devyā bhāvyaṃ lokasisṛkṣayā \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. (Defective Text) You are the embodiment of Śrutis, Smṛtis, holy rites, liturgical texts, lores, Devas and others. I am the great principle (?) and am identical with it. You, the goddess inseparable from me, should be one entertaining a desire for creating the worlds.

## \|\| 3.3.53 \|\|

*tasmāllokānurūpaṃ te prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate \|*  
*ṣaḍvidho gadito dharmaḥ śrutismṛtivicārataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Hence the expiatory rite for you is being laid down in the manner befitting the world.

After pondering over Śrutis and Smṛtis Dharma has been ascertained as of six types.

## \|\| 3.3.54 \|\|

*svāminā nānupālyeta yadi tyājyo'nujīvibhiḥ \|*  
*na tvāṃ vihāya śaknomi kṣaṇamapyāsituṃ kvacit \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. If it is not abided by the master it is likely to be abandoned by the dependents and followers. I am not able to stay anywhere even for a single moment after leaving you.

## \|\| 3.3.55 \|\|

*ahameva tapaḥ sarvaṃ kariṣyāmyātmani sthitaḥ \|*  
*pṛdhvī ca sakalā bhūyāttapasā saphalā tava \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. I myself shall perform the entire penance, stationed in the Ātman. The entire earth shall be fruitful through your penance.

## \|\| 3.3.56 \|\|

*tvatpādapadmasaṃsparśāttvattapodarśanādapi \|*  
*nirasyaṃti svasānnidhyādduṣṭajātamupadravam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. By the contact with your lotus-like feet and the sight of your penance and your own presence (the people) will dispel the trouble caused by defilement.

## \|\| 3.3.57-58 \|\|

*karmabhūmestvamādhikyahetave puṇyamācara \|*  
*tvattapaścaraṇaṃ loke vīkṣya sarvopi saṃtatam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*dharme dṛḍhatarā buddhiṃ nibadhnīyānna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kṛtārthayiṣyati mahīṃ dayā te dharmapālanaiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. Perform meritorious deeds for the uplift of the land of Karmans. On observing your austere rites in the world, all the people will have firmer inclination towards righteousness. There is no doubt about it. Your sympathy will make the earth contented and blessed through your activities in maintaining piety and virtuousness. You have been told about all these things, O gentle lady, by the eternal Vedas.

## \|\| 3.3.59-63 \|\|

*tvamevaitatsakalaṃ proktā vedairdevi sanātanaiḥ \|*  
*asti kāṃcīpurī khyātā sarvabhūtisamanvitā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*yā divaṃ devasaṃpūrṇā pratyakṣayati bhūtale \|*  
*yatra kṛtaṃ tapaḥ kiṃcidanaṃtaphalamucyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

*devāśca munayaḥ sarve vāsaṃ vāṃchaṃti saṃtatam \|*  
*tatra kaṃpeti vikhyātā mahāpātakanāśinī \|\| 61 \|\|*

*yatra sthitānāṃ martyānāṃ kampante pāpakoṭayaḥ \|*  
*tatra cūtadrumaścaiko rājate nityapallavaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*saṃpūrṇaśītalacchāyaḥ prasūnaphalapallavaiḥ \|*  
*tatra japtaṃ hutaṃ dattamanantaphaladaṃ bhavet \|\| 63 \|\|*

59-63. There is a city named Kāñcī. It is endowed with all riches and is well-known. It is a direct representation of heaven full of Devas on the surface of the earth. It is said that any penance performed there has infinite benefits.

Devas and all the sages desire to stay there forever. There (is a river) well-known as Kaṃpā. It is destructive of all great sins. Crores of sins of the men staying there tremble (with fear).

There is one mango tree there. It shines with perpetual sprouts. It has. perfectly cool shade along with flowers, fruits and sprouts. Japa, Homa and charitable gifts performed there yield infinite benefits.

## \|\| 3.3.64 \|\|

*gaṇāśca vividhākārā ḍākinyo yoginīgaṇāḥ \|*  
*paritastvāṃ niṣevaṃtāṃ viṣṇumukhyāstathā parāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Let the Gaṇas of different forms and sizes, Ḍākinīs, the groups of Yogins and others, the chief of whom is Viṣṇu serve you all round.

## \|\| 3.3.65 \|\|

*ahaṃ ca niṣkalo bhūtvā tava mānasapaṃkaje \|*  
*sannidhāsyāmi mā bhūstvaṃ devi madvirahākulā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. I shall be devoid of attributes and be undivided. I shall be present in your lotus-like mind. O gentle lady, do not become agitated due to separation from me.”

## \|\| 3.3.66 \|\|

*ityuktā devadevena devī kaṃpāṃtikaṃ yayau \|*  
*tapaḥ kartuṃ sakhīyuktā vismayākrāntalocanā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. On being told thus by the Lord of Devas, the goddess, with surprise in her eyes, went near Kaṃpā along with her friends in order to perform penance.

## \|\| 3.3.67-68 \|\|

*kaṃpāṃ ca vimalāṃ sindhuṃ munisamaghaniṣevitām \|*  
*ālokya komaladalamekāmraṃ dṛṣṭivāraṇam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*phalapuṣpasamākīrṇaṃ kokilālāpasaṃkulam \|*  
*prasasāda punardevaṃ sasmāra ca maheśvaram \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. On seeing Kaṃpā, the river without impurities resorted to by groups of ascetics, and the single mango tree Ekāmra with tender sprouts, warding off the (evil) eye, laden with fruits and flowers and completely agitated with the chirping sound of cuckoos, she became pleased. Then she remembered Lord Maheśvara.

## \|\| 3.3.69 \|\|

*kāmāgniparivītāṃgī tapaḥkṣāmeva sā'bhavat \|*  
*abhyabhāṣata sā gaurī vijayāṃ pārśvavarttinīm \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. With her limbs enveloped by the fire of love, she became as though emaciated on account of penance.

Gaurī addressed Vijayā who was present near her at her side.

## \|\| 3.3.70-72 \|\|

*kāmaśokaparītāṃgī purārivirahākulā \|\| 70 \|\|*

*imamaghaharamāgatāniśaṃ svayamapi pūjayituṃ tapobhirīśam \|*  
*ayamabhinavapallavaprasūnaḥ smarayati māṃ smarabandhurekacūtaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*kathamiva virahaḥ śivasya sahyaḥ kṣubhitadhiyātra bhṛśaṃ manobhavena \|*  
*tadapi ca taruṇeṃducūḍapādasmaraṇamahauṣadhamekameva dṛṣṭam \|\| 72 \|\|*

70-72. Her limbs were enveloped by (the feelings of) love and grief (because) she was agitated on account of the separation from Purāri (i.e. Śiva): “I have come here for perpetually worshipping the Lord, the dispeller of sins, by means of austerities. But this single mango tree, the kinsman of the god of Love, with fresh outcome of sprouts and flowers reminds me (of Śiva). My mind has been agitated much by the mind-born lord of love. How can I bear the separation from Śiva? Therefore the sole antidote for the same is seen in remembering the feet of the Lord who has the young moon on his crest.”

## Chapter 4 - Pārvatī Goes to the Hermitage of Gautama

## \|\| 3.4.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*athābhyadhatta vijayā praṇamya jagadambikām \|*  
*sāṃtvayantī stutiśatairupāyaiḥ śivadarśanaiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

1\. After bowing down to the Mother of the universe and consoling her by means of hundreds of eulogies from the scriptures of Śiva (?) Vijayā said to her:

## \|\| 3.4.2 \|\|

*devi tvamavinābhūtā sadā devena śaṃbhunā \|*  
*prāṇeśvarī tvamekāsi śaktistasya parātmanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. “O goddess, you are always inseparable from Lord Śaṃbhu. You are the goddess of his very life, the only Śakti of that Supreme Soul.

## \|\| 3.4.3 \|\|

*tathā māyāṃ tvamātmīyāṃ saṃdarśayitumīhase \|*  
*pṛthagbhāvamiveśānaḥ prakāśayati na svayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. You wish to show your own Māyā in such a way that Īśāna does not himelf \[himself?\] reveal any separate existence (from you).

## \|\| 3.4.4 \|\|

*ādeśaṃ pratigṛhyaiva samupetāsi pārvati \|*  
*alaṃghanīyā sevājñā śāṃbhavī sarvadā tvayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It was only after receiving his command that you have come (here), O Pārvatī. The behest of Śaṃbhu regarding service (unto him) should never be transgressed by you.

## \|\| 3.4.5 \|\|

*vidhātavyaṃ tapaḥ prāptaṃ sthānesmicchivakalpite \|*  
*nivṛttya nikhilānkāmācchaṃmumāśritayā tvayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Abstaining from all desires, you who have resorted to Śaṃbhu, should perform the penance in this place assigned to you by Śiva.

## \|\| 3.4.6 \|\|

*anyathāpi jagadrakṣā tvadadhīnā jaganmayi \|*  
*dharmasaṃrakṣaṇaṃ bhūyaḥ śivena sahitaṃ tava \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Even otherwise, the protection of the universe is under your control, O goddess identical with the universe. The protection and further maintenance of Dharma is yours along with. Śiva.

## \|\| 3.4.7 \|\|

*niṣkalaṃ śivamatyaṃtaṃ dhyāyaṃtyātmanyavasthitam \|*  
*viyogaduḥkhaṃ kañcittvaṃ na smariṣyasi pārvati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Eagerly meditating on Śiva who is devoid of divisions and parts, and stationed in your own soul, O Pārvatī, you will not at all remember the pangs of separation.

## \|\| 3.4.8 \|\|

*bhaktānāṃ tava mukhyānāṃ tavaivācārasaṃgrahaḥ \|*  
*upadeśitayā loke prathatāṃ dharmavatsale \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. All your leading devotees will take up your conduct (as the ideal to be followed). O gentle lady fondly devoted to Dharma, let it spread in the world by preaching.”

## \|\| 3.4.9 \|\|

*iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā gaurī susthiramānasā \|*  
*tapaḥ karttuṃ samārebhe kaṃpā nadyāstaṭe śubhe \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On hearing her statement thus, Gaurī perfectly steadied her mind and began to perform penance on the splendid banks of the river Kaṃpā.

## \|\| 3.4.10 \|\|

*vimucya vividhā bhūṣā rudrākṣagaṇabhūṣitā \|*  
*visṛjya divyaṃ vasanaṃ paryadhādvalkale śubhe \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Setting aside her ornaments of various kinds, she adorned herself with clusters (i.e. rosaries) of Rudrākṣa beads. Laying aside the divine garments, she wore two auspicious bark garments.

## \|\| 3.4.11 \|\|

*alakaiḥ sahasā śilpamanayacca kapardṛtām \|*  
*aliṃpata tanūṃ sarvāṃ bhasmanā muktakuṃkumā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. She immediately turned artistically her forelocks into matted hair. Giving up (the use of) saffron (as unguent), she besmeared her entire body with holy ash.

## \|\| 3.4.12 \|\|

*mṛgeṣu kṛtasaṃtoṣā śiloṃchīkṛtavṛttiṣu \|*  
*jajāpa niyamopetā śivapaṃcākṣaraṃ param \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Gleaning ears of corn alone with the deer, she became contented (with what she got as food). Strictly maintaining her observances, she continuously repeated the five-syllabled Mantra of Śiva (i.e. Namaḥ Śivāya).

## \|\| 3.4.13 \|\|

*kṛtvā triṣavaṇaṃ snānaṃ kampā payasi nirmale \|*  
*kṛtvā ca saikataṃ liṃgaṃ pūjayāmāsa sādaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. She took bath three times a day in the dear limpid waters of Kaṃpā. She made a Liṅga of sand and worshipped it respectfully.

## \|\| 3.4.14 \|\|

*vṛkṣapraropaṇairdānairaśeṣātithipūjanaiḥ \|*  
*śrāṃtiṃ haraṃtī jīvānāṃ devī dharmamapālayat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. She removed the fatigue and weariness of all living beings by planting trees, making charitable gifts and worshipping guests without leaving anyone. Thus, the goddess observed the code of religious conduct.

## \|\| 3.4.15 \|\|

*grīṣme paṃcāgnimadhyasthā varṣāsu sthaṃḍileśayā \|*  
*hemante jalamadhyasthā śiśire cākarottapaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. She performed penance seating herself in the middle of five fires during summer; she lay on the bare ground during rainy season and she remained in water during early and late winter.

## \|\| 3.4.16 \|\|

*puṇyātmanāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ darśanārthamupeyuṣām \|*  
*vismayaṃ janayāmāsa pūjayāmāsa sādaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. She caused surprise in the minds of meritorious-souled great sages who came to visit her. She respectfully adored them.

## \|\| 3.4.17 \|\|

*kadācitsvayamuccitya vanāṃtātpallavānvitam \|*  
*puṣpotkaraṃ viśeṣeṇa śodhituṃ samupāviśat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Sometimes she herself gathered and brought from the forests bunches of flowers along with sprouts and sat down for cleansing them particularly.

## \|\| 3.4.18 \|\|

*kṛtvā ca saikataṃ liṃgaṃ kaṃpārodhasi pāvane \|*  
*saṃpūjayitumārebhe nyāsāvāhanapūrvakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On the sacred banks of Kaṃpā, she, made a Liṅga out of sand and began to worship it with the ancillary rites of Nyāsa and Āvāhana (‘invoking’).

## \|\| 3.4.19 \|\|

*sūryamabhyarcya vidhivadraktaiḥ puṣpaiśca caṃdanaiḥ \|*  
*paṃcāvaraṇasaṃyuktaṃ kramādānarca śaṃkaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. After duly worshipping the Sun with red flowers and sandal paste, she gradually worshipped Śaṅkara equipped with five converings.

## \|\| 3.4.20 \|\|

*dhūpairdīpaśca naivedyairbhaktibhāvasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*aparokṣitamīśānamāluloke purohitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. She saw in front of her Īśāna, the cause of welfare, made perceptible by means of incenses, lamps, food offerings etc. with feelings of devotion.

## \|\| 3.4.21-22 \|\|

*atha devaḥ śivaḥ sākṣātsaṃśodhayitumaṃbikām \|*  
*kaṃpānadyāḥ pravāheṇa mahatā paryaveṣṭayat \|\| 21 \|\|*

*ativṛddhaṃ pravāhaṃ taṃ kampāyāḥ samupasthitam \|*  
*ālokya niyamāsīnāmāhuḥ sakhyastadāṃbikām \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. (Once) Lord Śiva himself, to test Aṃbikā, caused a big flood in the river Kaṃpā (which) surrounded her. On seeing that exceedingly great flood approaching, the friends said to Aṃbikā who was seated (there) in the course of her holy observances:

## \|\| 3.4.23 \|\|

*uttiṣṭha devi bahulaḥ pravāho'yaṃ vijṛṃbhate \|*  
*diśāṃ mukhāni saṃpūrya tarasā plāvayiṣyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “O goddess, get up. A big flow of water is rushing on. It will fill the quarters quickly and flood everything.”

## \|\| 3.4.24 \|\|

*iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dhyāyaṃtī mīlitekṣaṇā \|*  
*unmīlya vegamatulaṃ nadyāstaṃ samavaikṣata \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. As she was in her meditation with closed eyes, she heard these words. On opening her eyes she saw that unparalleled force of the current of waters of the river.

## \|\| 3.4.25 \|\|

*aciṃtayacca sā devī pūjāvighnasamākulā \|*  
*kiṃ karomi na śaknomi hātumārabdhamarcanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Worried at the possibility of an obstacle in her worship, the goddess thought: ‘What shall I do? I cannot forsake the worship that has been begun.

## \|\| 3.4.26 \|\|

*śreyaḥ prāptumavighnena prāyaḥ puṇyātmanāṃ bhuvi \|*  
*ghaṭate dharmasaṃyogo manorathaphalapradaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Generally it is in the case of meritorious-souled persons that the association of holy rites, the bestower of desired benefits, is actively conducive to the acquisition of welfare without obstacles on the earth.

## \|\| 3.4.27 \|\|

*saikataṃ liṃgamatulapravāhāllayameṣyati \|*  
*liṃganāśe vimoktavyaḥ sadbhaktaiḥ prāṇasaṃgrahaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. This Liṅga made of sand will be swept away by the unparalleled force of the current. If the Liṅga is destroyed good devotees should give up their lives.

## \|\| 3.4.28 \|\|

*pravāho'yaṃ samāyāti śivamāyāvinirmitaḥ \|*  
*viśodhayitumātmānaṃ bhaktiyuktaṃ nije pade \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. This flood is created by the Māyā of Śiva. It comes to test Ātman whether it is endowed with devotion to his feet or not.

## \|\| 3.4.29 \|\|

*āliṃgya sudṛḍhaṃ dorbhyāmetalliṃgamanākulam \|*  
*ahaṃ vatsyāmi yātāśu sakhyo yūyaṃ vidūrataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. With my pair of arms, I will closely embrace this Liṅga and will remain here unaffected and unagitated’: “Dear friends, all of you go far off quickly.”

## \|\| 3.4.30 \|\|

*ityuktā saikataṃ ligaṃ gāḍhamāliṃgya sāṃbikā \|*  
*na mumoca pravāhena veṣṭyamānāpi vegataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. After saying thus, Aṃbikā closely embraced the Liṅga. Although she was engulfed by the speedy flow, she did not let it go.

## \|\| 3.4.31 \|\|

*stanacūcukanirmagnamudrādarśitalāṃchanam \|*  
*mahāliṃgaṃ svasaṃyuktaṃ praṇanāma tadādarāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The nipples of her breasts pressed so hard against the Liṅga that an impression was left appearing like a scar on it. Then (the goddess) respectfully bowed down to the Liṅga clinging to it.

## \|\| 3.4.32 \|\|

*nimīlitekṣaṇā dhyānaniṣṭhaikahṛdayā sthitā \|*  
*pulakāṃcitasarvāṃgī sā smaraṃtī sadāśivam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Remembering Sadāśiva, she experienced a thrill all over her body making her hair stand on end. She remained with her eyes closed and her heart engrossed solely in meditation.

## \|\| 3.4.33 \|\|

*kaṃpasvedaparitrāṇalajjāpraṇayakelidāt \|*  
*kṣaṇamapyacalā liṃgānna viyogamapekṣate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. She was motionless and did not want to be separated even for a moment from that Liṅga which caused tremor, perspiration, protection, bashfulness and love-sport in her.

## \|\| 3.4.34 \|\|

*atha tāmabravītkāpi daivī vāgaśarīriṇī \|*  
*vimuṃca bālike liṃgaṃ pravāho'yaṃ gato mahān \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. A certain (mysterious) incorporal divine voice addressed her: “O girl, leave off that Liṅga. The great flood has receded.

## \|\| 3.4.35 \|\|

*tvayārcitamidaṃ liṃgaṃ saikataṃ sthiravaibhavam \|*  
*bhaviṣyati mahābhāge varadaṃ surapūjitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The sandy Liṅga worshipped by you will have a perpetual greatness. O exalted lady, it will be worshipped by Suras and will be a bestower of boons.

## \|\| 3.4.36 \|\|

*tapaścaryāṃ tavālokya racitaṃ dharmapālanam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ caitannamaskṛtya kṛtārthāḥ saṃtu mānavāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On seeing your penance (a test of your observance of Dharma) has been arranged. Let human beings become blessed and satisfied by bowing down to this Liṅga.

## \|\| 3.4.37 \|\|

*ahaṃ hi taijasaṃ rūpamāsthāya vasudhātale \|*  
*vasāmi cātra siddhyarthamaruṇācalasaṃjñayā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. I shall assume an effulgent form and stay here under the name Aruṇācala for the sake of (men’s) achievement of Siddhi on the surface of the earth (itself).

## \|\| 3.4.38 \|\|

*ruṇaddhi sarvalokebhyaḥ paruṣaṃ pāpasaṃcayam \|*  
*ruṇo na vidyate yasmindṛṣṭe tenāruṇācalaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The word Ruṇa means collection of sins because it prevents a man from all the worlds. When the good is seen there is no Ruṇa. Hence Aruṇācala.

## \|\| 3.4.39 \|\|

*ṛṣayaḥ siddhagaṃdharvā mahātmānaśca yoginaḥ \|*  
*muktvā kailāsaśikharaṃ meruṃ cainamupāsate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The sages, Siddhas, Gandharvas and noble-souled Yogins leave off the peak of Kailāsa (mountain) and of Meru and resort to this (mountain).

## \|\| 3.4.40 \|\|

*madaṃśa jātayoḥ pūrvaṃ yudhyatorbrahmakṛṣṇayoḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ mohamapākarttuṃ tejorūpo vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Formerly, in order to dispel the delusion of Brahmā and Kṛṣṇa (i.e. Viṣṇu) who were born of a part of mine but were fighting with each other, I stood here (between them) in the form of a fiery brilliance.

## \|\| 3.4.41 \|\|

*brahmaṇā haṃsarūpeṇa viṣṇunā kroḍarūpiṇā \|*  
*adṛṣṭaśekharapadaḥ praṇato bhaktiyogataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. My crest was not seen by Brahmā who assumed the form of a swan and my foot was not seen by Viṣṇu who took the form of a boar. I was bowed down to by them with devotion.

## \|\| 3.4.42 \|\|

*tataḥ prasannaḥ pratyakṣastasyāṃ varamabhīpsitam \|*  
*prādāṃ jagattrayasyāsya saṃrakṣāyāṃ tu kauśalam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Then I was pleased. I become visible to them. I granted them the boons desired by them. I granted them proficiency in the protection of the three worlds.

## \|\| 3.4.43 \|\|

*prārthitaśca punastābhyāmaruṇācalasaṃjñayā \|*  
*anaiṣi taijasaṃ rūpamahaṃ sthāvaraliṃgatām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Requested once again by them I assumed this fiery form with the name Aruṇācala. I was persuaded by them to assume the state of an immobile Liṅga.

## \|\| 3.4.44 \|\|

*gatvā pṛccha mahābhāgaṃ madbhaktiṃ gautamaṃ munim \|*  
*aruṇācalamāhātmyaṃ śrutvā tatra tapaścara \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Go to Sage Gautama of exalted fortune and ask him about devotion unto me. After hearing about the greatness of Aruṇācala, perform penance there.

## \|\| 3.4.45 \|\|

*tatra te darśayiṣyāmi taijasaṃ rūpamātmanaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpanivṛttyarthaṃ sarvalokahitāya ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. There I shall reveal to you the effulgent form of mine for the sake of dispelling all sins and for the sake of the welfare of the worlds.”

## \|\| 3.4.46 \|\|

*iti vācaṃ samākarṇya niṣkalātkathitāṃ śivāt \|*  
*tatheti sahasā devī gaṃtuṃ samupacakrame \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On hearing these words uttered by Śiva, the entire one without divisions, the goddess said “So be it” and began to go immediately.

## \|\| 3.4.47 \|\|

*atha devānṛṣīnsarvānpaścātsevārthamāgatān \|*  
*avādīdaṃbikālokya snehapūrṇena cakṣuṣā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Then looking with affectionate eyes all the Devas and sages who had followed her for rendering service to her, Aṃbikā spoke:

## \|\| 3.4.48 \|\|

*tiṣṭhatātraiva vai devā munayaśca dṛḍhavratāḥ \|*  
*niyamāṃścādhitiṣṭhaṃtaḥ kaṃpārodhasi pāvane \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. “O Devas, and the sages of steady holy observances, stay here on the sacred banks of Kaṃpā maintaining your holy vows.

## \|\| 3.4.49 \|\|

*sarvapāpakṣayakaraṃ sarvasaubhāgyavarddhanam \|*  
*pūjyatāṃ saikataṃ liṃgaṃ kucakaṃkaṇalāṃchanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Let this Liṅga, made of sand and marked by (ray) breast and bangles be worshipped by you. It causes the destruction of all sins and increases all types of good fortune.

## \|\| 3.4.50 \|\|

*ahaṃ ca niṣkalaṃ rūpamāsthāyaitaddivāniśam \|*  
*ārādhayāmi maṃtreṇa śoṇeśvaraṃ varapradam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Day and night I assume an entire, undivided, attributeless form and propitiate this Śoṇeśvara, the bestower of boons, by means of Mantras.

## \|\| 3.4.51 \|\|

*mattapaścaraṇālloke maddharmaparipālanāt \|*  
*malliṃgadarśanāccaiva sidhyaṃtviṣṭavibhūtayaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. In this world let all types of desired prosperity be achieved due to my performance of the penance and observance of piety and righteousness as well as by seeing the Liṅga (installed) by me.

## \|\| 3.4.52 \|\|

*sarvakāmapradānena kāmākṣīmiti kāmataḥ \|*  
*māṃ praṇamyātra madbhaktā labhaṃtāṃ vāṃchitaṃ varam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. I am called Kāmākṣī on account of my bestowing everything desired. Let my devotees here obtain the desired boon after bowing down to me under the name Kāmākṣī as they please.

## \|\| 3.4.53 \|\|

*ahaṃ hi devadevasya śaṃbhoravyāhato janaḥ \|*  
*ādeśaṃ pālayiṣyāmi gatvāruṇamahīdharam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Indeed I shall go to the mountain Aruṇācala and carry out the behest of Śaṃbhu, the Lord of Devas, the Lord of unobstructed prowess.

## \|\| 3.4.54 \|\|

*tatra gatvā tapastīvraṃ kṛtvā śaṃbhuṃ prasādya ca \|*  
*māṃ tu labdhavarāṃ yūyaṃ paścādrakṣyatha saṃgatāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. I shall go there, perform a severe penance and please Śaṃbhu. Afterwards you all shall gather together and see me when I will have obtained the boons.”

## \|\| 3.4.55 \|\|

*iti sarvānvisṛjyāśu sadbhaktānpādasevinaḥ \|*  
*aruṇādriṃ gatā bālā tapase śaṃkarājñayā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. After instantly bidding farewell thus to all the good devotees serving her feet, the gentle ‘girl’ went to Aruṇācala for the sake of penance at the bidding of Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 3.4.56-58 \|\|

*nityābhisevitā'kāri sakhībhirabhiyogataḥ \|*  
*āsasādāruṇādrīśaṃ divyaduṃdubhināditam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*aṃtastejomayaṃ śāṃtamaruṇācalanāyakam \|*  
*apsaronṛtyagītaiśca pūjitaṃ puṣpavṛṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*praṇamya sthāvaraṃ liṃgaṃ kautūhalasamanvitā \|*  
*siddhānāṃ yogināṃ sārthamṛṣīṇāṃ cānvavaikṣata \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. She was perpetually served by female friends and attendants devotedly. She approached the Lord of Aruṇācala for whom the divine Dundubhi drum was sounded. Though the Lord of Aruṇācala is of a fiery nature, he is internally quiescent. He is worshipped by the celestial damsels through dances, songs and showers of flowers. With great enthusiasm she bowed down to the immobile Liṅga and saw the group of Siddhas, Yogins and sages.

## \|\| 3.4.59-60 \|\|

*atrirbhṛgurbharadvājaḥ kaśyapaścāṃgirāstathā \|*  
*kutsaśca gautamaścānye siddhavidyādharāmarāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tapaḥ kurvaṃti satatamapekṣitavarāptaye \|*  
*gaṃgādyāḥ saritaścānyāḥ paritaḥ paryupāsate \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. Atri, Bhṛgu, Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa, Aṅgiras, Kutsa and Gautama as well as Siddhas, Vidyādharas and the immortal ones always perform penance here for the sake of getting the expected boons. Gaṅgā and other rivers serve and attend to him all round.

## \|\| 3.4.61 \|\|

*divyaliṃgamidaṃ pūjyamaruṇādririti smṛtam \|*  
*vaṃdasveti suraiḥ proktā praṇanāma punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. “This is a divine Liṅga remembered as Aruṇādri (or Aruṇācala). Salute.” On being told thus by the Suras, she bowed down again and again.

## \|\| 3.4.62 \|\|

*abhyarthitā punaḥ sarvairātithyārthe maharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*śivājñayā gautamo me draṣṭavya iti sāvadat \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On being requested to receive their hospitality by all the great sages, she said, “As per order of Śiva, Gautama should be seen by me.”

## \|\| 3.4.63 \|\|

*ayamatrarṣibhirbhaktairnirdiṣṭaṃ tamathābhyagāt \|*  
*sa muniḥ śivabhaktānāṃ prathamastapasāṃ nidhiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. She went to him as he was pointed out by the sages saying, “He is here”. That sage was the first and foremost among the devotees of Śiva. He was a storehouse of austerities.

## \|\| 3.4.64-65 \|\|

*vanāṃtaraṃ gateḥ prātaḥ samitkuśaphalāhṛteḥ \|*  
*atithīnāśramaṃ prāptānarcatheti dṛḍhavratān \|\| 64 \|\|*

*śiṣyānādiśya dharmātmā gataśca vipināṃtaram \|*  
*atha sā gautamaṃ draṣṭumāgatā parṇaśālikām \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. He had gone to the forest in the morning for fetching sacrificial twigs, Kuśa grass and fruits after bidding the disciples of steadfast holy rites, “Worship the guests who come to the hermitage.” The righteous-souled sage went to the forest. Then she came to the hermitage to see Gautama.

## \|\| 3.4.66-73 \|\|

*kva gato munirityuktairita āyāsyati kṣaṇāt \|*  
*śiṣyairabhyarthitetyuktvā phalamūlaissugaṃdhibhiḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*abhyutthānenāsanena pādyenārgheṇa sūnṛtaiḥ \|*  
*vacanaiḥ phalamṛlena sārcitā śiṣyasaṃpadā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*kṣaṇaṃ kṣamasvasūnustāmanye jagmustadantikam \|*  
*devyāṃ praviṣṭamātrāyāṃ maharṣerāśramo mahān \|\| 68 \|\|*

*abhavatkalpabahulo maṇiprāsādasaṃkulaḥ \|*  
*vanāṃtarādupāvṛttya samitkuśaphalāharaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*apaśyatsvāśramaṃ dūre vimānaśataśobhitam \|*  
*kimetaditi sāścaryaṃ ciṃtayanmunipuṃgavaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*gauryāḥ samāgamaṃ sarvamapaśyajjñānacakṣuṣā \|*  
*śīghraṃ nivartamāno'sau draṣṭuṃ tāṃ lokamātaram \|\| 71 \|\|*

*śiṣyaiḥ śīghracarairvṛttamāveditamathāśṛṇot \|\| 72 \|\|*

*atha maharṣirupāgatakautuko nijatapaḥphalameva tadāgamam \|*  
*śivadayākalitaṃ paricintayannabhajadāśramamāśritavatsalaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

66-71a. When the disciples were asked, “Where has the sage gone?”, they said, “He will come back in a short while.” After saying this, she was received by the disciples standing up in honour of her arrival, and offered fruits, roots, sweet scents, a seat, water to wash the feet, Arghya and courteous words of welcome. She was duly honoured with fruits and roots that constitute the assets of the disciples. They said to her, “Please wait for a moment.” Others went near her.

The moment the goddess entered it, the great hermitage of the noble sage became one full of jewel-set mansions with plenty of requisite furnishings.

After returning from the forest carrying sacrificial twigs, Kuśa grass and fruits, the eminent sage saw from far his hermitage sparkling splendidly with hundreds of vehicles. He thought with wonder, ‘What is this?’ By means of his vision born of knowledge, he saw that Gaurī had come there.

71b-73. In order to see Mother of the worlds, he hastened (back to the hermitage). The disciples, with great haste, intimated to him the news.

The great sage thought that her arrival was the fruit of his own penance. It was coupled with the kindness of Śiva. With great eagerness he came into the hermitage. He who was fond of those who resorted to him, came to the hermitage, thinking about all these things.

## Chapter 5 - The Greatness of Brahmapuṣkara

## \|\| 3.5.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*araṇyādgautamaṃ śāṃtamuṭajadvāra āgatam \|*  
*pratyādhātuṃ pravavṛte śivabhaktirjaganmayī \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

1\. Śivabhakti (? Śivaśakti), Śiva’s devotion (? Śiva’s power), identical with the universe prepared to welcome the quiescent Gautama who came back to the door of the hut from the forest.

## \|\| 3.5.2 \|\|

*āluloke samāyātaṃ gautamaṃ śiṣyasevitam \|*  
*laṃbamānaśiraḥśmaśrusampūrṇamukhamaṇḍalam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. She saw Gautama served by his disciples as he returned. His head was covered with long flowing hair. His face was fully covered with a beard.

## \|\| 3.5.3 \|\|

*jaṭābhiratitāmrābhistīrthasnānaviśuddhibhiḥ \|*  
*nyastarudrākṣamaṇibhirjvālābhiriva pāvakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He shone like fire with flames on account of the exceedingly copper-coloured matted hair that had become clean and pure on account of the holy bath in the Tīrtha and in which beads of Rudrākṣa had been placed.

## \|\| 3.5.4 \|\|

*bhasmatripuṇḍrakopetaviśālaniṭilojvalam \|*  
*śuklayajñopavītena pūrṇaṃ rudrākṣadāmabhiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He was resplendent with the Tripuṇḍra marked with sacred ash on his wide forehead. He wore a white sacred thread as well as rosaries of Rudrākṣa beads.

## \|\| 3.5.5 \|\|

*dadhānaṃ valkale rakte tapaḥ kṛśitavigraham \|*  
*japaṃtaṃ vaidikānmaṃtrānrudraprītikarānbahūn \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He wore two red bark garments. His body was lean and emaciated due to penance. He repeated many Vedic Mantras causing delight to Rudra.

## \|\| 3.5.6 \|\|

*śambhunāvasitodāttasārūpyamiva bhāṣitam \|*  
*tejonidhiṃ dayāpūrṇaṃ pratyakṣamiva bhāskaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On account of his highly dignified speech he was (as if) possessed by Śaṃbhu and hence had a sameness (of the exalted tone like that) of Śaṃbhu. He was full of kindness and was a treasure of refulgence like the veritable Sun-god.

## \|\| 3.5.7 \|\|

*ālokya taṃ mahātmānaṃ vṛddhaṃ śaṃbhupadāśrayam \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭā gaurī praṇantumupacakrame \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On seeing that noble-souled old sage who had resorted to the feet of Śaṃbhu, Gaurī joined her palms in reverence and began to bow down to him.

## \|\| 3.5.8 \|\|

*kṛtāṃjaliṃ munirvīkṣya samastajagadambikām \|*  
*kimetaditi sāścaryaṃ vārayanpraṇanāma saḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On seeing the Mother of the entire universe with palms folded in reverence, the sage wondered what the matter was. Preventing (her from bowing down), he himself saluted her.

## \|\| 3.5.9 \|\|

*svāgataṃ gauri subhage lokamātardayānidhe \|*  
*vyājena bhaktasaṃrakṣāṃ kartumatrāgatāsyaho \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “O Gaurī of great magnificence, welcome (unto you). O mother of the worlds, O storehouse of mercy, under some pretext you have come here to protect the devotees.

## \|\| 3.5.10 \|\|

*aho mānye mānyamarthaṃ vijñāyaiva purā vayam \|*  
*pṛthagbhāvamivālaṃbya śiṣyādibhiḥ samāgatāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O goddess worthy of being honoured, it was as though you had realized an objective worthy of being respected formerly. Assuming separateness, we have come here along with (her) disciples and others. (obscure)

## \|\| 3.5.11 \|\|

*yaddevi te na cetkiṃcinmāyāvilasitannijam \|*  
*tataḥ prapaṃcasaṃsiddhiḥ kathameva bhaviṣyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O goddess, if you have no sportive flash of your own Māyā, how can the worldly existence continue to be? (obscure)

## \|\| 3.5.12 \|\|

*tiṣṭhatvaśeṣaṃ me vaktuṃ māyāvilasitaṃ tava \|*  
*na śakyate yannirṇetuṃ tvadīyaiśca kadācana \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Let it be. I am not competent to speak of the sportive flash of your own Māyā which it is ever impossible to decide specifically by your (people i.e. devotees). (obscure)

## \|\| 3.5.13 \|\|

*āsyatāṃ pāvane śuddhaṃ āsane kuśanirmite \|*  
*gṛhyatāṃ pādyamarghaṃ ca dattaṃ ca vidhivanmayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Be pleased to sit on the clean holy seat made of Kuśa grass, Let the Pādya and Arghya duly offered by me be accepted.”

## \|\| 3.5.14 \|\|

*iti śiṣyaiḥ samānīte darbhāṃke paramāsane \|*  
*āsīnāmaṃbikāṃ vṛddho munirānarca bhaktimān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After saying this, the old sage devoutly worshipped Aṃbikā who was seated on the excellent seat made of Darbha grass brought by the disciples.

## \|\| 3.5.15 \|\|

*nivedya sakalāṃ pūjāṃ bhaktibhāvasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*gauryā samabhyanujñātaḥ svayamapyāsane sthitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After completing the entire worship, (the sage) endowed with the feelings of devotion, himself sat on a seat after being permitted by Gaurī.

## \|\| 3.5.16 \|\|

*uvāca daśanajyotsnāparidhautadiśāmukhaḥ \|*  
*pulakāṃcitasarvāṃgaḥ sānaṃdāśru sagadgadam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Washing the faces of the quarters with the moon-lightlike splendour of his teeth, with the hair standing on end all over his body through joyous thrill, he spoke in a choked voice with tears of joy:

## \|\| 3.5.17 \|\|

*aho devasya māhātmyaṃ śambhoramitatejasaḥ \|*  
*sadbhakta rakṣaṇāya tvāmādiśadbhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “Oh, the greatness of lord Śaṃbhu of unmeasured splendour! The Lord fond of his devotees has directed you to protect good devotees.

## \|\| 3.5.18-20 \|\|

*asiddhamanyallabdhavyaṃ kiṃ vānyattava vidyate \|*  
*ambaitadbhaktimāhātmyaṃ saṃdarśayitumīśvaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kailāsaśailavṛttāṃtaḥ kaṃpātaṭatapaḥsthitaḥ \|*  
*aruṇādrisamādeśaḥ sarvaṃ jñātamidaṃ mayā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*āgatāsi mahābhāge bhaktāśramamimaṃ svayam \|*  
*snehena karuṇāmūrte karttavyamupadiśyatām \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. O Aṃbā, is there anything not acquired, anything else yet to be obtained, by you? It is to point out the greatness of devotion that god Śiva (has directed you). The events at Kailāsa, the stay on the banks of Kaṃpā for penance and the directive of Aruṇācala—all this is known to me. O highly fortunate lady, you have yourself come to this hermitage of your devotee, out of affection. O goddess, the embodiment of mercifulness, tell me what I am to do.”

## \|\| 3.5.21 \|\|

*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā maharṣeḥ sarvavedinaḥ \|*  
*aṃbikā prāha kutukātstuvantī taṃ mahāmunim \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On hearing these words of that great sage who knew everything, Aṃbika eagerly spoke to him eulogizing him:

## \|\| 3.5.22 \|\|

*mahāvaibhavametatte devadevaḥ svayaṃ śivaḥ \|*  
*madhye tapasvināṃ tvaṃ tu draṣṭavya iti cādiśat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “This is the great magnificence of yours that Śiva, the Lord of Devas, himself commanded me that you should be seen. Among all the ascetics (it was you that he selected).

## \|\| 3.5.23 \|\|

*āgamānāṃ śivoktānāṃ vedānāmapi pāragaḥ \|*  
*tapasā śaṃbhubhaktānāṃ tvameva śivasaṃmataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. You are master of the Vedas and the Āgamas uttered by Śiva. It is on account of your penance that among the devotees of Śiva, you alone are (regarded as) the most honoured one by Śiva.

## \|\| 3.5.24 \|\|

*aruṇācala nāmnāhaṃ tiṣṭhāmītyabravīcchivaḥ \|\| \|*  
*asyācalasya māhātmyaṃ śrotavyaṃ ca bhavanmukhāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. ‘I am staying here by the name Aruṇācala’, said Śiva. The greatness of this Acala (mountain) should be heard directly from you.

## \|\| 3.5.25 \|\|

*prāptāsmyahaṃ tapaḥ kartumaruṇācalasannidhau \|*  
*bhavatāṃ darśanādeva svayamīśaḥ prasīdati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I have come to the presence of Aruṇācala in order to perform penance. It is only due to the sight of Your Holiness that Īśa himself becomes delighted.

## \|\| 3.5.26 \|\|

*śivabhaktena saṃbhāṣā śivasaṃkīrttanaśravaḥ \|*  
*śivaliṃgārcanaṃ loke vapurgrahaphalodayaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. (The opportunity) to converse with the devotees of Śiva and to worship Śivaliṅga—this is the benefit of being embodied (bom) in the world.

## \|\| 3.5.27 \|\|

*tasmānmamaitanmāhātmyaṃ śrotavyaṃ bhavato mukhāt \|*  
*suvyaktamupadeśena jñānato'si pitā mama \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Hence, this greatness orally transmitted by you directly should be heard by me. Due to your knowledge and teaching, you are clearly (like) a father unto me.”

## \|\| 3.5.28 \|\|

*iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā gautamastapasāṃ nidhiḥ \|*  
*ācakhyau giriśaṃ dhyāyannaruṇācalavaibhavam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On hearing her words, Gautama, the storehouse of austerities, recounted the greatness of Aruṇācala after meditating on Giriśa:

## \|\| 3.5.29 \|\|

*ajñātamiva yatkiṃcitpṛcchyate ca punastvayā \|*  
*avaimi sarvavidyānāṃ māyā śaivī tvameva sā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “Whatever is being asked by you, as though it is not known to you, I know that you alone are the Māyā of Śiva, which is the (repository) of all knowledge.

## \|\| 3.5.30 \|\|

*athavā bhaktavaktreṇa śivavaibhavasaṃśravaḥ \|*  
*śikṣaṇaṃ śāṃbhavaṃ teṣāṃ tava tuṣṭeśca kāraṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Listening to the greatness of Śiva uttered by a devotee and to the teachings of Śaṃbhu (handed over to them)—this is the cause of your delight.

## \|\| 3.5.31 \|\|

*paṭhitānāṃ ca vedānāṃ yadāvṛttaphalāvaham \|*  
*vadatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ loke śivasaṃkīrttanaṃ tathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Those who glorify or listen to the glorification of Śiva in the world attain the same merit as the study and recitation of the Vedas.

## \|\| 3.5.32 \|\|

*saphalānyadya sarvāṇi tapāṃsi caritāni me \|*  
*yadahaṃ śaṃbhunādiṣṭaṃ māhātmyaṃ kīrttaye śrutam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. All the austerities performed by me have become fruitful today, because I glorify the greatness as heard (by me) and as directed by Śaṃbhu.

## \|\| 3.5.33-46 \|\|

*śivāśivaprasādena māhātmyamidamadbhutam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*aruṇācalamāhātmyaṃ duritakṣayakāraṇam \|*  
*śrūyatāmanavadyāṃgi purāvṛttamidaṃ mahat \|\| 34 \|\|*

*aruṇādrimayaṃ liṃgamāvirbhūtaṃ yathā purā \|*  
*na śakyate punarvaktumaśeṣaṃ vaktrakoṭibhiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*aruṇācalamāhātmyaṃ brahmaṇāmapi koṭibhiḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇā viṣṇunā pūrvaṃ somabhāskaravahnibhiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*indrādibhiśca dikpālaiḥ pūjitaścāṣṭasiddhaye \|*  
*siddhacāraṇagaṃdharva yakṣavidyādharoragaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*khagaiśca munibhirdivyaiḥ siddhayogibhirarcitaḥ \|*  
*tattatpāpanivṛttyarthaṃ tattadīpsitasiddhaye \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ārādhito'yaṃ bhagavānaruṇādripatiḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭo harati pāpāni sevito vāṃchitapradaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kīrtitopi janairdūraiḥ śoṇādririti muktidaḥ \|*  
*tejaḥstaṃbhamayaṃ rūpamaruṇādririti śrutam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*dhyāyanto yoginaścitte śivasāyujyamāpnuyuḥ \|*  
*dattaṃ hutaṃ ca yatkiṃcijjaptaṃ cānyattapaḥ kṛtam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*akṣayyaṃ bhavati prāptamaruṇācalasaṃnidhau \|*  
*purā brahmā ca viṣṇuśca śivatejoṃśasaṃbhavau \|\| 42 \|\|*

*sāhaṃkārau yuyudhatuḥ parasparajigīṣayā \|*  
*tathā tayorgarvaśāṃtyai yogidhyeyaḥ sadāśivaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*agnitejomayaṃ rūpamādimadhyāṃtavarjitam \|*  
*saṃprāpya tasthau tanmadhye diśo daśa vibhāsayan \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tejaḥstaṃbhasya tasyātha draṣṭumādyaṃtabhāgayoḥ \|*  
*haṃsakroḍatanū kṛtvā jagmaturdyāṃ rasātalam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tau viṣaṇṇamukhau dṛṣṭvā bhagavānkaruṇānidhiḥ \|*  
*āvirbabhūva ca tayorvaraṃ prādādabhīpsitam \|\| 46 \|\|*

33-39a. This wonderful greatness (has been obtained by me) by the favour of Śiva and Śivā.

O lady of faultless limbs, let this great ancient lore, the greatness of Aruṇācala, the cause of the destruction of sins, be heard. Listen how the Liṅga in the form of Aruṇācala manifested itself formerly.

The entire greatness of Aruṇācala cannot be expressed with a crore of mouths by a crore of Brāhmaṇas. Lord Śiva, the Lord of Aruṇācala, has been worshipped for the attainment of the eight (super-human powers) by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the Moon, the Sun, the Fire-god and the Guardians of the Directions beginning with Indra. He has been adored by Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, serpents, birds, divine sages and Siddhayogins for dispelling different kinds of sins, for fulfilling different kinds of wishes, This Lord has thus been propitiated.

39b-42a. On being visited, the Lord dispels sins, On being served he bestows whatever is desired. If he is glorified as Śoṇādri (i.e. Aruṇācala) by the people even from far he bestows salvation. The Yogins who meditate in their minds on the form of the column of effulgence well-known as Aruṇādri, shall obtain salvation in the form of Sāyujya (‘perfect merger’) with Śiva. What is given as charitable gift, whatever is offered as Homa, the Japa performed and the penances practised in the presence of Aruṇācala acquire everlasting benefit.

42b-46. Brahmā and Viṣṇu who are born of parts of the splendour of Śiva, became proud aṇḍ arrogant. With a desire to conquer each other, they fought arrogantly. In order to quell their pride, Sadāśiva, worthy of being meditated upon by Yogins, assumed the form of fiery splendour devoid of beginning, middle and end. Illuminating the ten quarters, he stood in between them. In order to see the beginning and end portions of that fiery column (Brahmā and Viṣṇu) assumed the forms of a swan and a boar and went to the firmament and to the nether worlds. On seeing them weary and distressed, the Lord, the storehouse of mercy, appeared in front of them and granted them the boon they desired.

## \|\| 3.5.47 \|\|

*tatprārthitaśca deveśo yātaḥ sthāvaraliṃgatām \|*  
*aruṇādririti khyātaḥ praśāṃtaḥ saṃprakāśate \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On being requested by them the Lord of Devas assumed the form of an immobile Liṅga, well-known as Aruṇādri. He shines calmly yet brilliantly.

## \|\| 3.5.48 \|\|

*divyadundubhinirghoṣairapsarogītanarttanaiḥ \|*  
*pūjyate taijasaṃ liṃgaṃ puṣpavṛṣṭiśataiḥ sadā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. This effulgent Liṅga is always worshipped to the accompaniment of the sounds of divine Dundubhi drums, the songs and dances of celestial damsels and hundreds of showers of flowers.

## \|\| 3.5.49 \|\|

*brahmaṇāmapyatītānāṃ purā ṣaṇṇavateḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*viṣṇunābhisamudbhūto brahmā lokānsasarja hi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Formerly ninety-six Brahmās had come up and passed away. Then a Brahmā came out of the navel of Viṣṇu and created the worlds.

## \|\| 3.5.50 \|\|

*sa kadācittapovighnaṃ kartukāmena yoginām \|*  
*iṃdreṇa prārthito brahmā sasarja lalitāṃ striyam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Once that Brahmā was requested by Indra who was desirous of causing obstacles to the penance of Yogins. (So) he created a lovely and graceful woman.

## \|\| 3.5.51 \|\|

*lāvaṇyaguṇasaṃpūrṇāmālokya kamalekṣaṇām \|*  
*mumoha kaṃdarpaśaraiḥ sa viddhahṛdayo vidhiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. On seeing that lotus-eyed lady full of graceful charms and other good qualities, Brahmā was pierced in his heart by the arrows of Kandarpa (i.e. god of Love). He became deluded.

## \|\| 3.5.52 \|\|

*spraṣṭukāmaṃ tamālokya brahmāṇaṃ kamalāsanam \|*  
*natvā pradakṣiṇavyājādgaṃtumaicchadvarāpsarāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. On observing the lotus-seated Brahmā desirous of touching her, the excellent celestial damsel bowed to him and under the pretext of circumambulating him, she wished to go away.

## \|\| 3.5.53 \|\|

*asyāṃ pradakṣiṇāṃ bhaktyā kurvāṇāyāṃ prajāpateḥ \|*  
*catasṛbhyo'pi digbhyo'sya mukhānyudabhavankṣaṇāt \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. While she was devoutly circumambulating, there sprang up four faces of Brahmā in the four directions instantaneously.

## \|\| 3.5.54-57 \|\|

*sā bālā pakṣiṇī bhūtvā gaganaṃ samagāhata \|*  
*punaśca khagarūpeṇa samāyāṃtaṃ samīkṣya sā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*śaraṇaṃ yācamānā sā śoṇādrimimamāśrayat \|*  
*brahmaṇā viṣṇunā ca tvamadṛṣṭapadaśekharaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*rakṣa māmaruṇādrīśa śaraṇya śaraṇāgatām \|*  
*iti tasyāṃ bhayārttāyāṃ krośaṃtyāmaruṇācalāt \|\| 56 \|\|*

*udabhūtsthāvarālliṃgādvyādhaḥ kaściddhanurddharaḥ \|*  
*saṃdhāya sāyakaṃ cāpe sameghagaganadyutiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

54-57. That maiden then assumed the form of a bird and flew into the sky. On seeing him approaching in the form of a bird, she resorted to Aruṇācala seeking refuge.

‘You are the Lord whose foot and head have not been seen by Brahmā and Viṣṇu. O Lord of Aruṇācala, protect me. O Lord worthy of giving refuge, I have sought refuge in you.’

While she was lamenting with excess of agony and fright, a certain hunter wielding a bow rose up from the immobile Linga Aruṇācala. He had the lustre of the sky overcast with clouds and he had fixed aṇ arrow to his bow. When the hunter was seen in front (of him) his (Brahmā’s) delusion was dispelled.

## \|\| 3.5.58-71 \|\|

*niṣāde purato dṛṣṭe mohastasya nanāśa hi \|*  
*tataḥ prasannahṛdayotinamraḥ kamalodbhavaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*namaścakre śaraṇyāya śoṇādripataye tadā \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayakṛte namastubhyaṃ pinākine \|\| 59 \|\|*

*aruṇācalarūpāya bhakvavaśyāya śaṃbhave \|*  
*ajānatāṃ svabhaktānāmakarmavinivarttane \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tvadanyaḥ kaḥ prabhuḥ kartumaśakyaṃ cāpi dehinām \|*  
*upasaṃhara me dehaṃ tejasā pāpaniścayam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*anyaṃ vā sṛja viśvātmanbrahmāṇaṃ lokasṛṣṭaye \|*  
*atha tasya vacaḥ śrutvā śivo dīnasya vedhasaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*uvāca karuṇāmūrtirbhūtvā caṃdrārddhaśekharaḥ \|*  
*dattaḥ kālastava mayā puraiva na nivartyate \|\| 63 \|\|*

*kaṃ vā rāgādayo doṣā na bādheranprabhusthitam \|*  
*tasmāddūrasthito'pyetadaruṇācalasaṃjñitam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*bhajasva taijasaṃ liṃgaṃ sarvadoṣanivṛttaye \|*  
*vācikaṃ mānasaṃ pāpaṃ kāyikaṃ vā ca yadbhavet \|\| 65 \|\|*

*vinaśyati kṣaṇātsarvamaruṇācaladarśanāt \|*  
*pradakṣiṇā namaskāraiḥ smaraṇairarcanaiḥ stavaiḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*aruṇādrirayaṃ nṛṇāṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśanaḥ \|*  
*kailāse meruśṛṃge vā svasthāneṣu kalādriṣu \|\| 67 \|\|*

*saṃdṛśyaḥ kaścidevāhamaruṇādrirayaṃ svayam \|*  
*yacchṛṃgadarśanānnṝṇāṃ cakṣurlābhena kevalam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*bhavetsarvāghanāśaśca lābhaśca jñānacakṣuṣaḥ \|*  
*madaṃśasaṃbhavo brahmā svanāmnā brahmapuṣkare \|\| 69 \|\|*

*atra snātaḥ purā brahmanmoho'gājjagatīpateḥ \|*  
*snātvā tvaṃ brahmatīrthe māṃ samabhyarcya kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*maunī pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā viśvātmanbhava vijvaraḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

58-63a. Then the Lotus-born Lord became extremely humble and delighted in his heart. Then he bowed down to the 'Lord of Śoṇādri who is worthy of being resorted to:

‘Obeisance to you, the cause of the destruction of all sins, to the Lord wielding the Pināka bow. Obeisance to Śaṃbhu who has assumed the form of Aruṇācala and who is under the control of his devotees. Who, other than you, is competent to make his ignorant devotees refrain from misdeeds? This is impossible for (ordinary) persons to do. Destroy my physical body with your splendour because it has become sinful by (bad) intention. O Lord, the immanent soul of the universe, create another Brahmā for the purpose of the creation of the worlds.’

On hearing these words of Brahmā who was in a wretched condition, Śiva, the moon-crested Lord, the embodiment of mercy said:

63b-67a. ‘The period that has been formerly allotted to you cannot be changed or taken back. Which person in a position of power, defects such as Rāga (attachment) and others do not affect? Hence even if you are far way, worship this fiery Liṅga named Aruṇācala for dispelling all defects. All sins whether they are mental, verbal or physical perish quickly by visiting Aruṇācala. This Aruṇācala is destructive of all the sins of men through circumambulations, prostrations, recollections, worships and eulogies.

67b-71. I can rarely be seen in Kailāsa, peak of Meru or in my abodes on the various Kula mountains. I myself am Aruṇācala, on seeing the peak of which people will not only have the benefit of having their eyes but also the destruction of all sins and the acquisition of the vision born of knowledge.

Brahmā, born of a part of mine, formerly took his bath in Brahma Puṣkara named after him. Thereby the delusion of that Lord of the universe vanished. You too take your bath in this Brahma Tīrtha, worship me, keep your palms joined in reverence, keep silent and circumambulate me. O soul of the universe, you will become free from ailments.’

## \|\| 3.5.72 \|\|

*iti vacanamudīrya viśvanāthaṃ sthitamaruṇācalarūpato maheśam \|*  
*atha sarasi nimajya padmajanmā duritaharaṃ samapūjayatkrameṇa \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Maheśa, the Lord of the universe, remained in the form of Aruṇācala after uttering these words. The Lotus-born Lord had a plunge in the lake. He duly worshipped the Lord, the destroyer of sins.

## \|\| 3.5.73 \|\|

*imamaruṇagirīśameṣa vedhā yamaniyamādiviśuddhacittayogaḥ \|*  
*sphuṭataramabhipūjya sopacāraṃ gatadurito'tha jagāma cādhipatyam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. With his mind purified by means of the Yogic exercises of Yama, Niyama etc., the Creator duly worshipped the Lord of Aruṇācala clearly and with all requisite offerings and services. Thereby his sins being dispelled, he regained the lordship (of the universe).”

## Chapter 6 - Description of Various Holy Places at Aruṇācala

## \|\| 3.6.1 \|\|

*gautama uvāca \|*  
*purā nārāyaṇaḥ kalpe śayānaḥ salilārṇave \|*  
*śeṣaparyaṃkaśayane kadācinnaiva budhyata \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: This chapter tries to enhance the importance of Aruṇācala by showing in it the concentration of all important Tīrthas in the world. These Tīrthas are located on the way of the Parikramā or circumambulation of Aruṇācala.

Gautama said:

1\. Once upon a time, formerly, in another Kalpa, Nārāyaṇa was lying on his serpent couch in the vast ocean and he did not wake up.

## \|\| 3.6.2 \|\|

*tamasā pūritaṃ viśvamapajñātamalakṣaṇam \|*  
*vīkṣya kalpāvasāne'pi viṣedurnityasūrayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The eternal Sūris (i.e. great sages) saw that even at the end of the Kalpa the universe was enveloped in darkness, lying concealed and featureless. They were deeply grieved at this.

## \|\| 3.6.3 \|\|

*aho kaṣṭamidaṃ rūpaṃ tamasā viśvamohanam \|*  
*yena kalpāvasānepi viṣṇurnādyāpi budhyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. ‘Alas! the form of this darkness enchants and deludes the entire universe whereby even now at the end of the Kalpa, Viṣṇu does not get up.

## \|\| 3.6.4 \|\|

*jyotiṣaḥ puruṣaṃ pūrṇamapaśyaṃtaṃ surā api \|*  
*kathaṃ vā tamasaḥ śāṃtiṃ labheranparibhāvinaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When the perfect luminous Puruṣa cannot be seen, how can Suras get peace from the darkness that attacks (them)?’

## \|\| 3.6.5 \|\|

*iti niścitya manasā devadevamumāpatim \|*  
*ciṃtayāmāsurātmasthaṃ tejorāśiṃ niraṃjanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. After resolving thus in their mind they thought of the Lord of Umā, the Lord of Devas, the unsullied mass of refulgence, stationed in the Ātman.

## \|\| 3.6.6 \|\|

*tataḥ prasanno bhagavāṃstejorāśirmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*viśvāvanāya vijñaptaḥ praṇatairnityasūribhiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then Lord Maheśvara, the mass of refulgence, became pleased. He was requested to protect the universe by the eternal wise sages who bowed down.

## \|\| 3.6.7 \|\|

*tatastejomayācchaṃbhoḥ sphuliṃgāṃśusamudbhavāḥ \|*  
*udastaṃbhaṃta devānāṃ trayastriṃśacca koṭayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then thirty-three crores of Devas emanating from the rays of the flames of Śaṃbhu in the fiery form came forth.

## \|\| 3.6.8 \|\|

*bodhitaḥ sakalairdevaiḥ samutthāya ramāpatiḥ \|*  
*prabhātaṃ vīkṣya sakalaṃ manasyevamacintayat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On being awakened by all the Devas, the Lord of Ramā got up, found that it had completely dawned and thought thus in his mind:

## \|\| 3.6.9 \|\|

*mayā tamasi udrekādakāle śayanaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*prabodhāya paraṃ jyotiḥ svayaṃ dṛṣṭaḥ sadāśivaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. ‘Since Tamas (i.e. darkness) had predominated I slept at a wrong time. For the sake of waking me up Sadāśiva himself, the great luminary, had to be seen.

## \|\| 3.6.10 \|\|

*jagadutpattikṛtyāni svayaṃ kartuṃ vyavasyati \|*  
*kiṃ mayātra punaḥ kāryaṃ brahmaṇā vā svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He himself attempts to carry out the duties of creation of the universe. What other function has to be carried out by me in this matter or by the Self-born Lord Brahmā?

## \|\| 3.6.11 \|\|

*dhiṅmāṃ sthitamanātmajñaṃ nidrayā hṛtacetasam \|*  
*athavā sarvakartāraṃ śaraṇaṃ yāmi śaṃkaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Fie upon me who remained ignorant of the Ātman, with the mind overpowered by sleep! I shall seek refuge in Śaṅkara, the maker of all.

## \|\| 3.6.12 \|\|

*sarvadoṣapraśamanaṃ sarvābhīṣṭaphalapradam \|*  
*pavitramalpapuṇyānāṃ durlabhaṃ śaṃbhudarśanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The vision of Śaṃbhu quells all defects. It bestows all the desired benefits. It is sacred. It is difficult for the persons deficient in merit to get it.’

## \|\| 3.6.13 \|\|

*ciṃtayannevamātmasthaṃ jyotirliṃgaṃ sadāśivam \|*  
*praṇanāma harirbhaktyā devamaṣṭāṃgato muhuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Meditating thus on Sadāśiva, the fiery Liṅga stationed in the Ātman, Hari devoutly bowed to the Lord frequently with the eight limbs (touching the ground).

## \|\| 3.6.14-20 \|\|

*viśvasraṣṭāramīśānaṃ tuṣṭāva duritacchidam \|*  
*atha tejomayaḥ śaṃbhuḥ śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇāgatam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*anugṛhya kaṭākṣaistaṃ samuttiṣṭhetyabhāṣata \|*  
*utthāya karuṇāpūrṇaṃ śaṃbhuṃ caṃdrārddhaśekharam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*namastribhuvaneśāya trimūrtiguṇadhāriṇe \|*  
*tridevavapuṣe tubhyaṃ tridṛśe tripuradruhe \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tvameva jagatāmīśo nijāṃśairdevatāmayaiḥ \|*  
*kāryakāraṇarūpeṇa karoṣi svecchayā kriyāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*māṃ niyujya jagadguptau parimohya ca māyayā \|*  
*na doṣamuta saṃkalpaṃ vihātumapi necchasi \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kiṃ karomi jaganmūrttau nyastabhāro'smyahaṃ tvayi \|*  
*na doṣamīhase nūnamakālaśayanena mām \|\| 19 \|\|*

*hara śambho harerārtimanutāpaṃ samīkṣya saḥ \|*  
*ādideśa haraḥ śrīmānprāyaścittaṃ hareridam \|\| 20 \|\|*

14-20. Then Śaṃbhu in the form of refulgence, the Lord who was worthy of being sought refuge in, blessed (Lord Viṣṇu) who had sought refuge, by means of benign glances and spoke to him, “Get up.”

After getting up, he eulogized Śaṃbhu, the Lord who had created the universe, who dispelled sins, who was full of mercy and who had the crescent moon on his crest:

“Obeisance to the Lord of the three worlds, to the Lord who has three forms corresponding to the three Gūṇas. Obeisance to you with the body of the three Devas, to the Lord with three eyes, to the enemy of the three Puras.

You alone are the Lord of all worlds. You perform all acts through your own parts in the forms of Devas, by way of cause and effect.

You have engaged me in the act of protecting the universe, but you have deluded me by means of the Māyā. But you do not wish to eschew the defect (of Māya) or even the intention (viz. my assignment of protecting the world).

What shall I do? I have placed all the burden on you, the Lord having the universe for your form. You do not wish to find fault with me for this untimely sleep. O Hara, O Śaṃbhu, remove the agony and distress of Hari.” On seeing Han’s distress thus, the glorious Hara directed the expiation for Hari in this form:

## \|\| 3.6.21-24 \|\|

*aruṇācalarūpeṇa tiṣṭhāmi vasudhātale \|*  
*tasya darśanamātreṇa bhavitā te tamaḥ kṣayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*pūrvasmai viṣṇave tatra varo datto mayā purā \|*  
*tadaiva taijasaṃ liṃgamaruṇācala saṃjñitam \|\| 22 \|\|tejomayamidaṃ rūpaṃ praśāṃtaṃ lokarakṣaṇāt \|*  
*yadagnimayamavyaktamapāraguṇavaibhavam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*nadīnāṃ nirjharāṇāṃ ca meghamuktāṃbhasāmapi \|*  
*aṃtarjyotirmayatvena layastatraiva dṛśyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

21-24. “I stay on the surface of the earth in the form of Aruṇācala. Merely by visiting it, your Tamas will be destroyed.

To a previous Viṣṇu a boon had been granted by me formerly. It was at that time itself that this fiery Liṅga named Aruṇācala (came into being). For the purpose of protecting the worlds this effulgent form has become subdued and quiescent, since it is unmanifest and fiery as well as it has unlimited wealth of good qualities. Since it is internally fiery in form, the waters of the rivers, streams and those shed by clouds are seen merging with it.

## \|\| 3.6.25-26 \|\|

*aṃdhānāṃ dṛṣṭilābhena paṃgūnāṃ pādasaṃcaraiḥ \|*  
*aputrāṇāṃ ca putrāptyā mūkānāṃ vākpravṛttibhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sarvasiddhipradānena sarvavyādhivimocanaiḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpapraśamanairyatsarvavaradaṃ sthitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. It abides as the bestower of all Siddhis—such as regaining eyesight to the blind, the ability to walk on (one’s own) feet to the lame, begetting a son to the childless, ability to talk (fluently) to the dumb, conferment of all types of siddhis, dispelling all ailments and quelling of all sins.”

## \|\| 3.6.27 \|\|

*ityuktāṃtardadhe śambhurhariścaivāruṇācalam \|*  
*āgatya tapa āsthāya śoṇācalamupāsta ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After saying this, Śaṃbhu vanished. Hari came to Aruṇācala, performed penance and adored Śoṇācala.

## \|\| 3.6.28 \|\|

*tamadriṃ parito dṛṣṭvā surānkānanasaṃśrayān \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāmāśramānpuṇyānsthāpayāmāsa vai hariḥ \|*  
*vedānsāṃgopaniṣadānsamaṃtānmūrtidhāriṇaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After surveying the mountain all round, Hari made the Suras resort to the forests. He established the sacred hermitages of the sages. He established the Vedas along with their ancillary subjects and Upaniṣads all round, causing them to take up physical forms.

## \|\| 3.6.29 \|\|

*sasarja divyarūpāṇāṃ śatamapsarasāṃ kulam \|*  
*nṛtyairgītaiśca vāditraissevadhvamiti cādiśat \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He created a hundred families of celestial damsels with divine beautiful form and commanded them: “You serve (the Lord) by means of dances, songs, and instruments of music.”

## \|\| 3.6.30 \|\|

*snātvā brahmasarasyasminviṣṇuḥ kamalalocanaḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ cakārāmumaruṇādriṃ samarcitam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. After taking his holy dip in the Brahma lake, the lotuseyed Viṣṇu circumambulated the mountain Aruṇācala that was worshipped (by him).

## \|\| 3.6.31 \|\|

*apāpaḥ sarvalokānāmādhipatyaṃ ca labdhavān \|*  
*ramayā sahito nityamabhirūpasurūpayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He became free from sins and acquired the overlordship of all the worlds. He is always accompanied by Ramā who is beautiful, delightful and suitable to him.

## \|\| 3.6.32 \|\|

*bhāskarastejasāṃ rāśirasurairapi pīḍitaḥ \|*  
*brahmopadeśādānarca bhaktyāruṇagirīśvaram \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On the advice of Brahmā, Bhāskara (i.e. the Sun-god) who is a mass of refulgence but who was harassed by Asuras, devoutly worshipped the Lord of Aruṇācala.

## \|\| 3.6.33 \|\|

*nimajjya vimale tīrthe pāvane brahmanirmite \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ cakārainamaruṇārdri svayaṃprabhum \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After plunging into the sanctifying pure Tīrtha created by Brahmā, he circumambulated Aruṇācala, the Lord himself.

## \|\| 3.6.34 \|\|
