*madhudviṣā ca sa mahānmaṃḍūko'pi vilokitaḥ \|*  
*akhaṃḍamaṃḍalaṃ bhūmeryasya pṛṣṭhe pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. By the enemy of Madhu (i..e. Viṣṇu) that frog also was seen—the frog on whose back the entire sphere of the earth was established.

## \|\| 4.11.11 \|\|

*ādhāraśaktimapi tāmabhyapaśyadadhokṣajaḥ \|*  
*yadanugrahataḥ śeṣakūrmādyā api dhūrvahāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Adhokṣaja (i.e. Viṣṇu) saw that supporting Śakti also, by whose blessing Śeṣa, Kūrma (‘Tortoise’) and others are capable of bearing the burden.

## \|\| 4.11.12-13 \|\|

*atalaṃ vitalaṃ caiṣa sutalaṃ nitalaṃ tathā \|*  
*talātalaṃ ca pratalaṃ mahātalamiti kramāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dadarśa sapta pātālānapi vārijalocanaḥ \|*  
*tatratyānvividhākārānsarvānapi savismayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. The Lotus-eyed Lord (i.e. Viṣṇu) saw all the seven Pātālas, viz. Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Nitala, Talātala, Pātāla, and Mahātala in due order. With great wonder he saw all the residents of that place with diverse shapes and sizes.

## \|\| 4.11.14 \|\|

*atyagādbhogavatyākhyāṃ purīṃ vairocanīmapi \|*  
*jagāhenyāṃśca daityānāmāvāsānatigahvarān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He went beyond the city of the son of Virocana (i.e. Bali) named Bhogavatī. He went deeper into the other abodes of the Daityas deeper down in caves.

## \|\| 4.11.15 \|\|

*idaṃ dṛṣṭamidaṃ dṛṣṭamityupārūḍhakautukaḥ \|*  
*mūlaṃ mugdhāśayastasya vicinoti sma mādhavaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. ‘Oh! It is seen. Oh! It is seen.’ So thought Mādhava in his mind regarding the root. Like a person of immature mind he continued the search with his curiosity increasing (at every step).

## \|\| 4.11.16 \|\|

*adhastādapi gāḍhena payodhestena potriṇā \|*  
*tathaiva tejaḥstaṃbhaḥ sa nirvikāramavaikṣyata \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The boar penetrated far beneath the ocean, but the Column of Refulgence was seen just as before unaffected and unaltered.

## \|\| 4.11.17 \|\|

*dalitā kevalaṃ pṛṣvī pāthorāśirvilolitaḥ \|*  
*naivālokyata tanmūlaṃ kolarūpena viṣṇunā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Only the earth was rent and split; the ocean was shaken and stirred; but the root was not seen by Viṣṇu in the form of a boar.

## \|\| 4.11.18 \|\|

*itthaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi bhrāṃtyā saṃbhrāṃtamānasaḥ \|*  
*nālaṃ babhūva tanmūlaṃ līlākroḍo vilokitum \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After having wandered thus with extremely agitated mind (for thousands of years) Viṣṇu who had playfully assumed the form of a boar did not succeed in seeing its root.

## \|\| 4.11.19 \|\|

*avarugṇakhuraḥ kṣuṇṇadaṃṣṭro vidhvastavigrahaḥ \|*  
*bhagnapotraḥ sa bhūdāro jagāhe bahalaṃ śramam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. With his hoofs bent and broken, with his curved teeth pounded and crushed, with his body injured and shattered and with his snout impaired and fractured, that boar underwent a great deal of strain.

## \|\| 4.11.20 \|\|

*śrāṃtyā niśvasatastasya tādṛgdarpo viśṛṃkhalaḥ \|*  
*nanāśa tatkṣaṇātsākaṃ tanmūlāvekṣaṇecchayā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. With fatigue he began to gasp for breath. His original pride that had been unrestrained finished instantaneously along with his desire to search for the root of the Column of Refulgence.

## \|\| 4.11.21 \|\|

*anirvyūḍhapratijño'pi pratyāvartitumutsakaḥ \|*  
*na cakṣame sarojākṣaścalituṃ ca padātpadam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Though his vow had not been fulfilled, he was eager to return. But the Lotus-eyed Lord was not able to take even a single step.

## \|\| 4.11.22 \|\|

*śramāṃdhacakṣuṣastasya pātālāṃtaravarttinaḥ \|*  
*tatteja eva paṃthānaṃ punarapyudabhāvayat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Due to fatigue his eyes became blind. He was caught in the middle of Pātāla. But that Refulgence itself showed him the path.

## \|\| 4.11.23 \|\|

*kathaṃkathaṃciduttīrṇo 'pyakūpārādapārataḥ \|*  
*svedāṃbhaḥsāgarasrāve magno'bhūcchadmaśūkaraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With great difficulty he came out of the boundless ocean. But the boar in disguise (i.e. Viṣṇu) became drowned in the ocean of profuse sweat.

## \|\| 4.11.24 \|\|

*rajjveva tejaḥstaṃbhasya prabhayā sānubaddhayā \|*  
*labdhvācalaṃ vanaṃ kaṣṭaṃ nyavarttiṣṭa janārdanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The continuous lustre of the Fiery Column dragged him up as if by means of a rope. Janārdana returned with great difficulty to the immobile forest.

## \|\| 4.11.25 \|\|

*nāvaikṣi yanmayā mūlamamuṣya mahasāṃ nidheḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sraṣṭrāpi no dṛṣṭaḥ śirobhāgaḥ kathaṃcana \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. ‘Since the root of this Storehouse of Splendour has not been seen by me, the top region also could not at all have been seen by the Creator (i.e. Brahmā).

## \|\| 4.11.26 \|\|

*amuṣya mahasāṃ rāśeḥ prāgabhūdyatra saṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*tato nivṛttya yāsyāmi śaraṇaṃ śivamīśvaram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. I shall turn back and go to that place where previously this Mass of Splendour first manifested itself. I shall then seek refuge in Śiva.

## \|\| 4.11.27 \|\|

*sa hi viśvādhiko devaściraṃ mohāṃdhacakṣuṣā \|*  
*yadvismṛto mayā tasmāddurvipāko'janīdṛśaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Indeed, he alone is far superior to all. Since that Lord had been forgotten by me with my eyes blinded with delusion, such a great calmity as this has taken place with evil consequences.’

## \|\| 4.11.28 \|\|

*evaṃ vinirdhārya vimuktadarpo nivṛttavānāśu saroruhākṣaḥ \|*  
*tameva deśaṃ prababhūva yatra staṃbhaḥ sa tejomayatāṃ dadhānaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Deciding thus, the Lotus-eyed Lord got rid of his arrogance and returned to that place where that Column having excessive refulgence manifested itself.

## Chapter 12 - Brahmā’s Exploration of the Top of the Column of Splendour

## \|\| 4.12.1 \|\|

*naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*tatastejomayaṃ staṃbhamanusṛtya pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*utpapātonmukho vegānnirālaṃbe nabhastale \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:

1\. Then proceeding along the Column of Fire, Brahmā flew up speedily in the sky that has no support.

## \|\| 4.12.2 \|\|

*drutamutpatatastasya pakṣāvegena vāritāḥ \|*  
*vyaśīryata samudvartāḥ praṇunnā iva vāyubhiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. As he flew up rapidly the excess (of clouds) hit by the fluttering wings became scattered as though dispelled by winds.

## \|\| 4.12.3 \|\|

*sa vegādutpatandūraṃ nākṣṇorviṣayatāmagāt \|*  
*kevalaṃ dīrghadīrghaiva rekhā vyomni vyabhāvyata \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Flying rapidly to a great height, he could not be seen clearly by the eyes. Only a very (vertical) long line was seen in the sky.

## \|\| 4.12.4 \|\|

*māyāmarālo dadṛśe tejaḥstaṃbhasyapārśvataḥ \|*  
*saṃdhyāpayodharābhyarṇacārīva rajanīkaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Māyāmarāla (i.e. Brahmā who by his Māyā assumed the form of a swan) near the Column of Refulgence appealed like the moon going along and near the evening clouds.

## \|\| 4.12.5 \|\|

*prāgatyagādutpatatāṃ tato'dhvānaṃ payomucām \|*  
*vimānapadavīṃ paścāttārāvartaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. At the outset he went beyond the path of the birds, then beyond the path of the clouds, thereafter the path of the aerial chariots, and then the orbit of the stars.

## \|\| 4.12.6 \|\|

*tejasāṃ yāni dhāmāni hyatyuccānyūrdhvacāriṇām \|*  
*aticakrāma vegena tānyasau kuhanākhagaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. This bird in disguise (i.e. Brahmā) rapidly crossed all those lofty abodes of the luminaries going upwards.

## \|\| 4.12.7 \|\|

*maruto manaso vāpi javaḥ sūkṣmatarākṛteḥ \|*  
*so'bhūdadhaḥkṛtastena haṃsena gamanādinā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The speed of wind and mind of very subtle nature, shape and size was kept down (i.e. surpassed) by that swan while going.

## \|\| 4.12.8 \|\|

*yathāyathā cotpapāta sudūraṃ śramitacchadaḥ \|*  
*tathātathā ca dadṛśe tejaḥstaṃbhaḥ samunnataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The higher up he flew with the weary wings, the higher and higher appeared the Column of Refulgence.

## \|\| 4.12.9 \|\|

*atītya marutāṃ skaṃdhānsapta saṃprāptavismayaḥ \|*  
*bibhedāṃḍakaṭāhaṃ ca jvalaṃtaṃ tamudaikṣata \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After going beyond the seven pathways of the seven categories of winds he was dismayed much as he saw the Column burning and breaking through the semi-spheroidal top of the Cosmic Egg (and still higher up).

## \|\| 4.12.10-17 \|\|

*kathaṃ vā'dṛṣṭamūlasya sthātavyaṃ purato hareḥ \|*  
*avimocayataḥ śaurerasamāsamaśīrṣatām \|\| 10 \|\|*

*anirvyūḍhapratijñasya dīrghaiḥ kiṃ vā mamāsubhiḥ \|*  
*tadatraupayikaṃ kiṃ syātkāryaṃ kā mā gatirmama \|\| 11 \|\|*

*atisaṃdhitsato viṣṇuṃ kassahāyo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*ārjavaṃ naiva nirjetuṃ prativādinamakṣamaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*chadmanā vā tiraskuryānmānā hi mahatāṃ dhanam \|*  
*iti saṃcitayatyeva viriṃcau vyākulātmani \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ākāśe dadṛśe nātidūre kimapi nirmalam \|*  
*aiṃdavī kimiyaṃ rekhā tasyāḥ kathamihāgamaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yadvā mṛṇālaṃ tatsiṃdhau viyatyasyāṃ kutastu saḥ \|*  
*iti tasminsasaṃdehe nedīyastaṃ tadāgatam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*abodhi ketakībarhamiti rājīvajanmanā \|*  
*tatparyuṣitamapyudyatsaurabhaṃ vastuśaktitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*hiraṇyagarbho vimalamagṛhṇātketakacchadam \|*  
*gṛhītamātraṃ tenaitatsacaitanyaṃ kilābravīt \|\| 17 \|\|*

10-14a. He thought thus: ‘How will it be possible for me to stand in front of Hari who might have seen the root? (Proud of his success) Śauri (i.e. Viṣṇu) will not cease to keep his head turned away (from me) in a crooked manner.

Of what avail are my vital airs, though they be of long duration, since I have not fulfilled my vow? What shall be the proper thing to do now? What should be done? What help is there? I wish to deceive Viṣṇu. Who will help me? I am not at all capable of defeating my opponent through a straightforward course. One who cannot use a straightforward means should fraudulently surpass the opponent. Indeed honour is an asset unto great men.’ So thought Brahmā and became agitated in his mind. At that time something bright and pure was seen in the sky not very far away.

14b-17. Brahmā began to doubt like this: ‘Is this the outline of the moon? But how can it come here? Or is it a lotus stalk? That is in the river. How can it be in the sky?’ While he was doubting thus, it came very near. It was recognized as a Ketakī leaf (Pandamus odoratissimus) by the Lotus-born Lord. Though it was an old one it had much fragrance because of its inherent power. Brahmā caught hold of that Ketakī bunch. The moment it was caught it became alive and conscious. It spoke.

## \|\| 4.12.18 \|\|

*ketaka uvāca \|*  
*bho gṛhṇāsi kimarthaṃ tvaṃ muṃca māṃ viśramodyatam \|*  
*varṣāṇāṃ śatasāhasramutpatyaivaṃ vihāyasā \|\| 18 \|\|*

Ketaka said:

18\. Oh, why do you catch hold of me? Leave me off. I am inclined to take rest after having flown through the sky a hundred thousand years.

## \|\| 4.12.19 \|\|

*naṃdīśa uvāca \|*  
*tathā samedhamānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā śramamakhidyata \|*  
*aciṃtayatpadmasūtiratyaṃtaṃ vihatāśayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

Nandīśa said:

19\. On seeing his fatigue increasing in that manner, Brahmā became grieved. The Lotus-born Lord thought with a disappointed mind.

## \|\| 4.12.20-21 \|\|

*anirvyūḍhapratijñāvānnīcatāmapi saṃśritaḥ \|*  
*ākrāṃtarodovivaraḥ kva rāśistejasāmasau \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ahametatparīkṣāyāṃ kva paricchinna pauruṣaḥ \|*  
*bhajyete iva me pakṣau dṛśā cāṃdhāyate iva \|*  
*pradhvaṃsaṃta ivāṃgāni patāmīvāhamapyadhaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Since his vow had remained unfulfilled, he even stooped to despicable means: ‘Where is this Mass of Refulgence that has filled up the entire space in between heaven and earth? Where am I whose manliness has been finished (i.e. humiliated) in the course of this test? My wings seem to be breaking. The eyes have become blinded. All the limbs appear to be crumbling down. I seem to fall down headlong.

## \|\| 4.12.22 \|\|

*kiṃ vānyadbahunoktena saha niśvāsavāyubhiḥ \|*  
*mama prāṇāśca niyataṃ nirgacchaṃtīva sāṃpratam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Of what use is much talk on other topics? My vital breath appears (as if) coming out along with the wind exhaled now.

## \|\| 4.12.23 \|\|

*ahaṃkāramadagraṃthirayaṃ truṭatu cittataḥ \|*  
*mukuṃdena saha spardhā sā ca śīghṃ praṇaśyatu \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Let this knot of excessive pride snap and be dispelled from my mind. Let that unhealthy rivalry with Viṣṇu be terminated quickly.

## \|\| 4.12.24-27 \|\|

*yadeṣa rodaḥkuharapariṇāhādhikodyamaḥ \|*  
*aunnatyamayate'dyāpi tejastaṃbho yathā purā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tadasya tejasāṃ rāśernāhaṃ nārāyaṇo'thavā \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ dūrataścānye maheṃdrapramukhāḥ surāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ito notpatituṃ śaktirasti me tannivarttaye \|*  
*iti niścitya manasā vidhātā jātavismayaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pratyabhāṣata taṃ kastvaṃ kuto vā prāptavāniti \|*  
*sa ca pratyabravīdenaṃ vedhasaṃ ketakacchadaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. This Fiery Column it as lofty as it was ever before. In girth it is far more than the intervening space between heaven and earth. Neither Nārāyaṇa nor I can be the cause thereof. The possibility of the other Suras—the chief of whom is Mahendra—being so is still remote. I have no strength to fly up beyond this place, so I return.’

So decided Brāhmā within his mind. With some surprise he asked (the Ketaka Leaf): “Who are you? Whence are you coming?” That Ketakī Leaf replied to Brahmā:

## \|\| 4.12.28 \|\|

*ketakacchada evāsaṃ sacaitanyaḥ śivājñayā \|*  
*tejastaṃbhātmanaḥ śaṃbhorasya mūrdhni ciraṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. “I have (all along) been a bunch of Ketakī leaves. At the bidding of Śiva I remained on the head of Śaṃbhu of the form of the Column of Refulgence. I am sentient and conscious.

## \|\| 4.12.29-30 \|\|

*bhūloka icchayā vastuṃ tataḥ saṃprāptavānaham \|\| 29 \|\|*

*itthaṃ śrutvā ketakībarhavācaṃ labdhvāśvāsaṃ taṃ kilāṃbhojabhūtiḥ \|*  
*brūhi tvaṃ me tatkiyatyaṃtare vā tejaḥstaṃbhasyāgramityāvabhāṣe \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. I have come down from there with a desire to stay in the terrestrial world.”

On hearing these words of the Ketaka Bunch, the Lotus-born Lord got some relief. He asked it (i.e. Ketaka Bunch): “You do tell me how far is the top of the Column of Refulgence from here.”

## Chapter 13 - Brahmā Requests the Ketaka Bunch to Perjure

## \|\| 4.13.1-4 \|\|

*naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*ketakībarhamapyenaṃ vihasya punarabravīt \|*  
*ketakyuvāca \|*  
*api mūḍha na kiṃcittvaṃ vetsi kastvaṃ kuto na tat \|\| 1 \|\|*

*īdṛśyaḥ parito lagnā yasminbrahmāṃḍakoṭayaḥ \|*  
*tasya pramāṇametāvaditi ko vedituṃ kṣamaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*caturyugāyutairyātaṃ tato nipatato mama \|*  
*idānīmapi nāproti tanmadhyaṃ kila bhūtalam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*iti bruvāṇamenaṃ ca namaskṛtya sarojabhūḥ \|*  
*hitvā nijamahaṃkāramabhāṣata kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Naṇḍikeśvara narrated:

1 -4. The Ketaka Bunch laughed and spoke to him again:

## \|\| 4.13.5-6 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*mahātmansatyamevāsmi mūḍho'haṃ ketakacchada \|*  
*brahmaṇā hi mayā sparddhā viṣṇunā saha nirmitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dvābhyāmapīdamāvābhyāṃ vismṛtaṃ śivavaibhavam \|*  
*yannau mahānabhūdgarvassargasaṃtrāṇamātrataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

The Ketakī said:

O foolish one, you don’t know anything? Who are you? Whence have you (come)? Who is competent to know the dimensions and magnitude of that (Lord) round whom crores of Cosmic Eggs like this one, have been attached? Since I first began to fall off ten thousand sets of four Yugas have elapsed. Even now the middle of that (Column of Refulgence), i.e. the earth has not been reached.

As the Bunch of Ketaka spoke these words, the Lotus-born Lord bowed down to it. Giving up all his pride he spoke with palms joined in reverence:

Brahmā said:

5-6. O noble-souled Ketaka Bunch, it is true that I have been a stupid fellow. I, Brahmā, had a great rivalry with Viṣṇu. The greatness of Śiva had been forgotten by both of us. Merely because of (our ability of creation and protection of the universe) both of us were puffed up with excessive pride.

## \|\| 4.13.7 \|\|

*hrepaṇī saṃkathā tāvadāstāmadyāpyahaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*sparddhayā na vimukto'smi baddhayā garuḍadhvaje \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Even now I am not free from the rivalry with the Garuḍa-emblemed One. But let this shameful talk be left aside.

## \|\| 4.13.8-12 \|\|

*sakhyaṃ sāptapadīnaṃ hi kathyate tadbhavānmayi \|\| 8 \|\|*

*asaṃstutadhiyaṃ hitvā kartumarhasyanugraham \|*  
*ahaṃ viṣṇuśca mohāṃdhau tejaḥstaṃbhasya vīkṣaṇāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

*haṃsakolākṛtī dadhvo mithaḥ sāmyaṃ vyapohitum \|*  
*mūlaṃ didṛkṣuḥ sa daśāṃ kīdṛśīṃ yātavāniti \|\| 10 \|\|*

*na jāne mama cāsyāgraṃ didṛkṣorīdṛkṣī daśā \|*  
*gatamuḍḍīyamānasya me sahasreṇa hāyaneḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*jātaśramo'smi nitarāṃ viyujya iva cāsubhiḥ \|*  
*diṣṭyādya bhadra labdhastvaṃ mayā'laṃbovasīdatām \|\| 12 \|\|*

8-12. Friendship is said to be Sāptapadīna (‘formed when two people have walked together seven steps or talked together seven words’). So you do give up unworthy thought. It behoves you to do me a favour. Both Viṣṇu and I had been blind due to delusion. On seeing the Column of Refulgence, we wanted to dispel the notion of our equality (and decide as to who is superior). So we assumed the forms of a boar and a swan. He was desirous of finding out the root? I do not know as to what stage he has reached. But this is the plight of mine who am desirous of seeing the top (of this Column of Fire). A thousand years have passed since I first began to fly. I have become so utterly exhausted that I find as though I am parting with my life-breath. Fortunately, I have got you as the support of those who become frustrated.

## \|\| 4.13.13 \|\|

*tanme kuruṣva mitrasya saphalāṃ yācanāmimām \|*  
*sakhāhaṃ sahasaṃjalpādasmi dāsonuṣaṃjanāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Hence grant this request of mine who am your friend. I am your friend and companion because of mutual conversation. I am your slave because of your association with me.

## \|\| 4.13.14 \|\|

*tattvayā karaṇīyaivaṃ prārthanaiṣā kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*yadi paśyati mūlaṃ sa jito'hamamunā tadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. I have folded my palms in reverence (to you). This request (of mine) should therefore be carried out by you. If he (i.e. Viṣṇu) sees (i.e. happens to see) the root (of the Column of Fire), I am defeated by him.

## \|\| 4.13.15 \|\|

*yadvā na paśyati tadāpyasmi sāmyamupeyivān \|*  
*idaṃ dvayamapi prāyo mamātihrepaṇaṃ sakhe \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Or if he does not see, it comes to this that I am equal to him. Both these (alternatives), O friend, cause great shame to me.

## \|\| 4.13.16-20 \|\|

*tvayaiva parihāryatvamidānīṃ samupāgatam \|*  
*anṛtāmabhibhāṣa tvamucitāṃ ca suhṛtkṛte \|\| 16 \|\|*

*giramekāmimāmagre cakrapāṇerudīraya \|*  
*eṣa haṃsākṛtirbrahmā tejaḥstaṃbhasvarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*atyuccaṃ dṛṣṭavānagramatra sākṣye sthito'smyaham \|*  
*tenāpi tejaḥstambhatvameyuṣā candramaulinā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*saṃbhāvitoyaṃ sutarāṃ pitreva hi pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*ato'yamevābhyadhiko bhavato viṣṭaraśravāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ityuktvā mama sāhāyyaṃ sumahatkriyatāṃ tvayā \|\| 20 \|\|*

16-20. The avoidance of this situation (that would arise) is to be managed by you alone. For the sake of a friend utter a befitting lie; speak a word in front of the Discus-bearing Lord. “This Brahmā in the form of a swan has been to the highest point (of the Lord) in the form of the Column of Refulgence. I bear witness unto the same. This Pitāmaha (i.e. Brahmā) has been greatly honoured by that Moon-crested Lord who has assumed the form of a Column of Refulgence, as though he was his father. Hence, O Viṣṇu, he alone is superior to you.” Let this great help be rendered to me by you by kindly stating this.

## \|\| 4.13.21 \|\|

*naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ bhūyaḥ prārthito'yaṃ vidhātrā dākṣiṇyārdraḥ ketakībarhakopi \|*  
*tejaḥstaṃbhābhyarṇabhāje tathaiva prāhāśeṣaṃ viṣṇave brahmavākyam \|\| 21 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:

21\. Thus the Ketakī Bunch was repeatedly entreated by Brahmā. Being overwhelmed with kindness (to Brahmā), he told every word of what Brahmā had requested to Viṣṇu who was near the Column of Refulgence.

## Chapter 14 - Manifestation of Śaṅkara

## \|\| 4.14.1 \|\|

*naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*so'pi brahmāṇamudvīkṣya tāvatā dviguṇaṃ smayan \|*  
*nāgraṃ dṛṣṭamaneneti niścikāya vivekavān \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:

1\. Endowed with common sense and discrimination, he (i.e. Viṣṇu) looked at Brahmā smiling twice over and came to the conclusion that, the top (of the Column of Fire) had not been seen by him.

## \|\| 4.14.2 \|\|

*anugrahītuṃ māṃ mugdhaṃ haṃtuṃ cāsya vidhermadam \|*  
*devadevaḥ sa evālaṃ bhūtabhartetyamanyata \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He thought: ‘That Lord of Devas alone is competent to bless me, the immature, innocent one and to break the pride of this Brahmā. He is the protector and Lord of all living beings.

## \|\| 4.14.3 \|\|

*mūlasaṃdarśanāśaktyā tejaḥstaṃmbhasya me madaḥ \|*  
*vyapeta eva manye'dya yadbhaktistryaṃbake'jani \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Due to my inability to see the root of the Column of Refulgence, I think, my pride and arrogance has disappeared and devotion to the Three-eyed Lord has been generated.

## \|\| 4.14.4 \|\|

*stūyate vītagarvatvātsa idānīṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*yasya dakṣiṇavāmābhyāmaṃgābhyāṃ nau samudbhavau \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Since I am rid of haughtiness, that Maheśvara is being eulogized now, that Lord from whose right and left limbs we were born.

## \|\| 4.14.5 \|\|

*adyāpyavītagarvatvāllabdhvāsau kūṭasākṣiṇam \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbho māmevamatisaṃdhātumicchati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The pride of Brahmā has not been eradicated till now. Therefore, he has got a false witness. Thus Brahmā desires to deceive me.

## \|\| 4.14.6 \|\|

*tadadya sakalasyāpi duḥkhasyāpanaye kṣamaḥ \|*  
*sa eva śaraṇatvena prāptavyaḥ śaṃkaro mayā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Therefore, now that Śaṅkara alone should be sought as a refuge by me, because he is competent to dispel all miseries.

## \|\| 4.14.7 \|\|

*tathā kṛtāparādhasya kṛtaghnasya gurudruhaḥ \|*  
*tamṛte rakṣitā ko'nyastameva staumi śaṃkaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Except him (i.e. Śaṅkara) who else can be the protector of one who has perpetrated an offence, is ungrateful and malicious towards the elders? I shall eulogize (that) Śaṅkara.’

Viṣṇu prayed:

## \|\| 4.14.8 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*jaya pṛdhvīmayākāra jaya cāpomayākṛte \|*  
*jaya prabhākarākāra jayāmṛtakarākṛte \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Be victorious, O Lord, with the forms of Pṛthvī (i.e. element earth) and Āpaḥ (i.e. water). Victory to you, O Lord, in the form of Prabhākara (i.e. the Sun). Be victorious, O Lord, in the form of Amṛtakara (i.e. the Moon).

## \|\| 4.14.9 \|\|

*jaya vaiśvānarākāra jaya gandhavahākṛte \|*  
*jaya hotṛmayākāra jayākāśamayākṛte \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Be victorious, O Lord, in the form of Vaiśvānara (i.e. the fire). Be victorious, O Lord, in the form of the bearer of smell (i.e. the wind). Be victorious, O Lord, in the form of Hotṛ (i.e. the priest who performs sacrifice); be victorious, O Lord, in the form of Ether.

## \|\| 4.14.10 \|\|

*rakṣa māṃ triguṇātīta rakṣa māṃ kālavigraha \|*  
*rakṣa māmakṣayaiśvarya rakṣa māṃ karuṇākara \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Protect me, O Lord, who are beyond the three Guṇas; save me, O Lord, with the body of Kāla (i.e. Time or Death). Save me, O Lord, with inexhaustible prosperity; save me, O merciful one.

## \|\| 4.14.11 \|\|

*sraṣṭā tvaṃ sarvajagatāṃ rakṣitā sarvadehinām \|*  
*hartā ca sarvabhūtānāṃ tvāṃ vinaivāsti ko'paraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. You are the creator of all the worlds, the protector of all embodied beings. Excepting you who else is the annihilator of all living beings?

## \|\| 4.14.12 \|\|

*aṇūnāmapyaṇīyāṃstvaṃ mahāṃstvaṃ mahatāmapi \|*  
*antarbahistvamevaitajjagadākramya vartase \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. You are the minutest of all minute things. You are the greatest of all great ones. You alone occupy this universe both internally and externally (i.e. are both immanent and transcendent to the world).

## \|\| 4.14.13 \|\|

*nigamāstava niśvāsā viśvaṃ te śilpavaibhavam \|*  
*sa tvaṃ tvadīya evāsi jñānamātmā tava prabho \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Nigamas are your breaths. The universe is the magnificence of your craftsmanship. You belong to your own self and knowledge is your Ātman, O Lord.

## \|\| 4.14.14 \|\|

*amarā dānavā daityāḥ siddhā vidyādharā narāḥ \|*  
*prāṇinaḥ pakṣiṇaḥ śailāḥ śikhino'pi tvameva hi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The immortal ones, Dānavas, Daityas, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, human beings, living beings, birds, mountains and Śikhins (i.e. peacocks etc.)—all these are you alone.

## \|\| 4.14.15 \|\|

*svargastvamapavargastvaṃ tvamoṃkārastvamadhvaraḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ yogastvaṃ parā saṃvitkiṃ tvaṃ na bhavasīśvara \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. You are the heaven; you are salvation; you are Oṃkāra; you are Adhvara (‘sacrifice’). You are the Yoga-practice. You are the supreme consciousness, O Īśvara. What is it that you are not?

## \|\| 4.14.16 \|\|

*tvamādirmadhyamaṃtaśca tasthuṣāṃ jagmuṣāmapi \|*  
*kālasvarūpatāṃ prāpya kalayasyakhilaṃ jagat \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. You are the beginning, the middle, and the end of all mobile and immobile beings. Assuming the form of Kāla, you measure the entire universe.

## \|\| 4.14.17 \|\|

*pareśaḥ parataḥ śāstā sarvānugrāhakaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*sa eṣa me kathaṃkāraṃ sākṣādbhavati dhūrjaṭiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The one greater than the greatest, the chastiser, the Lord, blesses all. How shall this Śiva, Dhūrjaṭi, be directly visible to me?

## \|\| 4.14.18 \|\|

*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā śaraṇaṃ prāpto niḥśreyasamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*atha vā staumi taddhāma jātamātraṃ yathāmiti \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It is by seeing him and seeking refuge in him that one attains salvation. Or I shall eulogize that Refulgence that has occurred here in accordance with my intellect.

## \|\| 4.14.19 \|\|

*tacchrutvaiṣa kṛpāṃ kuryādavaśyaṃ sarvataḥ śrutiḥ \|*  
*iti niścitya vaikuṃṭhaḥ stotuṃ samupacakrame \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On hearing it the Lord with ears all round shall become kind.

After deciding thus Lo rd Viṣṇu began to eulogize.

## \|\| 4.14.20 \|\|

*tameva taijasaṃ staṃbhaṃ praṇamya parameśvaram \|*  
*ādimadhyāṃtarahitaṃ matvā taṃ jagadīśvaram \|*  
*haṭhāttena viraṃcena vāryamāṇopi sasmitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Viṣṇu bowed down to that Column of Refulgence as Parameśvara, considering him as the Lord of the universe, the Lord devoid of beginning, middle and end, though he was forcibly prevented by Viriñca (i.e. (Brahmā) smilingly.

## \|\| 4.14.21 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*jaya deva mahādeva vāmadeva vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*kālāṃtaka kratudhvaṃsinnīlakaṃṭheṃduśekhara \|\| 21 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

21\. Be victorious, O Lord Mahādeva, O bull-emblemed Vāmadeva, O destroyer of god of Death, O destroyer of the sacrifice, O blue-throated one, O Lord with the moon as the crest.

## \|\| 4.14.22 \|\|

*jaya śaṃbho śiveśāna śarva tryaṃbaka dhūrjaṭe \|*  
*smaravairinpurārāte sthāṇo bhava maheśvara \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Be victorious, O Śaṃbhu, O Śiva, O Īśāna, O Śarva, O three-eyed one, O Dhūrjaṭi, O enemy of god of Love, O enemy of the (three) Puras, O Sthāṇu, O Bhava, O Maheśvara.

## \|\| 4.14.23 \|\|

*jayeśa khaṃḍaparaśo śūlinpaśupate hara \|*  
*sarvajña bharga bhūteśa kapālinnīlalohita \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Be victorious, O Īśa, O Khaṇḍaparaśu, O trident-bearing one, O Paśupati, O Hara, O omniscient one, O Bharga, O Bhūteśa, O skull-bearing one, O Nīlalohita.

## \|\| 4.14.24 \|\|

*jaya rudra makhārāte pinākinpramathādhipa \|*  
*gaṃgādhara vyomakeśa girīśa parameśvara \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Be victorious, O Rudra, O Pināka-bearing one, O Lord of Pramathas, O holder of Gaṅgā, O Vyomakeśa, O Giriśa, O Parameśvara.

## \|\| 4.14.25 \|\|

*jaya bhīma mṛgavyādha kṛttivāsaḥ kṛpānidhe \|*  
*kṛśānuretaḥ kailāse nityameva hi vartase \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Be victorious, O Bhīma, O hunter of deer, O Lord wearing hides, O storehouse of mercy, O Lord having fire as semen virile, one who dwells on Kailāsa perpetually.

## \|\| 4.14.26 \|\|

*tvadājñayā marudrāti phaṇī vahati bhūbharam \|*  
*dīpyataḥ sūryaśaśinau brahmāṃḍaṃ plavateṃ'budhau \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It is at your behest that the Wind blows, the Serpent (i.e. Śeṣa) bears the burden of the earth; the Sun and the Moon shine and the Cosmic Egg floats in the ocean.

## \|\| 4.14.27 \|\|

*jyotīṃṣi saṃcaraṃte khe sarvaṃ tvacchāsanātprabho \|*  
*ahaṃ brahmā ca jagatāṃ sargasaṃtrāṇayoralam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. All the luminaries move about in the sky. O Lord, everything happens at your bidding. Brahmā and I are competent to create and sustain the universe.

## \|\| 4.14.28-31 \|\|

*vidhāya kalpase puṣṭyai sūte sasyāni medinī \|*  
*nākrāmaṃtyavyayaḥ sīmāṃ yacca tvanmahireva saḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*aṇimādimahāsiddhiniḥsādhāraṇavaibhavaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ tvāmamarairanyairupekṣe samabhiṣṭutam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*viśuktve vismarāmastvāṃ smarāmaḥ saṃkaṭepi ca \|*  
*na roṣo jātu bhakteṣu prasādaḥ sarvadaiva te \|\| 30 \|\|*

*yadā vidhitserbhaktiṃ tvaṃ yadā ca prāvṛṇoṣi tām \|*  
*mohabodhau tadā puṃsāṃ kalpete baṃdhamokṣayoḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

28-31. After creating (everything) you contribute to its nourishment; the earth gives birth to the plants; the oceans do not overflow the boundary. All these are (instances of) your greatness.

Great Siddhis such as minuteness etc. are the greatness (in you), not common to others. How can I neglect you who are eulogized by the Immortal Ones and others?

When we are devoid of worries, we forget you and remember you during difficulties. You entertain no anger towards the devotees. You are always gracious unto them.

When you cover up the desire to grant devotion, men are deluded and suffer bondage. When you grant them devotion, they have enlightenment and get salvation.

## \|\| 4.14.32 \|\|

*iti stutassāṃjalibaddhapāṇinā patiḥ paśūnāmatha cakrapāṇinā \|*  
*kṛtāpahāse ca sarojasaṃbhave madoddhate prādurabhūddayānidhiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On being eulogized like this by the Discus-bearing Lord with palms joined in reverence, the Lord of Paśus (i.e. individual souls), the storehouse of mercy appeared, though the Lotus-born One was deriding as he was haughty.

## Chapter 15 - Brahmā Prepares to Eulogize Śiva

## \|\| 4.15.1-8 \|\|

*naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*tejaḥstaṃbhaṃ vinirbhidya saṃdhyābhramiva caṃdramāḥ \|*  
*kailāsakūṭadhavalaṃ vṛṣendramadhitasthivān \|\| 1 \|\|*

*jaṭājūṭavatā bālacaṃdracūḍena maulinā \|*  
*kapālamālikāṃ vaidhīṃ srajaṃ cāragvadhī dadhat \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nāgakuṃḍalibhiḥ phālaphalakodbhāsilocanaiḥ \|*  
*paṃcabhirvadanairdīptaiḥ kṣveḍakalmāṣakaṃdharaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śūlaṃ kapālaṃ ḍamaruṃ sāraṃgaṃ paraśuṃ dhanuḥ \|*  
*khaṭvāṃgamamalaṃ khaḍgaṃ dorbhirnāgaṃ ca dhārayan \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śvasitoddhūlitākāro gajacarmottarīyavān \|*  
*sarvālaṃkārasaṃpannaḥ sarvadevairabhiṣṭutaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*paridhānīkṛtavyāghracarmā tābhyāmadarśi saḥ \|*  
*rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa ānaṃdaṃ nanartta nalinekṣaṇaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*na kiṃcidapi jānāno mumoha ca sarojabhūḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dṛśābhinaṃdya mādhavaṃ prasannayā maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*athodatiṣṭhipacca taṃ sahuṃkriyaścaturmukham \|\| 8 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:

1-6a. Bursting asunder the Column of Refulgence, the Lord manifested himself and was seen by both of them. He resembled the moon that breaks through the evening cloud and appears (in the sky). He was seated on a lordly bull white like the peak of Kailāsa. He had matted hair on his head with the (digit of the) rising moon as the crest. He wore a garland of skulls of demons and (also) of Āragvadha (Cassia fistula). He had five faces all having serpents as ear-rings, eyes shining on the broad foreheads and throats having the stain of poison. All the faces were bright. He held in his hands a trident, a skull, a Ḍamaru (drum), a deer, an axe, a bow, pure Khaṭvāṅga (i.e. skull-topped club), a sword and a serpent. Ash was sprinkled all over his body. The elephant-hide served as the upper garment for him. He was adorned with all ornaments. He was eulogized by all the Devas. He wore a tiger’s skin as his cloth. He was seen by them thus.

6b-8. On seeing that form of Bliss the Lotus-eyed Lord danced. Unable to understand anything, the Lotus-born Lord became confounded.

With his eyes indicating pleasure Maheśvara congratulated Viṣṇu and with an angry sound of Huṃ he lifted up the Four-faced Lord.

## \|\| 4.15.9 \|\|

*jagāda cādhikāritāmadādyuvāṃ samuddhatau \|*  
*na lajjitavyamatra vāmayaṃ kramo'dhikāriṇām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He said thus: “On account of pride due to your authority both of you had become vain and puffed up. You need not feel ashamed at this. This is the usual way of persons in authority.

## \|\| 4.15.10 \|\|

*parīkṣya vaibhavaṃ mama prabodhavānabhūddhariḥ \|*  
*ayaṃ na jātupadmabhūśchalanmano durātmavān \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After observing (critically) my greatness Hari became enlightened but not so in the case of this Lotus-born One who is of deceitful mind and is vicious.

## \|\| 4.15.11 \|\|

*aśāsi paṃcavaktratā yadopahāsito hyaham \|*  
*punaḥsvaputrikāratirmayaiṣa śikṣito'bhavat \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When I was laughed at for having five faces, he was chastised. Then he indulged in sexual dalliance with his own daughter and he was punished by me.

## \|\| 4.15.12 \|\|

*tṛtīya eṣa maṃturapyaho kathaṃ nu sahyate \|*  
*tadasya tu pratiṣṭhayā kvacinna bhūyatāṃ vidheḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. How can this third offence be endured? Therefore, let there not be any installation of Brahmā anywhere.

## \|\| 4.15.13 \|\|

*ayaṃ ca ketakacchado yadāpa kūṭasākṣitām \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ na jātu tanmamaitu mūrdhni saṃsthitim \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. This Ketaka Bunch gave false evidence. Never again hereafter shall it be placed on my head.”

## \|\| 4.15.14 \|\|

*śaptvaivametau giriśaḥ prītyā viṣṇumabhāṣata \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After cursing those two Giriśa spoke affectionately to Viṣṇu:

## \|\| 4.15.15-16 \|\|

*śrīmaheśvara uvāca \|*  
*vatsa mā bhaiḥ prasanno'smi bhavate bhaktiśāline \|*  
*nanu tvamaṃgānme jātassāttviko'si viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*māheśvarāgragaṇyo'si jagatyāṃ hi yathā purā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*na tavātaḥ paraṃ jātu bhaktihānirbhavenmayi \|*  
*pratikṣaṇaṃ varddhamānā kalpate ca vimuktaye \|\| 16 \|\|*

Śrī Maheśvara said:

15-16. O dear one, do not be afraid. I am pleased with you who are endowed with devotion. Indeed you are bora of my person. You are particularly Sāttvika. As before you are the foremost among the devotees of Maheśvara all over the world. Henceforth you will never be deficient in devotion to me. Devotion that increases every moment is conducive to salvation.

## \|\| 4.15.17 \|\|

*ityanugrahakṛtaṃ trilocanaṃ bhaktibhāji nirahaṃkriye harau \|*  
*bhītimānavanataḥ svayaṃ vidhiḥ stotumārabhata klṛptavaṃdanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When the Three-eyed Lord granted his blessings to Hari who was devoid of pride and equipped with devotion, Brahmā became frightened. After making due obeisance and bowing down he began to eulogize.

## Chapter 16 - Description of the Temple of Aruṇācala by Brahma and Viṣṇu

## \|\| 4.16.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*devadeva tavaiśvaryaṃ kena śakyeta veditum \|*  
*vinā bhāyaikyasulabhaṃ bhavadīyamanugraham \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

1\. O Lord of Devas, by whom can your glory and supernatural power be comprehended without your blessing which is easily accessible only through good fortune?

## \|\| 4.16.2 \|\|

*akartṛkāṇi vākyāni aiśvaryaṃ te niratyayam \|*  
*na stotuṃ śakyate kiṃ tu namaskurvaṃti dūrataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Words have no makers. Your supreme glory is faultless. It is not possible to eulogize you. They salute (you only) from a distance.

## \|\| 4.16.3 \|\|

*ko viṣṇuḥ ko'hamete vā dikpālā vāsavādayaḥ \|*  
*tvameva deva karttāsi jagatsṛjanarakṣayoḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Who is Viṣṇu? Who am I? Who are these Guardians of the Quarters beginning with Indra? You alone, O Lord, are the cause of creation and preservation of the universe.

## \|\| 4.16.4 \|\|

*patistvaṃ pārvatīnātha paśavo vayamapyamī \|*  
*baddhaṃ pāśena moktuṃ vā tvamevāsmānpragalbhase \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O Lord of Pārvatī, you are Pati (i.e. overlord). All of us are Paśus (i.e. animals, individual souls). You alone are competent to bind us with Pāśa (‘noose’) or to liberate us (from Saṃsāra).

## \|\| 4.16.5 \|\|

*ṣaḍviṃśattattvarūpastvamabhitaścābhivarttase \|*  
*kovidaḥ ko vinirṇetuṃ tava yāthātmyamīśvaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. You are of the nature of the twenty-six principles. You pervade all. O Īśvara, who is intelligent enough to ascertain your real nature?

## \|\| 4.16.6 \|\|

*kirātaḥ kila devastvaṃ sārameyaiḥ kilāgamaiḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍvargahiṃsrānsaṃhartuṃ karoṣyākheṭakautukam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Lord, you are indeed a Kirāta (‘Hunter’). With the help of the Āgamas as hounds, you indulge in the pastime of hunting in order to kill the wild animals, viz. the Ṣaḍvarga (‘the six bad qualities’, e.g. anger, lust etc.).

## \|\| 4.16.7 \|\|

*deva dakṣādhvare pūrvaṃ varibhadrastvadājñayā \|*  
*kāṃkāṃ śikṣāmakārṣīnna iti kāpi viḍambanā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Lord, formerly in the course of the sacrificial rite of Dakṣa Vīrabhadra reprimanded and punished us in different ways at your bidding.

## \|\| 4.16.8 \|\|

*tava kālāgnirūpasya sarvabrahmāṃḍadāhinaḥ \|*  
*poṣaṇātpuṣpacāpasya prāyo jihveti śemuṣī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Lord, you assumed the form of Kālāgni (‘destructive fire at the end of the world’) to burn down the entire Cosmic Egg. I have nourished and nurtured the god of Love and my intellect generally feels ashamed of it.

## \|\| 4.16.9 \|\|

*kṛtāparādhaḥ śūlena tvayā dīrṇo jalaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*antakoṃdhakadaityaśca prativīraśca ko'sti te \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Jalandhara who was guilty of an offence, was pierced and torn asunder by you by means of your trident. Antaka (i.e. god of Death) and Andhaka, a Daitya, were also (similarly punished). Who can be an opponent unto you?

## \|\| 4.16.10 \|\|

*adhārayiṣyatkaṇṭhena kālakūṭaṃ na cedbhavān \|*  
*kathaṃ ca dhārayiṣyāmo vayaṃ sarve'pi jīvitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If you had not retained the Kālakūṭa poison in your throat, how could we have sustained our lives?

## \|\| 4.16.11 \|\|

*devadāruvane pūrvaṃ munīnkevalakarmaṭhān \|*  
*prakṣobhya dhūrtaveṣastvaṃ dayayānvagrahīstathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Formerly, in the Devadāru (‘Himalayan Cedar’) forest, you assumed the guise of a knave. You stirred up and excited the sages exclusively devoted to the path of Karman and later blessed them on account of your kindness.

## \|\| 4.16.12 \|\|

*aṃghriṇākrāṃtavānno cedatyugrāṃ tvamapasmṛtim \|*  
*tayākrāṃtamidaṃ kṛtsnamaṃdhakārāyate jagat \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. If you had not attacked and kicked with your foot the exceedingly terrible evil spirit of Apasmṛti (‘Oblivion’), this entire universe would have been overwhelmed by it and would have been plunged in darkness.

## \|\| 4.16.13 \|\|

*ardhanārīśvaraṃ rūpaṃ tvayā cenna prakāśitam \|*  
*prabhavāmi kathaṃ sraṣṭuṃ jagadetaccarācaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. If you had not revealed your half-woman-half-man form, how could I have proceeded with the activity of creation of the universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings?

## \|\| 4.16.14 \|\|

*bhavatā staṃbhitaḥ śambho saṃraṃbhājjaṃbhajidbhujaḥ \|*  
*kiyaṃtaṃ haṃta kālaṃ te jayastaṃbha iva sthitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. With great wrath, O Śaṃbhu, the arm of the conqueror of Jaṃbha (i.e. Indra) was kept stunned and paralysed by you. For long it remained rigid like the column of your victory!

## \|\| 4.16.15 \|\|

*bhikṣoḥ kapālamāpūrya rudhireṇātmano hariḥ \|*  
*śūlenotkṣipya mumuhe hyetattvamavadhāraya \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After filling the skull of the mendicant with his own blood and lifting him up with a spear Hari swooned. Remember this.

## \|\| 4.16.16 \|\|

*na cedaśikṣayaḥ sarvaśastrāstrāṇyanukaṃpayā \|*  
*nirvāpayetkathaṃ vairaṃ kruddhopi jamadagnibhūḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. If out of sympathy you had not instructed and trained him in wielding all the weapons and missiles, how could the son of Jamadagni (i.e. Paraśurāma) have taken revenge, though he was exceedingly furious?

## \|\| 4.16.17 \|\|

*nṛhariṃ śarabhākāraḥ samahārṣīnna cedbhavān \|*  
*sa eva saṃharedviśvaṃ hiraṇyakaśiporapi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If you had not killed Nṛhari (Man-lion) by assuming the form of a Śarabha (i.e. a fabulous eight-footed animal) alone, he would have destroyed the universe like Hiraṇyakaśipu.

## \|\| 4.16.18 \|\|

*tvamācakṛkṣaḥ kalpābdhau kaivartto matsyakacchapau \|*  
*hariṃ baddhvāhirāṭsūtrairnṛsiṃhamatha sūkaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In the ocean at the end of the Kalpa you were the boatman who dragged Hari in the forms of Fish, Tortoise, Boar and Man-lion after binding him with the king of serpents for cords.

## \|\| 4.16.19 \|\|

*ekone padmasāhasre svanetreṇa kṛtārcanam \|*  
*śūlinsudarśanaṃ dattvā daityadviṣamatūtupaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When (the heap of) a thousand lotuses was short by one, the enemy of the Daityas (i.e. Viṣṇu) concluded (your) worship with one of his eyes (as the wanting one-thousandth lotus). O Trident-bearing Lord, you gave him the discus Sudarśana and satisfied him.

## \|\| 4.16.20 \|\|

*naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*stutyaivamasya viṣṇośca prārthanena prasedivān \|*  
*dhūrjaṭiḥ sṛṣṭikartṛtvaṃ punarasyābhyamanyata \|\| 20 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:

20\. On account of his eulogy and the prayer of Viṣṇu, Dhūrjaṭi became pleased and permitted him to resume (his) creative activity.

## \|\| 4.16.21 \|\|

*samaṃjyāsu dvijānāṃ ca pūjanaṃ cānuśiṣṭavān \|*  
*ubhāvapyabravīdetau vātsalyāccadraśekharaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He ordained the worship (of Brahmā) by Brāhmaṇas in the sacrificial assemblies. With great affection, the Moon-crested Lord spoke to both of them:

## \|\| 4.16.22 \|\|

*śrīśiva uvāca \|*  
*vatsau yuvāṃ na jñātvaivaṃ bhūyo bhavatamuddhatau \|*  
*guruṃ smarato māmeva jāgrataṃ sṛṣṭirakṣayoḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

Śrī Śiva said:

22\. My dear ones, do not be haughty hereafter due to ignorance. Remember me, your sire. Be watchful in the activities of creation and protection.

## \|\| 4.16.23 \|\|

*iha pradeśe yuvayoryanmayānugrahaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*puṇyakṣetramidaṃ puṃsāṃ tato mokṣāya kalpatām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Since I have blessed you both in this place, let this holy spot be competent to give liberation to men.

## \|\| 4.16.24 \|\|

*yojanatrayamātre'sminkṣetre nivasatāṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*dīkṣādikaṃ vināpyastu matsāyujyaṃ mamājñayā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In regard to the men staying at this holy spot to the extent of three Yojanas (i.e. 36 kms.), at my bidding, let them have Sāyujya form of liberation even without the requisite initiation.

## \|\| 4.16.25 \|\|

*yadvā tiraścāmapyatra sthāvarāṇāṃ ca dehinām \|*  
*abuddhipūrvikā buddhirapavargasya jāyatām \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Or, may all the embodied souls, mobile and immobile beings here, have the spontaneous knowledge leading to salvation.

## \|\| 4.16.26 \|\|

*nṛṇāṃ ca darśanāddūre kaivalyaṃ smaraṇena vā \|*  
*astu vedāṃtavijñānaṃ na sādhyaṃ niṣprayāsataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Let men have salvation by means of the vision (of this place) from afar or by means of recollection (as) the perfect knowledge enshrined in the Vedānta cannot be achieved without great effort.

## \|\| 4.16.27 \|\|

*śubhāya taijasī mūrtiḥ sthāvarā mama śāśvatī \|*  
*aruṇādririti khyātā nityamevātra varttatām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Let this perpetual and immobile Fiery Form of mine, famous as Aruṇādri, be present here forever.

## \|\| 4.16.28 \|\|

*yugātyayepi nainaṃ tu majjayeyurmahābdhayaḥ \|*  
*na cālayeyurmaruto na daheyuśca vahnayaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Even at the close of the Yugas the great oceans shall not submerge it, the winds shall not shake it and the fires shall not burn it.

## \|\| 4.16.29 \|\|

*jyotirmayamidaṃ liṃgaṃ jyotiḥṣvapi na jātucit \|*  
*kramaṃtā nirgamāgatyā khecarāṇi samaṃtataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. This Liṅga is of the nature of refulgence. Let it not be merged with the luminaries. In the course of their transit inward and outward, let the heavenly bodies move round it.

## \|\| 4.16.30 \|\|

*yasyānugrahamicchāmi jaṃto्tasyātra saṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*dehāṃte kalpatāṃ muktyai vinaupaniṣadīrgiraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Should I wish to bless any creature, let it be born here. At the time of death let it be competent to attain liberation without the words (i.e. teachings) of the Upaniṣads.

## \|\| 4.16.31 \|\|

*eṣa dūrātpraṇāmena nikarṣācca pradakṣiṇāt \|*  
*api pāpātmanāṃ puṃsāmastu niśreyasapradaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Let this holy place be the bestower of salvation on men of evil, sinful souls, through obeisance, if they are far off, and through circumambulation, if they are nearby.

## \|\| 4.16.32 \|\|

*atraiva niyataṃ vāsāḥ saṃbhavaṃti mahātmanām \|*  
*tasmātsthalamidaṃ hitvā na gaṃtavyaṃ kadācana \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The abodes of noble-souled men shall invariably be here. Hence you shall never leave off this holy spot and go.

## \|\| 4.16.33 \|\|

*śoṇācalamanādṛtya kvacitsthitvāpi muktaye \|*  
*tasmādyuvāṃ vidhiharī vasataṃ cātra nityaśaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Shall there be salvation by staying anywhere else after disregarding Śoṇācala? Hence, O Brahmā, O Hari, both of you reside here permanently.

## \|\| 4.16.34 \|\|

*naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*ityuktavaṃtaṃ kāmāriṃ praṇamya vidhimādhavau \|*  
*tau vyajñāpayatāṃ devaṃ dūrībhavadahaṃkriyau \|\| 34 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:

34\. After bowing down to the enemy of the god of Love who said thus, Brahmā and Viṣṇu intimated to him (as follows) with all their haughtiness receding to the background:

## \|\| 4.16.35 \|\|

*vidhimādhavāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*evametajjagadādhāra jagadādhāratāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*āstāṃ girirasau kiṃ tu tejo hyasya sudussaham \|\| 35 \|\|*

Vidhi and Mādhava (Brahmā and Viṣṇu) said:

35\. If it has to be so, O support of the universe, let this mountain remain as the support of this universe. But this brilliance is unbearable.

## \|\| 4.16.36 \|\|

*atoyamuttamo rudra tejaḥ sāmānyaśailavat \|*  
*tiṣṭhatvabhedyamahimā niśreyasamahākhaniḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Hence it is better, O Rudra, that its refulgence be like that of an ordinary mountain. Let it stand with indivisible (i.e. perfect) greatness. Let it be the great mine of salvation.

## \|\| 4.16.37 \|\|

*vivṛṇoti nijaṃ jyotirviśvasyāsya samṛddhaye \|*  
*pratyabdaṃ kārttike māsi kṛttikāsu dinātyaye \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. It discloses its own inherent brilliance and refulgence for the sake of the prosperity of this universe once every year in the month of Kārttika at the close of the day of the constellation Kṛttikā (i.e. on the full-moon night).

## \|\| 4.16.38 \|\|

*śarmadopi nṛṇāṃ deva śoṇādristava śāsanāt \|*  
*mahattvādarcituṃ śakyo na syādbhaktasya kasyacit \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Although, at your bidding, O Lord, the Śoṇādri is the bestower of happiness on men, it cannot be worshipped by any devotee on account of its huge size.

## \|\| 4.16.39 \|\|

*etasyopatyakāyāṃ tadadyārabhyāsmadarthanāt \|*  
*devena sannidhātavyamavanyāṃ liṃgarūpiṇā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Hence, beginning from today at our request our Lord should be present in the form of a Liṅga on the ground over the tableland of this (mountain).

## \|\| 4.16.40 \|\|

*taccāruṇagirīśānamāvāmārādhayāvahe \|*  
*abhiṣekānulepādyairupacārairyathāvidhi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. We too shall worship that Lord of Aruṇagiri by means of ablutions, application of unguents and other forms of service in accordance with the injunctions.

## \|\| 4.16.41 \|\|

*saṃtyatra keśarāścūtā nāgapuṃnāgakesarāḥ \|*  
*āragvadhāḥ kurabakā mālūrāḥ pāṭalā api \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Here there are (the following trees): Kesaras (Rottleria tinctoria), Cūtas (Mango trees), Nāgas (Mesua Roxburghii), Punnāgas (Mallotus philippinensis), Āragvadhas (Cassia fistula), Kurabakas (a kind of Barleria), Mālūras (Feronia elephantum) and Pāṭalas (Trumpet flowers).

## \|\| 4.16.42 \|\|

*atraiva sannidhātavyaṃ devadeva dayānidhe \|*  
*yatastvadbhaktidārḍhyaṃ nau bhavatāttvadupāsanāt \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O Lord of Devas, you must be present here itself, O storehouse of mercy, since by worshipping you we shall attain further firmness in our devotion to you.

## \|\| 4.16.43-44 \|\|

*nānyathā cittaśuddhirnnau deve'pyevaṃ praseduṣi \|*  
*anādyavidyāvṛtaye yo bhaviṣyati nityaśaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*śoṇādreḥ pūrvadigbhāge sa eṣa bhṛśamunnataḥ \|*  
*sa evālaṃ nivāsāya devasya hṛdayaṃgamaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Otherwise our minds cannot be pure even when your Lordship are pleased thus. There is a sufficiently lofty place on the east of Śoṇādri. It shall be conducive to the cessation of the primordial Avidyā perpetually. That alone will be a delightful befitting abode of the Lord.

## \|\| 4.16.45-46 \|\|

*sāṃgavedā dharmaśāstraṃ purāṇāni śivāgamāḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā ca sakalāḥ proktā bhavataiva bhavāvayoḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*niśreyasāya bhaktānāṃ tvayaiva gururūpiṇā \|*  
*aṣṭāviṃśatirākhyātā āgamāḥ śaivasaṃjñitāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. The Vedas with their ancillary subjects, Dharmaśāstras, Purāṇas, Śivāgamas—all these were composed by you and promulgated to us by you, O Bhava. For the sake of the welfare of the devotees, for the sake of their liberation the twenty-eight Āgamas designated as Śaivas have been narrated by you alone iṇ the form of preceptor.

## \|\| 4.16.47 \|\|

*teṣu kasya prakāreṇa kurvāṇau tvadupāsanām \|*  
*kadāpyajñānajāmārtiṃ nādhigacchāva śaṃkara \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Among them which procedure shall we follow in worshipping you, so that, O Śaṅkara, we shall never suffer from the agony and distress born of ignorance.

## \|\| 4.16.48 \|\|

*naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*iti tau dhātṛgoviṃdau pādapadmāvalaṃbinau \|*  
*jagāda karuṇāmūrttirjagatībhṛtsutāpatiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:

48\. The Lord of the daughter of the Mountain, the embodiment of kindness, then said thus to Brahmā and Viṣṇu who resorted to his lotus-like feet:

## \|\| 4.16.49 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*yuktamuktamidaṃ bhadrau mayāpyevaṃ manīṣitam \|*  
*kāmikoktena mārgeṇa māmarcayitumarhathaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

Śrī Mahādeva said:

49\. O gentle ones, what is proper has been spoken (i.e. asked by you). It has been desired by me (to say) also. You two deserve to worship me by the method described in the Kāmika (Āgama).

## \|\| 4.16.50 \|\|

*mohato vismṛtā manye bhavadbhyāṃ śaivasaṃhitā \|*  
*adhunā matprasādena punarudbhāsatāṃ hṛdi \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. I think, due to delusion the Śaivasaṃhitā has been forgotten by both of you. Now let it shine once again in your hearts by my favour.

## \|\| 4.16.51 \|\|

*nandīśa uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā śrīśavāgīśau giriśo'ntaradhādatha \|*  
*tadā prādurabhūttatra liṃgaṃ kimapi maṃgalam \|\| 51 \|\|*

Nandīśa said:

51\. After saying thus to Viṣṇu and Brahmā Giriśa vanished. Then there appeared a certain auspicious Liṅga there.

## \|\| 4.16.52 \|\|

*taccāvalokya sāścaryyau mukundakamalāsanau \|*  
*muhuḥ praṇamya sānaṃdaṃ prārcya tuṣṭuvatuściram \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. On seeing it Mukunda and the Lotus-seated Lord (i.e. Brahmā) experienced a great surprise. Bowing down repeatedly with great pleasure, they worshipped and eulogized it for a long time.

## \|\| 4.16.53 \|\|

*tāvakārayatāṃ śoṇagirināthasya cālayam \|*  
*nānāśilpādbhutaṃ viśvakarmaṇā pracayena ca \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. They caused a temple of the Lord of Śoṇagiri to be built by Viśvakarmā and a multitude (of other craftsmen). It was a wonderful temple with a variety of ornamental architecture.

## \|\| 4.16.54 \|\|

*khānayāmāsatustatra saraḥ kimapi pāvanam \|*  
*abhiṣekāya devasya sarvatīrthamayaṃ navam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. For the sake of the ablution of the Lord they caused a sacred lake to be dug there. It was fresh and full of (the water of) all the (other) Tīrthas.

## \|\| 4.16.55 \|\|

*aruṇākhyaṃ puraṃ cārātkalpayāmāsatuściram \|*  
*siddhyai notkaṃṭhate labdhvā kailāsāyāpi dhūrjaṭiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Nearby they built a city named Aruṇa for the sake of spiritual achievement. On getting this Dhūrjaṭi does not yearn even for Kailāsa.

## \|\| 4.16.56 \|\|

*tasyāṃ brahmarṣayo devā gaṃdharvā divyayoṣitaḥ \|*  
*siddhavidyādharā yakṣāḥ pauratvaṃ samupāyayuḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In that, city Brahminical sages, Devas, Gandharvas and celestial damsels, Siddhas, Vidyādharas and Yakṣas became citizens.

## \|\| 4.16.57-59 \|\|

*tīrthāni dhārya kūpatvaṃ gaṃgādyāḥ saritastathā \|*  
*naṃdanādīni ca vanānyabhavanniṣkuṭatvataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*goloko gogoṣṭhatayā naigamatvaṃ kilāgamāḥ \|*  
*śailāśca gopurāditvaṃ smṛtayo vidhitāṃ yayuḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*bhūtāḥ pretāḥ piśācāśca vetālāḥ kaṭapūtanāḥ \|*  
*prapannā mānuṣaṃ dehaṃ tasyāṃ kila pṛthagjanāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-59. The Tīrthas and the rivers beginning with Gaṅgā assumed forms of wells. The heavenly parks beginning with Nandana assumed forms of kitchen gardens. Goloka assumed forms of cowpens; Āgamas, that of the Nigamas; the mountains assumed forms of ornamental gateways of the temples; and Smṛtis, forms of codes of conducts. Bhūtas, Pretas, Piśācas, Vetālas, Kaṭapūtanas etc. assumed human bodies and became laymen in that city.

## \|\| 4.16.60-69 \|\|

*devopi dhūrjaṭistasyāṃ kautukī siddharūpadhṛk \|*  
*yogitvaṃ samupāsthāya mātrākaupīnamuṇḍadhṛk \|\| 60 \|\|*

*na kenacidavijñātaḥ sadā sarvatra dīpyati \|*  
*tau ca keśavalokeśau jaṭilau bhasmaguṇṭhitau \|\| 61 \|\|*

*dāṃtau śoṇādrināthaṃ tamarcayāmāsatuściram \|*  
*tatratyānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ varṇānāmānuguṇyataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*dīkṣādikāni cakrāte svayamācāryatāṃ gatau \|*  
*krameṇa hṛtanirmālyau sarvāgamarahovidau \|\| 63 \|\|*

*prātaḥ snātvā samāhṛtya puṣpapatrādikaṃ phalam \|*  
*maṃtraṃ cāruṇanāthasya tata eva rahaḥ śrutam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*jaṃjalpākau jajapatuḥ sarvamaṃtrādhikaṃ sadā \|*  
*dhūpapradīpanaivedyairgītavāditranartanaiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*pradakṣiṇānamaskārairmudrābaṃdhairnavairnavaiḥ \|*  
*āsanena ca mūrttyā ca mūlena ca yathāvidhi \|\| 66 \|\|*

*paṃcabrahmaṣaḍaṃgādyairarcayāmāsatuḥ śivam \|*  
*evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi ṣoḍaśāruṇaśaṃkaram \|\| 67 \|\|*

*vedhoviṣṇū samārādhya śivajñānamavāpatuḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*itīdamaśrāvi mayā rahasyaṃ pituḥ śilādasya mukhātpurā yat \|*  
*niveditaṃ cādya tadeva tubhyaṃ kimanyadākarṇayituṃ manīṣā \|\| 69 \|\|*

60-63a. Even Lord Dhūrjaṭi eager to live there assumed the form of a Siddhayogin wearing only a loin cloth and a topless piece of stick. He is not recognised by anyone but he shines everywhere. Viṣṇu and Brahmā wore matted hair and applied sacred ash over their bodies. With perfect control over their sense-organs, they worshipped the Lord of Śoṇādri for a longtime. They themselves became preceptors, and performed the rites of initiation etc. to the people there belonging to all the castes in accordance with their merits.

63b-67a. Conversant with the esoteric doctrines of all the Āgamas, they duly performed all the rites. They took away the remnants of the previous day’s worship. They took their bath in the morning, fetched flowers, leaves, fruits etc. and garrulously repeated the Mantra of Aruṇanātha that had been secretly heard from himself and that is superior to all other Mantras. They repeated the Mantra always. They worshipped Śiva by offering incense, lights, foods, songs, instrumental music, dances, circumambulations, obeisances, showing mystic gestures of very fresh varieties, seats etc. in accordance with the injunctions. They observed the five Brahmans (i.e. religious austerities of celibacy etc.) and the Ṣaḍaṅgas (that of study, teaching etc.).

67b-69. Thus Brahmā and Viṣṇu propitiated Aruṇa-Śaṅkara for sixteen thousand years and attained Śivajñāna.

This is the secret that has been heard by me directly from my father Śilāda formerly. The same thing has been recounted to you. What else do you wish to hear?

## Chapter 17 - The Sports of Śiva and Pārvatī

## \|\| 4.17.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvāsya vacanaṃ mārkaṃḍeyo'bhyabhāṣata \|*  
*mārkaṃḍeya uvāca \|*  
*śrutameva mayā deva śrotavyaṃ bhavato mukhāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tathāpi kautukenāhamākrāṃto munayo'pyamī \|*  
*gauryā kathaṃ tapastaptaṃ mahādevyātra kathyatām \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. On hearing his words, Mārkaṇḍeya spoke:

## \|\| 4.17.3 \|\|

*naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*kathayāmi tadapyetadyathā'dhigatamātmanā \|*  
*śṛṇu tvamavadhānena mārkaṃḍeya mahāmate \|\| 3 \|\|*

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

O holy Lord, what should be heard has been directly heard from you. Still I am overwhelmed with curiosity. So also are these sages. Let it be narrated how Gaurī, the great Goddess, performed a penance here.

Nandikeśvara said:

3\. I shall recount that also in the manner as it has been understood by me. Listen with attention, O Mārkaṇḍeya of great intellect.

## \|\| 4.17.4 \|\|

*nanu jānāsi tatpūrvaṃ yathā dākṣāyaṇī śivaḥ \|*  
*upayeme satīṃ nāma satīnāmadhidevatām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I hope you know that formerly Śiva married Satī, the Presiding Deity of chaste women, who was the daughter of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 4.17.5 \|\|

*yathā ca sā krudhā bharturdruhi dakṣaprajāpatau \|*  
*yogādahāsīdātmīyaṃ vapurityapi te śrutam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. (You know) how she became furious with Dakṣa, the Prajāpati who was malicious towards her husband, and how she cast off her body by means of Yogic power.

## \|\| 4.17.6 \|\|

*tadā harājñānighnena vīrabhadreṇa yatkṛtam \|*  
*adhvaradhvaṃsanaṃ dakṣasyāpi te viditaṃ mahat \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It is also known to you what had been done then by Vīra-bhadra obediently carrying out the behests of Śiva, viz. the enormous destruction of the sacrifice of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 4.17.7 \|\|

*aśrauṣīstasya dakṣasya gaṇaiḥ śīrṣāsakhaṃḍanam \|*  
*brahmācyuteṃdramukhyānāṃ devānāmapi śikṣaṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. You have heard about the cutting of the head (i.e. decapitation) of Dakṣa by the Gaṇas as well as the punishment meted out to the Devas, the chiefs of whom are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Indra.

## \|\| 4.17.8 \|\|

*daṃtaghātaṃ raveḥ pāṇipāṭanaṃ jātavedasaḥ \|*  
*aditiprabhṛtīnāṃ ca divyastrīṇāṃ parābhavam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. (You have learnt about) the knocking-off of the teeth of Ravi (the Sun-god), the chopping-off of the hand of the Fire-god and the discomfiture of the celestial women Aditi and others.

## \|\| 4.17.9 \|\|

*sā ca devī punarjanma lebhe himavato gṛhe \|*  
*umeti pārvatītyākhyāṃ dvitīyāṃ vibhratī punaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. That Goddess took birth again in the abode of Himavān by the name Umā and another one, Pārvatī, also.

## \|\| 4.17.10 \|\|

*devaḥ sthāṇuvane tāṃ ca paricaryāparaṃ rahaḥ \|*  
*arurocayiṣuḥ kāmamadhākṣītkālavahninā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In the forest of Sthāṇu she was devoted to his service secretly. The Lord was disinclined to her. Hence he burned down Kāma by means of Kālavahni (i.e. fire of world-destruction).

## \|\| 4.17.11 \|\|

*jiteṃdriyaṃ ca taṃ devaṃ kvāpi yātaṃ gaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*tapobhistoṣayāmāsa gaurī śikharavāsinī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Gaurī who stayed on the peak performed austerities. Thereby she pleased that Lord who had subdued all his sense-organs and gone away to an unknown place along with his Gaṇas (attendants).

## \|\| 4.17.12 \|\|

*upayamyātha tāṃ devo vṛttāṃtaiścittakhaṃḍibhiḥ \|*  
*ramayāmāsa caikāṃte modasveti vilāsinīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Lord married her. In a secluded spot he delighted that graceful lady saying “Rejoice”. He pleased her with various stories, incidents (i.e. acts) and love-sports.

## \|\| 4.17.13 \|\|

*vaidhavyakhinnayā ratyā prārthitā śailanaṃdinī \|*  
*kāmapīṭhe tapasyaṃtī kāmaṃ pratyudadīpayat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On being requested by Rati who was distressed on being widowed, the daughter of the Mountain, who was performing penance on Kāmapīṭha, rekindled (i.e. re-suscitated) Kāma once again.

## \|\| 4.17.14 \|\|

*punaśca menayā mātrā pitrā ca himabhūbhṛtā \|*  
*ānītā bhavanaṃ bhartrā sākaṃ ciramaraṃsta sā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Again she was brought home by her mother Menā and her father Himālaya. She sported for a long time with her husband.

## \|\| 4.17.15 \|\|

*tadā śuṃbhaniśuṃbhākhyau lebhāte vedhaso varam \|*  
*devadānavamartyeṣu māstu nau puruṣānmṛtiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. At that time (two demons) named Śuṃbha and Niśuṃbha obtained from Brahmā the boon that their death should never be at the hands of a male among Devas, Dānavas and human beings.

## \|\| 4.17.16 \|\|

*iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā jātatrāsaiḥ suparvabhiḥ \|*  
*abhyarthito'vadaddevo rahaścakradharādibhiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On hearing about this Devas became frightened. The Lord was secretly requested by the Discus-bearing Lord and others:

## \|\| 4.17.17-18 \|\|

*mābhaiṣṭa bhadra kālena tathā pratividhīyate \|*  
*yathā niṣūditau syātāṃ tādṛśau dānavāviti \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dattābhayānmukuṃdādīnvisṛjyāṃdhakasūdanaḥ \|*  
*aṃtaḥpuragato reme devyā saha yathā purā \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. “O gentle Sir, do not be afraid. When (opportune) time comes, it shall be so manoeuvred that such Dānavas would be slain.” He (thus) granted freedom from fear to Viṣṇu and others.

The slayer of Andhaka then bade farewell to them. Then he went to the inner apartment and sported with the Goddess as before.

## \|\| 4.17.19 \|\|

*kadācinmarmalakṣyeṇa prītyā kālīti niṃditā \|*  
*tasya prītyai kālikā ca tvacamevājahānnijām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Once out of love, but pricking her weak points, Pārvatī was (jocularly) criticised as being black. In order to please him Kālīkā immediately cast off her skin.

## \|\| 4.17.20 \|\|

*yatrotkṣiptavatī carma svecchayā parameśvarī \|*  
*mahākāśīprapātākhyaṃ tadabhūtkṣetramuttamam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Where the great Goddess willingly cast off her skin, there came up an excellent holy place named Mahākāśīprapāta (Mahākālīprapāta).

## \|\| 4.17.21 \|\|

*sā ca tvakkauśikī nāmnā kālī viṃdhyādrivāsinī \|*  
*tapasyaṃtī vṛṣasyaṃtau to jaghāna mahāsurau \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The black (Kālī) skin came to be known as Kauśikī. Kālī stayed on the Vindhya mountain performing penance. She killed both the Asuras who were lustful to her.

## \|\| 4.17.22 \|\|

*devī ca gaurī śikhare tasminneva manohare \|*  
*tapobhirlabdhagaurītvādbharttāraṃ samatoṣayat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The Goddess performed penance on that charming peak Gaurīśikhara. Attaining the state of Gaurī (‘White complexioned’) she made her husband delighted.

## \|\| 4.17.23 \|\|

*krameṇa daurhṛdavatī bhūtvā prāsūta pārvatī \|*  
*gajānanaṃ ca heraṃbaṃ senānyaṃ ca ṣaḍānanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Conceiving duly, Pārvatī gave birth to the elephantfaced Heraṃba and the six-faced Senānī (i.e. Subrahmaṇya or Skanda).

## \|\| 4.17.24 \|\|

*tau cāgamavidaḥ prāhurnārāyaṇacaturmukhau \|*  
*pūrvāparādhaśuddhyarthaṃ devīgarbhasamudbhavau \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Those who are conversant with the Āgamas say that those two are Viṣṇu and Brahmā who were born of the womb of the Goddess in order to purify themselves of the previous offence.

## \|\| 4.17.25 \|\|

*vardhamānau ca tau bālau pitrorālokamānayoḥ \|*  
*magnayoriva varṣābdhau premagraṃthirabhūddṛḍhā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. To the parents who were looking at the growing boys and who were immersed in the ocean of delight the knot of love became firmer.

## \|\| 4.17.26 \|\|

*jātu vīṇāninādena kadāciccitralekhanaiḥ \|*  
*vijahratuśśivau svairamekadā maṃḍanairmithaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The couple played and sported in diverse ways sometimes by playing on the lute, on some occasions by painting and drawing pictures. Śiva and Śivā sometimes sported about by adorning each other.

## \|\| 4.17.27 \|\|

*jātu vidyāgamālāpaiḥ kadāciccitravastubhiḥ \|*  
*ekadā lokavṛttāṃtairdaṃpatibhyāṃ vinoditam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Sometimes they talked about topics of learning and the Āgamas. On other occasions they sported about with wonderful objects. On some occasions they discussed the incidents and events of the worlds. Thus the couple diverted themselves.

## \|\| 4.17.28 \|\|

*puṣpāvacayanairjātu kadācidvārikhelanaiḥ \|*  
*adīvyatāṃ ca rāgārdrau dolākelibhirekadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Gathering of flowers, aquatic sports and playing on the swing were the means of diversion for the pair in the height of their passionate attachment to each other.

## \|\| 4.17.29 \|\|

*mainākenārcitau jātu menayā jātu pūjitau \|*  
*jātvarhitau himavatā daṃpatī tau vinoditau \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Sometimes they were welcomed and honoured by Maināka and on other occasions by Menā. The pair (i.e. Śiva and Pārvatī) were duly received and honoured by Himavān and adequately provided with amusements.

## \|\| 4.17.30 \|\|

*jātu dyūtavinodena gatigoṣṭhyā kadācana \|*  
*ekadā dānalīlābhiḥ śivau cikrīḍatuściram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Śiva and Śivā played about for a long time, sometimes by playing at the dice, sometimes by means of music parties and on other occasions by sportful indulgence in charitable gifts.

## \|\| 4.17.31 \|\|

*dyūtanirjitamācchidya patyurutsaṃgatāṃ gatam \|*  
*valayīkṛtameṇāṃkaṃ tāṭaṃkīkṛtavatyumā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Once, while playing with dice, Umā won the game. Therefore she seized the moon that was on the head of her Lord, annulated it and wore it as an ear-ring.

## \|\| 4.17.32 \|\|

*iti tau pitarau carācarāṇāṃ nivasaṃtau kanakācalādikeṣu \|*  
*rucireṣu padeṣu kāmabhogānatihṛdyānsuciraṃ kilānvabhūtām \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Thus the parents of the mobile and immobile beings stayed in various charming and fascinating places such as the Golden Mountain etc. and enjoyed for a long time hearty and romantic pleasures of love-play.

## Chapter 18 - Pārvatī’s Devotional Service to Aruṇācaleśvara

## \|\| 4.18.1 \|\|

*naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*gārhasthyaṃ bibhratī bharturekāmratalavāsinaḥ \|*  
*pakvānnapānaissā tatra paryyatarpayata prajāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:

1\. Managing the domestic duties on behalf of her husband (while) staying at the root of the Ekāmra (‘a Single Mango tree’) she once entertained people by means of cooked rice and beverages.

## \|\| 4.18.2 \|\|

*jātu saṃdhyānusaṃdhānamukulīkṛtalocanam \|*  
*baddhāṃjalipuṭaṃ devamadrākṣīdadrinaṃdinī \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Once the daughter of the Mountain saw the Lord engaged in performing Sandhyā-rote when his eyes were closed and the palms were joined in reverence.

## \|\| 4.18.3 \|\|

*dhyāyate nūnamadhunā kāpi saubhāgyaśālinī \|*  
*kriyate yanmayi prema tanmanye vacanaṃ mahat \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then she thought thus: ‘Certainly some fortunate woman is being meditated upon now (by him). (His professed) love making to me is, I think, a great fraud.

## \|\| 4.18.4 \|\|

*kathaṃ vijñāyate puṃsāṃ kuṭilā mānasī sthitiḥ \|*  
*mithyopacārāddakṣeṇa vaṃcitāsmyamunā bhṛśam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. How can the crooked mental attitude of men be known? I have been thoroughly deceived by this extremely clever one through pretended services.

## \|\| 4.18.5 \|\|

*mayi dākṣiṇyamevāsya manye manasi cedrahaḥ \|*  
*janaḥ saubhāgyavānyasmādbhavati snehabhājanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. I think there he entertains only an insincere courtesy for me in his mind. But when alone, it is the fortunate one who becomes an object of love.

## \|\| 4.18.6 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti te dāsastapobhiḥ krīta ityapi \|*  
*mugdheṃduśekhareṇāsmi vipralabdhā smarāriṇā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. “From now onwards I am your slave. I have been bought by you through your austerities.” Saying thus the enemy of god of Love, the Lord with the crescent moon as his crest-jewel, has deceived me.

## \|\| 4.18.7 \|\|

*asamānānurāgeṣu nārīṇāṃ mūḍhacetasām \|*  
*saubhāgyagarvo lokeṣu parihāsāya kevalam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The pride of matrimonial felicity in those women of deluded minds when love is not of an equal proportion can but evoke derisive laughter among the people.’

## \|\| 4.18.8 \|\|

*iti praṇayaroṣeṇa devyāḥ kaluṣacetasaḥ \|*  
*havyavāhātapālīḍhamivānanamalakṣyata \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When the Goddess had thus an excited mind on account of the anger of (unrequited) love, her face appeared (as if) scorched by fire and the heat of the sun.

## \|\| 4.18.9 \|\|

*vāṣpavāriplave tasyā ātāmre ca vilocane \|*  
*nīlotpale jalāpūrṇe iva bhūmnā virejatuḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Her slightly copper-coloured eyes welling up with tear drops shone much like the blue lotuses filled with water.

## \|\| 4.18.10 \|\|

*yattasyādhīnatilakaṃ bhruvoryugamabhajyata \|*  
*dvedhākṛtamivādarśi manmathasya śarāsanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When her two eyebrows were parted by the circular sectarian mark between them, it appeared as though the bow of the god of Love was broken into two.

## \|\| 4.18.11 \|\|

*aṃtarmanyubhareṇāsyāḥ kaṃpate smādharacchadaḥ \|*  
*muhuḥ pravālasthāyīva raktāśokasya pallavaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Her lower lip frequently quivered on account of the weight of her internal wrath, like the bud of the red Aśoka resting on a tender sprout.

## \|\| 4.18.12 \|\|

*atīva rajyamāne tatpārvatyā gaṃḍamaṃḍalam \|*  
*śāṇāvagharṣamāṇikyadarpaṇapratimaṃ babhau \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The circular (i.e. plump) cheeks of Pārvatī were highly flushed and they shone like polished ruby-mirror.

## \|\| 4.18.13 \|\|

*aṃtarvepadhutau tasyāścakaṃpāte payodharau \|*  
*padmakośāvivāṃtaḥstha caṃcarīkapracālitau \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Her breasts heaving with the internal tremor shook like a pair of lotus buds oscillated by the bees caught within them.

## \|\| 4.18.14 \|\|

*aciṃtayacca saṃbhūya saubhāgyābhāvato nanu \|*  
*mamāyamanyastrīciṃtāṃ kurute caṃdrabhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. She thought thus: ‘Altogether it is indeed on account of the (unfortunate) absence of my conjugal bliss that the Moon-adorned Lord thinks about another woman.

## \|\| 4.18.15 \|\|

*tadaiṣā kvāpi yāsyāmi kimatrāstyekayā mama \|*  
*tapasyate ca saubhāgyamarjanīyaṃ mayādhunā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Therefore, I shall go somewhere. What is (to be done) here by me alone and single. Now marital felicity should be acquired by me by performing penance.

## \|\| 4.18.16 \|\|

*nimīlitākṣiṇyevāsya gaṃtavyaṃ nibhṛtaṃ mayā \|*  
*na cenmāṃ vārayatyeṣa kaṃṭhādupari bhāṣitaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. I must go quietly even as he keeps his eyes closed. If not, he is sure to restrain me by means of (insincere) utterances coming from above his throat.

## \|\| 4.18.17 \|\|

*vatsau tu vardhayatyeva gaṃgeyamativatsalā \|*  
*devastu na smaratyeva māmanyastrīparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. This Gaṅgā who is fond (of them) will bring up my dear children certainly. But, my Lord will not remember me because he is devoted to another woman.’

## \|\| 4.18.18 \|\|

*iti niścitya devasya pārśvādāśu nivṛttya sā \|*  
*anirdiśya diśaṃ kāṃcidyātuṃ vyagrā pracakrame \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After deciding thus, she turned away at once from the side of the Lord. Without having any particular direction in view she began to go anxiously.

## \|\| 4.18.19 \|\|

*calāvatī mālyavatī mālinī vijayā jayā \|*  
*vāritā api saṃraṃbhātsvāminīmanvayuḥ svayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The friends Calāvatī, Mālyavatī, Mālinī, Vijayā and Jayā followed their mistress themselves in great bewilderment, though they were forbidden (by her).

## \|\| 4.18.20 \|\|

*tatra sāpi girīnpuṇyānvanāni nagarāṇi ca \|*  
*sarāṃsi saritaścaiṣā vicacāra samaṃtataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. She roamed about in the holy mountains, forests, cities, lakes and rivers all round.

## \|\| 4.18.21 \|\|

*bhramaṃtī sahyapādeṣu drāviḍākhye sunīvṛti \|*  
*tīrtvā śaktyāpagāṃ devī vijayāṃ samabhāṣata \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Wandering over the excellent territory named Draviḍa at the foot of the Sahya mountain, she crossed the river Śakti. The Goddess then spoke to Vijayā:

## \|\| 4.18.22 \|\|

*dṛśyo'yaṃ nātidūreṇa purastātsakalāruṇaḥ \|*  
*śṛṃgaissaṃlakṣyate'ṣṭābhirnūnaṃ māhātmyavāngiriḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “Not very far off in front is seen a mountain completely red in colour and having eight peaks.{GL\_NOTE::} This mountain certainly appears to be endued with greatness.

## \|\| 4.18.23 \|\|

*upatyakāsu caitasya dṛśyaṃte tāpasāśramāḥ \|*  
*atīva pāvanāḥ śāṃtāḥ puṇyāraṇyamanoharāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On its surrounding valleys and lowlands hermitages of ascetics are seen. They are very sacred and quiet. They are charming on account of the holy penance groves and forests.

## \|\| 4.18.24 \|\|

*gatvā nirūpayāmastānimānpuṇyāśramānvayam \|*  
*prasīdatitarāṃ ceta eṣāṃ saṃdarśanena me \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Let us go and view these holy hermitages. Looking at them my mind is exceedingly pleased.”

## \|\| 4.18.25 \|\|

*evamāhrādayatyāli krameṇa girinaṃdinī \|*  
*tasyādrerjagmuṣī pārśvamapaśyatkaṃcidāśramam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Delighting her friend, the daughter of the Mountain slowly went to the side of that mountain and saw a hermitage.

## \|\| 4.18.26-29 \|\|

*lūtāstaṃtūnnayaṃtyatra kumbhīrāḥ śaivalānyapi \|*  
*śiśūnpuṣṇaṃti nīvāraiḥ sapharānbhūrimāyavaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*haraṃtyavakarānvālaiścamarāḥ sphītaromabhiḥ \|*  
*samīkurvaṃti codbhūtairviṣāṇairyatra sairibhāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*vānarāḥ phalapuṣpāṇi madhupatrāṇi bhallukāḥ \|*  
*kroḍāḥ snānīyamṛtsnāṃ ca yatrarṣibhyo nayaṃtyaho \|\| 28 \|\|*

*kākolūkaiḥ śukaśyenairmṛgavyāghrairharidvipaiḥ \|*  
*kalāpisarpairyatrāsumārjāraiḥ sauhṛdaṃ śritam \|\| 29 \|\|*

26-29. Spiders weave webs here (?) Kuṃbhīras (i.e. sharks etc.) clear away the moss. (Some animals) nourish their young ones with Nīvāra rice; jackals take away fish: Camara deer take away dust heaps with their tails having plenty of hair; buffaloes level up (the bushes) with their raised horns.

Monkeys fetch flowers and fruits for the sages, bears potfuls of honey and boars clay for their ablution and cleansing purposes.

Mutual friendship has been cultivated by (creature with natural animosity such as) crows and owls, parrots and vultures, deer and tigers, lions and elephants, peacocks and serpents as well as rats and cats.

## \|\| 4.18.30 \|\|

*hūyamānapurāḍāśadravyasaurabhyahāriṇī \|*  
*yatra drumāṃtarālebhyo dhūmyā niryāti pāvanī \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Wafting the fragrance of the materials of sacrificial oblation consigned to the sacred fire, a thick cloud of sacred smoke came out through the spaces in between the trees.

## \|\| 4.18.31 \|\|

*paṭhaṃti śatarudrīyaṃ yatra vāyasavairiṇaḥ \|*  
*gṛṇaṃti kākāḥ stotrāṇi sāma gāyaṃti sārikāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Cuckoos here recite the Śatarudrīya text; crows loudly repeat the hymns and prayers and Śārikās (Turdus salica) sing Sāman verses.

## \|\| 4.18.32 \|\|

*śākaśāliṣu śārdūlāścaraṃti ca tathaiva gāḥ \|*  
*siṃcaṃti puṣkarāṃbhobhiḥ kuṃbhinī yatra pādapān \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Tigers as well as cows wander among the plants and paddy fields, and elephants spray the trees with the waters from their trunks.

## \|\| 4.18.33 \|\|

*kvacicca śobhane deśe puṇye puṇyamanohare \|*  
*dadarśa sā tapasyantaṃ yaṃ kaṃciddṛṣisattamam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. In a sacred place that was charming and sanctifying she saw a certain sage engaged in penance.

## \|\| 4.18.34 \|\|

*adhastātsaptaparṇasya citravyāghratvagāsane \|*  
*baddhavīrāsanaṃ samyakpāvane kuśaviṣṭare \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Beneath a Saptaparṇa tree (Alstonia scholaris) he was seated in the ‘heroic’ posture on a tiger skin of variegated colour placed on a sacred mat of Kuśa grass.

## \|\| 4.18.35 \|\|

*śāliśūkāruṇābhābhirjaṭābhirbhasmapāṃḍuram \|*  
*acaṃcalābhirvidyudbhiriva śāradavāridam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He was white in colour owing to the sacred ash smeared all over. With the matted hair having the red lustre of the awn of paddy he appeared like an autumnal cloud with streaks of lighting that are not fickle.

## \|\| 4.18.36 \|\|

*nāsāgraniścaladṛśaṃ samaprasphuritādharam \|*  
*āvarttayantaṃ rudrākṣamālikāmagrapāṇinā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. His eyes were motionlessly fixed at the tip of the nose; his lips throbbed evenly and with the tips of his fingers he was slowly rotating the rosary of Rudrākṣa beads.

## \|\| 4.18.37 \|\|

*pratyagranirṇejanato hyaṃtyaśyānadaśāṃcale \|*  
*vasānaṃ valkalayuge saṃdhyābhre bhūbhṛtāṃ yathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Fresh from his ablution, he was wearing two bark garments not very dry along the borders like a mountain having two clouds at the time of dusk.

## \|\| 4.18.38 \|\|

*ṣaḍvargahiṃsrabaṃdhāya sthāpitāṃ vāgurāmiva \|*  
*upavītatrayīmārādurogartasya bibhratam \|*  
*kṛtocitopacārā sā tamaprākṣīttapodhanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Near the cavity of his chest he had three sacred threads which appeared to be like a net fixed there for catching the wild animals of the six bad qualities, viz. anger, lust etc.

After the requisite customary greetings etc. she asked that ascetic:

Pārvatī enquired:

## \|\| 4.18.39-42 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*kastvaṃ ko'yaṃ girivaro yatra tvaṃ kuruṣe tapaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sa cāhāruṇaśailo'yaṃ puṇyakṣetreṣu pūjitaḥ \|*  
*gautamo'haṃ munirmuktyai tapasārādhaye śivam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ityuktvā vijayādīnāṃ mukhenaināmumāṃ vidan \|*  
*praṇamya bhaktyā bahuśo nītavānuṭajaṃ nijam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kandamūlaphalādyaiśca kṛtātithyāmimāṃ muniḥ \|*  
*jaganmaṃgalamūlāya tapase cānvamanyata \|\| 42 \|\|*

39-42. Who are you please? What is this excellent mountain where you perform penance?

He replied: “This is Aruṇa mountain highly honoured among holy places. I am sage Gautama. For the sake of salvation I propitiate Śiva by means of penance.”

After saying this he understood from Vijayā and others that she was Umā. He then devoutly bowed down to her many times and took her to his own hut.

With bulbous roots, roots, fruits and other things the sage entertained her and allowed her to perform penance for contributing to the auspiciousness of the universe.

## \|\| 4.18.43 \|\|

*jyotiḥstambhasya saṃbhūtimārabhyānukrameṇa saḥ \|*  
*jagāda cāsyai śoṇādrermahimānamaśeṣataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Beginning with the manifestation of the Column of Effulgence, he narrated to her everything and related to her the greatness of Śoṇādri fully.

## \|\| 4.18.44 \|\|

*śoṇādreḥ pūrvadigbhāge sthalīśvaramiti sthalam \|*  
*yatra saṃnihitaḥ śaṃbhurjyotirliṃgātmatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. “To the east of Śoṇādri there is a holy spot named Sthalīśvara. Śaṃbhu is present there in the form of a refulgent Liṅga.

## \|\| 4.18.45 \|\|

*vaikuṇṭhaparameṣṭhyādi gīrvāṇa nibiḍīkṛte \|*  
*na tatra me tapaḥ kartumavyākṣepeṇa śakyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. It is a place thickly crowded by Gīrvāṇas (i.e. Devas) beginning with Viṣṇu and Brahmā. Hence, O Umā, it is not possible (for me) to perform penance there without distraction or hindrance.

## \|\| 4.18.46 \|\|

*ayaṃ śoṇagireḥ pādaḥ pravālācalanāmavān \|*  
*puṇyāraṇyoparuddhatvādrahasyatvaṃ vigāhate \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. This is a foot (i.e. a valley) of the Śoṇa mountain named Pravālācala. Since it is covered and concealed by holy forests, it has some privacy and seclusion.

## \|\| 4.18.47 \|\|

*tata evāhamatraiva pratiṣṭhāpya trilocanam \|*  
*ārādhaye yathāśakti tapobhiḥ kalpitātmabhiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Therefore, I have installed the Three-eyed Lord here itself. I propitiate the Lord in accordance with my capacity by means of various forms of austerities devised by myself.

## \|\| 4.18.48 \|\|

*mamāśramasamīpe'sminpuṇyakṣetramidaṃ mahat \|*  
*kriyatāmāśramo devyā karttavyaṃ hi tapaściram \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In the vicinity of my hermitage is this great holy spot. Let a hermitage be created by the Goddess. Indeed a long penance has to be performed.”

## \|\| 4.18.49-52 \|\|

*munerevamanujñānātkṛtāśramaparigrahā \|*  
*udayuṃkta tapaḥ karttuṃ sumahatparvatātmajā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*āśramaṃ rakṣituṃ satyavatīṃ kānanavāsinīm \|*  
*śubhagāṃ dhuṃdhumāriṃ ca prāgādyāśāsvatiṣṭhipat \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tapovanasya sarvasya rakṣārthaṃ sā samādiśat \|*  
*durgāmanargalasphūrtimājñānirvāhaṇakṣamām \|\| 51 \|\|*

*anaṃtaraṃ sā dhammillaṃ maṃdāraprasavocitam \|*  
*jaṭābharatvaṃ tapase gamayāmāsa pārvatī \|\| 52 \|\|*

49-52. On being permitted by the ascetic the daughter of the Mountain had a hermitage got ready and engaged herself in the task of performing a great penance. In order to protect the hermitage she appointed Satyavatī, Kānanavāsinī, Subhagā and Dhundhumārī in the east and other quarters. For the over-all defence of the entire penance grove she commanded Durgā of unthwartable impetuosity who was capable of carrying out all orders. Thereafter Pārvatī converted her ornamented braid of hair accustomed to wear Mandāra (Erythrina Indica) flowers into a matted hair for the sake of penance.

## \|\| 4.18.53 \|\|

*haṃsacihnadaśaṃ hitvā dukūlaṃ mihakālaghu \|*  
*paruṣaṃ sukumārāṃgī paridhattesma valkalam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The lady of delicate limbs cast off her silk cloth as light as mist with the fringe as soft as the down of a swan and began to wear rough bark garments.

## \|\| 4.18.54 \|\|

*api prasūnāvacayanissahāṃgulipallavā \|*  
*alāvīdatitīkṣṇāgrāṇyavikāraṃ kuśāni sā \|\| 54 \|\|*
